about: Machine-readable changelog of @origingame/engine (docs/release.md §3). kind: patch (0.x.y, compatible) or minor (0.x.0, has breaks). simulation: changed when a game's world can step differently (the golden replays' hashes moved, scripts/replay-gate.ts), else unchanged; versions before 0.6.1 were not measured and say changed. breaking: what a game may have to edit, each with the fix; find lists the identifiers og upgrade searches the game's sources for, codemod a mechanical rewrite it applies. Merges record changes as fragments in changelog/unreleased/, folded in by scripts/release.sh fold and bump; release notes are generated from this file.

breaking.change: dump() returns a DumpResult again, never untyped JSON: `ui:layers` answers `{ kind: "layers", tick, layers }`, `ui:motion` answers `{ kind: "motion", tick, motion }`, and a registered subsystem dump (`physics`, `render`, `audio`, ...) answers `{ kind: "subsystem", name, data }` with the subsystem's report under `data` instead of its fields at the top level with `kind` set to its name. `what` takes `ui:layers` and `ui:motion` only (`ui_layers` and `ui_motion` are refused), and a subsystem dump that fails is an error naming why instead of an unknown name.
breaking.fix: Narrow the result on `kind`; read a subsystem dump's fields from `data` (`dump({ what: "physics" })` gives `{ kind: "subsystem", name: "physics", data }`); write `ui:layers` and `ui:motion` for `ui_layers` and `ui_motion`.

breaking.change: A UI pack extension's extension.json with a `skill` key is refused: the key is gone and unknown keys are refused.
breaking.fix: Delete the `skill` key from extension.json.

breaking.change: The art-bible template replaces {game} with {look}. The look's identity comes from og-project.json, not a project id, and the template no longer guesses assets/looks/<game>.ogt.
breaking.fix: The platform substitutes {look} with og-project.json look.$ogRef (for example base/looks/t7), or the literal preset name when look is a string. Stop substituting {game}; there is no game-id fallback. Resolve a physical file only through the checked project's look binding; boundary A still maps base/looks/t7 to assets/looks/t7.ogt. The engine's artBrief/create helpers do not fill artBibleTemplate.

breaking.change: All source starts in a tick now share ascending entity slot-index order, ignoring generation, before voice allocation and voice-cap selection. New AudioSources, AudioEvent voices, retriggers and sound replacements no longer depend on archetype/query order or on whether a source was already playing. This changes SoundStarted order, voice ids, audio stream hashes and tied fresh-source cap selection where the old code-path order differed.
breaking.fix: Consume SoundStarted in its documented slot-index order, not author call order or new-before-retrigger order. Removing and reinserting AudioSource on the same entity does not change its ordering key. startAt still controls sample-accurate timing; this does not impose chronological event order within the tick.

breaking.change: Plants accept a complete parent-first authored branch skeleton with per-ring radii and a centreline growth box, through the same cook/runtime growth implementation.
breaking.fix: Write branches in parent-first order (root parent -1) with path and radii, or repeated model.plant.branch blocks. Branches and trunk path are exclusive. Bounds stop procedural centreline growth, not foliage triangles.

breaking.change: Import model/texture/font settings and the newly catalogued authored readers reject unknown field names instead of silently accepting unused data.
breaking.fix: Use og api show file:<type> and its nested sections for accepted fields. Remove unused keys or move notes into comments; reflected scene component/resource fields retain their own schema, and vfx2d JSON notes remain ignored.

breaking.change: File field discovery now includes environment, vector, icons, texture arrays, navmesh profiles/areas/links, string tables, game-defined table value forms, humanoid rig mappings, motion-action and shader/post/ui-material fields from parser-owned metadata.
breaking.fix: Query file:environment, file:navmesh.link, file:strings, file:table.row, file:rig or file:shader rather than guessing file fields from runtime records. Table row schemas remain the game's own reflected records.

breaking.change: Removed: every light has a mobility instead (render.LightMobility: movable, stationary, static), which both the renderer and og bake lightmaps read. A light marked static before (one RenderSettings.staticLightReach may cache past its reach) is a stationary light now; stationary is the default, so an unmarked light may be cached too while the reach is above 0, unless it is movable.
breaking.fix: Write mobility: "stationary" for static: true (or leave it out: it is the default), mobility: "movable" for a light that moves; in scene text, mobility stationary.

breaking.change: Behaviours store validated native nodes, routes, keys and machines, including inlined subtree nodes. Loading never reparses author text or reads sibling source files.
breaking.fix: Re-cook behaviour assets and use a matching engine host; old behaviour blobs are not supported.

breaking.change: Checked TypeScript is the sole behaviour author entry. Named definitions compile directly to validated native nodes, keys, routes and machines; canonical subtree refs inline checked trees and participate in cache invalidation. The behaviour OGT parser, grammar and runtime text API are removed.
breaking.fix: Export file.behaviour({name, keys, routes, root}) from content/**/*.ts, use ref('module/ai/tree') for subtree sources, and load the canonical content ID. Use og.ai.create(world, definition) for runtime creation with the same structured shape and cooked subtree ID strings. State bodies are explicit nodes; movement and command controls are explicit. Re-cook assets; there is no text or old-blob fallback.

breaking.change: The pack's sixteen synthesized sounds are checked file.sfx declarations under content/audio; its effect tracks use canonical installed content IDs. Synth descriptions, PCM, WAV and cooked QOA bytes are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Reinstall cinematic-realism and replace vfx/cinematic-realism/sounds/<name>.ogt with base/vfx/cinematic-realism/audio/<name>.

breaking.change: The volumetric layer is drawn by a new model, so every sky with og.Clouds looks different at the same values. A cloud is a shape with a surface (a flat base, a dome of billows, creases eroded into it) and reaches `density` within some tens of metres of that surface, where before `density` was reached only at a cloud's core: the same number draws a more solid cloud. `coverage` is the share of the layer under cloud, which the old model fell well short of (0.4 drew a mostly clear sky; it draws a sky two fifths cloud now, which from the ground reads as broken). The clouds shade themselves over kilometres (dark bases, shaded flanks, bright rims towards the sun), so they are darker under a low sun or moon than before. `detail` erodes billows into the surface instead of thinning the whole cloud. The clouds are marched out to 160 km and fade into the air, where a flat layer stood in for them past 30 km. Under a gradient sky or an Environment's map, which have no air, a low layer fades with its distance and is gone before it reaches the horizon (a base 180 m up is a third as strong 3 km off). No field was removed or renamed.
breaking.fix: Look at each sky again. For a sparser sky lower `coverage` (0.2 to 0.3 is scattered fair-weather cumulus). For the old translucent look lower `density` (0.01 to 0.02) or raise `detail`; for a sheet or a sea of cloud set `kind: "stratus"` or `"stratocumulus"` instead of a cumulus layer at a high `coverage` (their tops and bases are billowed, never flat); for storm towers set `kind: "cumulonimbus"` with 6 to 10 km of `thickness`. Over an og.Environment map the clouds take the map's light at its `intensity`: at 1 they are shaded as the map's own clouds are, above it they stand evenly brighter than the sky behind them.

breaking.change: The cook records the project's profile in its manifest (`profile "3d"` or `"2d"`, from project.ogt's creation form as before), and `og build`, `og run --device` and the play page's build read it there. A manifest without the line is refused (`no profile line: cook the project again`), so a bundle cooked before this version, including one another project names in `cook { uses }`, is cooked again. web-build.ts's ProjectSettings has no `profile` (the `--settings` JSON og passes carries none), and `og build --publish` refuses a 2D project's 3D-world components after the cook rather than before it.
breaking.fix: Cook again (`og cook`; `og run` and `og build` cook first). Read the profile from cooked/.cook.ogt or og-build.json's `game.profile`, not from the build settings.

breaking.change: New projects no longer export an empty og.game({}). They wire built-in title, main menu, loading, pause (with a Quit to menu confirmation), settings, controls rebinding, save/load and credits screens through a session state machine and named presentation stores. Platform/input choices configure device defaults; lang writes imported shell tables and fonts; the look still selects the UI pack. The shell is only built-in screens and controls, in the dark scheme. Interactive films use the same shell over the engine FlowScreen.
breaking.fix: Keep the generated src/shell.tsx and shell-state.ts. Customize strings, give the title and main menu key art and a logo with setShellArt before startShell, initialize gameplay before startShell, and bind gameplay systems to state session / value playing. Complete locale entries seeded in English where the engine has no translation. Do not overwrite src/main.ts with an empty game. Existing og new --look --premise --no-prompt arguments, exit codes and manifest paths are unchanged.

breaking.change: `CreateOptions.profile` and the web shell's `profile` option are removed. An engine's profile is project.ogt's creation form's alone: `project` with `create { form "2d" }` is a 2D engine; any other form, or an engine without a project, is 3D. The play page's config carries no `profile`: the page passes project.ogt's text.
breaking.fix:
Delete `profile` from createEngine and Shell.start options. For a 2D engine without a project file, pass `project: 'type project
version 1
---
create {
  form "2d"
}
'`.

breaking.change: Removed separately stepped environment sun updates; the visible sky, Sky-View LUT, key light and default live environment capture now share the current sun.
breaking.fix: Remove DayNight.step assignments. To trade lighting freshness for lower peak live-sky GPU cost with 13-frame capture cycles, set RenderSettings.skyCaptureSliced to true or apply the low quality preset.

breaking.change: Removed. Every decal names its own texture; the renderer keeps the textures a frame's decals name in an atlas of its own, so decals from different effect packs and the game's own no longer share one texture the game had to build and set.
breaking.fix: Delete the line that sets decalAtlas and set that texture on each decal instead: og.Decal.texture, or a `texture "<id>"` line in a vfx file's `decal` element. uvMin, uvMax and `uv` stay as they are: they are now a region of the decal's own texture.

breaking.change: Removed. A decal's normal map is its own texture, og.Decal.normalMap, read over the same uvMin to uvMax region as its image.
breaking.fix: Put the normal map in a texture laid out as the colour texture is (each mark's map in the cell its colour has) and set og.Decal.normalMap to it.

breaking.change: A `decal` element's `uv` is a region of its own `texture` line, not of og.RenderSettings.decalAtlas. A decal with no `texture` draws a square of its colour.
breaking.fix: Add `texture "<the atlas's id>"` to each `decal` element that has a `uv` line.

breaking.change: Removed: an effect's decals carry their textures.
breaking.fix: Drop the flag and name the texture in the effect's `decal` element.

breaking.change: Mood is no longer a creation choice. `og create` (`og new`) refuses `--mood`, and the look file and project.ogt's create block it writes have no mood line: a new game draws in its look's own mood, the preset's or the chosen variant's. The creation document drops `options.mood`, `mood` from `schema`, `order`/`more` and `compat` (formFields, the looks' and variants' mood), and its `previews/mood/<mood>.webp` slots, so a release fills 37 preview slots, not 43. The look's `mood "<word>"` line, the mood layers and the briefs' mood are unchanged; `readAudioChoices` takes the mood from an older create block, else from the game's look.
breaking.fix: Drop `--mood` from `og create` calls. To give a game another mood, write `mood "<word>"` (bright, dark, warm, cold, soft, high-contrast) in its look file. A reader of creation.json stops reading `options.mood` and the mood previews.

breaking.change: District layout and ordered shape-grammar operations now have closed structured input schemas, generated readonly TypeScript declarations, content-reference metadata and typed decoding. Existing OGT cooking is not switched in this batch.
breaking.fix: Author integrations query the district or grammar entry in cook::source_schemas. Supply explicit region branches and operation objects; named dependencies, polygon validity and grammar terminal ordering remain domain validation.

breaking.change: External imports and model programs expose closed structured schemas, including model preparation, relaxSkin, animation settings, image/audio/font/map/Rive options and the full kernel operation/profile/path vocabulary. This schema batch does not switch existing file formats or execution paths.
breaking.fix: Author integrations query import/model-program in cook::source_schemas. Select an explicit import kind and captured source input (texture interpretation uses usage), or supply typed model operations and parameter values rather than sidecars or JSON source text. Video and other domain importers retain their own typed file schemas.

breaking.change: Authored models and material libraries expose structured schemas with ordered declarations, shared nested Geometry and reflected Transform, typed plants, explicit mesh preparation and fracture, and program material overrides. This batch does not switch existing cooking formats.
breaking.fix: Author integrations query model/materials in cook::source_schemas. Select the model's geometry or program branch, use content references for programs and transfer models, and explicit image inputs for source maps; keep geometric and named-dependency validation in the domain.

breaking.change: New type effect-texture cooks explicit density/heat or shared procedural noise sources into scattering/emission sheets and texture arrays. Particles, effect and vfx files accept one exclusive generate block returning EffectSource {text}, through the existing restricted TS executor. Their normal parsers still own validation and references.
breaking.fix: Declare all effect-texture parameters (og api show file:effect-texture), reference its id as a sheet or #array as a texture array, and return only body declarations from effect generators. See effects section 5 for the checked recipe.

breaking.change: Records include context (look, scene, position and camera). Preview isolates runtime metadata from the project's boot scene; --project-look or --look and --scene apply environment/scene resources to the six shots and cost runs while bounds remain black-stage measurements. Cost-only requires an identical recorded context.
breaking.fix: Regenerate old preview records before --cost-only. Use --project-look --scene <asset> to review in context, --position x,y,z for exact placement (no auto-lift), and --camera px,py,pz,tx,ty,tz,fov for an explicit world-space view.

breaking.member: og vfx import and effekseer-* packs
breaking.change: Effekseer conversion writes explicit file.import declarations for textures and meshes, with native model settings. All ten packs include declarations for their 243 textures and 41 meshes; model OGT sidecars are removed.
breaking.fix: Reinstall the packs or rerun og vfx import into content/. Keep its generated file.import declarations alongside file.vfx, file.particles and file.effect. Raw textures/models alone no longer cook; edit conform:'effect' in the model declaration instead of a sidecar.

breaking.change: Effekseer conversion returns native FX and checked TypeScript declarations instead of OGT effects, particles and timelines. CLI output belongs under content/, --root names the project root, and raw textures/models go under the corresponding assets/ path. Model import settings retain their sidecars.
breaking.fix: Import into <project>/content/<folder> (optionally --root <project>) and load the printed base/<folder>/<effect> ID. Edit the emitted file.vfx, file.particles and file.effect declarations; recook raw .efkproj/.efkefc assets with the new engine.

breaking.change: All ten downloadable Effekseer packs use checked TypeScript content declarations instead of OGT FX author files and require engine 0.9.0. Native fields and seeded timelines are preserved; models and textures retain their existing import path.
breaking.fix: Reinstall the updated pack and replace vfx/<pack>/<effect>.ogt with base/vfx/<pack>/<effect>. Edit declarations under content/vfx/<pack>/; raw textures and models remain under assets/vfx/<pack>/.

breaking.change: The engine resolves as a package: og keeps `node_modules/@origingame/engine` (ignored by Git) pointing at the engine it runs with, in place of `.og/engine`, and TypeScript, the bundler and an editor read `@origingame/engine` and every subpath from the engine's package.json `exports` (`moduleResolution "bundler"`). A tsconfig.json `paths` entry into `.og/engine` names a link that no longer exists. `bun:test`'s declarations are the export `@origingame/engine/bun-test`, named in `types`. A bare entry outside a project (no project.ogt) is no longer type-checked: it has no link.
breaking.fix: `og upgrade` drops the `@origingame/engine…` and `bun:test` entries into `.og/engine` from tsconfig.json's `paths` (and the block when nothing else is left in it) and adds `"@origingame/engine/bun-test"` to `types`; it lists a line it cannot take (two entries on one line) for you to edit the same way. Check a bare entry inside a project, or run it with --no-check.

breaking.change: Auto exposure brings a view's mean luminance to a key that follows how bright the view is (Krawczyk, Myszkowski and Seidel 2005), not to middle grey whatever the view. A daylit landscape, whose mean is about a sixteenth of a white in full sun, is exposed as before. A view that is mostly sunlit white (a cloud deck from above, a snowfield) is about a stop brighter and no longer grey; a stronger sun makes the same view brighter; a dusk is about a stop darker and a night two. Every auto-exposed frame whose mean is not a sixteenth moves.
breaking.fix: Look at each auto-exposed scene again. Take out a Camera.exposure that was opening up a white view (2 to 2.8) or holding a night down, and an autoExposureMax set only to keep a night from metering to grey. Where a view is now too bright or too dark, move it with Camera.exposure (2 is a stop up, 0.5 a stop down). A look with `autoExposure false` is unchanged.

breaking.change: HeightmapDesc accepts metre-valued heights up to 4097 samples per side. Cook and runtime reject invalid stage parameters instead of the runtime silently clamping them; terraceSharpness is replaced by terraceBlend (default 0.4), matching terrain.generate.terraces.blend.
breaking.fix: Pass heights with columns/rows to process a designed field, use terraceBlend for terrace smoothing, and supply parameters in the documented terrain generator ranges.

breaking.change: og.film.chart's links carry `points` (x, y pairs in graph units: the same level-leaving cubic, sampled in 16 segments) instead of `d`, an SVG path string. A UI `<Line>` draws points; nothing draws path data.
breaking.fix: Read `link.points` where you read `link.d`, and pass it to NodeGraph's link `points` (or a `<Line points viewBox>`).

breaking.change: Only the tolerance band is discarded as background; beyond it, the matte grows through locally explained blends instead of a second tolerance-wide alpha ramp. Colour-difference fitting and the Smith–Blinn alpha bound preserve neutral steel and prevent clipped RGB unmixing from inventing colours.
breaking.fix: Keep key colours, tolerance and holes settings. Re-cook animated-source flipbooks to get the corrected matte; tolerance still sets the fully removed background band and holes still includes enclosed pockets.

breaking.change: The creation form film is removed: forms are 2d, 2.5d and 3d, the world's. An interactive film is genre "interactive-film" in the form its live scenes and levels draw in, its flow run by project.ogt's flow line. og check and the cook refuse form "film", naming the fix.
breaking.fix: Write form "3d" (og upgrade rewrites it) and keep genre "interactive-film". To let the engine start and draw the flow, add flow "story/<name>.yarn" to project.ogt and delete the game's own og.story.load, og.flow.load, og.flow.start and its picture, Subtitles and FlowChoices mounts; read the flow with og.flow.current(world).

breaking.change: A form no longer decides which creation fields apply: formFields and GAME_ONLY are gone, CREATION_FIELDS lists the create block's fields, and the creation document's compat.formFields is compat.fields. Every genre but interactive-film names a view; an interactive film may leave it out. The creation document has no film form (byForm, looks' forms).
breaking.fix: Read CREATION_FIELDS (compat.fields) instead of formFields(form) (compat.formFields[form]), and treat view as optional for genre interactive-film.

breaking.change: The module that paces a Yarn dialogue by its segments is og.flow, in every name a game writes. API: `og.film.*` is `og.flow.*`, the component `og.Film` is `og.Flow`, `og.FilmDeck` `og.FlowDeck`, the events `og.FilmSegment`, `og.FilmChoice`, `og.FilmChapter` and `og.FilmEnded` are `og.Flow…`, and the types `FilmInfo`, `FilmView`, `FilmHotspot`, `FilmChart`, `FilmChartNode` and `FilmChartLink` are `Flow…`; `FilmDesc` is `FlowStartDesc` (og.nav has a FlowDesc). Yarn headers: `og-film`, `og-film-chapter`, `og-film-ending` and `og-film-dissolve` are `og-flow…`. Timeline markers: `film.open`, `film.lock` and `film.cut` are `flow.open`, `flow.lock` and `flow.cut`. Probe commands: `film:choose:<index>`, `film:play`, `film:pause` and `film:skip` are `flow:…`. Components and screens: `FilmChoices` is `FlowChoices` (screen `flow-choices`), `FilmChaptersScreen` `FlowChaptersScreen` (`flow-chapters`), `FilmFlowchartScreen` `FlowChartScreen` (`flow-chart`) and `FilmGalleryScreen` `FlowGalleryScreen` (`flow-gallery`), with their string keys (`screen.flow-choices.label`) and parts (`::part(flow-choices.shade)`). The guide is `og api show flow`. What the module does is unchanged, and a save taken before the upgrade restores: its og.Film records and its conversation's hold header are read as the new names.
breaking.fix: `og upgrade` rewrites all of these in src/, assets/ and tests/, Yarn files included. One rename is left to you: the field that names the flow on `FlowView`, `og.FlowDeck` and the four events was `film` and is `flow` (`view.film` becomes `view.flow`, an event's `e.film` `e.flow`); `og check` names each read of the old field. The persistence keys and telemetry names the guide suggests are now `flow.<dialogue>.seen`, `flow.<dialogue>.endings`, `flow_choice`, `flow_ending` and `flow_quit`; they are your game's own and `og upgrade` leaves them, so a shipped game keeps the keys its players' data is under.

breaking.change: The showcase's installed cinematic pack now uses the same sixteen checked file.sfx declarations and canonical sound references as the shipped pack. The synthesized audio is unchanged.
breaking.fix: Keep the showcase's content/vfx/cinematic-realism/audio declarations with its assets when copying the project; remove the obsolete assets/vfx/cinematic-realism/sounds OGT files.

breaking.change: Automatic site placement now uses the cook's shared Mitchell best-candidate sampler, including impact clustering; it no longer falls back to sites outside the mesh. The same seed may therefore produce different shards than the former runtime-only sampler.
breaking.fix: Recook generated fracture assets and rebuild games together. Supply explicit sites when a design requires fixed cut centres; insufficient interior sites fail instead of using an alternate sampler.

breaking.change: Descriptors with authored buffers use the generated binary wire on both hosts.
breaking.fix: Regenerate and rebuild host bindings together; game TypeScript continues to pass the generated descriptor. No JSON-wire fallback remains.

breaking.change: The GPU's culling and scatter counts stay on the GPU until a probe call reads them, instead of being read back every frame. Natively state().timings.triangles, dump_render's counts and expect:timings:triangles report the last frame's own counts, as before. On the web the call asks for the next frame's: the first state() or dump_render after it reports them, and one before any read reports triangles without the GPU-culled draws and dump_render's scatter as null.
breaking.fix: On the web, read triangles or dump_render twice with a frame between (advance 1, or a frame of the host), and check countsLag in dump_render before trusting the scatter counts.

breaking.change: Defaults to half instead of full (matching ssrResolution), tracing ambient occlusion at half resolution with a normal- and depth-aware bilateral upsample. QualityPreset.high keeps full.
breaking.fix: Set aoResolution: "full" on PostEffects or RenderSettings.aoResolution: "full" if full-resolution AO is required on medium quality.

breaking.change: Defaults to half instead of full, tracing screen-space GI at half resolution with a normal- and depth-aware bilateral upsample. QualityPreset.high keeps full.
breaking.fix: Set resolution: "full" on GlobalIllumination or RenderSettings.aoResolution: "full" if full-resolution SSGI is required on medium quality.

breaking.change: Local light shadow maps now project casters' back faces in a single R32Float pass (matching directional cascades) instead of rendering front and back faces in two Rg32Float Woo midpoint passes. Single-sided thin geometry with side: "front" no longer casts local shadows from its front face alone.
breaking.fix: Set side: "double" on single-sided thin wall, plane, or foliage materials that must cast shadows from local point, spot, or area lights.

breaking.change: Sharpens with contrast-adaptive sharpening in the tonemap, after depth of field and motion blur, instead of a pass right after TAA (or FSR's RCAS); with PostEffects.sharpen set, the stronger of the two applies once.
breaking.fix: Retune taaSharpen by eye; lower PostEffects.sharpen where both were set to add up.

breaking.change: A frame's answer no longer carries `maxFps`: the engine keeps the frame cap itself for every presenting host (`Engine.present`, the IDL's `og_present_frame`), so no host reads the cap to skip frames. og.render.display's `maxFps` still answers the cap resolved.
breaking.fix: A host or harness that paced itself by the answer's `maxFps` hands each display frame to `engine.present(nowMs)` instead, which draws or skips it and answers `nextMs`; one that only showed the cap reads `og.render.display(world).maxFps`. No codemod: the field had no reader in a game's code, and a host's loop is rewritten by hand.

breaking.change: A play `sample`'s `frames` are the engine's performance record binned, and a hitch is now a frame whose interval is more than twice the median of the 64 frames before it (none in the first 8), a long one also 250 ms or more; it was any interval of 50 ms or more. The shape `{ count, ms, bins, interval, work, hitches, longHitches, max }` is unchanged. A game drawn at a steady 30 no longer counts every frame a hitch.
breaking.fix: A dashboard that compares hitch counts across this version reads them as the new definition; nothing in a game changes. No codemod: the figures are the Player's, not a game's source.

breaking.change: A desktop package's exit report (`og-hermes`'s last line) carries the engine's performance record as `perf` (its `frame interval`, `frame work` and per-stage lines, after the first 60 drawn frames) in place of `measured`, `intervalMs`, `p50`, `p95`, `frameCallMs`, `gameMs`, `ticksPerFrame` and `gameMsPerTick`.
breaking.fix: Read `perf.lines` (`frame interval`'s median and p95, `cpu game systems` for the game's code). No codemod: the report is a tool's output.

breaking.change: The <hud> control's frame shadow is now --hud-frame-shadow. --hud-shadow is only the HUD text shadow the built-in components set their text with; the two shared one name, so a pack that set it for the frame gave that text an invalid text-shadow, and the default frame drew the text shadow.
breaking.fix: In a style pack, rename --hud-shadow to --hud-frame-shadow where it styles hud::part(frame); keep --hud-shadow only for a text shadow.

breaking.change: External models, textures, sounds, fonts, Rive and Tiled/LDtk maps require checked content/**/*.ts file.import declarations with exact owning-module assets/ or sources/ inputs. Cooked IDs are canonical module/content IDs; native controls and captured external dependencies replace OGT import sidecars, directory defaults, merge rules and filename guessing. Source moves keep content IDs stable.
breaking.fix: Declare each external asset with file.import({kind, source, ...controls}), share settings through TS imports, bind model libraries and map textures/tilesets with ref('module/content-id'), and load the declaration ID. Remove type import documents, import.ogt defaults and raw-filename loads. Bundled and downloadable FX packs, including installed copies, declare their raw resources the same way; effect meshes state conform: 'effect' on their model imports.

breaking.change: Renamed og.input.isActionLongPressed: it answers whether an action has been down for its holdMs (a long press), which `held` read as merely down.
breaking.fix: Call og.input.isActionLongPressed(world, name) where og.input.isActionHeld(world, name) was. For down at all, call og.input.isActionDown.

breaking.change: The development inspector's panel is a TSX component mounted on the game's UI at the `system` layer, so `dump_inspector`'s `elements` are its nodes as `dump_ui` lists TSX nodes: a path of op ids with each control's `role`, `text` and name, no longer named paths such as `Inspector/Tools/Undo` or `Inspector/Bar/Save`. The panel draws in the game's UI fonts, and it stays above every layer of the game's own UI.
breaking.fix: Find a panel control in `dump_inspector`'s `elements` by its role and text (the `button` whose text is `Undo`) and press its centre with `touch_move` as before.

breaking.change: Is an Option.u32: null for a non-cutting inspect hotspot, the ChoiceView.index otherwise; FlowHotspot also gains kind, shape, label and inspected.
breaking.fix: Check hotspot.kind === "inspect" (choice is null) and route it to og.flow.inspect; pass a choice hotspot's choice to og.flow.choose.

breaking.change: Is an Option.u32: null for a link from a node without choices, instead of -1.
breaking.fix: Test link.choice === null where the code tested -1.

breaking.change: og.timeline now runs before og.video in the same tick, and og.flow persists queued ops, gestures, inspected clues, transcript history, and persistent BGM in its own FlowBlock state block.
breaking.fix: Existing world snapshots taken before this change are incompatible; re-record snapshots and golden hashes.

breaking.change: A project look (project.ogt's `look`) that fails, such as a mood the look does not know, now stops `og cook` with `assets/<look>: <error> (project.ogt's look)` and changes nothing in cooked/. Before, the cook went on without the look, cooking every model texture without it and again once the look was fixed.
breaking.fix: Fix the look file the error names, then cook again.

breaking.change: The file directory includes look root/UI seed fields and writable reflected resource fields, derived lightmap binding fields and the full video source field table. Lightmap records now refuse unknown fields at every nesting level.
breaking.fix: Query file:look.PostEffects, file:lightmap.model.part or file:video. Use og bake lightmaps to regenerate a lightmap record rather than adding unrecognized fields. Look field limits and enum names come from the same IDL records the cook validates.

breaking.change: Material libraries can declare a source image for deterministic periodic and derived-map preparation during cook. Generated maps are virtual inputs consumed by the normal model and texture pipelines.
breaking.fix: Write generate { source "input.png" } and explicit map destinations instead of maintaining a preprocessing script. Generated destinations must not also be authored files.

breaking.change: Model files and import.model settings declare repair, decimate, unwrap, bake and rig processing through the existing mesh kernels.
breaking.fix: Use an explicit process block instead of an external preparation script. Static meshes only: existing skins, morphs and animation are rejected rather than discarded; unwrap of textured input requires bake.

breaking.change: Model processing can project explicitly registered authored views into prepared UV maps during cook, through the existing og-bake projection kernel.
breaking.fix: Declare project.size and repeated view image paths with position, target and either fov or ortho. Images are square with alpha masks, tracked as content dependencies. Cameras are explicit; cook does not fit, draw or request concept images.

breaking.change: Models can explicitly relax existing skin weights in regions stretched by the cook's stress probes, before welding and LOD generation. Defaults to false; reports changed vertices and remaining stretch after at most 12 deterministic widening passes, retaining a result that worsens no probe pose. Probes and position welding now use model-space skin binds, including quantised meshes' dequantisation, rather than treating accessor units as model units. The Last Light uses its original unsmoothed asset with this import setting instead of an external repair script.
breaking.fix: Set model { relaxSkin true } in import settings to repair flagged regions; inspect the cooked character in its animations and review any remaining skin stretch warnings. Leave the setting absent to preserve authored weights.

breaking.change: Model OGT sources, bufferGeometry.generate script wrappers, scanned .shape.json programs and sibling-program guessing are removed. Models and model programs are checked TypeScript declarations consumed directly by the native cook. Model processing, fracture, materials, plants and animation options share the checked declaration snapshot.
breaking.fix: Declare content/**/*.ts with file.model({kind:'geometry',desc:{items,...}}) or file.model({kind:'program',desc:{program:ref('module/program'),...}}); declare programs with file['model-program']({...}). Compute bufferGeometry arrays in ordinary imported TS helpers. Use canonical content refs for mesh operands and animation libraries, and explicit owning-module assets/ or sources/ paths for images and fonts. Put model import controls in desc.options. og model tools accept checked program declarations; bake writes a new .baked.ts declaration under content/ and captured maps under sources/baked/. Standalone kernel JSON remains a modelling-tool exchange input only.

breaking.change: Animation graph blobs now store validated native motions, layers, transitions and clip bindings instead of author text. Old graph blobs are rejected.
breaking.fix: Re-cook animation graphs and use matching native and web hosts.

breaking.change: Flipbook blobs store bounded native little-endian sheet fields instead of reparsing canonical author text at load. Playback data and behavior are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Re-cook flipbooks and install matching engine hosts. Old cooked flipbook blobs are unsupported.

breaking.change: Font-pack indexes store native metadata, ordered face IDs, language tags and Unicode coverage rows. Runtime no longer parses an index text document and old blobs are refused.
breaking.fix: Re-cook font packs with the matching engine; rebuild native and web hosts together with the cook. Font files, their import settings, lazy downloads and conditional hyphenation/segmentation dictionaries retain their behavior.

breaking.change: Humanoid rig maps load native fields and bone rows instead of an embedded author document.
breaking.fix: Re-cook rigs and use matching native and web hosts; old rig blobs are not supported.

breaking.change: 2D rig blobs store validated native bones, slots, attachments, constraints, animation channels, skins and child armatures instead of canonical OGT text. Old rig blobs are rejected.
breaking.fix: Re-cook 2D rigs and use matching native and web hosts.

breaking.member: cook delivery references / Web pruning / manifest dependencies
breaking.change: Delivery validation, publish pruning and manifest dependencies now follow retained native payload references, not author declaration strings or all outputs sharing a source. Embedded cook inputs no longer create download edges. Runtime companions, texture layers, scene relocations and all video playback variants remain reachable. Existing index checkpoints are invalidated.
breaking.fix: Re-cook before exporting. Keep dependsOn for references actually loaded across delivery packs; remove edges needed only for embedded author inputs if desired. Declare publish.keep for otherwise unreachable assets loaded through external conventions; computed game-code loads remain conservative.

breaking.change: Cooked string tables contain reflected locale metadata, ordered font references and ICU message sources, not an embedded author document. Runtime localization loads the native payload and compiles only ICU messages; the old runtime text payload is removed.
breaking.fix: Re-cook with the matching engine runtime. The TypeScript author-entry cutover follows in the same migration stack; this format step does not introduce a second author path.

breaking.change: A `poly` point's `bulge` is now in half-chords, as DXF and CAD polylines give it (1 is a half circle; 0.3 on a 370 mm edge rises 55.5 mm). It was the arch's rise in mm, so the fractions an author writes arched nothing visible.
breaking.fix: Divide an old bulge by half its edge's length: an edge of length L with bulge s (mm) becomes s / (L / 2).

breaking.change: A lit mesh particle emitter takes `translucency <0..1>` (TS: `translucency`), default 0: the share of the light on a piece's far side (the sun with its shadow, the sky, local lights) that passes through it. A thin piece such as a paper card, a leaf or confetti seen from its shadowed side now shows that light through its colour instead of going dark. Only meshes take it; any other render mode refuses a value above 0. Emitters that leave it out draw as before.
breaking.fix: Set `translucency` (about 0.4 to 0.7) on lit mesh emitters of thin pieces that turned black away from the sun; leave solid debris at 0.

breaking.change: 3D bodies now enable gyroscopic torque by default; spinning asymmetric bodies can follow different trajectories.
breaking.fix: Set gyroscopic: false explicitly if the game wants rotation without gyroscopic torque, and retune spinning bodies.

breaking.change: Physics now precedes og.camera and og.ui.end/sound/audio. Camera collision and world-anchored UI read this tick's simulated transforms rather than the previous tick's.
breaking.fix: Remove compensating one-tick camera/UI offsets and order systems against the new post-physics presentation boundary.

breaking.change: All scene queries use the live Rapier world, including ragdoll bones and 2D wheels. Before og.physics they see tick-start colliders; after it they see the new step. Between ticks they see the last simulation state, not unsynchronized ECS edits. The boundary system initializes once, without rebuilding a shadow BVH each tick.
breaking.fix: Run gameplay queries before og.physics for tick-start visibility; run post-step queries after it. Expect newly spawned or moved ECS colliders only after physics synchronizes them. Exclude the caster to apply ContactHook.ignore and compound self-exclusion.

breaking.change: Engine save migrations, automatic engine/session layout mapping and RestoreDesc.migrate are removed. Saves use og-save:4 with the exact engine version, strict saved layouts and physics state format 2; old formats and other engine versions are refused, never upgraded.
breaking.fix: Start new saves on engine/layout changes; remove migrate from RestoreDesc. Register collider assets before restoring a current-format save. Explicit SaveEdit edits of game-owned data remain available within the current engine version.

breaking.change: Compound mass/centerOfMass no longer double-count collider mass; sensors contribute no mass. Parented bodies and static colliders now use full world transforms, including mirrored mesh winding and negative scale.
breaking.fix: Remove mass/COM and parent-transform workarounds, then retune bodies that depended on the previous incorrect inertia or collider placement.

breaking.change: Changing damping, gravity scale, locks, CCD or other nonstructural body/collider parameters patches the live objects rather than rebuilding them and losing contact warm starts or joints. Kinematic motion retains pose-derived velocity.
breaking.fix: Do not rely on parameter edits to reset simulation; explicitly reset the intended pose/velocity. Keep body kind, mass/COM and shape/topology changes separate when a rebuild is intended.

breaking.change: Queued forces, torques, air drag, buoyancy and force-field effects now act through the substep loop instead of only the first substep. Buoyancy samples the evolving body pose.
breaking.fix: Remove substep-count multipliers from forces and retune drag/buoyancy against their physical units.

breaking.change: Solid impacts that begin and end inside one tick's substeps now emit CollisionStarted and CollisionEnded even when no contact survives the final substep. Contact impulses accumulate across substeps.
breaking.fix: Handle a Started/Ended pair in the same event batch and avoid assuming every impact appears in the final og.Contact list.

breaking.change: Hooks apply symmetrically to both sides and inherit from a compound's body. Two friction/restitution overrides are averaged; conveyor surface velocities combine as their relative motion. Each one-way side keeps independent contact state. Hook changes wake affected contacts.
breaking.fix: Remove handle-order-dependent hook workarounds and specify each surface's own velocity/one-way direction rather than the pair's combined result.

breaking.change: Nonstructural joint edits preserve warm starts and hinge reference angles; breakForce/breakTorque use solver load over substeps rather than an extra gravity-load approximation.
breaking.fix: Remove joint-recreation/angle-offset compensation and retune break thresholds to the solver's force and torque.

breaking.change: Settled bodies lose residual velocity without rolling their simulated pose back. Sleeping connected islands are traversed coherently and wake on relevant gravity, body, collider and hook changes.
breaking.fix: Do not depend on restSpeed freezing a previous pose or on parameter edits leaving bodies asleep; use explicit locks or constraints for fixed poses.

breaking.change: Water, Wind, WindMotor, ForceField and Volume inputs synchronize immediately before physics, after gameplay and scene/stream updates, rather than in an early before-tick hook. Terrain restore edits replay before initial physics queries.
breaking.fix: Remove one-tick environment buffering and apply environment edits in gameplay systems for this tick's step.

breaking.change: Ray, point-projection and shape-cast reaches must be finite and nonnegative; zero remains unbounded. Compound self-exclusion uses the body identity and heightfield chunk hits are deduplicated.
breaking.fix: Pass 0 for unbounded reach instead of Infinity, reject negative/NaN distances in game input, and stop manually filtering duplicate chunk hits.

breaking.change: Controllers move before rigid-body substeps, publish poses sequentially, and exclusively own dynamic pushing. Teleports no longer become kinematic sweeps.
breaking.fix: Read controller and sensor results on the next game tick as before; set pushBodies, mass and pushStrength explicitly for virtual pushing.

breaking.change: Dynamic pushing uses virtual controller mass, contact-point effective mass and torque, with a shared pushStrength impulse budget. Standing applies controller weight at the support point. Both new mass fields default to zero and push nothing.
breaking.fix: Set mass in kg, pushBodies true and pushStrength in N to enable pushing; retune old forces that depended on infinite kinematic mass.

breaking.member: CharacterController.up, addVelocity, jumpBuffer, buffer, inheritedVelocity, platformInherit; PlatformerController.platformInherit
breaking.change: Characters use an up axis for grounding, slopes and jumping; zero derives up opposite Physics.gravity each step, with no inferred axis under zero world gravity. Added velocity is consumed once; jumpBuffer holds presses; platformInherit controls momentum on leaving support. New numeric controls default to zero (off).
breaking.fix: Leave up zero to follow world gravity, or set a nonzero up axis to override it. Use gravityScale zero for free movement. Set jumpBuffer seconds and platformInherit share explicitly; use addVelocity for springs and knockback. Do not write buffer or inheritedVelocity.

breaking.member: CharacterController and PlatformerController groundBody, groundPoint, groundPosition, groundQuaternion; CharacterController.velocity
breaking.change: Support tracks the collider and parent frame separately, carrying compound and moved static platforms with swept displacement and 3D yaw. Character velocity includes carry. New support fields are written state and shift with WorldOrigin.
breaking.fix: Use ground for the supporting collider, groundBody for its parent; leave support points and frames to physics. Do not add platform velocity to CharacterController.velocity again.

breaking.member: PlatformerController.dropTime, droppingThrough, wallCoyoteTime, wallCoyote, lastWall, oneWayMask
breaking.change: dropTime is deleted. Drop-through ignores only droppingThrough until the character bounds clear that entity, clears coyote time, and accepts sloped one-way faces. Wall coyote time is explicit and zero means off; walls exclude walkable slopes and prefer input in narrow gaps.
breaking.fix: Remove dropTime reads and writes; read droppingThrough instead. Set wallCoyoteTime to enable grace after leaving a wall and leave wallCoyote/lastWall to physics.

breaking.change: New clearance-checked capsule resize returns a boolean, preserves feet through Collider.offset, and edits the existing body without losing velocity or joints.
breaking.fix: Use resizeCharacter(world, entity, cylindricalHeight, radius), rather than replacing Collider to crouch or stand. Handle false for blocked clearance; inside systems declare Collider writes and Transform, Parent and controller reads.

breaking.member: CHARACTER_CRUSHED, CHARACTER_BUMPED, CharacterEvent.speed; PlatformerController gravity; controller ContactHook
breaking.change: CRUSHED is kind 7; BUMPED comes from actual upward hits and LANDED reports this tick's impact speed. Movers recover overlaps, resolve multiple planes, and obey ContactHook.ignore/oneWay/surfaceVelocity. Platformer gravity scaling now preserves designed jump height, apex hang applies on both sides, and 3D platformers return an error. Swimming retains entry momentum and blends flow by immersion.
breaking.fix: Handle CHARACTER_CRUSHED alongside existing events, use the 2D profile for PlatformerController, and retune jump/water behavior that relied on the old bugs. Apply ContactHook rules to controllers just as to bodies.

breaking.change: Replaces frequency/damping and tip multipliers with independent stiffness and drag. Chains use complete Parent world matrices, segment collisions and joint-local collider radii. Animation state format is 2; old snapshots are not supported.
breaking.fix: Author stiffness (acceleration per metre) and drag (velocity decay per second) explicitly. Set tailOffset for leaf tails, teleportDistance and maxSpeed for reset/capping, wind for wind coupling, and worldColliders for optional world collision. Recreate old saves.

breaking.change: Extracted motion is reported as rootDelta and rootYawDelta; rootMotionMode selects direct Transform motion or collision-safe controller movement.
breaking.fix: Use rootMotionMode controller with CharacterController for swept root displacement. Read the Skeleton deltas instead of inferring desired motion from Transform changes. New controller input rootDelta is consumed once.

breaking.change: Requires an explicit skin-joint whitelist; never infers a humanoid from names. Rigs are built from the rest pose and entity world scale. Each bone supports mass, shape, jointKind, hingeAxis and asymmetric twist bounds.
breaking.fix: Pass the bones array or author RagdollRigDesc. Supply a nonzero bone-local hingeAxis for hinges, and author the desired joint bounds.

breaking.change: Dynamic bones must be selected in boneMask (empty means none); layers/mask are explicit and zero disables contacts. Owner capsules and adjacent bones are excluded pairwise, not by a global layer. Activation uses COM velocities and mass-weighted total impulse; blending is local-space FK.
breaking.fix: Set boneMask to rig indices and layers/mask to the desired collision groups. Set motorStiffness/motorDamping for PD drive and driveTransform to follow the root. Use applyRagdollImpulse for a world-space point hit on one bone. Recreate old physics snapshots.

breaking.change: Locks are world-space across Parent motion and drop their anchor immediately beyond maxDistance. Ground adaptation and ankle normal alignment respect weight.
breaking.fix: Set groundReach for PhysicsQuery ground rays and pelvisDrop for optional pelvis adaptation. Use maxDistance to release teleports without pulling a leg towards the old anchor.

breaking.change: Returns an exact Mat4 inverse rather than an inexact TRS under rotated non-uniform scale.
breaking.fix: Use inverse_transform_point for points, or multiply the inverse matrix with matrices. Use Mat4::transform_point3 for matrix point transforms.

breaking.change: Replaces the raycast controller with substep wheel angular dynamics and combined-slip tyres. Grip is the actual tyre friction coefficient times ground friction, without hidden multipliers. engineForce and brakeForce are wheel torques in N·m in both profiles. suspensionDamping and driftGrip are deleted. Adds compressionDamping, reboundDamping, bumpStopStiffness, antiRollStiffness, brakeBias, wheelCast, aeroDrag, aeroDownforce, rollingResistance, ackermann, steeringFade, abs and tcs; new numbers are off at zero. Physics snapshots containing vehicles use the new wheel state without migration.
breaking.fix: Retune wheel torques and use grip around 1–1.5 for road tyres on friction-1 ground. Set compressionDamping and reboundDamping explicitly instead of suspensionDamping; remove driftGrip and tune real grip and handbrakeGrip. Opt into suspension, steering, aero and driving assists with nonzero values. Start new saves.

breaking.change: The drivetrain couples an engine flywheel through a clutch to measured wheel angular speeds, with gearbox hysteresis and one direction transition. Adds engineInertia, clutchStrength, engineBraking, differential, differentialStrength and awdBias. The handbrake no longer discards engine torque.
breaking.fix: Set nonzero engineInertia (kg·m²) and clutchStrength (N·m) to enable drivetrain drive. Select open, lsd or locked differential; set differentialStrength for LSD. Zero axle/brake bias means equal per-wheel torque; positive values are front-axle shares.

breaking.change: Supports up to sixteen wheels in both profiles with in-place geometry and grip updates. Adds an explicit chassis-local mount and separate compressionDamping/reboundDamping; deletes suspensionDamping. Zero mount captures the initial local Transform once, independent of visual pose updates.
breaking.fix: Author mount explicitly for multi-axle vehicles and copy vehicleWheels poses to game-owned visual Transforms. Replace suspensionDamping with explicit compressionDamping and reboundDamping.

breaking.change: Adds suspensionCompression, load, contactPoint, contactNormal, groundEntity and angularVelocity. Slip is measured from wheel/ground relative motion in both profiles, not the old skid multiplier.
breaking.fix: Use contact and load to gate road effects, contactPoint/contactNormal and groundEntity for marks and material sounds, and angularVelocity for wheel-speed telemetry.

breaking.change: CPU ropes use explicit-velocity small-step XPBD. New stiffness (default 100000 N/m), mass (default 0.1 kg per point), substeps (default 4), coupling and breakForce fields control compliance, point mass, stepping, two-way rigid attachment/contact impulses and persistent overload breaks. Length edits reel the existing rope instead of rebuilding it; end accepts any Transform.
breaking.fix: Choose physical stiffness and point mass, enable coupling to transfer loads to dynamic endpoints and colliders, and set breakForce when breakage is wanted. Zero stiffness, substeps, coupling and breakForce disable their respective behaviors. Recreate old simulation state.

breaking.change: CPU cloth replaces Verlet/PBD with explicit velocities, area-lumped masses and XPBD. Stiffness is now physical N/m (default 100000); new bending, tether, density (default 1 kg/m²), drag and lift fields control dihedral bending, unilateral long-range attachments and aerodynamics. Wind is air velocity in m/s, not acceleration. Thickness enables vertex-triangle and edge-edge self-contact without the old speed cap; solids exchange momentum.
breaking.fix: Retune stiffness in physical units. Set nonzero drag/lift to make wind act, bending/tether to enable those constraints, and density to set surface mass (zero fixes free points). Choose substeps for contact resolution; zero substeps pauses simulation.

breaking.change: CPU garments use area-lumped explicit-velocity XPBD with physical stiffness (default 100000) and dihedral bending. New density (default 1), drag, lift, bodyRadius, backstopRadius and teleportDistance fields replace planar backstop and index-hashed wind behavior. MaxDistance/backstop scale with the character; wind is air velocity in m/s. Solid and body contacts remove inward relative velocity instead of accumulating gravity.
breaking.fix: Retune physical stiffness/bending and set drag/lift for wind. Set backstopRadius for spherical backstops and backstop for their offset, bodyRadius for posed skeleton capsules, and teleportDistance for pose-jump resets; zero disables each optional mechanism. Recreate old garment state.

breaking.change: CPU soft bodies use explicit-velocity XPBD, area-lumped masses, centroid-relative signed volume and gradients, and two-way solid contacts. Stiffness and volumeStiffness are physical coefficients (both default 100000); new density (default 1 kg/m²) and tetraStiffness enable surface mass and per-centroid-fan hydrostatic Neo-Hookean volume constraints. Registered mesh content revisions rebuild the shape on hot reload.
breaking.fix: Retune the physical edge/volume stiffness, set density for mass and tetraStiffness when local tetrahedral volume preservation is needed (zero disables it). The tetrahedral fan uses the surface centroid as a virtual interior vertex. Recreate old soft-body state.

breaking.change: PBF replaces DDR. New solverIterations (default 3, zero disables pressure passes) and vorticity (default zero/off) control density projection and confinement. Stiffness is the density relaxation fraction [0,1] (default 1); nearStiffness is the dimensionless s_corr coefficient (default 0.001); restDensity is the unnormalised poly6 count including self, multiplied by interpolated material density to obtain target mass density (default 2, zero disables pressure). Viscosity is stable mass-conserving XSPH. Count zero produces no particles; size edits rebuild the lattice. Mixed properties interpolate by composition; contacts push dynamic bodies.
breaking.fix: Retune density/stiffness/artificial pressure for PBF instead of DDR and set solverIterations/substeps for convergence. Use vorticity only when confinement is wanted. Recreate old fluid state.

breaking.change: CPU fluids use the same PBF, symmetric pressure, XSPH, mixed-material and two-way contact contract as Fluid2D, with solverIterations default 3, vorticity default 0, stiffness default 1, nearStiffness default 0.001 and restDensity default 2. Reflected radius now agrees with the Rust default, 0.2 m. Size edits rebuild the lattice and lowering maxCount truncates particles in order even when emission is disabled; maxCount zero empties the fluid.
breaking.fix: Retune the CPU material for PBF and recreate old fluid state. Use solverIterations zero to turn off density passes, vorticity zero for no confinement, and explicit maxCount for the particle budget. Visual GPU simulation is a separate solver.

breaking.change: EmitOffset, emitVelocity, the emitter cube, sinkOffset and the sink box now use entity-local axes and rotate with the entity. Emission rejects overlapping spawn candidates rather than fusing zero-distance particles.
breaking.fix: Express emitter offsets/velocities and sink boxes in local coordinates. A point emitter can defer drops while its previous drop still occupies the nozzle.

breaking.change: Triangle mesh colliders bake with ORIENTED pseudo-normals for point-solid inside classification, including reflected winding under negative scale. The triangle-mesh bake header is now OGTM version 2; old bakes are rejected.
breaking.fix: Recook triangle mesh assets and use consistently outward-wound closed meshes for solid interiors.

breaking.change: CPU soft and particle-fluid integration samples ForceField and WindMotor at every point, and the physics block stores the new XPBD/PBF state layout instead of Verlet/DDR state. Deferred reaction impulses update rigid velocities and wake events in the same tick.
breaking.fix: Recreate snapshots/replays from this engine version; old physics saves are not supported. Recheck spatial wind and force tuning because midpoint-only sampling is gone.

breaking.change: The Rust host pose contract adds world-space capsules: Vec<GarmentCapsule>, with endpoints a/b and endpoint radii radius_a/radius_b for tapered body contacts. The runtime supplies posed skeleton capsules when Garment.bodyRadius is nonzero.
breaking.fix: Host pose constructors must supply capsules (an empty vector disables body capsules), in canonical skeleton order and with radii already scaled into world metres.

breaking.member: Cloth, SoftBody, Garment and Fluid3D visual simulation
breaking.change: GPU visual bodies use relative air velocity for drag and lift, tick-normalised contact friction, corrected volume compliance and skinned garment rest lengths; they also sample ForceField acceleration at every point. Sensors and zero-layer colliders no longer collide, negative scales keep positive radii, and cylinders and convex hulls are extracted. Terrain collision uses an independent patch per body, respects holes and pushes along the surface normal. Visual fluid emitters clamp to the grid, accumulate pressure without signed-integer wrap, draw count-zero emitters at their requested radius and recycle sink particles only at emitRate. GPU simulation state survives render-origin and WorldOrigin shifts rather than restarting.
breaking.fix: Use wind as air velocity in metres per second and friction as the share of slide lost per tick. Retune visual wind and volumeStiffness where needed; use sensor or layers: 0 for non-solid triggers. No game-code change is required for origin shifts.

breaking.change: Water volumes have an explicit vertical depth (zero disables the volume). Queries select the highest enclosing volume at the point's height, not a waterway above it. Rectangular Water volumes respect the entity's rotation.
breaking.fix: Set depth on Water and WaterSurface. Query a point inside the volume; use waterHeight for a named surface from above. Supply rotation and depth when constructing a Rust WaterBody.

breaking.change: Hull samples are cached by collider geometry. Lift and drag are summed from one substep snapshot and applied once; rotation damps exponentially. Overlapping pools lift once at the highest level. Ragdoll lift uses each bone's actual collider volume. Buoyancy also works in 2D.
breaking.fix: Retune waterDensity for ragdolls using their actual mass and volume. Use Buoyancy on 2D rigid bodies for sampled hull lift instead of the pool's automatic lift. Retune floating bodies for the corrected per-substep forces.

breaking.change: WaterLine replaces springs with conservative 1D shallow-water depth and momentum fluxes; tension and spread are removed. WaterSurface preserves waveSpeed with CFL substeps, supports sponge borders, scales splash forcing by dt and raises wakes from horizontal hull motion with clipped planar hull displacement.
breaking.fix: Delete tension and spread; depth and gravity set the shallow-water wave speed. Set both spongeWidth and spongeDamping to enable absorbing borders (zero is off), and retune splash.

breaking.change: Ocean surface inversion uses three Newton steps. River queries use a canonical segment AABB grid and f32 geometry; translated rivers translate their index with the course.
breaking.fix: Expect corrected water queries and floating motion; no alternate solver or legacy save format is retained.

breaking.change: Chunks use material density and true body COM velocities; foundations and zero-tension masonry carry compression only. Capped stress solves persist their warm starts. Removed destructibles retain budgeted visible orphan chunks. Pixel outlines are native seamless polylines, detached pieces preserve concavities with compound convex colliders, and same-tick blasts accumulate symmetrically.
breaking.fix: Retune destructible impulses and stress strengths for real masses and unilateral support. Recreate saves: destruction, pixel terrain and tilemap state formats changed; old snapshots are not accepted.

breaking.change: innerRadius greater than radius is rejected, radius zero does nothing, and ExplosionDesc.occlusion optionally shields chunks behind live colliders. Explosions cull props outside their world bounds.
breaking.fix: Pass 0 <= innerRadius <= radius; set occlusion true when cover should block a blast. Leave occlusion false to disable ray testing.

breaking.change: Baked colliders use content hashes, reuse trimesh BVHs at arbitrary scale and support collider convex or collider vhacd. Fracture format 3 stores real hulls, contact section inertia, anchor normals and debris samples. Tiled imports retain all closed shapes and orthogonal maps collide through seamless chunk-local union outlines respecting parent transforms.
breaking.fix: Cook assets again. Use collider true for trimeshes, collider convex for a hull, or collider vhacd for a convex compound with a convex collider. Custom fracture anchors use anchor plane nx ny nz distance with the normal pointing into the model. Rust hosts use bake_collider(mesh, BakeKind) and set_baked_collider instead of the removed trimesh-only methods.

breaking.change: The destruction module is split into independently guarded destruction3d and destruction2d modules; texture edits upload dirty rectangles without replacing texture bindings. debug:physics displays destruction load, anchors, supports and pixel edit boundaries.
breaking.fix: Rebuild web exports and deploy their generated wasm module manifest as a unit. Do not reuse an old destruction module or cooked assets.

breaking.change: The web module's three pipeline hooks are gone. The renderer now keeps one pipeline cache on every host, with one state per pipeline (queued, creating, ready), and a host supplies only its compiler. A host glue installs it with `og_web_pipeline_compiler(asking, count, made, compiled, finish)`. `asking(on)` wraps each pipeline the cache makes, so the glue can ask the browser for it asynchronously and number it. `count()` and `made()` report how many are numbered and how many of those are compiled, `compiled(n)` whether pipeline `n` is, and `finish(n)` makes pipeline `n` at once. `og_web_frame_skipped()` replaces `og_web_pipelines_held()`: it returns how many draws the last frame skipped and how much work it left for a pipeline that was not ready. The probe's `boot.pipelines` counts rename `fallback` to `waited` and `spans` to `asks`.
breaking.fix: A host that runs the engine's Worker (src/web/worker.ts) needs no change. A host glue of its own calls `og_web_pipeline_compiler` with its compiler instead of the three removed calls, as src/web/worker/start.ts does with src/web/pipelines.ts, and draws its first frame again while `og_web_frame_skipped()` is above 0. A script that reads the probe's `boot.pipelines` reads `waited` and `asks`.

breaking.change: The pixel preset renders 270 lines (Stylise.pixelHeight 270, ArtPixels.logicalHeight 270) instead of 224, so a 1080p output scales by a whole 4x and fills the frame without a border.
breaking.fix: Games on the pixel preset see more of the scene vertically (and horizontally, which follows the aspect); frame cameras, tile counts and sprite sizes for 270 lines. A game that wants 224 sets Stylise.pixelHeight 224 and ArtPixels.logicalHeight 224 in its own look.

breaking.change: The engine package's knowledge/presets/ holds the look presets as og-cook's look step flattened them, not their source: `<slug>.json` lists the preset as a game's look asking for each of its variants (or none) in each mood (or its own), each `{ variant, mood, look: { name, mood, variant, ui, antialias, uiSeeds, blocks } }` with every field's values as written; `moods.json` holds each mood's layer under a look that reaches no preset, and `palettes.json` the built-in palettes' text by file name. The `.ogt` presets and their `assets/palettes/`, `moods/` and `variants/` directories are gone from it. The art brief (`readLook`, `presetLook`, whose signatures are unchanged) reads these files, so it can no longer disagree with the cook: a look that reaches no preset and asks a mood now gets the mood's layer, as the cook gives it. `ReadLookOptions.presets` names a directory of this shape.
breaking.fix: Read `knowledge/presets/<slug>.json` and pick the entry whose `variant` and `mood` are the ones asked (null for none), or call `presetLook(slug, { variant, mood })`, which does. A `presets` option pointing at a copy of templates/looks points at knowledge/presets instead.

breaking.change: The verdict is the renderer's record of the last frame drawn, written by the culls that drew it (the GPU cull's camera pass with its occlusion test, or the CPU cull on the GL tier), instead of a separate CPU frustum test over a fresh extraction. Without a renderer no cull runs: an entity with a drawing component answers untracked (visible null) instead of drawn, outside_view or layer, and an expect:entity:<id>:visible.* check is unchecked. On the web the record is the newest frame whose readback landed (a frame or two old); the first call after a while answers untracked and asks for the next frame's. An entity in view but behind the occluders answers occluded instead of drawn, one fading in with nothing shown fading_in instead of loading, one whose material is wireframe untracked (detail wireframe) instead of loading, and Visibility.culled counts occluded drawables too.
breaking.fix: Run the checks that read a verdict with a renderer (og test on a GPU host, og run); call visible again a frame later on the web; accept occluded and fading_in where a test expected drawn or loading for such entities.

breaking.change: Returns a native Float32Array transferred over the OGB1 binary wire instead of a JSON number array.
breaking.fix: Consume the returned Float32Array directly (or wrap with Array.from(...) only if a plain JS Array is required).

breaking.change: BspResult.cells is now a native Uint8Array transferred over binary wire (0 wall, 1 room, 2 corridor), and BspResult gains room-graph edges.
breaking.fix: Read cells directly as a Uint8Array; indexing and length work identically, or call Array.from(res.cells) if a plain JS Array is required.

breaking.change: WfcResult.tiles is now a Uint32Array and WfcResult.rotations is now a Uint8Array transferred over binary wire.
breaking.fix: Read tiles and rotations directly as TypedArrays; indexing works identically, or convert with Array.from(...) if a plain JS Array is required.

breaking.change: The top-level `profile` line is gone: the creation form, `create { form "2d" }`, is the one field the profile follows. Form 2d is the 2D profile (rapier2d, the art brief's sprites, the cook's 2D conformance and style check, the 2D publish module); 2.5d, 3d, film or no form is 3D. A project that still has a `profile` line is refused naming this fix. A game `og create --form 2d` made before this change had no `profile` line and ran, was briefed, conformed and published as 3D; it is now 2D.
breaking.fix: `og upgrade` moves the line: `profile "2d"` becomes `create { form "2d" }` (a line of the create block when there is one), `profile "3d"` is deleted. It lists a `profile` line beside a create block whose form disagrees for you to settle by hand.

breaking.change: `resolveCreationChoices(premise, input?, catalogue?)` takes no `profile` argument: the form chooses the profile the look is picked for (`profileOf(form)`, exported by the art brief and @origingame/create-game).
breaking.fix: Drop the third argument; pass `{ form: "2d" }` in `input` for a 2D look. A call that passed a catalogue fourth passes it third.

breaking.change: A `gamepad` event is now the pad's raw state, which og-input maps to the standard layout: `layout`, `guid`, `buttons` as raw values (numbers, not names), `axes` and `hat`. `triggers` and `device` are gone: the triggers are buttons 6 and 7 of the standard layout, and the family comes from the GUID's vendor or the mapping's name.
breaking.fix: `og upgrade` rewrites a one-line `gamepad` event: `buttons` by name become values by index (`["a"]` becomes `[1]`), `triggers` fold into buttons 6 and 7, and `device` becomes its vendor's `guid` (030000004c0500000000000000000000 for playstation). It lists any event spread over lines or built from variables for you to rewrite the same way. The `gamepad:` probe command is unchanged.

breaking.change: The web shell no longer presses keys for pad buttons (A Space, B Escape, the d-pad and left stick the arrows, Start Enter…). No replacement keeps it: pads press only pad controls, so a game that read only keys does not answer a pad.
breaking.fix: No replacement: the shell's key fallback is the loss. Bind pad controls beside the keys: `og.input.defineAction(world, { name: "jump", kind: "button", bindings: [{ control: "Space" }, { control: "pad.a" }] })`; a TSX UI's confirm, back and navigation already read the pad.

breaking.change: Removed all Markdown author guides, wiki/guide-*.md pages, guide recipes, guide search entries and the api show --guide / api_list guide options. The search.tsv format is now version 6. og migrate reports reference names instead of numbered guide sections.
breaking.fix: Use og api find/show for API members, file:<type> checked inputs and named UI components. File entries now come directly from input schemas; component entries come from their TypeScript source. Consume the wiki and index shipped by the same engine version; stop opening or mounting guide pages. Author guides will be redesigned separately.

breaking.change: A restart event payload mismatch reports the first differing event's zero-based index and fields (with start and now values) in restart.diff.events, and names its index, field and values in restart.first, instead of reporting only queue counts.
breaking.fix: Read index and fields for payload differences; start and now on each event queue remain its counts. Entity fields still compare through the same structural pairing as components; event order remains significant.

breaking.change: A playtest restart check (and `og run --restart-at`) compares a tick number, a field of the new unit `tick` (og.Vfx.startTick and ran, og.ParticleSystem.startTick, og.destruction's Chunk.looseTick), as how long before its world's og.Time it was, not as the number: a restart at tick 1870 that writes 1870 matches a fresh start's 0, and an effect kept from the first start whose startTick stays 0 now differs (`startTick is {"ticksAgo":1871}, a fresh start's {"ticksAgo":1}`).
breaking.fix: On a restart, write the tick to the startTick of every effect and particle system the restart keeps instead of spawning again (og.vfx writes ran from it).

breaking.change: Synthesis layers accept explicit mono PCM, sample rate, tuning reference and looping through the same Rust synth as type sfx. File layers can reference an authored audio file with tracked content dependencies.
breaking.fix: Set sample instead of an oscillator waveform; keep the envelope duration explicit. Stereo file sources average to mono; FM is oscillator-only and rejected for sample layers.

breaking.change: The public art-brief kind union adds material and facade after keyframe; exhaustive dispatchers must handle both image kinds.
breaking.fix: Handle material as an opaque unlit base-colour image tiling both axes, and facade as an opaque elevation tiling horizontally only. Preserve the supplied prompt and references.

breaking.change: Now also sets a sea's caustics: the short waves that focus its bright lines, in cells per metre, which its longer waves bend and move. A sea's caustics were its long waves alone, read from a 0.4 m grid about the camera: the few waves some 2 m and longer that grid holds interfered into a regular lattice of soft blobs, and the waves that focus the light at those depths were missing.
breaking.fix: Set causticsScale on a sea with caustics for the size of their cells (0.6, the default, a breeze's wavelets).

breaking.change: A built-in screen draws an action row or button only when the game passes its handler. PauseScreen draws Resume, Settings, Controls, Save, Load, Quit to menu and Quit game only with onResume, onSettings, onControls, onSave, onLoad, onQuitToMenu and onQuit; MainMenuScreen its entries only with onContinue (and canContinue), onNewGame, onModes, onSettings, onCredits and onQuit, and its news card is pressable only with onNews; ResultsScreen Replay, Again and Continue; GameOverScreen Retry, Checkpoint, Quit, Revive and Decline; SettingsScreen Back, Defaults, Revert and Apply; ModeSelectScreen Back and Play; SaveLoadScreen Back, Delete, Load, New and Save; TitleScreen its press prompt only with onStart. Before, each was drawn and did nothing when pressed.
breaking.fix: Pass the handler of every row the game shows; a row it leaves out is not drawn, so leave a handler out (or pass undefined) to hide its row. Save still greys by canSave, Apply and Revert by pending.

breaking.change: The catalogue and shipped presets now contain only pixel (topdown variant), cartoon-2d, faceted-low-poly, toy-3d (paper variant), inked-comic-3d and neon-vector. Removed cinematic-realism (muted), painterly-3d (lush, luminous-layers, expressionist), minimal-geometric (layered-silhouette), low-resolution-3d (monochrome-dither), pixel-3d-hybrid and anime-cel-3d. Also removed pixel variants 8bit, monochrome, detailed, luminous and coarse; cartoon-2d variants watercolor, storybook and rubber-hose; toy-3d variants voxel, clay and diorama; inked-comic-3d variants bold-comic and heavy-ink. Their previews, authored art, art bibles and mood overrides are no longer shipped. The six base moods remain.
breaking.fix: Refresh the platform catalogue, preset and preview payload together. Replace cinematic-realism and minimal-geometric with faceted-low-poly; painterly-3d with toy-3d or cartoon-2d; low-resolution-3d and pixel-3d-hybrid with pixel for a 2D view or faceted-low-poly for 3D; anime-cel-3d with inked-comic-3d. These are new art directions, not visual equivalents. Replace a retired variant with its retained base look, pixel:topdown or toy-3d:paper as appropriate; remove its variant field otherwise. New film creation defaults to faceted-low-poly. No aliases or fallback for removed presets.

breaking.change: Removed cinematic-realism, cartoon-2d-watercolor, cartoon-2d-storybook and cartoon-2d-rubber-hose downloadable packs and the realistic-starter bundled pack. They are not used by the scaffold or default creation flow.
breaking.fix: Use geometric for faceted-low-poly, cartoon-2d for flat 2D effects, pixel-scenario for pixel effects, or the retained effekseer-* packs for 3D effects. Update effect IDs and review the replacement's placement, timing and art; no compatibility packs or old IDs remain.

breaking.change: Pure story function bodies use the same structured expression schema as file.dialogue and file.quest. Yarn expression strings and the public standalone Yarn expression parser are removed.
breaking.fix: Replace body:'$value * 2' with body:{kind:'binary',op:'mul',left:{kind:'variable',name:'value'},right:{kind:'literal',value:2}}. Keep existing typed parameters and returns. External Yarn files remain explicit file.dialogue input.text imports.

breaking.member: file.dialogue, file.quest, og.story.load and story saves
breaking.change: Story authoring is checked TypeScript and cooked native data only. Automatic Yarn scanning, quest OGT parsing, runtime story.parse and old story save formats are removed. Stable line identities are independent of localization keys.
breaking.fix: Declare nodes, lines, conditions and commands with file.dialogue, and stages/objectives with file.quest under content/. Load canonical base/... IDs. Import external Yarn explicitly with file.dialogue({yarn:input.text('sources/story.yarn'),assets:{name:ref('base/...')}}). Recook stories and start new saves.

breaking.change: Removed the obsolete author-OGT formatter, its MCP tool and the creator's ignored --choices switch.
breaking.fix: Author TypeScript declarations through og add/og set and discover creation flags with og create --creation; omit --choices.

breaking.change: Development pages accept only structured source edits naming scene, entity, component, field and value, and emit source_changed on the dev stream and probe wire. Source file/line/column metadata is development-only; publish scenes carry none.
breaking.fix: Send {og:'dev',v:1,from:'host',type:'edit',id,edit:{scene,entity,component,field,value}} in the same document/origin. Handle edit_result and source_changed; computed values are refused with their location and no write. Do not retain runtime overrides or send source text.
