breaking.member: font import settings: charset, em_px, px_range, page_size, runtime, features, color, color_px, palette
breaking.change: The cook no longer makes a font atlas: a font blob carries the face's file, whole, and every character is laid out and rastered from it at the size it is drawn, COLR glyphs in colour. The settings that chose and sized the atlas are gone, and the cook refuses a font .ogt or a .riv import's font block that still names one. A font blob has no glyph table, kerning or pages: FontInfo's glyphs and pages are 0.
breaking.fix: Delete the lines (og upgrade does). A character outside the old charset now draws with nothing to do. A features line's tags go in CSS font-feature-settings or font-variant-* (or TypeStep.features); a palette line's choice in CSS font-palette.

breaking.member: font import setting chars (a font .ogt's font block and a .riv import's font <name> block)
breaking.change: chars only checked a face for the characters it listed, a check left from the atlas, which drew only the characters cooked into it. A face now ships whole and any character it has draws, and a character it lacks falls back through the chain, so the cook refuses a chars line. A .riv's font still notes the characters its own runs show that the face lacks.
breaking.fix: Delete the line (og upgrade does). To see which characters a text draws from which face, read the probe's missing-glyph warnings.

breaking.change: A font has no atlas of its own any more (every glyph is rastered from its file at the size it is drawn), so FontInfo no longer reports one. It reports the face instead: family, weight (its OS/2 weight class) and axes (its variation axes' tags). ascender, descender, lineHeight, icons and pixel are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Read family, weight or axes; a game that sized text from emPx or pxRange sets TextDesc.size or a CSS font-size in px instead.

breaking.change: The cook keeps a font's file whole and lays text out from it, so the number of glyphs cooked into a font is no longer a cost: the budget is gone and project.ogt refuses it as an unknown budget. og cook --report's font entry gives glyphs (the file's), fileBytes and icons.
breaking.fix: Delete the fontGlyphs line from project.ogt's budgets block; a font's size shows under budgets.assetBytes.

breaking.change: Stdout is JSON Lines and nothing else: the `og test: bun test (N file(s))` line, the bun tests' own report, the `did not run: the type check failed` line and the closing summary now go to stderr. Each playtest line carries `event: "playtest"` beside its `playtest` name.
breaking.fix: A tool that read the summary from stdout reads the last line's `test` event (or stderr); one that found playtest lines by their `{"playtest"` prefix may keep doing so or select `event == "playtest"`. Scripts without --json see no change.

breaking.change: The `touch.xy` control and InputBinding's `radius` are gone: touch sticks have one model, the on-screen stick the UI lays out (TouchControls, or a View with `touchStick`).
breaking.fix: Drop a `touch.xy` binding and its `radius`, and put TouchControls (or a View with `touchStick` and the action) on the HUD instead.

breaking.change: A `touch` binding no longer takes a zone: it reads a touch anywhere on the play surface. A touch in one part of the screen has one model, the on-screen button the UI lays out (a View with `touchButton`), which also shows its press. A saved binding's `zone` is ignored.
breaking.fix: Drop the binding's `zone` and put a View with `touchButton="<action>"` over that part of the screen on the HUD (`absolute` with the zone's fractions as percent insets, such as `absolute left-1/2 top-0 w-1/2 h-full` for the right half). No codemod: the replacement is a node in the game's UI tree, not an edit of the binding.

breaking.change: Animation graphs are structured TypeScript data. GraphDesc.text, the OGT author parser, grammar and field tables are removed. Cook and runtime use the same named graph builder and native validation. Blend children are named objects, not tuples.
breaking.fix: Export file.animgraph({sprite:true,motions:{idle:{kind:'clip',clip:'idle'}},layers:[{name:'base',entry:'idle',states:[{name:'idle',motion:'idle'}]}]}) under content/. Use canonical ref IDs in skeletal bindings and canonical IDs in og.load.animgraph. At runtime pass params/motions/layers to og.anim.graph instead of text. Write blend children as {motion,threshold} or {motion,point:[x,y]}. Re-cook with matching hosts.

breaking.change: Each evaluated entry is limited to 64 MiB of canonical binary output, one million structural nodes and 128 nested containers; typed array samples occupy a packed buffer rather than individual structural nodes.
breaking.fix: Split larger worlds into independently cooked tiles or content entries and use numeric typed arrays for dense samples. Do not rely on one unbounded default export.

breaking.change: TypeScript shapes for closed object alternatives now forbid other closed alternatives' missing keys with optional never fields, including local definition references. This rejects mixed source selections that schema and serde already refused, rather than letting TypeScript's excess-property union rule accept them. Open dictionaries remain open; runtime validation is unchanged.
breaking.fix: Supply one source alternative, not fields or external tags from multiple alternatives. Keep common fields shared by the schema branches and leave all other alternatives' keys absent.

breaking.change: project.ogt is removed as project configuration and discovery. Ordinary og-project.json (version 1) is the sole project marker and name/engine/look authority; project.ts exports defineProject configuration. Hosts receive structured ProjectStartup, not OGT text. Cook consumes the restricted TS index/evaluator/reference graph, and watch refreshes bootstrap, generated types and import dependencies on edits. No old-project fallback is provided.
breaking.fix: Create a new-format project with og new. Keep engine/name/look only in og-project.json, put configuration in project.ts, and use canonical content refs. Replace OGT startup strings with checked og project --json startup data. Capture scripts are a project.ts screens map; storyFunctions declares ordered parameters and typed returns. Unmigrated scene/prefab/look/Yarn dialogue retain their one physical cooked ID: only project refs use base/<assets-relative-stem>, bound through actual scan results before ProjectStartup is emitted. Existing scene references and game og.load IDs remain unchanged; no lookup fallback or OGT bridge is added. Duplicate canonical TS/scanned identities fail. Each domain cutover moves its outputs to canonical IDs and deletes its binding with its author parser: P1 look, P2 dialogue, P3 scene/prefab.

breaking.member: knowledge scaffold / defaultRoots / payload / readLook / readAudioChoices / creationBlock
breaking.change: The scaffold payload and release overlay replace project.ogt with og-project.json and project.ts. defaultRoots discovers that JSON marker. readLook and readAudioChoices read the checked og project --json snapshot instead of parsing project OGT, and now require the matching installed og executable on PATH or OG_BIN. The creationBlock OGT serializer and its create-game re-export are removed. Signatures and return shapes of defaultRoots, payload, installed, mount, summary, readLook, readAudioChoices, presetLook and artBrief are unchanged; presetLook and artBrief still need no executable.
breaking.fix: Switch platform scaffold/layout validation to require og-project.json plus project.ts and read name/engine/look from JSON. Install the matching released og before invoking project briefs (or set OG_BIN). Use parseCreationInput/inferCreationChoices/resolveCreationChoices objects as project.ts defineProject create input, or call og new, instead of creationBlock. Do not execute TS in the platform. Release pin stamping now updates og-project.json engine rather than project.ogt engine lines.

breaking.change: Building grammars use checked TypeScript declarations consumed directly as native shape rules. The grammar OGT author parser and grammar tables are deleted; there is no TS-to-OGT stage.
breaking.fix: Export file.grammar({params,start,rules}) from content/**/*.ts. Write ordered discriminated operations in each named rule; each ends in exactly one terminal operation. Numbers are literals or declared parameter names. Insert models use canonical content refs. District buildings.rule names the grammar's canonical module/content ID instead of an assets/*.ogt path. Re-cook; old grammar sources are unsupported.

breaking.member: author ContentIndex kinds and reference constraints
breaking.change: ContentIndex and evaluated graphs distinguish the source factory from its primary output kind. Domain schemas map model-program to model, effect-texture to texture, sfx to sound, vfx2d to flipbook, theme to pack and font-extension to font-pack. Output reference constraints no longer include source-factory aliases. Model program and theme inheritance references require original source declarations, not other same-kind or derived outputs.
breaking.fix: Use the entry's factory to identify its source decoder and kind to identify what consumers receive. Keep the existing factory calls and reference IDs. For parameterized models, point program at a model-program entry; for theme inheritance, point extends at a theme entry. This foundation does not yet switch CLI/scaffold formats or domain cook frontends.

breaking.member: tileset author input and native tilemap snapshots
breaking.change: Tilesets are checked TypeScript declarations with native binary payloads. The tileset author parser, text writer, grammar tables and old cooked-text loader are removed. Embedded Tiled/LDtk tilesets and tilemap snapshots use the same native codec.
breaking.fix: Write file.tileset under content/ with tileWidth, tileHeight, columns, rows, tiles and terrains. Use an optional canonical texture ref with a different ID from the tileset. Animations use matching frames and positive durations; uniform fps is frames.map(() => 1 / fps). Tiled external TSX/TSJ and LDtk image overrides use explicit tilemap import bindTileset source-path canonical-ID settings, never guessed siblings. Update map tileset IDs, re-cook and install matching hosts; old tileset files, cooked maps and saves are unsupported.

breaking.change: Cook modules reject dynamic import and await before execution. Source outputs reject undefined, functions, symbols, BigInt, promises, class instances, sparse arrays, hidden/accessor properties and cycles instead of silently dropping or coercing them through JSON.stringify.
breaking.fix: Use synchronous static imports and explicit plain data. Omit optional fields rather than setting undefined; return numeric typed arrays or dense arrays. Type-only imports are erased before the executable dependency graph is collected.

breaking.member: project.ts.packs / og cook --pack / cooked bundle dependencies
breaking.change: Checked delivery packs now partition native payloads into independent runtime bundles. The base manifest contains only base outputs and pins its declared dependency manifests; other packs live under cooked/delivery/<id>/.cook.ogt. Stream group names are pack-qualified with explicit packs. Bundle loaders wait for pinned dependencies, protect them from release, and reject duplicate global asset identities rather than resolving by requester or open order. Web builds ship runtime files only and keep non-boot packs out of preload and offline precaching. Cook JSON adds pack selection and per-delivery file/byte/reference reports.
breaking.fix: Assign canonical content IDs with project.ts.packs include patterns and explicit dependsOn/roots. Use og cook --pack ID only for scoped iteration and a full cook before export. Load region/DLC directories with og.load.bundle and address stream groups as pack/local-name. Platforms must ship nested manifests and their relative files intact, consume delivery metadata in og-build.json, and stop assuming cooked/.cook.ogt lists every project asset. Duplicate bundle IDs are errors, not overrides. Build tooling can read the complete internal .og/cook/manifest.ogt; never publish it. Projects without packs keep the single-bundle layout.

breaking.change: Districts consume checked TS declarations and captured material-library bytes. The district OGT reader and line tables are removed. Generated streamed scenes and models are registered as actual children of their canonical district ID before scene references are bound.
breaking.fix: Export file.district({...}) from content/**/*.ts, use ref('module/id') for grammars, models, terrain and material libraries, and load the district by its canonical ID. Streamed children are id#cell-X-Y and id#cell-X-Y#model; unsplit geometry is id#model. Entity names remain <cell>/model (or <cell>.<building>/model when unmerged), not <cell>#model/model; update only their district/cell prefix to its canonical ID. Regenerate types and re-cook. Material libraries and import settings migrate in their own domain cutovers. Platforms must retire district OGT generators and physical-path scene IDs.

breaking.change: Effect-texture authoring now uses checked TS content declarations and the native typed volume/noise cooker. The OGT frontend and its separate field table are deleted. The actual producer reports all sheet, emission, array and layer outputs to the project reference graph; missing or wrong-kind derived references fail before cooking.
breaking.fix: Write content/<name>.ts with import {file} from '@origingame/engine/author' and export default file['effect-texture']({...}). Keep the same explicit parameters, using TS arrays for source/color/emission/light. Load <module>/<content-relative-stem> instead of an .ogt path; retain #emission, #array, #emission#array and #layerN suffixes. Use og api show file:effect-texture for the schema-generated contract. No OGT fallback or TS-to-OGT bridge is provided.

breaking.change: Environment authoring now consumes checked TS declarations directly. The OGT environment parser, grammar and sibling/asset-root fallback are deleted. HDR/LDR prefiltering, authored LDR background, sun extraction, hemisphere fill, KTX2 formats and prefiltered mip handling keep the same bake and runtime representation. Exact image bytes are captured before cook cache lookup.
breaking.fix: Export file.environment({source:{equirect:'assets/env/day.hdr'}}) from content/env/day.ts, importing file from @origingame/engine/author, and load base/env/day. Alternative sources are {ktx2:'sources/studio.ktx2'} or {faces:[px,nx,py,ny,pz,nz]}. Every path is canonical under the owning module's assets/ or sources/. Do not keep environment .ogt sources. See og api show file:environment.

breaking.member: file.field / og cook / terrain preserve / particle field / generate.FieldSource
breaking.change: Field author OGT, its generator wrapper and its text codec are removed. Field cooking, terrain preserve (including navigation and projected scatter), and particle force fields share one checked TS lattice snapshot; consumer stamps include the native lattice identity.
breaking.fix: Export file.field({dimensions:[2,2,1],channels:1,values:[0,0.5,1,0]}) from content/protect.ts and load base/protect. Compose procgen, static TS imports and input.bytes/text directly. For separately typed helpers use Parameters<typeof file.field>[0], not the removed hand-maintained generate.FieldSource interface. Existing terrain generate.preserve and particle field strings name base/protect or another canonical module/content ID, never protect.ogt. See og api show file:field.

breaking.change: Flipbooks use checked TypeScript declarations and native sheet fields. The OGT sheet/animated-source parsers, writer, grammar tables and sibling-file guessing are removed. Animated sheets expose #sheet; array sheets expose actual #array and #array#layerN outputs.
breaking.fix: Export file.flipbook from content/**/*.ts. Use canonical texture refs or sources with explicit owning-module assets/ or sources/ paths, and input.text for external Aseprite/TexturePacker JSON. Clips name frames rather than falling back to numeric indexes. Inspect animated content entries by their .ts path. Re-cook with matching hosts; old author text and blobs are unsupported.

breaking.member: font-extension author input and font pack installation
breaking.change: Font-pack membership and hyphenation inputs are checked TypeScript declarations. The cook no longer reads faces or dictionaries from extension.json. Distributed packs install content and binary asset roots together.
breaking.fix: Export file['font-extension']({kind:'font',name,languages,scripts,faces:[ref('base/fonts/body')],hyphenation:['assets/fonts/en.hyph']}) under content/. Keep extension.json for discovery tags only, with no faces or hyphenation fields. Reinstall shipped packs and re-cook with matching hosts.

breaking.member: file.icons / og cook / default UI iconSet
breaking.change: Icons consume checked TS declarations directly; the OGT icons parser and grammar are deleted. SVG paths are canonical relative to the owning module, without source-relative fallback. Exact SVG bytes are captured before cook cache lookup. Native glyph baking, tone runs, sticker and atlas layout are unchanged. The shared built-in iconSet is now @styles/shared/icons/game.ts, evaluated by the same closed TS evaluator.
breaking.fix: Export file.icons({source:'assets/icons',icons:[['close','xmark']]}) from content/icons/ui.ts and load base/icons/ui as a font. source defaults to assets/icons; names are unique single lines and SVG stems stay beneath source. Replace references to @styles/shared/icons/game.ogt with @styles/shared/icons/game.ts. See og api show file:icons.

breaking.member: lightmap author input and og bake lightmaps
breaking.change: Baked lighting is checked TypeScript with explicit scene associations in the cooked manifest. The author OGT parser, writer and filename-based lookup have been removed. Native tables and captured KTX2 bytes are the sole runtime payload.
breaking.fix: Run og bake lightmaps to write content/lightmaps/**/*.ts plus assets/lightmaps/**/*.pages.ktx2 and *.bindings.bin in the scene module; re-baking retains existing declaration ownership. Dense arrays use tracked input.bytes and typed arrays (flat u/v/page triples and twelve coefficients per probe). Reference scenes/models with canonical content refs; HLOD records use {hlodProxy: nodeNumber} and an empty entity. Re-cook and install matching hosts; old lightmap files and blobs are not supported.

breaking.member: file.look / og new / og project --json / readLook / Look binary payload
breaking.change: Looks, engine presets, variants and mood layers are checked TypeScript declarations. The look author OGT parser, text serialization and same-slug project fallback are removed. Cook validates reflected fields, composes inheritance and emits only native binary look payloads. Startup and runtime use canonical content IDs. readLook consumes the last successful cook's checked report and rejects missing or stale source/dependency snapshots; its signature and BriefLook result shape are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Write content/looks/<id>.ts exporting file.look({extends:["pixel"], ...resourcePatches}); use typed ref('module/looks/id') for another project look and full IDs such as ref('@canvas/paper.png') for engine art. Name base/looks/<id> in og-project.json and runtime loads, not looks/<id>.ogt. Re-cook all look payloads. Platforms must run og cook after og new before the first readLook/artBrief, and after editing the project, look, imported helpers or raw dependencies. A face's `family`, `weight`, `style` and `unicodeRange` are removed with no replacement. Lost: one alias family over several files (Cartoon Label, Scifi Label, Fantasy Caps), a weight range narrower than the file's (a label family held at 600 to 700), and a range that kept a face to some characters (a CJK face now also draws any other character the families before it lack).

breaking.change: `UiDesc.font`, `displayFont`, `monoFont` and `roundedFont` set the theme's fonts: each puts its font's family first in its role's CSS family list (`font-sans`, `font-display`, `font-mono`, `font-rounded`), ahead of the style pack's families. A role's fallback is that list and nothing built in: display and mono end with the sans list, rounded with the display list. Before, a role with no font took a fixed chain (rounded, display, body) of whole fonts; now each character takes the first family of the list that has it.
breaking.fix: None needed where a role's font has every character its texts show. To keep a role in one face, give that role its font.

breaking.change: TSX text is laid out once by Parley from the font files and drawn as glyph coverage at its drawn size on whole device pixels, not from cooked distance-field atlases. A line sits by CSS's half-leading with its baseline on a pixel, so labels move down by 1 to 3 px at 12 to 20 px (more at large sizes) to where a browser draws them, and small text is lighter. `font-bold`, `italic`, `font-display`, `font-mono` and a pack's families now pick real faces and weights (weight 600 and up was a 3 % thickening of the body face); bold or italic the family has no face for is synthesised. Text measures with kerning and shaping, so boxes sized to their text change by up to a few px. `truncate` and `text-ellipsis` end a cut line in "…"; `text-center` and `text-right` align wrapped lines; `tabular-nums`, `oldstyle-nums` and `small-caps` ask the font for those forms, and digits are proportional unless `tabular-nums` asks. A text outline (`text-stroke-*`) is the stroked outline at its full width, and a text shadow a blur of the glyphs. A text with no line height set anywhere above it takes CSS's `normal`, its fonts' ascent and descent, where it took 1.2 of its size (a style pack's type steps set one, so this shows in a UI with no pack classes on its text). A font with an optical size axis (`opsz`, as fantasy's Newsreader) draws at its size's design, as CSS's `font-optical-sizing: auto` does: small text is wider and sturdier, large text finer. `UiDesc.textScale` scales every TSX text's size, line height and spacing, and its box follows.
breaking.fix: Capture the game's screens again and look at them; add `tabular-nums` to timers, scores and counters whose digits must not shift.

breaking.change: A font ships its whole file, and TSX text draws every character the file has: an import's `charset` no longer limits what a TSX label draws from that font. The missing-glyph warning for TSX text names a character only when no font of the UI has it, and no longer names a face or its charset. A cooked game carries each font at its file's size. Text queued with og.render.text and floating text still read the cooked atlas and its charset.
breaking.fix: None needed where the charset only cut the atlas. A game that used `charset` to keep a face from drawing some characters lists another family first in the role's family list, or ships a font file without them.

breaking.change: A style pack's font files no longer ship in a web build's first download: each cooks to `<id>.face.ogb`, as a font pack's faces do, and the web fetches it after the boot. Until a file lands, the characters it would draw come from the next face (the default face, then the locale's fonts), and it takes over the moment it lands; the first frame waits only while it shows a character no loaded face has. Native builds read every file at once, as before. The UI gallery's first download goes from 14.2 MB to 3.2 MB, its Chinese faces whole on demand.
breaking.fix: None needed. A game that must show a pack's face on its very first frame keeps a character of it on that frame, which holds the frame until the face lands.
