breaking.change: typeRamp is removed: a step's size is fontSize[name] and its leading lineHeight[name] (a ratio of the size), by the token scale's names (xl2 is 2xl, displaySm is display-sm).
breaking.fix: Read fontSize and lineHeight by the token name; tracking[name] for trackingEm. cjkLineHeight, cjkTrackingEm, weight and uppercase have no per-step successor: the pack's fontWeight names weights, and TSX text takes `uppercase` as a class.

breaking.change: Removed: no style pack reads it; TSX controls size by their classes and the pack's breakpoints.
breaking.fix: Delete density from og.ui.configure calls.

breaking.change: Removed: they set old og-ui's global glass policy. A TSX element blurs what is behind it with its own backdrop-blur-* class. Known gap: old og-ui also forced glass off under the player's reduced-transparency preference; the TSX UI does not honour that preference yet (blurs and translucent fills stay) until the UI's presentation environment carries it with a variant that makes them solid.
breaking.fix: Delete glassBackdrop from og.ui.configure calls; give the element `backdrop-blur-<name>` (UiTheme.blur's names).

breaking.change: Paint.role names a colour of the style pack's theme by its token name (UiTheme.colors' keys); a style's old `roles` block is gone with old og-ui.
breaking.fix: Name a key of og.ui.theme(world).colors; a game's own colour goes in the pack's theme.colors.

breaking.change: `well` follows the scheme: pale glass in light, near black in dark as before. It was near black in both, so the scheme's dark inks on a `bg-well` tag, ledger or day header could not be read in light.
breaking.fix: Nothing to do for `bg-well` under `text-fg`, `text-fg-muted`, `text-gold` or `text-danger`. Text in a HUD colour takes its ink role: `text-hud-accent` → `text-hud-accent-ink`, and the same for `foe`, `ally`, `boon`, `fever` and `late`. A ground that must stay dark in both schemes is a pack slot (`packClass`), not `well`.

breaking.change: Behaviour change: `rootMotion: "off"` (og.Skeleton's default) now does what it says. The root joint's horizontal (xz) travel is held at its rest place, so a travelling clip such as a run or a swing on a rope plays on the spot. Before, the root joint still travelled and carried the drawn body away from the entity. The root keeps its height (a bob, a crouch, a jump) and its turns. An in-place clip whose hips sway sideways now holds the hips still and lets the feet sway instead. Games without travelling clips see no change.
breaking.fix: Remove any workaround that played a travelling clip in place, such as `rootMotion: "full"` plus overwriting og.Transform every tick; `off` alone holds it. A clip whose drawn travel was wanted while the entity stood still has no mode for that now: move the entity with `planar` or `full`. Where held hips make planted feet slide, add og.FootLock.

breaking.change: muzzle-auto now fires a flame tongue, side petals and a wisp of smoke on every 0.1 s cycle; before, its one-shot emitters played on the first cycle only and the loop left a bare glow ball in place. shocked and electric-sparks get brighter, wider arcs with glows, charge flecks and molten arc sparks, and electric-sparks discharges at once. impact-flesh adds a red mist and thrown droplets. drip has a larger drop, a brighter ripple and a darker wet spot, and mark-wet soaks darker.
breaking.fix: Reinstall the pack with og vfx add cinematic-realism. Retune anything that depended on the old look of these six effects; their names, durations and loops are unchanged.

breaking.change: The explosion leaves an 8 m soot mark with a shallow crater and embers that die out, and the impact a sooted dent with a bare rim, each a decal with the pack's own textures. Their instances now last 14 s and 10 s (the marks' lives) instead of 4.5 s and 1.2 s.
breaking.fix: Reinstall the pack with og vfx add cinematic-realism. Set the first param to 0 (og.Vfx.params) on an instance that should leave no mark, such as a hit on a character or a blast in the air.

breaking.change: Rework all nine cinematic-realism effects: the explosion adds a flash, ground dust skirt, debris and a lingering smoke column (4.5 s, about 9 m reach); muzzle flash becomes a forward tongue with side petals and gun smoke; impact, dust, splash, exhaust, pickup, magic and celebration gain layered sparks, grit, water column, plume and glints.
breaking.fix: Reinstall the pack with og vfx add cinematic-realism; leave room for the longer, larger explosion and retune any timing that assumed its old 3.2 s duration.

breaking.change: The splash becomes a torn crown sheet, rim droplets, a delayed central jet, flat surface foam and soft-banded ripples; debris, grit, sparks and confetti now land on the drawn depth instead of falling through the ground, and the explosion adds a short heat haze.
breaking.fix: Reinstall the pack with og vfx add cinematic-realism; particles that land on the drawn depth do not collide off screen, so frame splashes and blasts where their ground is visible.

breaking.change: Each emitter element of a vfx now draws its own random stream, mixed from the effect's seed, its `seed` and its place in the file. Before, every emitter whose `seed` was left at 0 drew the same stream, so emitters alike but for colour (five confetti colours, two checkpoint streamers) threw their particles to the same places and only the last colour drawn showed. Every multi-emitter effect's particles now land in other places than before.
breaking.fix: Nothing to write; drop `seed` lines that only existed to pull look-alike emitters apart. Re-check captures of multi-emitter effects whose exact particle placement a test or a shot relied on.

breaking.change: Add downloadable cinematic-realism and geometric effect packs covering explosions, impacts, muzzle flashes, pickups, magic, dust, splashes, trails and celebrations without gameplay logic.
breaking.fix: Install the pack matching the look with og vfx add cinematic-realism or og vfx add geometric, then spawn its named vfx asset; no pack is added to games automatically.

breaking.change: Ignore animated film grain while measuring an effect's bounds instead of framing the changing noise as a 96-metre effect. Shown frames keep the project's authored grain.
breaking.fix: Regenerate effect previews made in a look with film grain enabled; their cameras now frame the effect rather than the full measuring viewport.

breaking.change: Recipe-generated effect sheets preserve their authored grid, colour ramps, alpha and outlines instead of being conformed a second time as sprites. Pixel looks no longer shrink thin effects or replace ramp steps and highlights with a black sprite outline.
breaking.fix: Re-cook vfx2d effects. Author their resolution, palette, ramps and outline in the recipe; the look still controls frame-level treatment. No per-effect conform override is needed.

breaking.change: Particle-layer spawn area uses separate areaX and areaY fields; the old area tuple is rejected.
breaking.fix: Replace area: [x, y] with areaX: x, areaY: y inside each recipe particle layer. These are vfx2d recipe fields, not file.particles emitter fields.

breaking.change: Checked recipes reject the formerly ignored note field at the recipe root and inside layers.
breaking.fix: Remove note properties from recipe data and put the same text in TypeScript comments beside the recipe or layer.

breaking.change: Defaults to 0 (no contact foam). The band is now measured in water depth, is none at the contact line, and appears only where the water moves (its waves, ripples, wakes or current), as lace: still water touching a post or a floating body no longer draws a hard white ring.
breaking.fix: Set foamWidth (m of water depth, for example 0.35) on water that should foam against what stands in it.

breaking.change: `downloads.later.modules` is new: the single-threaded page's split engine modules (`modules/`) the game does not reference, each fetched on its first call (one variant: the lanes page's own are not added). `downloads.boot.single.engine` and `downloads.boot.lanes.engine` now count, beside the engine module, the split modules the game references (og-build.json `modules.referenced`), which the page puts in place before its first tick. Only a build that carries its modules (`--modules local`, or an engine built in a checkout) counts them: a CDN build's modules are no file of it, so its `later.modules` is zero and its boot counts none.
breaking.fix: Read the referenced modules' bytes in `boot.<page>.engine` and the others' in `later.modules`; for a CDN build, take module sizes from the engine version's `modules.json`.

breaking.change: `basis/` (the Basis transcoder) is left out of a publish build's `dist/` unless its cooked bundle holds a texture, texture array or lightmap, or it names a content base or opens a bundle at run time (og.load.bundle). `av1/` (the AV1 fallback decoder and its Worker) is left out of any build without a video that neither references the `video` module, names a content base nor opens a bundle at run time. The page's configuration then says `noBasis` or `noAv1` and fetches neither.
breaking.fix: Expect `basis/` and `av1/` only in a build that can use them; a host that copies or serves them by fixed path checks that they exist.

breaking.change: The web module no longer takes textures pushed to it. `og_web_texture_target`, `og_web_texture_ktx2` and `og_web_pack_ktx2` are gone: a host glue no longer reads a texture's target encoding or KTX2 bytes, or a pack's, to transcode them ahead. The engine now asks for each Basis texture it needs through the transcoder the host installs with `og_web_set_transcoder(transcode)`, calling `transcode(key, ktx2, target)`. The host answers `og_web_put_texture(key, width, height, rgba, srgb)` or `og_web_put_texture_encoded(key, format, width, height, srgb, levels)` with that key, or `og_web_fail_texture(key, reason)`. `og_web_put_texture` now takes the job's key instead of the texture's id and returns `""` or the reason it refused the texture. `og_web_prepare_textures(engine)` asks for the game's bundle's textures before the first frame, as the engine's own Worker does (src/web/boot.ts `installTranscoder`, `prepareTextures`).
breaking.fix: A host that runs the engine's Worker (src/web/worker.ts) needs no change. A host glue of its own installs a transcoder with `og_web_set_transcoder` and answers each job by its key, as src/web/boot.ts `installTranscoder` does, and drops its calls to the three removed functions. Nothing replaces pushing textures ahead of the engine: textures are prepared when the engine asks for them, and the boot asks for the bundle's through `og_web_prepare_textures`.

breaking.change: device.json's `measured.device.gpu` is removed: it came from a second adapter the page asked for, which was not always the one the game drew on (Chrome on an NVIDIA host answers a request without a power preference null). `measured.adapter` names the renderer's own adapter.
breaking.fix: Read `measured.adapter` (such as `nvidia/lovelace`, or `google/swiftshader (software)` on CPU WebGPU) instead of `measured.device.gpu`.

breaking.change: Takes the player's lowPower (boolean): it asks for the adapter the renderer will ask for, `low-power` or `high-performance`, never one with no preference.
breaking.fix: Pass the lowPower the page starts the engine with: webGpuMissing(storedLowPower(key)) or webGpuMissing(false).

breaking.change: Asks for the adapter once. It no longer asks a second time after a null, which covered Chrome answering null while its GPU process starts (a request in the first moments after launch on a headless test host). The engine's own boot asks only where it needs the device, after the wasm and the first world.
breaking.fix: Call webGpuMissing where the page needs the answer (before starting the engine, say), not as the page loads; read a null as no adapter.

breaking.change: Name or rename live entities through World.setName(entity, name); find/nameOf observe the change immediately and snapshots retain it. Spawn and rename share the ECS name grammar, including the 256-byte limit.
breaking.fix: Use world.setName for runtime names. Invalid names, including overlong names and invalid names spawned inside systems, are now refused before queuing.

breaking.change: A publish build ships one engine module whatever the game's profile, so og-build.json's `variant` is `publish` (or `full` for a dev build), never `3d` or `2d`. The profile is still `game.profile`.
breaking.fix: A reader that picked the engine by `variant` reads `variant === "publish"` for a publish build and `game.profile` for the profile.

breaking.change: A version's split engine modules are under `wasm/publish/` and `wasm/lanes/` only: the 2D variants `wasm/publish2d/` and `wasm/lanes2d/` are gone, with `dist/web-publish-2d` in the engine package and `build.wasmPublish2d` in a dist's origin-engine.json.
breaking.fix: Fetch a game's modules from the `base` its og-build.json `modules` listing names (og build writes it), or from `wasm/publish/` and `wasm/lanes/`; read the publish wasm from `dist/web-publish`.

added.summary: Lists all engine API modules and guides with summaries (`--kind module|guide`, `--json`), also available via MCP `api_list`.

Supports `--json` output, prints a compact overview and section TOC for large guides unless `--all` is passed, resolves guide section titles (such as `og api show Button`), and runs in-process with index caching inside `og mcp`.
Adds MCP tools for `api_list`, `frame`, `cost`, `vfx`, `sfx`, `sprite`, `materials`, `i18n`, `flow`, `fmt`, and `font`, and aligns `style` and `create` schemas with the CLI.

Generates and indexes `ui-tsx` (every export of `@origingame/engine/ui`: primitives, hooks, signals, `HostProps`, `UiEvent`), `theme-tokens` (default pack colour roles, theme scales with the utilities that read each, `packClass` slots, sounds, images, and built-in icons) and `playtest` (every export of `@origingame/engine/playtest`) guides from source in `og api gen`/`og api check`.

Documents `og sfx` and the `type sfx` entries (`audio §9`), `type rig2d` 2D auto-rigging templates (`animation §14`), built-in `@canvas/*` and `@palettes/*` look assets (`looks §20`), and theme authoring commands (`themes §6`).

Cook and load type animgraph files using the existing graph grammar, with bind lines for model clip references or sprite true for 2D targets. Cook checks graph structure and clip names, tracks animation dependencies and caches validated assets; loaded handles are reused.

The shared author schema registry now covers scatter, look, effect, particles, vfx, sfx and effect-texture with typed structured inputs, reference-kind metadata, field constraints and generated TypeScript declarations. Look patches reuse real reflected resources; effect-texture reuses its existing cook configuration. Domain relationships remain domain validation, and legacy author parsers are unchanged.

Tooling can obtain closed record-patch schemas directly from the IDL reflection registry or a real Reflect layout, including ranges, units, enums and tuples, plus writable fields and reference metadata where the IDL supplies them. The shared typed patch container validates even direct serde decoding. This foundation does not switch any author file format.

Persist validated source overlays with a cross-process project lock, snapshot conflict checks, conditional multi-file rollback and interrupted-save recovery; author semantics remain the caller's responsibility.

The shared author schema registry now covers terrain and theme with structured inputs and generated TypeScript declarations. Terrain composes the existing heightfield, shared geometry and reflected placement schemas, with ordered brush/stamp edits; theme composes the shared style-pack schema. Cross-field and graph validation remain domain-owned. Existing author parsers and file formats are unchanged.

Add typed style-pack inputs and the complete 23-kind model geometry union, with content references, reflected Transform placements, structural validation and generated TypeScript declarations. This prepares the TS author format without changing existing file readers.

Add typed field, PCM sound, icons, vector, texture-array and environment inputs with structural validation and generated TypeScript declarations. Raw texture kind names and omitted source-dependent environment overrides remain author data; existing OGT readers are unchanged.

Append explicit model-local translation, quaternion, scale, morph-weight and step-visibility key channels to imported or static models. Authored keys share glTF sampling, compression, event, library and mirror processing; query file:import.animation.clip.

Discover the remaining scene/prefab, district/grammar, rig2d/flipbook, timeline/story/behaviour, project/import, UI pack/theme and model-program fields through parser-owned vocabularies. API generation now refuses a registered cook kind without a catalogue entry.

Query parser-owned fields for text model geometry, paths, materials, plant levels and fracture; material libraries, oscillator sound layers, animation graphs and animation import processing are indexed alongside typed generator source contracts. Generated references remain drift-checked.

How a light may change while the game runs, as Unreal's light mobility. Movable: drawn every frame, never baked. Stationary (the default): drawn every frame, its bounce baked by og bake lightmaps. Static: og bake lightmaps bakes its direct light too, and while its scene's bake is drawn the renderer leaves it out. The light components grow a field, so a world with any of them hashes differently.

added.member: navmesh, lightmap, strings and font-extension author schemas
added.summary: Tooling has closed Rust-derived inputs and readonly TS declarations for navigation sources/profiles/areas/links, complete baked lighting bindings and probes, locale ICU messages and font packs. Navigation model placement reuses Transform reflection; resource identities use content references and lightmap u64 hashes remain lossless hex text. Domain normalization, topology, locale agreement and font coverage stay with their validators. This does not switch source formats or change another font's cook settings.

Opt-in physical shutter seconds scale motion blur to its simulation-time motion inputs, including fixed-tick captures and interrupted mixed-mode shots. TileMax/NeighborMax preserve the authored sample budget and centred shutter support. Snapshot-owned CoC primitives retain exact interruption state with observable four-source overflow; aperture/focus and manual physical exposure remain reserved. Artistic DoF is unchanged.

Opt-in physical lens projection with explicit focal length and sensor dimensions, vertical/horizontal/fill/overscan gate fitting and lens shift. Zoom, picking and screen queries follow the fitted gate. Virtual cameras blend authored physical lenses, and interrupted mixed-lens projection blends are snapshot-owned. Artistic projection remains the default; physical post integration follows separately.

A .ts or .tsx that imports a string table (`import "./x.en.ogt"`) that is not beside it fails with OG9106, naming the importer and the line: a bad import now fails the author's check instead of the cook, where it dropped every table of the asset.

Reports literal-zero or omitted TitleScreen keyArt/logo (OG9112), and named local screen-role candidates composing View/Text without a direct use of their corresponding built-in (OG9113), with built-in import and og ui eject pointers. Text warnings and a ui-screens JSON event are informational and do not change exit status; the same screen facts are reported by the pre-bundle check. The screens guide explains built-in-first composition, title art wiring and comments for whole-screen replacements.

`og check` warns of an installed font pack (assets/fonts/<pack>) whose faces differ from this engine's pack of that name, such as an older engine's chinese-simplified copy that lacks GB 2312's level 2 hanzi, and says to remove the directory and run `og font add <pack>` to take the engine's; `og font add` writes nothing over an installed pack. `--json` gives a `font-packs` event.

The kind of cloud in the volumetric layer, set apart from its cover: cumulus (the default), stratus, stratocumulus or cumulonimbus. The resource grows a field, so a world with og.Clouds hashes differently.

Read a UTF-8 command script from a file, like og replay record, without passing its contents through process arguments. Long recordings no longer hit the operating system's per-argument limit, including replay record's internal host launch.

added.member: scene, prefab and table author schemas
added.summary: Tooling can bind typed scene/prefab shells to project component/resource layouts and table rows to a fixed record. Closed fields, recursive entities, prefab edits, streaming and stable ordered row ids generate readonly TS contracts. All table columns may be omitted; decoding preserves omissions for later canonical-default normalization. Context-dependent kinds are not registered as context-free factories. This establishes structural contracts only; formats, parsers, graph semantics and persistence are unchanged.

The cook records the engine modules each asset needs (`modules physics nav` in its block: its records' and those of every scene, prefab, model or clip it places or plays) and the ones the bundle needs (a top-level `modules` line: the boot scene's). og.scene.preload, og.scene.change, og.load.scene and og.load.bundle fetch them as the content is prepared, so a later level's physics or a cutscene's video no longer loads at its first call. og build's og-build.json `modules.referenced` takes the boot scene's from the manifest, beside the modules the game's code names; other scenes' modules load as those scenes are prepared, not at boot.

project.ogt's `cook { uses "<cooked dir>" }` names other cooked bundles whose textures and texture arrays a terrain may use as layer maps by asset id. The cook checks each name against that bundle's manifest and type and packs none of them, so many terrain packs can share one material pack instead of each carrying a copy. og.terrain.load finds them in the boot bundle or an open pack, as before; open the material pack first.

A first-level creation choice: 2d, 2.5d, 3d or film. A game's view is one of its form's (its genre's first by default), and a look that does not draw the form or view is refused, naming the looks that do. `film` writes the og.film skeleton beside the usual one: a Yarn story, two segments, a placeholder stream and an entry that starts the film paused; genre, view and players do not apply to it. `--variant` picks one of the look's variants and writes it into the game's look.

Prints the creation document: the schema, every option with its English and Chinese label and description, preview slots for looks, variants, UI packs and moods, the compat rules (form views, genre default views, the fields each form asks for, each look's forms, UI pack, mood and variants) and the defaults per form. `creationDocument(previews)` and `previewSlots()` from @origingame/create-game make the document a release publishes as creation.json (packages/create/README.md §Creation document).
Explicit live sky capture latency/cost choice: false by default and on medium/high; true on low. Sliced faces retain their coherent sky snapshot rather than sampling a newer Sky-View LUT.
A decal's image and its tangent-space normal map, each any loaded texture (a sheet of several marks is one texture, each decal a region of it).

A `decal` element takes `texture`, `normal`, `normalScale`, `emissive`, `roughness`, `metallic`, `wet`, `angleFade` and `turn` (a random turn per instance), so an effect leaves a scorch with glowing embers, a crater with a raised rim, a bullet hole or a wet splash mark with its own textures.

The render dump reports the og.TerrainScatter copies the frame drew, which its `triangles` never counted: `scatter.chunkDraws` and `scatter.built` (the main pass's chunk draws and the chunks placed for the frame) and, under the GPU cull, `scatter.scatters`, one row per scatter entity with the chunks it took, the copies placed in them, the copies the main camera drew at each level of detail (`levels`) and as the impostor's card (`cards`), and their triangles across every part of the model. The rows are counted on the GPU and read back `countsLag` frames later (usually 1 or 2); `scatters` is null before the first count arrives or without the GPU cull. Drawing is unchanged.
The vendored `bun:test` declarations as an export of the engine package: `"types": ["@origingame/engine/bun-test"]` in tsconfig.json types a playtest file's describe, test and expect.

The environment cook accepts sRGB PNG, JPG and WebP panoramas or six faces through the existing prefilter, keeps authored LDR background colours apart from lighting, supports upper-hemisphere ground fill, and reports seam/clipping/lower-hemisphere cues and an estimated extracted sun. EnvironmentSun includes its angularSize; environmentSun accepts optional Environment rotation and intensity, returning world direction and strength directly assignable to DirectionalLight. Recook environment assets for the extended blob format.
The least exposure auto exposure applies, in EV (default -10, as before).

The most exposure auto exposure applies, in EV (default 10, as before): a lower maximum keeps a night dark instead of metering it to grey, without the game setting Camera.exposure each tick (render §5).

An Input is drawn by the pack's field slot by default: `Field.frame`, or the new `Field.area` once it is multi-line (multiline or rows), unless its class names a slot of its own. The slot draws its focus, invalid (`invalid`), read-only (`readOnly`, now a `data-readonly` state) and disabled states. Every engine theme draws each state in its own art (`field-focus`, `field-invalid` as a double rule, `field-readonly`, `field-disabled`), with the text ink solved against the art.

Processes an existing PNG/EXR heightmap or a deterministic TS heightfield through the same erosion, thermal, terraces, shore, automatic rivers and biome stages as runtime. Authored metre heights are not implicitly normalised or clipped.

Runs cook's synchronous deterministic TS generator with tracked relative imports, parameters, seed and explicit byte inputs, reusing the cook action cache; also exposed as MCP script. No ambient I/O, clock, process or network.

Adds the file namespace to list/find/show and MCP: every registered type is discoverable with an explicit field-coverage status; terrain's nested parser tables are generated and drift-checked. The generating guide's multi-file OGT/TS recipe runs through real cook and headless execution.

The captions the world's timelines are saying as of the last tick, as { id, text } rows in the timelines' and tracks' order: what a TSX subtitles screen takes as a prop, since a TSX component never reads `$captions`.

An interactive film's window and captions as TSX. FilmChoices takes og.film.view's value (`view`) and derives the choices, the pending one, each QTE's progress, the hotspots, the time left and the lock itself, calling `onChoose(e, index)` for a row or hotspot pressed; Subtitles takes the game's `lines` and og.timeline.captions as `captions`.

An interactive film's story-so-far screen as TSX: og.film.chart drawn through NodeGraph (nodes, links with their points, view as [0, 0, width, height], zoom and pan), the picked node's detail and Play from here. It reports onPick(e, id), onPlay (only while canPlay), onZoom, onPan and onBack.

flow "story/<name>.yarn" makes that dialogue the game's flow: the engine loads, prepares and starts it before GameDesc.start, the cook counts its segments, footage and scenes among the bundle's first modules, and the built-in FlowScreen draws it (a flow { screen game } block leaves drawing to the game).
The flow project.ogt's flow line started: what a playable segment passes to og.flow.advance, and what a title screen pauses and plays.

Built-in screens (@origingame/engine/ui/components): FlowScreen draws a flow's picture with its dissolve, its captions and its choice window; FlowPicture is the picture alone, with a Skip button for a cutscene.

The keyframe kind asks for an image-to-video model's first frame at the project's aspect (BriefOptions.aspect, 16:9 by default); medium sets a prop's or character's medium, image or model, over the profile's.

`og flow list [project] [--json]` reads every flow dialogue from its sources without running it: each node's segment (footage, live or both, its length, window and hold), footage (missing, streamed, placeholder), scenes, choices, outcomes, hotspots, the nodes each leads to through logic nodes, and the problems found. `og flow routes [project] [--json]` walks every route from the start to an ending as the steps a test sends (`choose`, `advance` with the outcome, or `cut`), marks a step an `<<if>>` decides as `condition`, and names the endings no route reaches (`unreached`). The flow guide §8.

The probe's `dump_flow[:path]`: per flow its dialogue, node, paused, held and ended, and per deck the node it holds (current, previous, warm or free), its segment's time and pre-roll, whether each scene its scene track places is prepared (and why not), and the engine modules the segment needs.
A video's `placeholder true` marks stand-in footage; `og flow list` reports every segment that still plays it. The interactive-film skeleton's opening clip carries it.

The skeleton's `leave` ending is a live segment: `segments/live.ogt` places `scenes/ending.ogt`, a night set of built-in geometry (`models/set.ogt`) under its own sky, moon and lamp light, with a scene track and a camera track pushing in, warmed on a deck before the cut. The flow guide §9 covers cutscenes and minigames in any game.

A flow node whose segment holds for the game (`flow.hold`) and branches on the story's variables before its choices are taken (an `<<if>>` in its body, or a choice's condition) is a cook warning naming the line, the variables and the fix: og.flow runs the node as its segment starts, before the game is played, so give each result a choice tagged `#outcome:<name>` and call og.flow.advance(world, flow, "<name>") when it is decided. The dialogue still cooks.
Reads a game's Yarn files (`.yarn` under src/, assets/ and tests/) with its other sources, so a rewrite or a line to edit by hand can name one.

A flow segment can be live: a timeline with a `scene` track (and a `camera` or `shot` track) instead of footage, or footage over a scene. A playable segment stops at its `flow.hold` marker until the game calls og.flow.advance(world, flow, outcome), which takes the node's hidden `#outcome:<name>` choice; a choice the player takes while it holds cuts at once. og.Flow.held, FlowView.held and WindowView.held say it holds. The cook checks outcomes (one word, named once, only on a held segment, never with #default, #qte or #hotspot) (flow §3).

og.flow.advance(world, flow, outcome?) ends the segment playing now: by the named #outcome, else the window's choice or the default. What a level or minigame between segments calls when it is won or lost.
A camera track takes `blendIn` and `blendOut` seconds: it eases from the camera it took at the timeline's start, and back to it before its end, cubic in and out (animation §13).

GPU particle simulation now runs through a slab-allocated Mega-Pool with batched wave compute passes, GPU sub-emitter event queues, alive-index compaction, indirect draws, tight alpha-cutout billboard cropping, and half-resolution soft-particle rendering with bilateral depth upsampling.
EffectMesh draws use a dedicated instanced renderer with full Weighted Blended OIT support, and alpha-blended trails, hooked billboards, and effect-material mesh particles participate in OIT.

added.member: FX volumetric fog, distortion & temporal reactivity
added.summary: Forward particles, effect meshes, and ribbons sample the 3D volumetric froxel volume at true depth; distortion particles refract the full lit transparent scene with bilinear sampling and depth rejection; and transparent FX stamp TAA/FSR3 reactivity cleanly.

Author scalar/vector lattices as explicit data or deterministic TS generation. Dimensions, channels, origin and positive spacing are explicit; cook stores lossless finite f32 values without resampling or normalization. Scripts compose the same noiseGrid, noiseGrad, Worley and curlNoise mechanisms as runtime. File fields are indexed from the parser table.

Model parts and nested operands accept explicit bufferGeometry arrays or a deterministic TS generator returning MeshSource. Source attributes share runtime validation and preserve colours, UVs and tangent frames through model cooking and placed merges; missing normals/tangents use the existing generation mechanisms.

Deterministic TS modules return SceneSource entity trees and reflected resource fields. Cook appends declarations to the authored scene and uses the existing prefab, reflection, reference and cycle validation; models and sub-scenes are asset paths, not runtime handles.

Deterministic source modules return typed mono/stereo PCM with an explicit sample rate. Cook feeds these samples into the ordinary sound importer and QOA/Opus/streaming encoders; games load the asset instead of regenerating samples. Oscillator-based files remain type sfx.

Deterministic TS generators return typed row-major tile grids for named authored layers. Cook validates dimensions and tile ids and uses the normal tilemap compiler; scripts can compose shared BSP and WFC without rerunning generation at game startup. Authored tilesets, layer properties and objects are retained.

added.member: og.procgen.poissonDisk, bsp, wfc, worley, plant, fracture
added.summary: Supply authored Poisson regions, holes, retained points, density and variable separation; BSP writable cells and retained rooms; WFC per-cell allowed tiles; Worley feature sites; plant trunk curves and custom foliage geometry; explicit Voronoi fracture sites. Offline generators and runtime use the same Rust mechanisms and validation. Model plant and fracture blocks accept the corresponding authored geometry and sites.
Exposed Tier::Full hardware capability flags: rg32Renderable, highBindingSlots, rg11b10Renderable, depthClipControl, shaderF16, subgroup, multiDrawIndirectCount, and bindlessTextures.
Added 4 bpp compressed texture formats (Bc1, Bc4, Etc2Rgb8, EacR11), automatic metallic/roughness/AO (ORM) texture packing, and resident mip-tail streaming support.

Added Tier::Full subgroup WG=256 scans and reductions, FP16 compute SPD bloom, single-pass conservative SPD Hi-Z, balanced 2-stage meshlet culling, tile-classified 8 B/px VisBuffer resolve, native multi-draw indirect coalescing, native 1024-slot bindless opaque material table, Hillaire Sky-View LUT, compute histogram auto-exposure, single-pass compute pre-skinning, and automatic native pipeline cache persistence.

`og cost . --off "<og run options>"` measures what a feature costs the real frame: at least 4 traced runs a side, on and off alternating, each side's median GPU frame span with its range and the machine's load, and their difference (render guide §10).
`og run --gpu-serial` makes every render-graph pass wait for the one before it, so a pass's alone time in the trace is its cost in isolation. Not in a publish build.

`og api show components --guide` lists every built-in component, control and screen that @origingame/engine/ui/components exports, one section each: what it draws, its props with their types and docs (from its `<Name>Props` interface), the row types those props name, the pack slots it dresses, whether it is a piece of a panel, its fixtures and the input actions it answers. `og api gen` writes it from the components' own source and `og api check` fails on any difference, so it cannot drift; `og api find` ranks its sections (`og api find health bar` answers with the components that draw one), and the `ui` module points at it. It replaces the CSS-era catalogue removed with og-ui.

`og bake lightmaps` lights a scene's HLOD proxies by its static models' bake: each proxy takes the irradiance the models' lightmap holds where it stands for them, written into the scene's lightmap as an entry keyed by the proxy's asset. A proxy whose entry matches its geometry draws lightmapped while RenderSettings.bakedLighting is on, so a baked town no longer turns flat-lit where it turns to proxies; a stale bake leaves the proxies unbaked as it leaves the models. dump_render's `hlod` gains `lit`, the proxies drawn with their bake. Run `og bake lightmaps` again to light existing scenes' proxies.

An HLOD proxy no longer replaces its models in one frame: where a node turns between its proxy and its models (or its children's proxies), both are drawn for 0.4 s and dithered against each other in the lit, prepass and shadow passes, the side fading out keeping exactly the pixels the side fading in leaves, so no pixel is drawn twice or left empty. Turning back during a fade reverses it from where it is. A node with a model destroyed, hidden, moved or given a look of its own, or a cell not loaded, still switches at once. While a fade runs dump_render's `hlod.replaced` does not count its models. Presentation only: world state, events and hashes are unchanged.

A scene that places cells (entities with a `scene` line and og.StreamCell) and has an `hlod` block of its own grows nodes over its cells: the cells' sub-scenes' HLOD roots, grouped by where they stand, merged into one proxy drawn in place of every cell under it, loaded or not, while each cell is where the cook read it and a loaded cell's models are unchanged. A distant streamed world is a few draws instead of one per cell. The tree blob gains a `cells` table; scenes with an `hlod` block cook their trees again once. A node over cells switches at once, without a cross-fade, and is not lit by `og bake lightmaps`. Presentation only.

An HLOD proxy carries a normal map: what its models' surfaces and normal maps show that its simplified surface does not (a wall's relief, a roof's ridges) is painted into a tangent-space page in the proxy's own MikkTSpace frame, so a distant town keeps its shading where it turns to proxies. Each proxy cooks one more texture, `<scene>#hlod-<n>-normal`; scenes with an `hlod` block cook their proxies again once.

An HLOD proxy's textures stream by level, as a model's `stream_textures` do, when the scene's `hlod.texels` passes the mip tail (256): spawning the scene or placing its cell loads each page's levels from 256 texels down, and the whole chain (`<page>#mips`) is read only while the proxy covers enough of the screen to want it, within the mip budget (`mip_stream`). A distant world no longer holds every proxy's full pages in GPU memory. The probe's `mip_stream:resident` makes them whole as before. Presentation only.

added.member: Present host interface (og_present_frame, og_present_resume, og_present_refresh, og_present_fullscreen)
added.summary: A presenting host's duties are one interface every host implements: it hands the engine each display frame's timestamp, and the engine paces it under the frame cap, measures the display's interval (or takes the monitor's refresh), records the frame's time and answers when the next drawn frame is due. The web Worker and the desktop shell both use it.

added.member: og_engine_perf_frames, perf report mean and p99
added.summary: The performance record is the engine's only record of frame times: field telemetry's binned frames, `og run --json`'s and `og run --device`'s frame figures and the desktop report read it. Its report gains a `frame work` line and each line's mean, p99 and frame count, and it records frames that draw nothing (a headless run) too.

An Input edits as a text field does: Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z) undoes and Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes, typing grouped into one step until a pause or a caret move, a paste or cut its own step; a press places the caret at the nearest character edge, a drag selects, a double press selects the word and a triple press all; ↑ and ↓ move between lines of a multi-line Input keeping the caret's x; a long one-line text scrolls to keep the caret in view instead of widening the field. New prop `rows`: a multi-line Input at least that many lines tall.
Adjust playback speed (0.25x to 4x) on the active flow segment.
Seek within the active flow segment (0..cut), updating hold and loop state.
Trigger non-cutting inspect hotspots (track hotspot kind "inspect") and emit og.FlowInspected.
Feed deterministic swipe and drag gestures into mobile QTEs; added timing, sequence, swipe, and drag QTE types emitting og.FlowQteResult.
Cross-segment persistent background music (also via og-flow-music header) with smooth crossfade and automatic voice ducking.
Deterministic transcript backlog recording shown captions and chosen options.
Lightweight branch-rewind checkpoint and og.flow.jump direct chapter/node jump with variable restore.

Presentation-only ABR quality selection (auto, high, medium, low) backed by #stream and #stream720, plus #stream480 for a stream cooked with `lowRendition true` (low plays the 720p without it), and og.video.buffering status.
Added WebVTT (.vtt) import, speaker labels, rich inline markup spans, and top/bottom cue positioning.
Added sub-range looping (loopStart/loopEnd on VideoPlayer and Timeline) powering seamless flow.loopStart..flow.loopEnd idle choice loops.
CLI continuity checker comparing outgoing last frames and incoming first frames across cuts, plus cycle/unreachable analysis in og flow routes.
`tactical-arctic` is a creation `ui` choice.

The lanes (multi-threaded) engine is split like the single-threaded one: a game whose page offers lanes downloads the primary and the modules it references (`modules-lanes/`, or the engine version's `wasm/lanes` and `wasm/lanes2d` on the CDN), and each pool Worker loads a module the first time one of its lanes calls into it. A module that loads late changes no result.

Installs report their progress as events a tool reads (docs/release.md §1 The launcher's events): `og engine install [<v>|latest] --json`, or with no version its project's pin, prints resolve, download (bytes, total), retry, verify, unpack and installed as JSON Lines, or error with a stable code (network, not_found, checksum, signature, disk_full, ...) and retryable, exiting 1. Any other command that installs its engine first prints the same events on stdout with --json, on stderr when stderr is not a terminal. Downloads retry network failures with backoff and resume an interrupted archive with a Range request.

A style pack directory may hold a `pack.json` (og-ui-next's CONVENTIONS.md §Theme and packs: scheme, seeds, a Tailwind theme with `{ light, dark }` values, `Component.slot` variants, fonts, icons and sounds). The cook checks it (unknown keys, every variant's classes against its theme over the default in both schemes, every asset it names) and writes an `og.UiPack` blob. The built-in cartoon, fantasy and scifi packs carry theirs, ported from their CSS tokens.

A pack.json face's `weight` may be a range `[min, max]`, as CSS `font-weight: 100 900`: on a variable face the part of its `wght` axis the entry serves, on a static face the weights it draws without synthesis. Omitted, it is 400 for a static face and the whole axis for a variable one. The built-in packs ship option A's faces: cartoon is Lilita One with ZCOOL KuaiLe for display, and Fredoka (variable, 300–700) with Noto Sans SC (variable) for text and labels. Fantasy is Cinzel (variable, 400–900) and Newsreader (variable, 200–800), each with Noto Serif SC (variable). Scifi is Chakra Petch SemiBold and Bold with Barlow Semi Condensed, each with Noto Sans SC (variable). Every role's family ends in its Chinese face, and the families no longer end in a generic family such as `sans-serif`.

The design tokens name the six rarity colours, `--color-common` to `--color-mythic` (each a status colour, so it keeps that colour's contrast in both schemes); tokens.json carries them as `color.common` … `color.mythic`.

An og.Water drawn over a mesh is water to the simulation too: still water standing only over the mesh's triangles, at their height as drawn (the entity's pose and scale included). og.physics.water and og.physics.waterHeight answer it, og.Buoyancy floats on it and bodies crossing it are og.Splash events. Before, mesh water was a look only. A lake that follows its shore floats boats like a sea, without a square that covers the lower ground around it. It has no waves and no current.
The role token for a round map mark's corner shape (round), beside --map-round.

Model files accept ringGeometry, circleGeometry and tubeGeometry through the same Rust primitives as og.render. Tubes accept explicit xyz points or an authored path, including closed paths, and participate in normal model cook, instancing and detail budgets.

Use a source model and optional mesh node as a static rest-geometry operand in model parts, CSG or merges. Normal import and generation run first; UVs, colors, tangent frames and affine placements are retained. The outer part owns materials; skins and animation are not copied.

A model's import settings state the file's axes that are its front (nose) and up: `model { front "-x" up "+y" }`. The cook turns it so the cooked model faces +Z with +Y up, as the facing guide says; meshes, skins, clips and fracture chunks turn together. A generated or bought model facing another way no longer needs a turn in game code. Axes along one line are refused.

Draws the engine's axes at the model's origin over each view, labelled +Z FRONT (blue), +Y UP (green) and +X (red), and says so in the report's `axes`: a fact an agent can see to check a model's nose before using it.

Carry an imported base model's painted maps into named variant parts through the shared og-bake metric transfer kernel. Cook orders base dependencies, rejects cycles and hashes the processed source and all external file contents; the destination keeps its geometry and other material channels. Query file:model.process.transfer.

target += source * scale over a view's rows in the engine, one call per archetype in place of a JavaScript loop over its entities (position += velocity * dt). The same bits as the loop; an f32 field or vector each, the target among the system's writes.

added.member: FX author inputs and native data transport
added.summary: Checked particles/effect/vfx inputs can build native fields directly. Native FX resource tables support validated encoding and host-handle binding without author text. This foundation does not change existing author entries, cook outputs or runtime loading.

A desktop store package answers og.platform from the local document, kept in the player's data directory (Application Support, %APPDATA%, the XDG data home) across runs: the store and leaderboards work offline in every package.

@origingame/engine/provider: a store's provider for a desktop package, bundled with the game by `package.ts --provider <module>`; with `--provider-lib <lib>` it calls that library's one C entry, og_provider_call(method, json), through context.native. The store's SDK and credentials stay in the module and library.

Patches many rows of a collection in one exchange with the engine, as patch does each, with subscribers settling once: a HUD's markers each tick. A refused row is the answer's reason; the other rows are patched.

TSX nodes answer input. `hover:`, `active:`, `focus:`, `focus-visible:`, `focus-within:` and `disabled:` classes follow the pointer, the press (which stays active within 8 px of its node, where a release still presses), and the keyboard focus. Tab and Shift+Tab move focus: positive `tabIndex` first, then tree order. Enter, Space or the `confirm` action presses the focused control, and the ring shows only for focus the keys moved. A `modal` node keeps focus and presses inside it while it shows, then returns focus. `onAction={{ confirm, details }}` (the `actions` prop and event 10) gets the UI's input actions on the focused node or around it. `<Glyph action>` (the `glyph` prop) shows an action's current binding. A double press sets `value` "2", and `onWheel`, `onKey`, `onFocus`, `onBlur` and the pointer events fire as CONVENTIONS.md §Input says.

A `Text` with `glyph="<action>"` now draws the binding's icon art in the text colour, one em square, instead of its name: a keycap for every key og.input binds, Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and generic pad buttons, sticks and d-pad directions, the mouse's buttons and touch's tap. It follows the last-used device, switching on the next input from another one. The Meta key shows ⌘ on Apple systems and WIN elsewhere. A style pack's `icons` replace any of them by glyph name (`xbox.a`, `key.keye`); a binding without art shows its name as before.

The arrow keys, the gamepad's d-pad and its left stick move the focus between TSX controls. Focus goes to the nearest control in that direction, its own row or column first, and wraps to the far end of the row or column. With nothing focused, a move lands on the first control. The stick repeats while held, after the theme's slow duration and then every fast one. A focused node that listens to `onKey` (a slider) gets the arrows itself; the d-pad still moves the focus from it.

`overflow-auto` and `overflow-scroll` (and their `-x-` and `-y-` forms) make a scroll container, as in CSS: the wheel, a dragged or flung finger and keyboard focus moving into view scroll it along the axes it names, as a `Scroll` does. `order-*` (`order-2`, `-order-1`, `order-first`, `order-last`, `order-none`, `order-[n]`) is CSS's `order`: flex rows and columns and grid auto-placement take their items in that order, while focus and reading order stay in document order. Sizes take CSS math and the viewport units: `w-[calc(2rem+4px)]`, `h-[16vh]`, `size-[max(4rem,min(8.286rem,16vh))]` (`calc`, `min`, `max` and `clamp` over px, rem, vw, vh, vmin and vmax).

`<Scroll>` scrolls. Its children move with the wheel (notches stay on one list while they keep coming), with a finger dragged past 8 px on a touch screen (flinging on when let go while moving), and with keyboard or pad focus, which scrolls the focused control into view. Its children are clipped to its box. A finger held still for 0.5 s fires `onLongPress`. A `hold` prop (seconds) makes a control press only once a press or `confirm` has been held that long: `onHold` reports the progress in `value` each frame, "1" when it completes and "0" when it lets go early. An `autofocus` control takes the focus as it shows, with the focus ring for a pad player. Pointer events carry the box of the node that hears them in `value` ("x y width height"), so a slider maps a drag to its own track.

Deterministic cook and script modules can compose every og.procgen mechanism through the same Rust implementations and IDL parameter readers as game hosts, preserving nested typed buffers inside the generator. Game code can import the same module through its normal host bindings.
Creates parent directories and atomically publishes the complete JSON result, without exposing file writes to the generator.

og check warns at a host element's inline style property that the UI never draws: a name no style property has (CSS's `background` and `inset` shorthands among them), which is dropped where it is applied, or one read into a field the UI does not draw (mixBlendMode, tintColor). The warning names the property's file, line and column and the class that draws it instead: `bg-<role>` for a theme colour, `backgroundColor` or `backgroundImage` for a colour from data.

Serves a project's development web build (inspector, Tune, Pause and Step, the probe) with every save pushed to the open page over one WebSocket: assets and UI cooked alone and applied in place, src/ bundled alone and swapped in with the world kept, a page reload only when project.ogt changes; each change's steps on window.__og_dev_reloads__ and the server's state on _dev/status (testing guide §1).

`og export gltf <asset> [project] -o <file.glb> [--lod N]` writes a cooked model as a glTF binary: generated plants and part models included, with normals, uvs, tangents, vertex colours, PBR materials and PNG textures, instances as nodes, and a skinned model's skins, clips and morph targets. One level of detail: the full mesh, or --lod N (the assets guide §8).

og mcp serves the og tool over MCP on stdio: the tools probe, run, test, render, compare, api_find and api_show answer with the same JSON the commands print (testing §9). run with a port starts the game in the background and answers its probe's hello.

Paints a model's base colour from concept images (front, back, left, right, top, three_quarter or a camera, framed as og model preview frames them): each texel takes the view that sees it most squarely, a texel no view sees takes the nearest painted colour on the model, and the report gives each material's coverage. Writes <name>.<material>.basecolor.png beside the model, and the program's <name>.ogt or the mesh file with the maps. A program (.shape.json, or a type model naming one) is painted on its parts packed into one atlas of the texture's size, which the .ogt records as `atlas <px>` for og cook; images that paint no texel are an error. og model measure, preview and compare take a type model naming a program as the model og cook builds.

A variant of a baked program takes the base's maps part by part, in each part's own metric frame: no new concept images, the same texel density, and where a part grew past the base it reads the nearest region of the same part. The report gives each part's transferred and extended fractions; the variant keeps its own atlas.

`og api show model`: model programs (.shape.json) — units and axes, primitives, generators (extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, wire, body), CSG, bevels, materials, params and variants — with a checked recipe, and the og model commands with their --json contract.

added.member: og model measure, og model process: issues
added.summary: `issues` lists every defect at once (open, non-manifold or flipped edges, degenerate or repeated triangles, floating pieces, a triangle, colour or texture budget the look states and the model is past), each with the option that fixes it; process adds `next`, the command to run after it. Parts of a program that only touch are an assembly, not an issue.
Repeated, compares every view in one call: each view's facts in `views`, ranked by `byIou`, `byAspect` and `byColour` (rankings, no thresholds). `--image <png> --view <view>` is as before.

Every 3D preset whose art direction gives a triangle range or a texel density now states a prop budget and a largest texture: painterly-3d and inked-comic-3d 30k triangles and 2048 texels, anime-cel-3d 40k and 2048, cinematic-realism 100k and 4096 (its muted variant 10k), pixel-3d-hybrid 4096 texels; inked's bold-comic and heavy-ink variants hold props to their character budgets. The cook holds props to them, and og model measure reports them. Looks whose palette is free (painterly, inked, cinematic, low-resolution) state no colours, and measure gives the palette facts as absent with that reason.

Writes a prop named after the folder: the processed GLB standing on its base, its import settings (levels of detail and a baked collider for og cook) and its convex hulls, and reports its size in metres, scale, triangles, texture memory before and after, open and non-manifold edges before and after the repair, levels and the look's facts. --max-texture PX shrinks its maps.

added.member: og model place --size, og model process --size
added.summary: --size x,y,z (GLB axes, 0 leaves an axis free) scales a model by the one factor nearest every axis given and reports what is left per axis.
A length without a unit (--height 1.2) is metres; m, cm and mm still name their unit.
Take a mesh's import settings (boulder.glb.ogt) for the model they set.

og cook builds an og-shape program as a model, deterministically: the program file itself, or a `type model` text naming it (`program "chair.shape.json"`) with `params { height 1100 }` over the program's "params" and `material "<name>" { color map metalness roughness opacity emissive }` blocks over its materials. A program declares "params": {"height": 900} and gives any operation's field as "$height". A field may also be an expression over the params and numbers ("($width - 40) / 2": + - * / and parentheses), evaluated in f64 at cook time; an undeclared name, a stray character or a division by zero is an error naming the expression.

added.member: og model compare widthPx, resolved, iouOnePixel, byWidth
added.summary: Beside each view's IoU: each part's width in the image's pixels, the share of its pixels on its edge and whether it is at least two pixels wide (`resolved`), the IoU the model's own silhouette keeps when off by one pixel (`iouOnePixel`, the most a fit at this size can show), and `byWidth` ranking the parts thinnest first over every view. A low IoU on thin legs reads as the view's resolution, not as a wrong shape.
`og style init <name> [project] [--from <theme>]` starts a style at `assets/styles/<name>/theme.json` from one of the engine's themes (minimal by default); it never overwrites.
`og style validate <directory>` compiles the style's theme.json, parses its pack.json and reports pack variants that paint a ground without its ink; it exits 1 on a problem.
Reads `.tsx` as well as `.ts`, and reports class literals: an arbitrary hex colour (`bg-[#0af]`), a fixed corner (`rounded-lg`, `rounded-t-md`) and the retired cuts (`nine-socket`, `nine-panel-cut`).

The publish engine boots on a smaller primary wasm; physics, story, nav, motion, destruction and video are separate modules on the engine version's CDN directory. The modules a game references download beside the primary during the loading screen, the rest on their first call, and og-build.json records them under `modules`. `--modules local` copies them into the output for an offline or self-hosted build; otherwise the page's Content-Security-Policy must allow `connect-src https://origingame.ai`.

added.member: probe (protocol 5, additive): logs, set, get; observe.truncated
added.summary: Strictly additive wire members on EngineProbe (dev/release builds only): `logs(take?)` returns recent probe log and warning entries (including refusal reasons from `patch`, `reload`, `commands`, and `save_scene`) without disturbing `take_log`; `set(target, value)` synchronously writes any reflected component or resource field as JSON and reports `{ ok, error? }`; `get(target)` synchronously reads any reflected resource, entity, component, or field as `{ ok, value?, error? }`. `observe` now includes a `truncated` map (`{ Component: totalCount }`) when any component exceeds the 256-row cap.

`og mcp` expands from 7 to 20 tools (`run_logs`, `check`, `cook`, `build`, `create`, `explore`, `replay`, `ui`, `style`, `model`, `assets`, `prefab`, `doctor`, alongside existing tools), extracts PNG/WAV binaries for `capture_views`, `sweep`, and `listen` instead of returning raw base64, and continuously drains background `run` stderr into a ring buffer. `og probe` adds `--timeout` / `OG_PROBE_TIMEOUT` (default 30s) and decodes `sweep` frames and `listen` WAVs.

added.member: @origingame/engine/ui/components: Checkbox, Switch, Slider, Select, Tabs, Dialog, Tooltip
added.summary: Added seven reusable core TSX UI controls under `packages/engine/src/ui/controls/` (exported from `@origingame/engine/ui/components` and individually under `@origingame/engine/ui/controls/*`) with pack slots, ARIA roles, keyboard/pointer interaction, and fixtures.

added.member: @origingame/engine/ui Input (IME, clipboard, password, multiline, maxLength, readOnly)
added.summary: Extended `<Input>` with `type`, `inputMode`, `autoComplete`, `secret`, `multiline`, `maxLength`, and `readOnly`, IME preedit composition (`input.composition` rendered underlined until commit), `Ctrl/Cmd+C`/`X` clipboard copy/cut, and `Ctrl/Alt+Arrow` word movement. Added missing ARIA roles (`tree`, `treeitem`, `table`, `columnheader`, `rowheader`, `searchbox`, `scrollbar`, `article`, `banner`, `form`, `complementary`, `contentinfo`, `search`) in `og-ui-next`.

added.member: probe command actions: dump_physics, dump_audio, expect:audio
added.summary: Added non-publish `dump_physics[:path]` (gravity, body/collider counts, tracked bodies, joints, active solid contacts and sensor overlaps, characters, vehicles, ragdolls, soft bodies, fluids, step timings) and `dump_audio[:path]` (bus gains, stream hash, active voices with playheads, user buses, snapshots, music clocks, reverb zones, listeners, sound bank residency, recent listen peak/RMS, and mixer render stats), plus `expect:audio:[<sec>:]<audible|silent|<metric><op><value>>` (unchecked when no audio listener hook is installed).

added.member: og explore UI and pointer game support
added.summary: Extended `og explore` to support `mouse.left` / `touch` button bindings and dynamically discover interactive UI controls via `probe.dump({ what: "ui" })`, issuing atomic `touch_move_to` / `move_to_text` + `touch_start` / `touch_end` click units that shrink and replay deterministically.

added.summary: Exposed `og_node_dev_refresh` on the native host and wired `og dev` + `run.ts` (`--watch-refresh`) to refresh cooked assets/UI in place on asset-only edits without re-bundling or reloading the world, and to watch `project.ogt` for automatic re-cook, re-bundle, and clean restart.

added.summary: Exposed `skin` (region rig `bones` and bone-heat `joints`), `humanoid` (Mixamo auto-rig + bind), and `morph` (target part, explicit deltas, or region offset/scale) ops in `.shape.json` programs, transforming skin bones across placements and unit scaling. Extended `type model` `material` override blocks with `normalMap`, `normalScale`, `roughnessMap`/`metalnessMap`, `emissiveMap`, `aoMap`, `aoMapIntensity`, `emissiveIntensity`, `clearcoat`, `clearcoatRoughness`, `sheen`, `sheenRoughness`, `transmission`, `iridescence`, `alphaTest`, `transparent`, and `doubleSided`.

added.summary: Added `surface_roughness`, `surface_metalness`, and `surface_ao` hooks to material shaders (lit, prepass, physical, and scatter passes), exposed `inv_view_proj` and `camera_pos` on `PostInput` in custom post passes, and enabled HLSL (DX12, SM 6.0) naga validation in `validate_shader` and `validate_post`.

added.member: type sfx declarative synth DSL (layer / synth blocks)
added.summary: Extended `type sfx` `.ogt` files to support custom multi-layer `layer` / `synth` blocks (standalone or layered over a `preset`) with `sine`/`square`/`saw`/`triangle`/`noise` oscillators, `freq_end` sweeps, full ADSR envelopes (`sustain_level`, `release`), FM modulation (`fm_freq`, `fm_index`), resonant 2-pole SVF low-pass (`q`), and soft-clip `drive`, keeping all 18 built-in presets bit-identical.

The cartoon and scifi packs have painted nine-slice art for their buttons (normal, hover, pressed, disabled, and a primary set), panels, HUD plates and chips: cartoon's glossy navy and gold plates, scifi's chamfered cyan and amber frames. Fantasy gains a gold-rimmed HUD plate and an oxblood ribbon chip beside its filigree and iron and red plates, so every built-in pack dresses `Button.plate`, `Button.plate.primary`, `Panel.frame`, `Plate.frame` and `Chip.frame`. Cartoon's primary label takes the dark `fg-inverse` ink (9.9:1 on its gold).

Every look has six shape images coloured by the element's fill (`bg-*`): `nine-disc` and `nine-ring` for radial cooldown and progress wipes, `nine-tile` for a square slot, and `nine-plate-cut`, `nine-panel-cut` and `nine-chip-cut` for cut-corner HUD plates, panels and badges. A game with a TSX UI or a document carries them.

The default pack declares the slots a pack dresses: `Button.plate` (and `.primary`), `Panel.frame`, `Plate.frame`, `Slot.frame`, `Chip.frame` and `Field.frame`, so `packClass("Panel", "frame")` resolves under every pack. A variant may be an empty string, which declares a slot and adds nothing. The fantasy pack dresses buttons in its iron and red plates and panels in its filigree frame; scifi dresses all six in its cut shapes.

A nine-slice image may set `tint: true`: a shape the element's fill colours (its alpha kept), so a chamfered plate follows the theme in either scheme; unset, the image is a picture drawn as it is. The built-in fantasy pack names its filigree frame and its iron and red button plates as images, and scifi its corner-bracket frame (per scheme) and its chamfered frame, plate, button, cell, chip and field cuts.

A pack.json may name nine-slice art in `images` (`{ src, slice, width?, fill?, repeat? }`, per scheme if it differs), and the class `nine-<name>` gives an element that art, in a variant or a component's own class. The cook refuses a `nine-<name>` that names no image and an image that is not in the bundle.

The perf report gives every GPU pass's cost alone, even when passes overlap: one frame in 30 runs serially and its main and prepass passes are timed per draw class (`main: terrain`, `main: scatter`, `prepass: grass`, …). The table `gpu cost per pass, alone` and the JSON `costs` list them with their sum and the real frame's span; the other lines come from the real frames only (perf guide §2).

`og run --perf <dir>` records every drawn frame and writes perf.txt and perf.json at the end: each line of the frame's cost (the interval, the GPU's frame, overlap and idle time, each pass alone and in flight, the CPU's ticks, physics, UI, game and engine systems, its wait for the GPU and the render's sync, build, encode and submit) with its median, p95 and max, flagged against project.ogt's `perf { budget "<line>" <ms> }` or `--budget <line>=<ms>`, and every hitch with its cause (the line that grew, or a pipeline compiled in the frame). The web shell's `perf("start" | "stop" | "report", budgets)` reads the same record in the engine Worker. Guide perf.

The perf report also counts what each frame moves between the CPU and the GPU: bytes uploaded and the writes, buffers made, readbacks started, blocking waits for the GPU and pipelines made, each with its time. It lists the engine places that moved it (uploads in steady play and at load, buffers made, readbacks, waits, late pipelines), and a hitch names the first-use work its frame did. Guide perf.

On the web physics is three modules loaded on first use: `physics`, and the simulations `physics3d` (rapier3d) and `physics2d` (rapier2d). A world loads only its profile's simulation. The cook records it in a scene's `modules` (from its `resource og.Physics { profile }`, else the project's profile), so og.scene.preload of a 2D minigame's scene fetches rapier2d before the switch (physics §2, loading §12).
Dominance groups control one-way mass influence in contact resolution.
Enable or disable a body without replacing its component.
Control 3D gyroscopic torque explicitly.
Request extra iterations on an island containing this body.
3D cone colliders and query shapes.
Open or segmented mesh polylines in both physics profiles.
2D heightfield profiles in addition to 3D height grids.
Rounded boxes, cylinders, cones, convex hulls, diamonds and hexagons.
CombineRule average/min/multiply/max friction selection.
CombineRule average/min/multiply/max restitution selection.
Separate solver force-resolution membership bits; zero inherits collision layers.
Separate solver force-resolution mask bits; zero inherits the collision mask.
Enable or disable collision detection and scene-query participation.
Generic six-degree-of-freedom joints with Joint.lockAxes.
JointMotorModel selects mass-independent acceleration or force/torque motor interpretation.
Ball joints support swing/twist limits.
Filter dynamic, fixed and kinematic bodies with QUERY_DYNAMIC, QUERY_FIXED and QUERY_KINEMATIC; zero includes every kind.
RaycastDesc and RaycastAllDesc choose immediate inside hits (default true) or exit-surface hits.
ShapeCastAllDesc returns capped, sorted swept-shape hits with collider and body identities; ShapeCastHit.body also identifies compound owners.
PointOverlapDesc returns every collider containing a point.
Read the live solver's computed mass, world center of mass and principal inertia.
Read a live body's linear plus angular velocity at a world-space point.

Data tables: an `.ogt` of `type table` holds a game's items, abilities, recipes, loot or waves as `row "id" { ... }`, read as one of the game's components with og.table.load (cooked) or og.table.parse (text), field by field, all or nothing, a refusal naming the table, line, row and field. og cook checks every id is there once, every `asset "path"` exists and every `row "table" "id"` names a row; `text "key" "Base"` fields join og.i18n and `og i18n extract`. A row is held in the world as a TableRow field (a 52-bit handle of its table and id) that names the same row after a reload or in a save; og.table.get reads its values, og.table.name its id and og.table.missing every field still holding a deleted row. Guide: `og api show data`.

Every entity inside a sensor now, each once, in entity order: who stands on a pressure plate, what lies in a pickup zone. It reads og.Contact, the pairs of the last step, so it is what og.SensorEntered and og.SensorExited have added up to and stays right through a restore and a hit stop; a system that calls it lists og.Contact in its reads. Refused for an entity without an og.Collider; a solid holds nothing.

og.AnimationEvent says where a marker came from: `state` (the graph state that played its clip, its index in its layer; 0 for an og.AnimationPlayer's), `layer` (the graph layer, 0 the base) and `dominant` (its clip weighed most of its layer that tick: in a cross-fade the state left until the fade passes half, then the state entered; a tie goes to the state entered, then to the later clip of a blend). Every contributing clip still fires its markers; the game decides which to act on. A save holding a pending event of the version before restores it with 0, 0 and false.

A buffered press: ActionDesc.bufferTicks keeps an action's press for that many ticks after it went down (0: only its own tick), ActionState.buffered says one is waiting, and og.input.consume takes it, true once per press. A jump or a combo pressed a few ticks early happens when the game can act, and one press never does two moves.

When in its tick an action went down, in seconds from the tick's start (-dt to dt), from the time its key or pointer press carried: a rhythm game judges `time.elapsed + pressedAt` against the beat instead of the 16.7 ms tick. It comes from the press events, so a replay gives it again; 0 for a pad or an on-screen control.

A hit volume (sphere, capsule or box) on a posed bone through og.BoneAttachment, or on any entity, swept each tick from its last pose along the turn and slide between the two, so a fast swing meets what it passed through; it strikes each og.HurtVolume of another team and owner, and the colliders on its `colliders` layers, once per owner's swing.
What a hit volume strikes: a shape on a bone or entity with a team and an owner; a body's hurt volumes share their owner, so a swing strikes it once.
A hit volume struck a target for the first time in its owner's swing: the volume, owner, swing, target, the hurt volume met first, and where and which way they met.

Every entity carrying a component within a range and a cone of a point, nearest first with entity order breaking ties, with its distance, its angle off a forward direction and, when asked, whether a collider stands in between.

Melee attacks a game lists by name: og.Attack plays og.AttackMove frame data (startup, active, recovery in ticks) and drives its hit volumes in the active window, a new swing per move; an og.AttackLink is taken when its action's buffered press (og.input.consume) lands in its window, so combos chain; og.Attack.cancelable says when a dodge may cut the move; a hit stop holds every move. Every number is the game's: zero does nothing.
What a target has left: a hit of a move's swing takes the move's damage, never below 0, and sets `dead` at 0.

How a target takes a hit: ticks of invulnerability (a dodge writes invulnerableUntil for its i-frames), ticks of stagger that cut its own attack, and a knockback speed og.Damaged carries away from the volume.
A hit took damage: the target, the attacker, the move and swing, the amount, what is left, where, and the knockback; sent the tick the hit is read.
A target's health reached 0: sent once, with the attacker whose hit it was.

Interaction a game lists by name: an og.Interactor focuses one og.Interactable among og.play.candidates by its rule (nearest, centred, or priority then nearest), skipping what is out of sight, and uses it on a buffered press of its action or after holding the action on it for its holdTicks (let go sooner, nothing happens); it writes the focus and the hold's progress for a prompt and sends og.Interacted. Every number is the game's: a zero range focuses nothing.
A door that flips when used or follows an og.Toggle, and opens and closes its navmesh link with it (og.nav.setLinkOpen), so agents path through only while it is open.
A lever or switch that flips when used, or a pressure plate that is on while its sensor holds anything (og.physics.sensorContents).
A body an interactor picks up: kinematic and moved to a carry point in the carrier's frame while held, thrown along the carrier's forward at throwSpeed on the next press.

Items as entities: an og.Container places `slots` og.ItemStack children (a TableRow and a count), each stack held to its row's limit, the item table's field the container's `stack` names (no default: 0 fits none). og.inventory.add, remove, move, split, merge and craft are all or nothing (refused, both containers stay as they were); slots, count and canFit read them; roll draws a loot table on og.Rng. An og.Pickup's stack goes into the container of the og.Collector inside its sensor, sending og.PickedUp. List `...og.systems.inventory` in GameDesc.systems. Guide: `og api show items`.
Also answers `schema`, the component the row's table was loaded as, so code given only a TableRow can read it with og.table.get.

Abilities, statuses and stats: an og.Ability is used on a press of its action or by og.abilities.use when it has a charge, its lock has run out and its pool (an og.Stat) holds its cost, sending og.AbilityUsed; its charges return one at a time every rechargeTicks, holding through a hit stop. An og.Status spawned on a target merges with one of the same kind by refresh, stack (to maxStacks) or strongest, and runs out after its ticks with its og.Modifier children. An og.Stat's value is its base with its modifiers: adds, then the percents' sum, then each multiply, each kind in ascending order, whatever order they came in. List `...og.systems.abilities` in GameDesc.systems. Guide: `og api show abilities`.
Two reason codes from the frame's own cull: occluded (inside the camera's view, behind what the occluders drew) and fading_in (og.render.reveal, none of it shown yet).

`dump_ui` carries `moving`: whether the TSX UI's transitions, exits and finite keyframe animations (an entrance's `animate-pop`) are still running. Loops that never end (`animate-spin`, `animate-shimmer`) do not count, so a capture can wait for `moving: false` before it judges a frame.

The probe's visible member, dump_entity's visible field and the dump_drawn action say why the main camera draws an entity or not at the current tick: drawn, hlod, hidden (naming the visible field), loading (naming the asset), layer, outside_view, untracked or nothing_to_draw, with how many of its drawables survived the cull. It runs on the CPU over the extracted frame, so it answers without a GPU.

capture_views captures one tick from up to 16 cameras in one call (position, target, up, fov or an orthographic height, near, far), without writing og.Camera. og probe writes its frames beside --out as <stem>-<view>.png (capture-0.png, ...) and prints each frame's path in png.

Two surface patterns for large-scale value: `facing` masks where the surface faces `axis` (frost on tops, dark undersides, a step per facet), and `gradient` runs along `axis` across every part painted with the material (a dark foot, a pale crown). Both take `threshold` and `softness`.
Deterministic seed on og.Clouds driving 3D cloud-noise phase offset so different worlds generate distinct cloud formations.

Added analytical gradient noise (noiseGrad), divergence-free curl noise (curlNoise), Worley cellular F1/F2 (worley), ridged/billow/worley/worleyEdge FbmDesc kinds, multi-octave domain warping, toroidal Poisson-disk wrap, BSP loop corridors and room adjacency edges, procedural eroded heightmap/biome generation (heightmap), procedural plant mesh generation (plant), and deterministic 3D Voronoi mesh fracture (fracture).
Create live procedural terrains at run time from height, control and hole TypedArrays, with full renderer, physics heightfield collider, sampling, editing, stamping and restore support.
TerrainSample now reports the dominant biome/control layer index (layer).
Added deterministic runtime procedural sound synthesis (og.audio.synth returning Float32Array PCM, and og.audio.createSynthSound registering directly into the sound bank).

Upgraded og.render.bufferGeometry, og.render.updateGeometry, og.audio.createSound, og.load.dataBytes, og.tilemap.fill, og.nav.grid, og.terrain.create and og.procgen bulk buffers to zero-JSON 8-byte-aligned TypedArray binary transfers.
`profileOf(form)` in the art brief (packages/knowledge/scripts/brief.ts, re-exported by @origingame/create-game): the profile a creation form draws in, "2d" for form 2d, else "3d".

Compiles every pipeline the world draws with in the background, a few a frame, as three.js renderer.compileAsync: call it behind a loading screen and keep the screen up until og.loading.idle, so a level never compiles a pipeline in play. Presentation only.
LoadingStatus.pipelinesRequested and pipelinesReady count the pipelines compiled off the frame and those made, for a loading bar such as 41/96; both only go up.
Projected decals can now override the receiver's metalness (0 to 1, default -1 keeps the receiver's metalness) and update F0 accordingly on both standard and physical surfaces.
Added glTF KHR_materials_specular dielectric specular intensity and specularColor controls on physical materials.
Added glTF KHR_materials_dispersion chromatic RGB refraction dispersion on transmissive physical materials.

WebGPU's compatibility mode (Chrome 146+ on GLES and D3D11 devices) as a tier: the renderer made at that mode's limits (4096-texel textures, compute workgroups of 128), no MSAA (`msaa4` resolves to `fxaa`), blended surfaces sorted back to front instead of order-independent transparency, normal-mapped 2D receivers lit as flat ones, and clustered meshes drawn without the meshlet path (`visibilityBufferRefused` says why). No host picks it yet: the web host can once wgpu asks for the mode.

Two capabilities `og.render.capabilities().caps` reports: colour targets blended each their own way (order-independent transparency and the 2D lights' directions need it) and two-channel 32-bit storage textures (scattered impostor cards take the depth prepass's surface with it and search their frames again without it). Both are true on every core device.
