A new project starts with AGENTS.md: the project layout (og-project.json, project.ts, content/**/*.ts with their base/ IDs, assets/, src/, tests/), how to look up the API, file types and UI components with `og api find`, `og api show` and `og api list --kind`, the everyday og commands, and the rules to use the built-in UI and theme and keep simulation deterministic.

Cook authored or deterministic TS-generated points and transforms as normal model/prefab scene placements. Compose the shared Poisson mechanism in TS; optional terrain projection and normal alignment use the runtime terrain sampler, rejecting holes and off-surface points. No gameplay composition or distribution is inferred.

A district asset (`type district`) lays out a whole area from rules and a seed at cook time: a street grid over a region or one street's both sides, blocks, lots fronting the streets, a building per lot from weighted building rules (`type grammar`, CGA-style split grammars where every part carries a label), and roadside props along the pavements with their colliders. A material library (`type materials`) gives each label its materials, drawn per building by weight with its own brightness, warmth and texture phase. The district cooks into an ordinary scene: buildings merged per cell (`merge false` keeps one model per building), levels of detail from the grammars' `detail`, a box collider per building, instanced props, and with `cells` a streaming cell per square with its own group and the district's `hlod`. Deterministic from the seed on every host. The districts guide covers the three formats and the workflow.

A ground-storey composition shows recessed entrances, framed shop windows and a projecting plinth using the existing grammar mechanisms, with residential and retail variants chosen by the building seed. Aging is assigned to the actual ground-floor surfaces, not only walls above its height band; structural glazing stays in every LOD. The district-street validation fixture keeps these authored rules separate from engine presets.

Authored grime, grimeColor, grimeHeight and dry stains age surfaces without a WeatherState. District walls preserve height in metric UVs independently of image repeat, so grime rises from every building's base through cell merging. Stochastic tiling breaks up ordinary 2D PBR maps with histogram-preserving patch blending; array maps and structured facade modules are excluded, and minified surfaces fade to ordinary mip sampling. All amounts default to zero.

Material libraries describe authoring-time image requests using the project's look; deterministic processing makes periodic colour, signed-relief normals, authored packed roughness and cavity maps, with source-and-options caching and verified outputs. No image service runs in the engine.
metalnessMap (green roughness, blue metalness) and aoMap (red occlusion) survive model and district cooking.

A district can name a terrain asset with `terrain "terrain/land.ogt" { depth 0.25 }` to carve its street and pavement footprint at cook time, using the existing TerrainStamp kernel. Block interiors and ground already lower are preserved. Region grids and path turns work alike; tiles, terrain colliders, sampling and terrain nav bakes use the same carved heights. District and terrain share local coordinates; streets remain at y = 0, without runtime generation or automatic grade selection.

`nine-none` draws no nine-slice art, so a state can drop the art its base names and let the component's fill show: a pack whose Chip.frame is `nine-chip` writes `data-kind-owned:nine-none` and the Shop's Owned chip shows green, not the dark chip art. The cook and the unknown-class check took `none` for a missing image and refused the pack.

`size: "lg"` draws a result's grade as the puzzle summary does: 78 px stars (52 on a phone), the middle of three raised and 100 px, unearned ones dim. `class` places the row, after its own classes. md, 32 px stars in a line, stays the default.

`class` comes after the shop's own classes. The shop fills its parent by default; `grow-0 basis-auto` makes it hug its offers, so a short catalogue (four ships) ends with its last row instead of leaving the panel half empty. A long catalogue still scrolls inside a filling shop.

An Entity field a game declares can be `weak` (`Entity(0, { weak: true })`): it may outlive the entity it names, such as a handle to an effect that despawns itself, and the default live-entity invariant no longer reports it once that entity is gone. Only an Entity field takes the option; on any other field, the declaration is refused.

og.transform.matrixWorld(world, entity) reads any entity's world matrix: its og.Transform composed down its og.Parent chain (a bone attachment's posed bone included), as it stands. A game could not place a child in the world before: og.MatrixWorld is written for bone attachments only, which its doc now says.
A results reward may name an `icon` (an atlas icon, as a Shop price's), drawn in its well when it has no `texture`: a currency reward with no picture showed an empty dark box above its amount.

og.Rng.reset() returns the main stream to its seed's first draw, as a fresh start has it. A game's restart (Retry, Play again) calls it so the restarted world draws what a fresh start draws; until now no call could, so a game that drew from og.Rng could never pass a playtest's `restart` check. Needs og.Rng among the system's writes.

restart takes `keep`: the progress a game deliberately carries across a restart (`keep: ["Run.best", "Wallet.coins"]`), each a field of a component or a resource the world declares. Those fields are left out of the comparison and `run.restart.kept` reports each with its value at the fresh start and after the restart (by entity for a component). A name the world does not declare fails the playtest, naming the fields the type has. `og run --restart-keep Type.field,...` beside --restart-at. Until now a game with in-world progress could not pass the restart check once a run had earned anything.

added.member: og.ui class text-shadow-tag, pack theme textShadow
added.summary: The theme halo class text-shadow-tag: the default pack carries --tag-halo (eight unblurred copies 1 to 1.5 px round the glyphs in contrast-color() of the ink) as textShadow.tag, and a pack's theme may set its own textShadow entries, each a CSS text-shadow list.

Model programs gain a `displace` op: a part's surface moved along its normals by deterministic noise, `fbm` (soft lumps), `ridged` (crests and creases) or `crater` (bowls with rims), with `scale`, `amount`, `octaves`, `seed` and crater `density`. Over a subdivided `box` or `sphere` it makes rocks, asteroids and cratered moons that cook like any program (LODs, collider, fracture) and build the same bytes everywhere.

A model program's `material` takes a procedural `surface`: layers of noise, ridged, craters, strata, stripes, panels, rivets, veins, edges (convex wear) and cavities (dirt), cooked deterministically into base-colour, metallic-roughness, normal and emissive maps on a fresh atlas at `density` texels per metre. Props, pickups and displaced rocks carry patterned, lit surfaces with no painted image; `og model preview` draws them as the cook writes them.

og.FramingCamera frames a level rectangle whole: set `area` (its width across the view and its depth along the ground ahead, lying through `centre`) and each beat's screen height becomes the share of the frame the rectangle's on-screen bounds fill in their tighter direction, with x and y placing the centre of those bounds. The system solves the perspective (the near edge spans wider than the far one), so one beat fits a shooter's playfield or an arena on a phone and at 16:9, at any pitch and fov. The camera guide's §5 has a recipe.

dump_world names, for each system that ran but whose query never matched an entity, the smallest set of its required components no entity ever had together (such as Boss and og.Chunk), so a system silently disabled by a component in its reads or writes shows up.

After a run, og run and og test print a WARN line on stderr and add it to `warnings` in --json for each game system whose query never matched an entity, with the components kept apart. A fact, never a failure; the JSON shape is unchanged.

og.vfx.spawn takes `delay`, seconds before the effect starts (og.Vfx.startTick that many ticks on, rounded up), so a system can set off a timed chain of blasts in one call each: a spawned entity cannot be written by the system that spawned it before the system ends, so startTick could not be set at spawn.
An offer may carry a picture (a Texture, such as a render of the item) that fills its art well in place of the icon; 0 or absent keeps the icon. Additive: existing offers draw as before.
level, xp and gained are optional. Without level, Results draws no level, XP or progress bar, for a game without levels.

A shot's damage beside its og.HitVolume, carried out by og.systems.combat without an og.Attack: each projectile is its own owner, so it strikes a target once and two strike it twice; a hit takes its `damage` under the target's og.Hurt (invulnerability, stagger, knockback) and reports og.Damaged and og.Died from its `shooter`, which it never strikes. Only a strike that takes damage counts towards `pierce`: a target without og.Health (a graze ring), a dead one or one in its i-frames lets it pass. Once `pierce` strikes have taken damage it is spent and og.systems.combat despawns it before it strikes again; a pierce of 0 is never spent. Projectiles never enter og.CombatAttackers, so a bullet hell has no cap.

Reads the handle a field of entity i holds (a TableRow, an Entity, an asset) from the view, typed as the field's value: `og.table.get(world, a.handle(Foe, "row", i), Enemy)`. A handle column holds two u32 words a row, so `a.column(Foe).row[i]` was half of some row's handle and typed as a plain number; reading it took a world.get of the whole component per entity.

A game's own pause rows (Restart stage): `rows={[{ key: "restart", label: "Restart stage", after: "resume" }]}` and `onRow={(e, key) => …}`, drawn as the built-in rows, after the row `after` names or at the end of their group, a `minor` one below the rule.

The built-in UI speaks Simplified Chinese: every engine component and screen string table (`x.en.ogt`) ships a `x.zh-CN.ogt` beside it, bundled with it and registered as a translation of the English base, so under zh-CN PauseScreen reads 已暂停 / 继续游戏. A game's own zh-CN table still overrides any of its keys, and its base table stays the one every locale falls back to.

Shared objects (guide shared-worlds §5): state the world server owns and every visitor near it sees the same, such as a door one visitor opens or a block one places. og.shared.shape's `object` names the game's component every object carries; og.shared.put and og.shared.remove change one by key, optionally only at the version the visitor saw, and og.SharedOpAnswered says whether the server took it. Each object within sight is an og.SharedObject entity with an og.Transform and that component, spawned, rewritten and despawned by the engine (og.SharedObjectChanged, og.SharedObjectGone); og.shared.object names its key and version. Like remote avatars they are host input kept in og.platform.journal. A world that names none of the records keeps its type table and hash.

The world server keeps shared objects: it takes each put or remove in arrival order when the expected version matches and the object is within the sender's two cells, answers every op, and sends the whole object to the clients near it. --store FILE appends every change to a log the next start reads back, so objects outlive a restart.

Marks a light that never moves or changes. Nothing changes while RenderSettings.staticLightReach is 0 (the default); a light that casts a shadow or has a cookie is always shaded per pixel. The three components grow a field, so a world with any of them hashes differently; what its ticks do is unchanged.

Past this many metres from a static light, its diffuse light comes from a 32 × 12 × 32 grid of probes round the camera (half the reach apart, recomputed on the CPU when the camera moves a cell or a static light changes) instead of being shaded per pixel, and a static rect light sends rough surfaces (roughness 0.5 or more) nothing there. Glossy surfaces keep every static light's highlights. The grid takes 0.6 MB of GPU memory while it is on; nothing is baked or downloaded.

Recooked scene fields update every live placement and later instantiations from the cooked scene, preserving simulation changes to unedited fields. No runtime override store or writeback path is retained. Entity-tree changes ask for a restart rather than patching mismatched rows.

Generate schema-checked content declarations, nested game source and playtests from the CLI or MCP. Explicit --replace updates supplied code/tests under the source lock. Set edits project/content literals through the TypeScript AST, validates before committing, resolves inherited fields to their defining prefab, then incrementally cooks. JSON results include file, line, column and old/new values; computed expressions report their location without writing.

Creation returns structured identity, choices, file lists and failures without prompts. Help exposes creation discovery, detailed model/projection/server options, model compare/bake and flow check-cuts; new shows the full create help.

Carve explicit valley and river polylines with the shared parabolic river section; river lines must not rise downstream and can share endpoints as an authored network. Preserve a scalar field of original-shape weights or a boundary band after processing. Cook tracks generated preservation fields and uses the same constraints as runtime, without resampling or inferring branches.

Author local terrain brushes and placed primitive, buffer or model geometry stamps directly in a terrain file. Cook applies edit and stamp blocks in written order after generation and shape protection, using the same Rust brush, projection and patch kernels as live terrain edits. Projected scatter samples the processed terrain, including its imported model operands.
Discover authored tileset, tilemap layer and object fields from parser line tables, and model-program operation and profile keys from the JSON parser's accepted-field tables.

A focused Input takes the platform's input method in a native window as it does on the web: Chinese, Japanese and Korean preedit shows underlined at the caret and commits into the field, the candidate window opens at the caret, Ctrl+C/X (Cmd on macOS) put the selection on the OS clipboard and Ctrl+V pastes from it.

Prepares a stopped timeline without showing it: nothing of it is evaluated (no camera, caption, sound, effect or event), the entity's og.VideoPlayer holds the frame its own video track starts with, paused, and the engine modules the timeline needs are fetched. Set it some ticks before playing a cutscene that opens on footage, so its first frame is already decoded. Playing, pausing or seeking the timeline evaluates it as before.

A timeline has a `scene` track: `track scene { key 0 { scene "scenes/kitchen.ogt" } }`. From a key to the next (or `scene none`) that scene is in the world, its entities under a root that is a child of the og.Timeline's entity, so a cutscene, a level or a minigame brings its own world and takes it away. The cut happens between ticks: the tick whose time reaches the key decides and the next starts with the old scene gone and the new one in place, on every host, in a replay and after a restore. A timeline that ends keeps its scene until it is stopped; a seek inside a key keeps the scene that is there. The cook refuses a scene the bundle lacks, and a timeline now needs the engine modules of the scenes, videos and timelines its tracks name.

og.scene.progress says whether the scene would be drawn whole the frame it is placed: every streaming group in, and everything it spawns with loaded, with no pipeline of it still compiling. Wait for it instead of `ready` to change scene without a first-frame hitch.
The build line carries `event: "build"`, after the `check` event.

The shapes of `og test --json`, `og probe`, `og build --json` and where every command's output lands are documented as a contract and pinned by tests; the start guide §1 gives the non-interactive `og new --look --premise` a tool runs.

A held on-screen d-pad (`touchPad`) carries the way it reads as `data-dir-up`, `data-dir-right`, `data-dir-down` and `data-dir-left` (two on a diagonal, none in its dead middle), so a class lights the pressed arm: `group-data-dir-up/pad:bg-accent` on a child of a `group/pad` pad.

Every look has three more shape images coloured by the element's fill: `nine-cross`, a d-pad's body, `nine-cross-rim`, its outline, and `nine-cross-arm`, its top arm in the same box (`rotate-90`, `rotate-180` and `-rotate-90` turn it to the others).

Transfers deterministic authored values from the closed evaluator to owned canonical binary data and caches those same bytes. Numeric typed arrays retain element type, little-endian samples and view bounds instead of expanding through JSON text. The existing JSON consumer entry projects this one representation; there is no second evaluator or old-cache fallback. Project/content graph integration and author-format cutovers remain separate.

Recognizes direct imported file-kind factory calls before evaluation and maps literal edits to their argument, preserving original TypeScript spans and comments. Aliased factories, lookalike local objects, type-only imports and computed kind selections cannot masquerade as static content declarations. Candidate source overlays evaluate edits and helper changes with the existing closed executor, input tracking and cache without writing project files. This is the source/provenance foundation; persistent save integration and format cutovers remain separate.

Indexed TS entries now have a tooling stage for scoped deterministic evaluation, original-schema validation and reference closure. It checks actual primary/subresource kinds, direct module permissions, project roots and snapshot completeness, and records executable imports, captured inputs, schema identity and reverse reference edges without retaining every source/IR. Original reference expression locations are mapped in a single source pass. Domain producers must report actual derived outputs; suffixes are never guessed. This foundation does not yet switch CLI/scaffold formats, discover project records, schedule domain cook jobs, assign packs or implement transitive action caches.

Adds pre-evaluation file-to-ID-to-kind discovery and per-module ContentIndex declarations. Content roots contain direct file.<kind> TypeScript entries; import entries require a literal schema-defined kind. Module relocation preserves IDs. Helpers, binary inputs and external exchange text belong outside content/. This foundation does not yet switch CLI/scaffold author formats, infer derived outputs or validate reference graphs.

Indexed TS content now has a closed preparation path that checks every executable helper import against declared pure roots and direct module dependencies before reading it, including already captured helpers. Literal inputs are captured from the entry module's assets/ or sources/, never another helper's root. Stale entry snapshots are refused; actual source import edges and raw inputs are recorded separately. This foundation does not yet validate content references, bind contextual records or switch CLI/scaffold author formats.

Adds schema-derived typed content factories and immutable ref(id) identities in the closed cook realm. Each factory returns one kind-tagged descriptor without cooking other entries. og api gen/check now generate and drift-check author-inputs.d.ts from the Rust domain input schemas. Project-bound scene, prefab and table inputs require contextual record schemas; no global arbitrary-object fallback is provided. This foundation does not switch existing file parsers or project formats.

Cook scripts can call input.bytes/text with literal root-relative paths. Cook captures transitive helper inputs before evaluation, hashes their bytes into the action key and refuses dynamic paths, symlinks, root escapes and input capability aliases. Bytes are independent Uint8Array copies; text is strict UTF-8. The module also exposes the existing offline procgen mechanisms. This establishes the input foundation, not a file-kind or project-format switch.

Schema-generated variable-length array inputs accept the nine numeric typed arrays when their item type accepts arbitrary numbers, including aliases and nullable unions. Fixed arrays, tuples, numeric literal restrictions and nonnumeric items keep their existing constraints; schema decoding still checks sample ranges and counts.

Adds Rust-schema-derived defineProject/defineModule author declarations and a closed project bootstrap over the existing deterministic executor and binary data boundary. Bootstrap validates the installed engine pin, canonical source paths, independent module/delivery dependency graphs, optional-pack boundaries and candidate overlays without running the game entry or content. Real imported manifest helpers support original-source literal diagnostics and patches. This is foundation only: CLI/scaffold/project consumers and legacy author readers switch together in a later format cutover.

Discover named pure record declarations without importing the game entry. Bind scene, prefab and table input schemas to engine records plus records from the owning module and its direct dependencies; retain field order, defaults and handle-reference metadata.

Pure record and column factories share the runtime's token implementation without loading a host. Declare project components, resources and events in src/schema and import those same tokens in game code.

Author input schemas mark actual content-reference positions, including reflected handle fields. Reference extraction validates with the same schema and Rust decoder, selects applicable union branches with the original validator, preserves container kind constraints and JSON Pointer locations, and ignores token-shaped arbitrary JSON. A reusable schema graph prunes numeric payloads from reference traversal. This foundation does not yet resolve content identities or subresources, validate module access, assemble the evaluated project graph or switch CLI/scaffold author formats.

Cook scripts can create independent seeded streams with rng(seed), next() and fork(label), using the existing Rust RNG rather than a separate JS algorithm or runtime handles. Seeds must be u32 integers; UTF-16 labels derive fresh streams without advancing the parent. The RNG implementation is part of the cook action key. Math.random remains forbidden. This adds an author foundation without switching file formats.

Prepared TS data entries retain their original source snapshot. Tooling can locate direct literals by JSON Pointer and propose byte-preserving value patches or missing-property insertions with expected-value checks. Changed sources, computed/shared expressions, ambiguous objects and overlapping edits reject the whole patch. This is an in-memory source-edit foundation; schema/type validation, entity provenance and atomic native/web persistence remain with the consuming author service. No file kind or project format is switched by this batch.

TS projects refresh contextual author types under .og/types/author and check one isolated configuration per source module. Each module sees engine records, its own records and its direct dependencies without leaking other modules' ambient augmentations.

Register structured Rust/JSON Schema inputs for animgraph, rig, motion-action, timeline, flipbook, rig2d, tileset, tilemap, video, vfx2d, behaviour, dialogue, quest, shader, post and ui-material. The same closed input types drive serde decoding, structural validation and TypeScript declarations, with tagged content references and field units/ranges. Dialogue defaults to typed nodes, lines, conditions and commands; Yarn is an explicit import and WGSL remains text. This schema foundation does not switch file formats or connect the author factories to cooking.

The TSX backpack's tiles drag again: a tile dropped on another reports onMove with { dragged, target }, the two items' keys, by pointer, touch, keys or pad. A locked tile is not picked up; the game reorders, swaps or stacks.

The arena's scoreboard and draft as TSX, beside their .svelte: ArenaScoreboard (each team a table of K, D, A and score or score alone, You and Disconnected marks, side by side or stacked, scrolling inside its height) and ArenaDraft (the phase band with the turn's HudTimer, struck bans and player picks per team, lock in). The teams wash in the default blue and red (the seed-team colours have no class surface), the portraits' octagons are rounded and the scroll fades are dropped.

Ten more HUD components as TSX, beside their .svelte: HudBar, StatBar, HudTimer, AmmoCounter, HudHint, ActionButton, HoldButton, Crosshair, Combo and Celebration. Styles are Tailwind classes; SVG arcs (rings, the crosshair's circle, charges) stand in on Views, the bars' tick masks are drawn views, and the celebrations' particle emitters, burst keyframes and play sounds are dropped.

Ten more HUD components as TSX, beside their .svelte: ActionHints, Cooldown, HudEffect, BossBar, Killfeed, HudLootEntry, OrbMeter, OverlayBar, PickupFeed and ProgressBar. Styles are Tailwind classes; SVG waves, weapon silhouettes and glare arcs are dropped (the orb's liquid is a flat fill, the killfeed's weapons show in words), the boss bar's phase thresholds stand as diamonds, and the overlays bar's horizontal scroll has no surface yet.

The last twelve HUD components as TSX, beside their .svelte: CombatLog, DamageDirection, HeroButton, PerfReadout, HudPortrait, ProgressRing, QtePrompt, RadialMenu, RadialMeter, HudSlot, StarBar and StatusGrid. Styles are Tailwind classes; the radial menu's and the damage direction's SVG wedges and arcs are sampled Line polylines, cooldown sweeps, charge rings and the effects' time wipe stand as top-down veils until the wipe surface covers rings, the slots' and portraits' octagon and hexagon cuts are rounded, and the status grid's type notch is dropped (the rim carries the type). DamageNumbers and TouchControls stay svelte: the first is nothing but world anchors, the second needs the joystick and dpad widgets.

The touch controls as TSX, beside their .svelte: TouchControls, its stick, d-pad and action buttons built from Views. The buttons feed their og-input actions through the engine's touch wiring; the stick and the d-pad report their axis to a new onMove prop each move, dead-zoned and re-centred on release (the document widgets' stick zones have no TSX surface), and the d-pad's eight ways need two fingers on two arms. The overlay bar's buttons row scrolls along when it runs over. The hold controls hold again: HoldButton, the action hints' hold hint and the QTE prompt's hold run holdMs with their progress fill and confirm on completion.

The shooter HUD's ability bar, squad, vitals, loadout and combat frame and the arena's round HUD, ready check, lobby, roster, versus reveal, spectator bar and vote as TSX, beside their .svelte: ShooterAbilities, ShooterSquad, ShooterVitals, ShooterLoadout, ShooterCombatHud, ArenaRoundHud, ArenaReady, ArenaLobby, ArenaRoster, ArenaVersus, ArenaSpectator and ArenaVote. Styles are Tailwind classes; the roster's and lobby's cut corners, portraits' octagons, the versus seal's hexagon and the ability slots' conic cooldown masks are approximations (rounded corners, top-down veils), the arena cards' and verdicts' gradient text fills are solid inks with glows and the team inks are the default blue and red (the game's seed-team colours have no class surface), the round HUD's banner entrance and the versus reveal's entrance replay are dropped, and the touch controls and damage numbers stay svelte: their roots are world anchors, which have no TSX surface.

The HUD's damage numbers and the world blocks the new anchor serves as TSX, beside their .svelte: DamageNumbers, Nameplate, Waypoint, SpeechBubble, InteractionPrompt, OverheadBars and LootLabel. Styles are Tailwind classes; the anchors' edge clamping, chevron, decluttering, avoidance, occlusion fade and max distance, the ground pools and planes (a loot glow, the path, placement, selection-ring and telegraph grounds), the GPU mass figures and overhead bars (pooled, instanced), the plate's lean, the wings' and brackets' and tails' and chevrons' clip-path shapes, the interrupted cast's hatch, the hold ring's drain and the key caps' action glyphs are dropped or stand in (diamonds, a nine-ring wipe, notch marks).

The compass, minimap, minimap view and seven shooter HUD blocks as TSX, beside their .svelte: ShooterPrompt, ShooterDamage, ShooterEffects, ShooterObjectives, ShooterPickups, ShooterRadar and ShooterRound. Styles are Tailwind classes; the compass band's mask fade, the minimaps' region crop, the radar's sweep mask and range rings and the effects', pickups' and round plates' cut corners are approximations (rounded corners, full-surface overlays), the radar's filled player arrow is a stroked Line and the objective diamonds are rotate-45 squares. The ten world-anchored world blocks (loot-label, nameplate, overhead-bars, path-line, placement-ghost, selection-ring, telegraph, waypoint, speech-bubble, interaction-prompt) stay svelte: their roots are world anchors, which have no TSX surface.

Seven panel components as TSX, beside their .svelte: Backpack, Breadcrumbs, Carousel, Conversation, ConversationBacklog, Crafting and DataGrid. Styles are Tailwind classes with pack slots and cut shapes; the backpack's drag-onto-another-tile move, the conversation's typewriter reveal, the carousel's scroll-snap and the pips' lean, and cut elements' gradients, glows and rolled rims are dropped.

added.member: RpgItemCard, RpgLoot, RpgMenu, RpgQuestLog, SplitView, TooltipCard, RpgTrade
added.summary: The item card, loot, menu, quest log, split view, tooltip card and trade panels ship as TSX beside their component documents: same props, states, strings and accessibility, styled with Tailwind classes and the new UI's primitives. Cut shapes, glows and gradients the classes cannot express are approximated or dropped, each noted in the component's docstring.

A theme is a recipe (`theme.json`) that picks a value per dimension (material, shape, type, motion, ornament, effects, sound, icons, density) and a `color`, with `extends` (one parent), `with` (mix-ins, in order) and `pack` (a pack.json laid over the result, so a hand-drawn image replaces a generated one by name). Unknown keys and `extends` loops are errors naming the file. og-cook reads it in a later release; the format is in og-ui-next's CONVENTIONS.md §Theme recipes.

An anchored TSX element with `occlusion="fade"` draws at 0.35 opacity, and with `"hide"` hides, while a drawn mesh other than its own entity's stands between the camera and its point (a line trace against og.render.raycast's meshes at each tick's end); it carries `data-occluded`. Nameplates and loot labels fade.

Anchored TSX elements with `declutter="stack"` move straight up clear of each other instead of overlapping, and with `"hide"` hide while they overlap; a higher `priority`, then the nearer, keeps its place, and one pushed past the top of the screen hides. Nameplates, loot labels, speech bubbles and interaction prompts (priority 1) stack.

An anchored TSX element with `clamp="edge"` stays on screen when its point leaves it or goes behind the camera: it pins `clampMargin` px (24) inside the edge on the line from the screen's centre toward its point, and carries `data-clamped` and `data-edge-top|right|bottom|left`. Waypoints clamp.

--seed-hud, the game components' light (--hud-accent): by default the accent seed when it has a hue, otherwise the instrument cyan the default style has always drawn with. A pack or a game's --seed-accent (or --seed-primary, which the accent follows) now recolours the light of every family, and a pack may set --seed-hud apart from the accent.

--action-* roles: the one main action of every built-in screen and component (Play, Continue, Buy, Equip, Send) is a plate in the families' light with two corners cut, glowing while it can be pressed; a button wears it with class="go". data-tone=reward is the same plate in gold, for a claim; data-tone=confirm in green, only beside a decline. A style pack restyles every main action by setting them.

--chosen-* roles: the one selection every built-in family draws. A chosen row is washed in the families' light from a leading bar (--chosen-fill, --chosen-edge), a chosen tab lit along its foot (--chosen-tab-*), a chosen tile ringed in it with a glow (--chosen-tile-*). The families' own selection tokens (front end, results, select, inventory, cards, party, data, system, quests, social) alias them, so a style pack restyles every selection by setting them.

The engine's game icon set: `<Icon name>` draws 113 game icons before the Lucide fallback (which keeps only the names the set lacks, such as back, close, chevrons and gear). Twenty hero icons are drawn as multi-tone stickers in the pack's colours (coin, gem, star, heart, shield, energy, ammo, lock, key, chest, gift, crown, potion, ticket, xp, alert, new, rarity, trophy, hourglass); the rest are filled game-icons.net silhouettes in the icon's ink, covering stats, navigation, settings, social, shop, rewards and status effects. The names are listed in templates/styles/shared/icons/README.md; a game's own icons still win by name.

The icon set's tones: icon-gold, icon-red, icon-blue, icon-green, icon-purple, icon-orange, icon-steel, icon-wood, icon-glass, and the sticker's icon-outline, icon-shadow, icon-shade, icon-gloss and icon-mark, the same in both schemes; a pack's theme restyles every toned icon through them. The scifi, fantasy and cartoon packs set their own.

The Credits screen lists the engine's credits (the authors of the icon set's game-icons.net icons, CC BY 3.0) after the game's sections; `engineCredits` (@origingame/engine/ui/screens/engine-credits.ts) holds them for a game that rolls its own.

An icon set's SVG may paint a path in a theme colour, `fill="var(--color-<role>)"` (or stroke): the icon is then drawn in tones, each run of one tone in the pack's colour for that role, over an outline and drop shadow of its silhouette (`sticker <outline> <dx> <dy>` in the set, in 24ths of the em; colours `icon-outline` and `icon-shadow`).
A pack.json's `iconSet` names the icon set (.ogt of type icons) `<Icon name>` draws from under the game's own icons; a later pack layer's set wins by name, so a pack can restyle a few hero icons.

Five more pack sound events: `toggle`, `tab`, `levelup`, `purchase` and `countdown`, which a node's `sound` prop names and a pack.json's `sounds` remaps or mutes like the others. An event a pack has no clip for sounds the nearest one it has: toggle and tab fall back to select, purchase to confirm, levelup to reward, countdown to press (and confirm and back to press, as before), so a pack without the new clips still sounds.

The engine's UI sound set: twelve short clips (`tap`, `toggle`, `tab`, `countdown`, `back`, `close`, `open`, `confirm`, `error`, `purchase`, `reward`, `levelup`) mastered to one balanced mix, in four styles. The default pack now sounds every event from `@styles/shared/sfx/default/`, so a TSX UI clicks, confirms and rewards without a pack naming any sound; scifi, fantasy and cartoon carry their own clips in `sfx/` instead of the synthesised `@styles/shared/sfx-*` presets. A pack lies over the default one: an event it leaves out sounds the default clip, and `"volume": 0` mutes it.

Frame art with depth for every pack: the default pack's `button`, `button-primary`, `button-danger` (each with `-hover` and `-pressed`), `button-disabled`, `panel`, `plate`, `field`, `slot`, `badge` and `divider`, and the tint pieces `slot-rim` (a slot's rarity, `nine-slot-rim bg-epic`) and `chip-bevel`, drawn as `nine-<name>`; and the theme colours `art-fg`, `art-button-fg` and `art-primary-fg`, the ink on that art. A pack's own image of the same name replaces one, as before.

New frame art for scifi and cartoon. Scifi: dark translucent glass with a lit hairline, a soft drop and one cyan accent per piece (a leading-edge bar, a header tab, a corner notch), rounded on one radius rule, and a flat lit-cyan primary; it adds `slot` and `divider`. Cartoon: a thick navy outline, two-tone faces under a glossy band and a deep lip, sky-blue, yellow and red buttons, a cream panel under a tangerine header (`Panel.frame` now `scheme-light` with `fg` ink), navy plates, chips and slots; it adds `button-danger` and `slot`, and its plain button's ink is `art-button-fg`. The fantasy pack names its red buttons `button-primary` too, so its primary art matches its `art-primary-fg`.
`animate-charge`: a one-shot keyframe animation that gathers to 1.08× over its first 40%, jumps to 1.15× and settles back to its size (0.6 s), a reveal's charge and pop on the thing revealed.

`Flourish`, the engine's UI effect presets: it wraps what it decorates (an icon, a slot, a price, a button) and plays over it, once per shot with its pack sound and at three to four times its size, a `reward` (flash, rays, ring, star glints, motes), a `levelUp` (screen wash, column of light, rays, rising stars), a `purchase` (a fountain of spinning coins catching the light, the target popping), a `reveal` that charges (glints drawn in, a swelling glow, the target gathering), bursts and settles, richer by `rarity` (rays from rare, more from epic, a column and a screen wash from legendary), or, while it shows, a `highlight` (an aura in the pack's `art-primary`, a sweeping sheen, twinkling stars). Built on `Particles`: fourteen emitters in components/hud/fx/ and six particle textures the default pack carries as the images `fx-sparkle`, `fx-glint`, `fx-shard`, `fx-coin`, `fx-ray` and `fx-ring`, which a game's own emitters can name too (`texture "@styles/shared/fx/sparkle.png"`).

The theme colour `art-primary`, the primary button art's own colour (gold in the default pack, cyan in scifi, red in fantasy, yellow in cartoon): what lights it, such as a highlight's aura (`bg-art-primary`, `shadow-art-primary`).

A TSX text element in dump_ui lists brokenWords: each place its laid-out lines cut a word where UAX #14 gives no break (`end|start`), the sign of a text measured narrower than it draws. The gallery lists them in defects.txt and exits non-zero.

An `.ogt` an engine component imports gives its asset id as the import's default (`import sparks from "./fx/sparks.ogt"`), and a `type particles` file reached this way is bundled as an emitter under that id. The built-in emitters are `@ui/components/hud/fx/confetti.ogt`, `sparks.ogt`, `embers.ogt` and `firework.ogt`, written white so the node's ink colours them.

useClock() reads the world's tick and its length in seconds as of the last tick boundary, for a component that paces itself (a reveal, a countdown) without the wall clock; a replay sees the same values on the same tick.

The TSX conversation takes rate again: the line shows that many characters per second by the world's tick, starting again with each new line, and reports onRevealed once it is whole; a screen reader always reads the whole line. Under reduced motion it still reveals at the rate (the TSX UI cannot read that setting yet).

Exports every built-in component, control and screen (211), not 21; each module is also importable by its path (`@origingame/engine/ui/components/hud/ability-bar.tsx`, `ui/controls/*`, `ui/screens/*`) with its `fixtures`.
Exported from the components barrel; they were reachable only by deep import.
`onNavigate` reports the normalized point pressed or dragged across the map, and `onPing` the point of a long press; both are clamped to 0..1.
`previousLabel` and `nextLabel` name the arrow keys for a screen reader; absent, they keep the navigation's label (Pagination) or the month (Calendar).

added.member: Waypoint, Nameplate, SpeechBubble, InteractionPrompt, LootLabel, OverheadBars
added.summary: Take the world-anchor scaling and `occlusion` (`fade`, `hide` or `none`) props; Waypoint and Compass markers take `elevation` (`above`, `below`, `level`) and draw a chevron for it.
The default icon set gains `eye` and `eyeOff`.

OG9107 covers the text inside a theme's art slot: an ink a child sets, or a state's ink on the slot element, that reads under its ratio on the slot's art is reported at its class, with the fix (leave the ink to the slot, or give the state its own shape: `data-on:nine-chip-cut`).

A style directory may hold a theme recipe (`assets/styles/<name>/theme.json`) instead of a pack.json: the cook compiles it into the style's pack and draws its art (cached by spec under `.og/ui-art/`), and a look's `ui "<name>"` names it as any style. `ui "<name>"` also finds an engine theme (`@themes/<name>`) before a built-in style, and only the named theme is bundled. A style with both files is an error.

A compiled theme gives each art slot its own ink (`art-<piece>-fg`), solved on the art it draws, and moves every ink role in OKLCH lightness until it holds its ratio on the theme's art as well as the design's surfaces.

A count beside a tab's label (`<Text class={packClass("Tab", "count")}>`) sits on its own ground in that ground's ink, lit with the accent while its tab is selected. `Tab` is a `group/tab`, so a slot inside it can style itself with `group-selected/tab:`.

Ten engine themes a look's `ui "<name>"` names: anime, minimal, scifi, tactical, fantasy, storybook, cartoon, candy, pixel and ink, plus tactical-arctic, a theme derived from tactical with `extends`. A game derives its own the same way in `assets/styles/<name>/theme.json`. A new material, `matte`, gives a clean flat face with a hairline and a soft drop.

A development build's page takes re-cooked files ([path, bytes][]) and applies them in place without a hot reload (the world and bundle stay; only the changed documents, styles and default style are read again): an edited document, style or (in an origin-engine checkout) default style shows without reloading the page. It answers each step's time in ms. The UI gallery (docs/ui.md §6.5) uses it.

A TSX element that draws text reports it in its UI dump's detail as drawn: ink (sRGB 0-255 and alpha 0-1, its opacity included), fontSize and textLines (each laid-out line's box on screen, in CSS px, bounded under a transform). The UI gallery reads each line's ground from its frame and lists text under the screens guide's contrast bar (4.5:1, 3:1 over 24 px) in defects.txt; disabled controls are exempt. The gallery's --only also takes a comma list.

A grid of tiles names its tile's least width on the spacing scale: `grid-cols-fill-33` is `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(132px, 1fr))` and `grid-cols-fit-48` is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(192px, 1fr))`; `grid-rows-fill-*` and `grid-rows-fit-*` do the same for rows.

`og check` warns (OG9108) where a game's TSX writes a ground or an ink by hand: a thinned ink (`text-fg/66`: use `text-fg-muted` or `text-fg-subtle`), a literal `white` or `black` ground or ink, a hand-written colour (`bg-[#…]`), or a ground under text less than 85% opaque (`bg-well/82`, `from-entry-lo`). Each warning names the slot or theme role that fixes it. Text sits on a pack slot or an opaque theme ground in that ground's ink, so it reads over any scene and in every pack.

added.member: Style pack slots Row.frame and Head.frame
added.summary: Two new pack slots for the lists, tables and feeds a HUD lays over the scene: `packClass("Row", "frame")` (an opaque `bg-raised-lo text-fg` row; `selected` for the chosen or local player's row, `muted` for one out of play) and `packClass("Head", "frame")` (a table or list's head row). A game's pack restyles them like any slot.

A new game's ui choice is one of the engine's themes (anime, candy, cartoon, fantasy, ink, minimal, pixel, scifi, storybook, tactical) or default, labelled in English and Chinese, each with its preview. A look's preset names its theme in its ui line and the catalogue's ui does the same (toy-3d candy, painterly-3d fantasy, neon-vector scifi …), so a game made from a look starts in its theme.

`og api show themes`: the engine's themes and what each fits, picking one in the look, deriving the game's own theme.json with extends, replacing a piece of drawn art by hand, and the contrast the cook guarantees.

`og check` warns (OG9109) where a game's TSX writes by hand a value the theme names, and names the class that replaces it: a bracketed length, type size, tracking, leading or radius (`w-[17.143rem]`: `w-60`; `text-[1.714rem]`: `text-title`; `tracking-[0.14em]`: `tracking-label`), a bracketed percentage (`size-[40%]`: `size-2/5`), a shadow written out (`shadow-[0px_0px_12px_#38e8ff]`: `shadow-glow`), a colour, `var(--…)` or literal `white` or `black` in a border, ring, stroke or shadow (`border-white/8`: `border-rim-soft`), and an opacity modifier on a role (`bg-well/79`: `bg-well`). Where no step is exact it names the nearest. `og check --json` carries the replacement as `fix` and whether it draws the same value as `exact`. Grid tracks of `auto` and `fr`, flex factors, `env()` insets and an inline `style` that carries data are not values and are left alone.
Takes charge, 0 to 1 (a super or a focus meter): a bar fills along its foot, and the button lights and breathes when it is full. Negative, the default, shows none.

Pack slots for a hero action (Hero.frame with .premium, .secondary, .danger and .ready; Hero.label; Hero.charge and .fill), a hold's progress (Hold.fill with .danger and .primary) and more of an ability's parts (Ability.icon and .disabled, Ability.tint, Ability.slash, Ability.pip and .on, Ability.chip.cost, .short and .count).

Pack slots for an ability slot on a HUD's ability bar: Ability.box (its side; .ultimate), Ability.frame (shape and rim; .ultimate, .ready, .disabled), Ability.face (.ultimate: its inset is the charge ring's width), Ability.ring and Ability.ring.fill (the ultimate's charge), Ability.sweep (.ultimate), Ability.count and Ability.chip.ult, .ready, .key and .charges. A theme recipe dresses them from its own slot art, and a theme sets their sizes.

Design tokens for the combat HUD, each a theme's to set: duration-ready-pulse, -flash, -damage, -damage-stagger, -trail-hold, -trail, -hit and -arc; scale-ready-pulse, -damage-pop and -combo-pop; opacity-sweep and -flash; and the stroke arc. The scifi, candy, tactical and anime themes set their own.

Draws every part from the Ability slots, so it takes the theme's shape, art, sizes and glow. The ultimate's charge fills round it clockwise from the top, a cooldown sweeps round the art instead of a veil from the top, and a full ultimate shows Ready (shooter.abilities.ready) under it, its charge in figures while it fills.

More of the RPG action HUD's blocks, usable by name in a game's own HUD: one buff or debuff tile (its time as a radial sweep and a tag), one key cap with its action, and one looted row (edge by rarity, name, rarity tag, count). A game lays them out with flex or grid where it wants them.
HudBar measures a shield too (kind shield: --hud-shield-fill and --hud-shield-glow, in cells with segment), so a shooter's armour bar is the same block as an RPG's health bar.
One token each for a HudSlot ultimate's ring (gold by default) and a harmful HudEffect's tag ink (--hud-harm by default), so a HUD family sets its own on the place it gives the block.

A new layout primitive for one line of like blocks (ability slots, party frames, quick items). Its data-fit children are each --layout-strip-item wide, so the strip is as wide as what it holds; where it is given less room they shrink alike, down to --layout-strip-item-min. With data-wraps and its count in --layout-strip-count it breaks into lines instead of going under that minimum.
A slot fills the place it is given: --ability-slot-size is its side (100% inside a strip), and its icon, lock and ring scale with it. It takes count, a quick item's number left.
Each threshold's star sits on the track where it falls, and the stars are the style's rating stars (--star-*): a lit star is gold with a glow, an unlit one a faint outline in a dark seat.

Opt-in hit feedback: the screen's edges flash for each new hit id (flash), pulse while the game says the player is critical (critical), and an arc points to each recent hit (hits, as DamageDirection). Its look and timing are the theme's: Hit.vignette (.critical), Hit.ring, Hit.arc (.shield, .critical), duration-hit, duration-arc and the inset-shadow-vignette token.
A hit takes kind: crit (larger, in gold), heal, shield, weak or miss, each a Damage.number slot a theme dresses; color still overrides it.

Pack slots for the combat HUD: Damage.number (.crit, .heal, .shield, .weak, .miss), Hit.ring, Hit.arc, Hit.vignette, Combo.plate, .count and .multiplier, Feed.row (.self), Feed.name, Feed.plate, Celebrate.title and .halo, Boss.phase and Ring.rest.
A class may pad by the HUD's safe area: `env(hud-inset-top|right|bottom|left)` in a padding (`pt-[calc(env(hud-inset-top)+16px)]`).

Pack slots for the HUD's meters, so a theme restyles them all at once: Bar.frame (.thick, .low), Bar.tone (.mana, .stamina, .shield, .xp, .boss, .low, .invulnerable), Bar.ghost, Bar.tick and Bar.value; Ring.box, Ring.track, Ring.fill (.success, .warn, .danger, .info), Ring.spin and Ring.label; Orb.box, Orb.rim, Orb.well (.mana), Orb.fill (.mana), Orb.glass, Orb.value and Orb.label; Radial.box, Radial.track, Radial.fill (.exhausted) and Radial.sheen; Boss.status and Boss.figure.

World-anchored UI nodes now support distance scaling (scaleAt, scaleMin, scaleMax), depth culling (maxDistance), and LOD state bands (lod -> data-lod-near, data-lod-mid, data-lod-far); Nameplate and InteractionPrompt wire maxDistance directly.
HudEditorScreen now supports interactive pointer-draggable and keyboard-nudgeable HUD regions inside the safe-area guide frame with grid snapping and a scale, opacity, and visibility inspector dock.

Re-exported previously internal controls (Accordion, Collapsible, ContextMenu, DropdownMenu, List, MenuItem, MenuLabel, MenuSeparator, NumberInput, Popover, Radio, RadioGroup, Sheet, Tab, ToastStack, Toggle, ToggleGroup, Toolbar, ToolbarSeparator) from the components barrel.

The default pack names the HUD's own colours, so a TSX component styles them by role (bg-hud-accent, text-foe, border-ally…): hud-accent with hud-accent-fg and hud-accent-hi, foe and foe-fg, ally, boon and boon-fg, critical, fever, late, well, key-hi, key-lo, key-fg, gold-fg, gold-hi, epic-hi and chart-easy to chart-master. A style pack restyles them like any other theme colour; -fg is the ink on that fill, -hi the lit top of its gradient.

added.member: UI classes skew-*, wipe transitions, animate-shake, animate-flash, animate-recoil
added.summary: A UI element can skew (skew-x-*, skew-y-*) and both a skew and a radial image wipe transition between styles; animate-shake, animate-flash and animate-recoil are new keyframe presets, and the preset animations take their durations from the theme's duration tokens (ready-pulse, damage, flash).
A theme or pack names scale, opacity and stroke-width tokens (scale-press, opacity-flash, stroke-arc …) that classes read like its other tokens.

added.member: UI classes mix-blend-normal, mix-blend-add, mix-blend-screen, mix-blend-multiply
added.summary: A UI element and the particles it emits blend with what lies under them by its mix-blend class (normal, add, screen or multiply), down its subtree.

A node's haptic prop (tick, tap, thud, double, buzz, success, warning, error, or none to silence it) plays when it fires an interaction or sound cue other than hover; a pack's haptics table sets them per slot and event, falling back like sounds, scaled by the player's haptic strength.

A theme's effects (glow, pixel-burst, ink-splash …) and density (comfortable, touch …) compile into its pack's shadows, text shadows and control heights; the cartoon, fantasy, ink, minimal, pixel and storybook themes tune their Combat HUD with them.

A style pack's theme takes four more scales, filled from the design tokens in the default pack: `duration` (ms: duration-instant, -fast, -base, -slow, -control and the loop names, also for delay-*), `opacity` (opacity-dim, -muted, -soft, -faint, -wash), `stroke` (line widths for border-*, ring-*, inset-ring-* and outline-*: hairline, thin, regular, thick, edge) and `scale` (scale-press, -swell, -pop, -shrink). A theme that sets one restyles every component that names it; a colour of the same name still wins on ring and border.

The built-in components name these tokens instead of fixed numbers (duration-control for a control's own state change, opacity-dim for a disabled or down state, ring-regular and border-thick for their edges), so a theme's motion, dimming and line weight reach them. They look and move as before under the default pack.

`Touch.base`, `Touch.knob`, `Touch.pad`, `Touch.button` (`.primary`), `Touch.charge` (`.ready`), `Touch.icon`, `Touch.actions` and `Touch.bar`: a theme sizes and dresses the touch stick, d-pad, action buttons, their charge ring and the cluster's spacing. A full charge on an enabled button glows and breathes.

`Pips.units`, `Pips.pip`, `Pips.fill` (`.success`, `.warn`, `.info`, `.primary`), `Pips.label` and `Counter.value`; Pips takes a `class`. The screens guide has a recipe that builds a weapon level from Pips, Counter and HudBar.

TSX classes for where a line may break inside a word: `hyphens-manual` (the default) breaks only at a soft hyphen, `hyphens-auto` also where the language's dictionary allows, `hyphens-none` never. They inherit like the other text classes and take variants (`md:hyphens-auto`); a game whose code writes `hyphens-auto` ships its locales' dictionaries.
Ten more game icons: `vip`, `pass`, `ad`, `settings`, `refresh`, `inventory`, `skillTree`, `rank`, `stamina` and `claimAll`.

`kind="collect"`: coins fly from `from` (px from the counter's centre, default below it) into the counter it decorates, staggered, and flash and glint as they land. `icon` picks what flies (default `coin`).
An element's `style` (inline declarations) now applies over its classes, last.

Line takes viewBox ([w, h], or SVG's "x y w h") and fit ("fill", the default, or "contain"): its points are in the view's space and map onto the laid-out box as it paints, stretched or uniformly scaled and centred, with the stroke width staying in screen px. A chart, map or graph whose box is a flex remainder no longer has to guess its width.

`<Line points={[x0, y0, x1, y1, …]} closed class="stroke-accent stroke-2" />`: a polyline in its box (CSS px from its top left), stroked with round joins and caps by `stroke-*` classes (the ink and 1 px without), for charts, graphs and paths drawn from data. It has no fill, curves or dashes.

TSX classes that mask an element and everything inside it with a gradient's alpha, as CSS's `mask-image`: `mask-[linear-gradient(to_right,black,transparent)]`, a radial or conic gradient the same way; opaque draws, transparent hides. The gradient is measured over the element's own box, and an inner mask replaces an outer one. `mask-none` clears it. Only gradients mask; an image URL is no class.

Variants `menu` and `menu-danger`: a front-end menu entry, type that fills with the HUD accent (or the danger colour) when hovered, focused or pressed, dressed by the pack's `Button.plate.menu` and `Button.plate.menu-danger`. A new `name` prop names its node for tests and the probe.

A front-end menu as a built-in control (`@origingame/engine/ui/controls/menu-list.tsx`): its entries are `menu`-variant Buttons that enter one after another (`List.cascade`, `List.item`), and one bar glides to the entry hovered or focused on the pack's glide spring (`MenuList.indicator`, `MenuList.indicator.danger`). MainMenuScreen and PauseScreen are built on it.
`onFocus` and `onPointerMove` props.

On the web, screen readers read the TSX UI: the page's accessibility mirror is built from the new core's tree (each node's tag, its `role`, `label`, `description`, `checked`, `selected`, `expanded`, `pressed`, `busy`, `hidden`, `modal`, `current`, `disabled`, `tabIndex`, `level`, `live`, `valueMin`, `valueMax`, `valueNow` and `valueText` props, and whether it listens to press or tap), and a frame carries only the nodes that changed. A view that listens to press is a button named by its text; a plain layout view is left out. A status, an alert or a `live` node is announced by the page itself as its text changes.

In a native window, the platform's screen reader (VoiceOver, Narrator, Orca) reads the TSX UI too: the window is sent the new core's accessibility tree, only the nodes that changed after the first, and a reader's focus, activate, increment and decrement reach the game as the web page's do (an `a11y` input naming the node).

A style pack's `contrast` key (theme sections, like `theme`, light/dark pairs allowed) sets what its theme takes in high contrast. The default pack's comes from the design's `:root[data-contrast=more]` tokens: muted and subtle ink step up, fills, tiles and borders take the strong border.

og-ui's new core takes the TSX renderer's op batches (crates/og-ui-next/CONVENTIONS.md §Ops) through the UI patch call: nodes made, inserted, moved, removed and released, their texts, classes, styles, props and the events they listen to. The first batch builds the tree while the game loads, and the reply carries the presses since the last batch for the renderer to dispatch by id.

The probe's dump_ui and `og ui check` list the TSX UI's nodes that show: `id` (op id), `parent`, `path` (op ids from the top, what `touch_move_to` names), box and `text`; a control also has its `role`, its `name` where it differs from the text, and `disabled`, `checked` or `focused` among its states. `og ui check`'s focus-reach and focus-trap walk the new core's focus order; its `a11y-name` and `a11y-locale` rules are gone.

onPinch, onRotate and onSwipe on any host element: two fingers that went down on it pinch and turn it (key start, move, end; value the scale or the turn in radians since they began), and a pointer let go moving fast swipes it (key left, right, up or down; value "vx vy" in px/s). They come from NSH's recognisers over every pointer og-input tracks.
knob on a node inside a touchStick moves it with the stick's knob as og-input reads it.

The cook warns about a `nine-<name>` class whose image is in neither the default pack nor a pack the game holds ("`nine-panle` names no image in the default pack or a pack the game holds: it draws nothing"). It reads the class from the game's code, the built-in components the game imports or a pack's variants, so a misspelt or missing frame never draws nothing silently.

A class `nine-<name>` draws the pack image of that name as the element's box art (nine-sliced, a `tint: true` image coloured by the element's fill), under any variant: `hover:nine-plate-lit` holds only on hover, the last holding one wins. `og check` reports a name the pack lacks.
`<Image src={texture}>` draws a texture from `og.load.texture` over its box; `src` is the texture handle, not a string.

`wipe`, `wipeStart` and `wipeCcw` props on any element with a box image (an `Image`'s `src` or a `nine-<name>` class) wipe it radially: the share shown 0 to 1, bound per tick, from `wipeStart` radians (0 up), clockwise unless `wipeCcw`. Cooldowns and progress rings use it.

`text-stroke-<number>` or `text-stroke-[<length>]` outlines text with a stroke of that width under its fill, in the text's colour or `text-stroke-<color>`'s. Inline styles take `-webkit-text-stroke-width` and `-color`.

Opacity `veil` (0.15) and `quiet` (0.78); scale `nudge` (0.98), `lift` (1.06) and `enter` (0.8); stroke `heavy` (4px), `marker` (5px), `beacon` (9px), `dial` (8px), `pointer` (11px) and `pointer-side` (7px). A theme's `pack.theme` sets them like the others.

NodeGraph is back as TSX: nodes (circle, square, hex or diamond; available, locked, active, done or current; ally or enemy) on the HUD's glass with lines between them, the view fitted whole into the well and centred, and the game's zoom and pan. onPick(e, id), onZoom(e, delta) from the wheel and onPan(e, dx, dy) from a drag.
Chart is back as TSX: bars on a hairline grid with the axis figures, a gold line series through each bar's middle, and each bar's name under it (every other one past eight bars).

Every look has five generated pictures as nine-slice classes: an octagon item or ability `nine-socket`, its `nine-socket-rim` (a white mask the element's bg colours, such as a rarity), a radial `nine-glow` (a mask the bg colours), a `nine-sheen` and an ornate gold `nine-card-frame` with an open centre.

The strategy, racing, rhythm and role-playing components wear the pack's shapes: every plate, panel, chip and button body takes its slot (plate, panel, chip, field or button plate) so a pack dresses them, and the cut-corner plates, panels and tags draw the pack's cut masks instead of approximate corner radii.
A command's cooldown sweep and a queue step's progress wipe over the pack's nine-slice tile, so a pack's art shows through as the clock runs down.
The reticle is the pack's ring again: four arcs wipe around the target instead of one solid band.
The rev dial is the pack's ring: the revs and the red zone wipe from the lower left over the dial's 270 degrees instead of top-down bars.

og-ui's paint pass draws borders (each side its own width), per-corner border-radius (scaled down together when corners overlap, as CSS does), box-shadow layers outside and inset with a Gaussian blur, outline with outline-offset, and a linear-gradient aimed `to` a corner at the box's own diagonal. Transforms, text-shadow, text-decoration and backdrop blur still parse without painting.

On og-ui's new core, a box's image can be tinted by its fill (`bg-*`) instead of the text colour: the white mask takes the fill's colour and the fill is not drawn under it, so a pack's plate art follows the theme and colour scheme.

On og-ui's new core, background takes a linear-gradient() over a base colour (an angle or to-sides, stops with or without percentages); First Light's quest tracker plate (--plate-fill) draws. Other images and a second gradient are listed in the sheet's skipped.
On og-ui's new core, an icon from a texture grid paints: a picture in its own colours, a mask tinted by the text colour. It appears once its texture has loaded.

og-ui's paint pass draws `<Line>`: a stroked polyline, open or closed, with round joins and caps, antialiased, clipped, transformed and faded like any other node. A semi-transparent line's joins draw once, not twice.

og-ui's new core paints a box's image: a texture region nine-sliced (four slice insets, edges and centre stretched or tiled in whole tiles, the centre optional, each slice sampled without bleeding into its neighbours), in its own colours or tinted as a mask, and cut by a radial wipe (the share shown, its start angle and direction) for cooldowns and progress rings. Its texture is a run-time handle the UI renderer sets.

On the web, perf's report lists every pipeline asked for asynchronously with when it was asked for and made (json `pipelines`), and the UI's and the overlay's by name in its text, so one still compiling at Play shows.

On og-ui's new core, a style takes border (and its sides, width and colour, which take layout space), per-corner border-radius, box-shadow (up to four layers, inset or not), outline and outline-offset, translate, scale, rotate, transform-origin, backdrop-filter: blur(), text-shadow and text-decoration, and a linear-gradient's to-corner direction. The paint pass does not draw them yet.

og-ui's new core draws a text outline (`-webkit-text-stroke`, its width and colour) under the text's fill, half its width showing outside each glyph, for HUD text over a 3D scene. Stroke under fill is the only order (`paint-order` is accepted and ignored). An outline reaches at most as far as the font's distance field: a font cooked with `px_range` a third of its `em_px` carries a 2 px outline at 16 px.

og-ui's paint pass draws translate, scale and rotate about transform-origin, composed down the tree as CSS composes them (layout and hit testing do not move, and a transformed box's overflow clip stays axis-aligned), text-shadow (one layer, its blur as far as the glyph's distance field reaches) and text-decoration's underline, overline and line-through.

`export const ground = "panel"` in Steps, Avatar, Pips, ItemSlot, CardPiles and KeyValues: they are pieces of a panel and draw on its ground, never straight over the scene. The UI gallery mounts such a component inside a panel's frame.
-og-fit-min on a widget part (button::part(base)) steps the part's label down through the type steps by measured fit, as it does on a label, so a squeezed button keeps its whole word.

`<Particles emitter={e} seed={1} delay={0.2} restart={key} class="size-2 text-gold" />`: an engine particle emitter drawn in the UI. `emitter` is an `og.load.emitter` handle, the same `.ogt` of `type particles` an og.ParticleSystem runs. It sits at the centre of the node's box, 1 unit a CSS px and +y up; a `box` shape is the node's box. It steps on the UI tick, starts when the node first draws (`delay` seconds later) and again when `restart` changes, and draws in painter's order under the node's clip, in the node's ink times the emitter's colour. Reduced motion draws none. Lines that need the scene (fields, collision, light, distortion, trails, meshes, effect materials, sub-emitters) do not draw, and the UI warns naming the first.

A motion value sets its own scale steps (`nudge`, `lift`, `enter`) under what a recipe's pack sets: bouncy lifts and arrives farther (1.1, from 0.7), snappy and calm less, and stepped (pixel) does not scale at all.
ProgressBar takes a `class`, merged after its own, so a caller can set its track's fill (`class="bg-layer-3"`).

Surface layer roles after rune-kit's Kit: `layer-1` to `layer-4` (each a step further from the page, darker in light and lighter in dark), plus `hover`, `pressed`, `knob-on` and `border-muted` in both schemes; elevation shadows for `overlay`, `control` and `input`; and the `disclosure` spring. `glass`, `glass-hi`, `plate-hi`, `raised-lo` and `raised-hi` stay as aliases of the layers.

added.member: Checkbox, Radio, RadioGroup, Switch, Tab, Tabs, Toggle, ToggleGroup, Toolbar, ToolbarSeparator, Slider, NumberInput (ui/controls)
added.summary: The built-in controls ported from NSH base: each owns its presses, keys, states and role for screen readers, and leaves its look to the pack's slots (`Checkbox.indicator`, `Radio.indicator`, `Switch.track` and `Switch.thumb`, `Tab.item` and `Tab.mark`, `Toggle.item`, `ToggleGroup.frame`, `Toolbar.frame`, `Slider.track`, `Slider.range` and `Slider.thumb`, `NumberInput.frame`, `NumberInput.field` and `NumberInput.step`). Tabs, RadioGroup, ToggleGroup and Toolbar are one Tab stop whose arrows move among their items; a segmented control is a ToggleGroup with one toggle pressed.

rune-kit's variants and sizes: `variant` takes neutral (the default), primary, danger, warning, contrast, outline, ghost, ghost-muted and ghost-faint (`quiet` is ghost-muted), `size` sm, md or lg (each 44 px tall or more; `small` is sm), and `selected` and `busy` states (a busy button shows the pack's `Button.spinner`). Every variant and state is the pack's `Button.plate.<variant>` slot; a theme with button art keeps the variants that have no art of their own on their own plate.
`indeterminate`: a bar whose extent is unknown, with no value for screen readers and the pack's `Progress.indeterminate` indicator. Its track is the `Progress.track` slot.
`invalid`: a control whose value fails the game's checks; screen readers say so and `aria-invalid:` classes apply.
`scheme-normal` returns an element to its parent's scheme over a `scheme-dark` or `scheme-light` an earlier class or slot set.

`focusRoving` on a `focusGroup` makes the group one Tab stop, as WAI-ARIA's tab list, radio group and toolbar have it: Tab enters it at its focused member, else its selected, checked or pressed one, else the one it last had, else its first; the arrows move among them all.

added.member: Dialog, Sheet, Popover, Tooltip, ToastStack, Select, Collapsible, Accordion (ui/controls)
added.summary: The built-in overlays and disclosures ported from NSH base, each owning its open state for screen readers, its focus and its keys (`back` closes) and leaving its look to the pack's slots: `Dialog.frame`, `Dialog.title`, `Dialog.body` and `Dialog.actions` over `Modal.scrim`; `Sheet.frame` (sliding up) and `Sheet.grabber`; `Popover.frame` and `Tooltip.frame` following their trigger; `Toast.stack` and `Toast.frame[.success|.danger]`, announced as they arrive; `Select.trigger`, `Select.list` and `Select.option`; `Collapsible.trigger`, `Collapsible.chevron`, `Collapsible.panel` and `Accordion.item`. The game owns every open state and value.

`clamp="edge"` on an element anchored to a UI node (a tooltip, a popover) shifts its drawn box along each axis to stay `clampMargin` px inside the screen, as Floating UI's `shift` does; Popover and Tooltip use it with 8 px, so one on a trigger at the screen's edge is no longer cut.

A node hears `onContextMenu` when the secondary button (a right click) goes down over it, at the pointer, or when Shift+F10 or the Menu key is pressed while the focus is in it, with `value` "key" and at its box's bottom start: the innermost node that listens, as a page's `contextmenu`.

A menu of actions on a trigger, ported from NSH base: `Menu` opens from its trigger (a dropdown on a button), `ContextMenu` from a right click, a finger held, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on its trigger. The popup follows the trigger, stays inside the screen and takes the focus while open (the arrows move among its items, the trigger gets the focus back); choosing an item, a press outside and `back` close it. `MenuItem` reports `onSelect`, and with `checked` (and `radio`) it is a checkable setting or one choice of a group; `danger`, `icon`, `shortcut` and `closeOnSelect` dress and keep it. The pack draws `Menu.frame`, `Menu.item[.danger]`, `Menu.indicator`, `Menu.shortcut`, `Menu.separator` and `Menu.label`. The game owns `open` and every value.
`provide(context, value, fn)` sets a context for what `fn` makes, which `useContext` reads below it, as a component's provider.

A long list that makes only the rows near its view, as NSH's `List` does: give it `each`, a fixed `itemSize` and a row function; thousands of items cost what the visible rows cost, rows are kept by key while in view, and `overscan` adds rows beyond each end.

added.member: Scroll's scroll bar, scrollbar, thumb, pinned (ui elements)
added.summary: Every `Scroll` now draws its own scroll bar over its edge, ported from NSH base's `Scrollbar`: the thumb is as long as the share of the content shown, moves with the scroll, hides while nothing runs over, and dragging it (or pressing the track) scrolls. The pack draws `Scrollbar.track` and `Scrollbar.thumb`; `scrollbar={false}` hides it, and screen readers and the probe see it as a `scrollbar`. A node with `thumb="<name>"` is the thumb of the scroller of that name, for a bar placed by the game, and `pinned` keeps a node in a scroller in place as the content scrolls.

A `Scroll` hears `onScroll` once a frame when its offset moves, and when its viewport or content changes size: `x`, `y` the offset and `value` `"viewportWidth viewportHeight contentWidth contentHeight"`.
Flourish takes `class`, merged after its own: it hugs what it decorates by default, and `w-full` lets a full-width target (a tile's art well, a card's foot) fill its place.

Shop takes `purchases`, keyed rows of { id, offer } for the purchases the game completed: a new row throws Flourish's coins from that offer's art and pops it, with the pack's purchase sound (drop a row once it has played).

The built-ins draw Flourish where the game already says so: Celebration's levelUp adds the level-up light (a column, a wash, rays and rising stars) round its new level and sounds levelup once; Reveal's revealed rewards each burst in with a reveal of their rarity; DailyRewards' Claim foot pulses with the highlight's aura, sheen and stars while today can be claimed. Reduced motion draws none of the particles.

The built-in screens enter and leave: every full-screen built-in takes Screen.frame before its caller class, and Confirm pops in by Modal.frame. The built-ins' own active:scale-96/97 are gone, so the pack's Press.feedback squashes them all alike (touch-controls' pad keeps its own).

Every enabled control a finger presses (a press or tap handler, or an action's touchButton) squashes under the press and springs back, by the pack's new Press.feedback slot: scale-96, in over 50 ms, back on a spring from motion.css's press row. Colours keep their own transition. A control whose classes move it under active: keeps its own; disabled controls and full-screen press catchers stay still.
onTab(e, key) reports a tab pressed (global, friends or league); before, the tabs took only the tabNext/tabPrev actions and a finger could not switch them.
onTool(e, key) reports a tool pressed (select, move, rotate, scale) and onPanel(e, key) a phone panel tab (hierarchy, inspector, catalogue); before, neither took a press.
A TSX element's frame entry says how it moves: press (a press squashes it), presence (enter and/or exit: it has starting: and exit: records) and modal.

Two new pack slots: Screen.frame (a screen fades in from 1.04x and out to 0.98x on motion.css's enter and exit rows) and Modal.frame (a dialog pops in from 0.9x on the emphasis spring). A game's own screen or dialog takes them with packClass("Screen", "frame") or packClass("Modal", "frame").

A new pack slot, Modal.scrim: the scrim behind a dialog, which dims the screen and fades in and out on motion.css's enter and exit rows apart from the dialog's pop. Confirm draws it behind its panel; a game's own dialog takes it with packClass("Modal", "scrim") on a sibling before the panel.

transition-count on a Text rolls the one number in it to a new value on the Text's duration-* and ease-*, written as it was (its separators and decimals); the text a probe or a screen reader reads is the new one at once. A number whose words or unit change jumps, and so does every number under reduced motion. The pack slot Count.roll (400 ms ease-out in the default pack) carries the timing; Currency, the shop's wallet, idle resources, the rhythm score and the results' values roll.

stagger-<step>/<cap> (ms) on a parent makes the children put on screen together enter one after another, step apart and never spread past cap, through their starting: transition or their animate-*; a new animate-rise brings a row in from 12 px below. The pack slots List.cascade (stagger-40/400 in the default pack, from motion.css's cascade row), List.item (animate-rise) and Reward.pop (animate-pop) carry the timing, and the built-in quest, achievement, news, daily-reward, leaderboard, loot, shop, results and card-reward lists use them.

A control drawn disabled that becomes enabled plays the pack's new Attention.cue slot once (animate-nudge in the default pack: a swell to 1.08x and back over 420 ms), over its own motion; reduced motion skips the swell. animate-nudge is a new keyframe class.

New pack slots Bar.fill (a fill easing to a new value, 240 ms ease-out) and Bar.trail (what was just lost draining after the fill, 350 ms after a 450 ms hold), from motion.css's bar and trail rows. HudBar's fill now eases (it jumped), and BossBar, ProgressBar, StatBar, Meter and Progress take them; the ghosts keep their colours (BossBar's stays light).

glide-<name> on an element with transition-layout makes it slide, when put on screen, from where the nearest element of that name was drawn (the one it replaces, shown or removed in the last half second), as Framer Motion's layoutId does. The new pack slot Tab.indicator (a spring of damping 0.8 and 300 ms response from motion.css's glide row) carries it; the built-in tabs and segmented choices (Shop, Settings, Results, Backpack, Collection, the RPG menu bar, idle purchase amounts) draw one gliding indicator under the selected one in place of their static underlines.

Every control a keyboard or pad focuses shows a focus ring, the pack's `Focus.ring` slot (default `outline-2 outline-focus -outline-offset-2`, drawn inside the control so no edge cuts it), as a browser's :focus-visible outline does; a press shows none. A component whose classes read `focus-visible:` or set an outline keeps its own look. A pack or the game's own pack restyles the ring through the slot.
animate-breathe: a 1.05x swell and back every 1.2 s, looping, for a call to action waiting on a tap. Reduced motion holds it still.

Tailwind's safe alignment classes: justify-center-safe, justify-end-safe, items-center-safe, items-end-safe, self-center-safe, self-end-safe, content-center-safe and content-end-safe (and `safe` / `unsafe` before an alignment keyword in a style). Content that fits is centred or at the end; content that overflows starts at the start, so a page that centres when short no longer pushes its top above a scroll's when long.

The RPG action HUD's blocks, usable by name in a game's own plate: an octagon portrait, one leaning bar (health with its ghost, mana, stamina in cells, experience; low turns it to danger) and one skill slot (cooldown sweep, charges, count, reason, ultimate ring, key cap). A block's size is a token set on the place it is given: --rpg-portrait-size, --rpg-bar-size, --rpg-skill-slot-size.

RpgBar can stand its figure (value / max) upright over the bar (showValue). A plate can set the fill tokens of the bar's kind (--hud-life-fill, --hud-mana-fill and their glows) on the place it gives the bar, as RpgParty does for the page's health and mana colours.

TSX classes that name the scheme an element's art is drawn in, as Tailwind's color-scheme utilities: the element and everything inside it resolve their theme roles (`text-fg`, `bg-surface`, a pack's images) in that scheme whatever the page's is, so dark art keeps light ink on a light page. A nearer `scheme-*` inside wins; they take no variant.

A slider now plays the pack's `step` sound each time its value changes, and a `transition-count` number plays `tick` as it rolls (at most every 50 ms; restyle it under `Count.roll`). Neither plays on the first value, and reduced motion lands a roll silently.

`sound="reward"` on any node: the pack event it sounds when it first paints, once. `open`, `close`, `error` and `reward` are the events no input fires. The sound is the node's pack slot's (the slot `packClass` names in its class), else the pack's own; a pack without one is silent. A keyed row sounds once per key.

Five new pack sound events, with clips in the default set and all seven theme sound sets: `tick` (a count rolling up), `step` (a slider notch), `swipe` (a page or card turned), `notify` and `unlock`. Play them with `sound="unlock"` like the other events. A pack without them falls back: tick, step and swipe to `select`, notify to `open`, unlock to `reward`.
