A `spotlight` element carries `data-lit` while the element it names is showing, and loses it while that element is missing or hidden, so its classes and its group's read it in the same frame: `data-lit:bg-scrim` shades only around a target that shows, and a fallback card with `group-data-lit/<g>:hidden` shows only when there is none.

added.member: TSX element props: name, spotlight, anchor
added.summary: `name` gives an element a name to find it by. `anchor` now also takes a name: the element then stands on that UI element's box (its top left, plus `lift`'s x and y as fractions of the box's size, so `lift={[0, 1, 0]}` sits under it) and follows it every frame. `spotlight="<name>"` makes an element a tutorial's shade: its `bg-*` colour covers the screen outside the named element's box, and it takes every press there, so the lit element keeps its own presses.

The ink on a fill of a status or rarity colour: `success-fg`, `danger-fg`, `warn-fg`, `info-fg`, `epic-fg`, `legendary-fg` and `critical-fg` (`bg-danger text-danger-fg`). The status colours are inks first, dark in the light scheme and light in the dark one, so the ink on one flips with the scheme; each pair holds 4.5:1 in both, for the default seeds and for a pack's. They are in the default pack, in a pack's palette derived from its seeds, and in `@origingame/design`'s tokens.json.

`stick`, the colour of a touch stick's knob on its ring (`bg-stick`): dark on the pale ring in the light scheme, pale on the dark one, and darker still under high contrast. It holds 3:1 against `tile` and `tile-pressed` in both schemes; `knob` stays a slider's and a switch's thumb.

`Switch`/`Match` choose the first case whose `when` holds, made again only when which case holds changes. `packClass(component, slot, variant?)` gives a slot's style-pack classes (an `@Component.slot.variant` token the UI resolves from the active pack, so a pack switch restyles it). `mount` and the event's `world` take the engine's `World`.

An element a TSX component makes takes its look from its `class`: Tailwind v4.1's utilities and variants (`hover:`, `focus-visible:`, `disabled:`, `data-*:`, `dark:`, breakpoints, the size classes `narrow:`, `short:`, `compact:` and `touch:`), resolved against the active style pack's theme over the engine's default pack in the UI's scheme. Colours, radii, type, shadows and eases are the design language's names (`bg-surface`, `text-fg-muted`, `rounded-card`, `shadow-panel`; og-ui-next's CONVENTIONS.md §Theme and packs lists them). A scheme, pack or breakpoint change restyles every element in place.

Classes animate: `transition-*`, `duration-*` and `ease-*` run a change of class on the tick's time; an element inserted into a shown parent enters from its `starting:` classes, and one removed with `exit:` classes stays drawn until its exit settles. The player's reduced-motion setting is honoured.

`break-words` (`wrap-break-word`), `wrap-anywhere` and `break-normal` (`wrap-normal`) set CSS `overflow-wrap` on TSX text: under `break-words` a word wider than its box breaks at the box's edge while the other words wrap whole, and a box sized to its content still keeps its longest word; under `wrap-anywhere` it may shrink to a letter.

Every TSX UI's bundle carries the `chinese-simplified` font pack (Noto Sans SC) and reads it only when a frame first draws a character it covers, so Chinese draws in every style pack with nothing installed and costs a game that never shows it nothing. A project's own `chinese-simplified` pack replaces it.

A `<Text>` is one paragraph: its text runs, the `<Text>` spans nested in it and the `<Icon>` and `<Image>` in it are laid out as one text that wraps, aligns, clamps and ellipsizes together. A span draws in its own size, weight, slant, family, spacing, colour and decoration; an icon or image takes its own px size (an em square without one) as an inline box centred on the text's middle. A span with `onPress` is pressed on its glyphs, on every line it runs over, which makes a link; the probe gives it the box of its first line.

`select-text` makes a text selectable, read only: a drag selects, a second press in a row selects the word and a third the whole text, and Control or Command + C copies it to the clipboard (+ A selects it all). `selection:bg-*` colours the highlight.

`ruby` on a `<Text>` span in a paragraph is its annotation (furigana): `<Text>東京<Text ruby="とうきょう">駅</Text></Text>`. It is drawn at half the span's size, in its ink, centred over the span's first line, and that line grows to hold it.

On a touch screen a `select-text` text is selected the way phones do: a long press selects the word under the finger, and dragging then extends the selection until the finger lifts. A plain drag still scrolls and selects nothing.

`writing-vertical-rl` lays a `<Text>` (or a paragraph) out in columns, CSS's `writing-mode: vertical-rl` with upright glyphs: lines break at the box's height, the first column is on the right, and CJK punctuation takes its vertical forms. Selection and hits follow the columns; `writing-horizontal-tb` turns it back. Inputs stay horizontal; decoration lines and ruby are not drawn in columns yet.

The default theme names the steps the engine's components were writing by hand, so a class reads `text-title` where it wrote `text-[1.714rem]`. Type: `text-2xs` (11 px, the smallest label) and `text-title` (24 px, a menu row or a HUD's leading figure). Tracking: `tracking-label` (0.14em, a HUD label's capitals), `tracking-kicker` (0.18em) and `tracking-tight` (-0.01em). Leading: `leading-loose` (1.6). Shadows: `shadow-glow-sm`, `shadow-glow` and `shadow-glow-lg` (the HUD accent's light, or another role's with a colour class: `shadow-glow shadow-gold`), `shadow-key` (a key cap's foot), and inside a face `inset-shadow-lit`, `inset-shadow-lip`, `inset-shadow-sunk`, `inset-shadow-glow`, `inset-shadow-underline`, `inset-shadow-overline` and `inset-shadow-bar` (the last four coloured the same way: `inset-shadow-bar inset-shadow-danger`). Inks on the HUD's fills: `fever-fg` and `chart-easy-fg` to `chart-master-fg`.
floatingStick centres the move stick at finger-down; lookPad feeds per-tick drag deltas through the same action and multi-pointer path. Custom UI uses floatingStick and touchLook.
Renders `fallback` (or `fallback(error, reset)`) when its subtree throws while rendering; `reset` retries the children.
The pack sound a node plays once when it is removed (`close` on a dialog, sheet, popover or menu).
Also takes an object with `set(node)`.

Game UI can be TSX components (crates/og-ui-next/CONVENTIONS.md §Components): `og build` compiles .tsx/.jsx with NSH's JSX compiler to renderer calls, the primitives View, Text, Image, Icon, Scroll, Input, Show and For come from @origingame/engine/ui, `mount(world, Component, props, { layer })` puts a component on a world's UI, `useStore` reads a store as a signal, `t` and the formatters read the mount's world, and handlers get the world on their event. Signals, memos and effects follow Solid's model.
An unknown Tailwind class in a game's TSX is an error (OG9105) at its line and column, checked against the default style pack and the game's own (assets/styles/game/pack.json).

The engine's components as TSX, imported from @origingame/engine/ui/components: the controls Button, Progress, Meter, Art and Counter; the base set (Avatar, Currency, EmptyState, ErrorState, ItemSlot, ListItem, Pips, Ribbon, SkeletonGroup, Spinner, Steps); and AbilitySlot, AbilityBar and RpgQuestTracker. Props are camelCase values or accessors, actions are callback props that get the event (`onUse={(e, id) => …}`), and states are data-* attributes the classes read.

A game's TSX typechecks: the project template's tsconfig sets `jsx: preserve`, includes src/**/*.tsx and assets/ui/**/*.tsx, and maps @origingame/engine/ui and @origingame/engine/ui/components (og check maps them too when a game has no tsconfig of its own). Fix: an existing game adds the same three entries to its tsconfig.json.

TSX elements drag and drop: `draggable` (the data it carries) makes an element one to pick up with the mouse or a finger, `dropTarget` (an id) one that takes it, with `onDragStart`, `onDragMove` (the target under it), `onDragEnd` (the target, empty when cancelled) and `onDrop` on the target. Keyboards and gamepads do the same: Enter or confirm picks the focused element up, focus moves over the targets, Enter or confirm puts it down, Escape or back puts it back.

The idle set (IdleResources, IdleGenerators, IdlePurchases, IdlePrestige, IdleOffline), the puzzle set (PuzzleGoals, PuzzleBoosters, PuzzleLevelPath, PuzzleSummary) and CardPiles as TSX beside their Svelte sources, same props, states, interaction and accessibility. The Svelte sources stay until the port's deletion head.

The card set (CardCollection, CardDeckList, CardFace, CardHand, CardReward) and the meta set (Achievements, Chat, DailyQuests) as TSX beside their Svelte sources, same props, states, interaction and accessibility. The Svelte sources stay until the port's deletion head.

The meta set (DailyRewards, Friends, Inbox, News, PassTrack, Profile, Reveal, ShopConfirm, Shop) as TSX beside their Svelte sources, same props, states, interaction and accessibility. The Svelte sources stay until the port's deletion head.

The screens Banner, Calendar, Calibration, Card, Confirm, Credits, DataList, FilmChapters, FilmGallery and GameOver as TSX beside their Svelte sources, same props, states, interaction and accessibility. The Svelte sources stay until the port's deletion head.

The screens HudEditor, KeyValues, Leaderboard, Loading, MainMenu, ModeSelect, Notifications, ObjectiveTracker, Pagination and Pause as TSX beside their Svelte sources, same props, states, interaction and accessibility. The Svelte sources stay until the port's deletion head.

The screens CreatorTools, Results, SaveLoad, Settings, Splash, StarRating, Table, Title, Tree and Tutorial as TSX beside their Svelte sources, same props, states, interaction and accessibility. The Svelte sources stay until the port's deletion head.

TSX elements take `focusGroup` ("stop" or "wrap") and `focusMemory`: the arrows, d-pad and stick move among the group's focusable members first, and at its edge leave it or wrap inside it; with `focusMemory`, coming back into the group lands on the member focused last (a toolbar, a tab row, an inventory grid).

TSX elements take `onLongPress` (a finger held still 0.5 s) and `onHold` with `hold={seconds}` (the held press's progress, 0 to 1, in the event's `value` each frame; "0" when let go early), and `autofocus`, which takes focus when the element appears.

A TSX `<Input>` edits: focused, it takes typed text at a drawn caret, Backspace and Delete remove a whole character (an accented letter or emoji as one), the arrows, Home and End move the caret, and `onChange` fires with the field's whole text in `value`. `placeholder` shows dimmed while it is empty; `value` set from outside replaces the text. Before, an Input showed nothing and took no typing.

TSX controls play the style pack's `sounds`: `hover` as the mouse comes over a control, `press` when it is clicked, `confirm` when the confirm action presses it, and `confirm`/`back` when its `onAction` takes them. A component slot's sounds (`"Button.plate": { "press": … }`, the slot `packClass("Button", "plate")` names, its variant before it) come before the pack-wide ones; `confirm` and `back` fall back to `press`. Before, the new core played no pack sounds.

added.member: StrategyAlerts, StrategyClock, StrategyCommands, StrategyGroups, StrategyMinimap, StrategyQueue, StrategyResources, StrategySelection, StrategyTower, StrategyWave
added.summary: The strategy HUD components ship as TSX beside their component documents: same props, states, strings and accessibility, styled with Tailwind classes and the new UI's primitives. The art keeps its size at any text scale; a cooldown's radial sweep and a queue tile's radial wipe stand in as top-down bars until the radial wipe reaches TSX, and art that the game marks unready dims under a veil instead of a filter.

TSX elements take `touchStick`, `touchPad` and `touchButton` naming an input action (and `deadZone` for a stick): the element's box becomes an on-screen stick, d-pad or button that feeds that action as the documents' `<joystick action>`, `<dpad action>` and `<button data-og-touch>` do, so movement and buttons work with no handler. A disabled or hidden one feeds nothing.

One input binding drawn the same everywhere: an action's glyph on the device used last, or a key cap from `keyLabel` (`pad` for a round face button, `pressed`, `disabled`, sizes sm/md/lg). InteractionPrompt, Hint, RpgPrompt, ShooterPrompt, AmmoCounter, LoadingScreen, SplashScreen and CreditsScreen draw their keys with it.

added.member: Badge, Divider, IconButton, TextField, TextArea, RichText
added.summary: New controls: a status tag or count (`Badge.frame.<tone>`, `Badge.dot`), a labelled hairline (`Divider.line`, `Divider.label`), an icon-only button on the Button plates (`IconButton.frame`), labelled text fields with hint, error and count (`Field.label`, `Field.hint`, `Field.error`), and text in toned spans with glossary keywords (`RichText.keyword`, `RichText.gloss`).

A cast or channel bar: icon, name and remaining time (tenths under ten seconds) over a fill that follows `elapsed / duration`, draining for `channel`; `locked` and `interrupted` show through `data-locked` and `data-interrupted`. Dressed by `CastBar.frame`, `CastBar.track`, `CastBar.fill`.
Non-blocking keyed banners at the top centre (achievements, milestones): each enters with the unlock cue and plays its exit while `leaving`; the game owns the queue. Dressed by `BannerQueue.item`.
Lay the gameplay HUD out from the regions a player saved in HudEditorScreen, inside the safe area; save and restore the regions as text, merged over the game's defaults.
`renderRegion` draws the live HUD element inside each region's tile.

A control rebinding screen: keyboard and gamepad columns, category filter, search, conflicts and locked bindings marked; `onRebind` asks the game to capture the next input, `onClear`, `onReset`, `onBack`.
A marker or blip with `pinned` stays on the rim, dimmed, when out of range (MinimapView adds a tick pointing its way); MinimapView markers take `elevation` (`above`, `below`) and draw a chevron.
`leftHanded` mirrors the layout: the stick at the end side, the buttons and look stick at the start side.

`hud-accent-ink`, `foe-ink`, `ally-ink`, `boon-ink`, `fever-ink` and `late-ink`: a HUD colour as an ink (`text-foe-ink`). Each holds 4.5:1 on the scheme's grounds and on `well` in both schemes: the colour itself where it already reads, scaled down in linear light on a pale ground, mixed with white on a dark one. `hud-accent`, `foe`, `ally`, `boon`, `fever` and `late` themselves stay the same in both schemes and are for fills, edges and glows.

Any TSX node takes anchor (an Entity, or a world point [x, y, z]) and lift (a world offset): it leaves its parent's flow and its box's top left sits where the tick's camera sees the point, at its laid-out size, offset and pivoted by translate-* classes. A target off the screen, behind the camera or a dead entity hides it: it paints nothing, takes no press and leaves the accessibility tree and the probe's elements. For nameplates, damage numbers, interaction prompts, waypoints and speech bubbles; no occlusion and no scaling with distance.

The new default for RenderSettings.upscaler and the medium preset: FSR 3.1 while the scene is drawn below render scale 1 (automatic quality's included), TAAU at render scale 1. A game that never set the upscaler now upscales with FSR 3.1 whenever its render scale drops, which keeps thin geometry and moving detail that TAAU lost, for about 1 to 2 ms more GPU time at 1080p and 1440p on an M4 Pro. At render scale 1, and on every native run, the frame is TAAU's as before. Set upscaler taau to keep TAAU at every scale; the low preset does.

Per-skin joint-to-Animation.nodes mapping from og.load.animation, so IK and foot locks can resolve named joints without parsing glTF; their target and lock frame semantics on moving parents are documented.

Read a node's final model-space simulation matrix from the last completed animation tick (rest before the first), including constraints, without creating a socket or advancing animation; snapshot restore is immediately visible. BoneAttachment documents the same pose timing, with MatrixWorld populated only after the first tick.

`math.sqrt(x)`, Math.sqrt under its `math` name (correctly rounded, so already the same bits on every host): OG9001's advice to write Math.sinh, cbrt, hypot and the rest with math.exp, math.log and math.sqrt now names functions that all exist, where `math.sqrt` used to throw.

A playtest states its frame budget (`budget: { frameMs: { p95: 16.6 }, gpuPasses: { main: { p95: 6 } } }`) and fails over it, naming the timing, its value and the ceiling. `run.timings`, `og run --json`'s `timings` and `og test --json`'s playtest event carry each rendered frame's step + render milliseconds and each render pass's GPU milliseconds (p50, p95), null with the reason in `missing` without a renderer or GPU timestamps, never 0; a budget the run could not measure is reported unchecked, never passed. The playtest event echoes the budget it held (`budget`), absent when none was set.

A restart check: `restart: { at }` holds the world after the restart's tick to a fresh start's after its first tick (both ran one tick), structurally: entities paired by name, then in spawn order within their component set, handle fields read through that pairing, the entity allocator and the clock left out, so despawning everything and spawning it again is a restart. A difference, or an extra or missing entity, fails naming the first one by entity path (`run.restart`, the playtest event's `restart`, `og run --restart-at`); every module's state (og.physics bodies, colliders and joints, og.anim layers and foot locks, tweens, paths, emitters...) compares by paired entity, so a respawning physics or animated game passes, and a body left moving names its entity and field; registry handles (grids, navmeshes, flow fields, behaviours) compare by what they name, a module's ticks (a state's start, a cooldown's end) relative to each world's clock, and contact impulses are summed in a canonical order, so a restart that reloads in another order passes.

The Environment.rotation that stands a cooked map's sun at an azimuth around a view direction (0 ahead, pi behind the viewer, negative to its left), with the sun's direction after the turn and its elevation, so a sky is turned by where its sun should be instead of a hand-tuned angle. Render §4 adds it and a recipe for matching an authored LDR sky's exposure (autoExposure meters the models alone; a fixed exposure with toneMapping none at intensity 1 keeps the source's brightness).

The probe's describe lists the joints of an entity with og.Skeleton: DescribedEntity.joints is `[{ name, point, depth, visible }]`, its skin's joints as the last tick posed them, projected through the main camera. A joint is named by its humanoid role when og.anim.humanoid recognises the rig (`hips`, `head`, `leftFoot`, `rightHand` ...), else by its node name. `visible` means on screen, in front of the camera, and hidden by nothing else drawn and no opaque UI. describe's new `joints` param is `all` (the default), `humanoid` or `none`. The field is additive: other entities and secondary views carry none.

og.FramingCamera frames the entity carrying it by beats, the way a shot list or a reference clip states them. Each beat gives a time, the subject's height as a fraction of the frame, where its centre sits (x and y from the top left), and the view's yaw and pitch. og.systems.cameras' new og.framingCamera solves the camera's distance and place from og.Camera's fov and the play surface's aspect, and eases between beats. Its clock (`time`, `speed`, `ticks`) can follow the world or be set by the game. The camera guide's §5 has a recipe.

og.Hang hangs a skeleton from a rope. og.anim places the skeleton entity's og.Transform so the grip joint, as this tick's clips pose it, sits at `point`. The body's +Y runs from the grip towards `anchor` by `lay`, and its front turns towards `facing`. Each of `limbs` (og.IkChain entities) gets its target on the rope at its `reach` from the grip. `weight` blends the hang in and out, and `held` reports it. It runs after root motion and before foot locks and IK chains. The animation guide's §8 has the swing recipe.

The model cook records each model's shape in its own space: its long axis (`forward`) and `up` from a principal-axis fit of its triangles, its `length`, its centre, and its `top` surface at 16 stations along its length. og.load.gltfInfo answers it as GltfInfo.shape (null for og.load.gltfData), and the probe's dump_entity shows it under `render.shape` for an og.Model. The physics guide's §6.1 explains how to stand a character on a moving or turned model: a trimesh collider and a downward og.physics.castRay each tick (og.render.raycast is a render query). It has a recipe. Every model re-cooks once (cooker r33).

A workflow for turning one or several gameplay videos into a playable game, with timestamped design evidence, asset preflight, a shared input route and separate mechanic, frame and performance acceptance.
A `beam` element takes `stretch <param>`: the param multiplies its `to`, so one file draws a laser, a tracer or an arc as long as the instance says (og.Vfx.params) without growing wider.

The pack grows from 9 effects to 89: weapons and projectiles (heavy, automatic and suppressed muzzles, a spent case, tracer, rocket, grenade thread, energy bolt, laser, flame stream), impacts by material with their marks (concrete, earth, timber, glass, water, cloth, an energy shield, a blade's arc, bullet hole, burn, wet and skid marks), explosions (grenade, large, airburst, water, energy, smoke screen, flash charge), vehicles (afterburner, attitude jet, road exhaust, tyre smoke, wheel dust, booster, damage smoke, hull wake, rotor downwash, jump), fire, smoke and water, character states, interaction and destruction, magic, ambience and UI. One-shot effects play a sound of the pack, synthesised by the cook from `type sfx` layers; no recording ships. The pack's README lists each effect's placement, scale and params.

`--stage day` shows an effect on a grey ground under an overcast day instead of the dusk, so what is lit (smoke, dust, debris, a mark on the ground) reads; the default stays the dusk, where what glows reads. An effect of decals alone (a bullet hole, a skid mark) is now measured, on a lit ground from above, so its sheet frames the mark, and a mark flat on the ground is looked down on instead of seen as a line from the side.

An effect that leaves a mark (a `decal`) has its six frames taken over the time it drew anything else and a quarter more, instead of over its whole length: the last frame shows the mark alone and the others what left it, where most of the sheet showed only the mark. The record's `frameSeconds` lists when each frame was taken.

A `mesh` or `glow` element takes `stretch <param>`: its length alone, along its own y after `rotate`, is multiplied by the param every frame. A jet plume lengthens with the thrust a game writes to og.Vfx.params without growing wider; `amount` still scales the element whole.

Two downloadable toy effect packs for the toy-3d look, 72 effects each with the same names, timing and placement: `toy-3d` (satin plastic) and `toy-3d-paper` (cut card with light through it, for the paper variant). Every effect is lit solid matter: puffs, pieces, drops and flame shapes as small lit meshes with rings and point lights, so smoke and dust pop up and shrink away. Install one with `og vfx add toy-3d` and spawn `base/vfx/toy-3d/<name>`; a game changes look by changing the pack name.

A vfx2d recipe takes `supersample` (1 to 8) and `line`: the cook draws it at that many canvas pixels an output pixel, outlines it `line` output pixels wide by exact distance and shrinks it, and with `innerLine` a thinner line where a later layer covers an earlier one, so a flat-colour 2D effect (cartoon, storybook, watercolour) has smooth edges and a round contour, and its sheet is filtered linearly. Particle shapes are drawn as filled outlines there, and a new `heart` shape joins them (in pixel art too). Without it the frames are the Forge's pixel art, as before (`pixel-vfx` §6).

A vfx2d recipe takes `scale` (0.25 to 4, default 1): a half-canvas unit is that times half the shorter side, so a larger `w` and `h` with `scale` below 1 keeps the drawing's pixel size and gives rings, debris and drifting particles a margin instead of a cut at the sprite's edge (`pixel-vfx` §6).

`alpha true` in a `type video` keeps the source's alpha (ProRes 4444, QuickTime Animation, PNG in .mov, VP8 or VP9 WebM with alpha; a source without alpha is refused). A clip's frames hold it; a stream packs the matte below the colour in each AV1, HEVC or H.264 unit, folded back into the texture's alpha by the decoder natively and on the GPU on the web, so keyed footage drawn over a live scene shows the scene where the matte is clear. The cook fills the colour under a clear matte from the visible edge, so a screen's green (or any colour the source keeps there) never fringes the edge through chroma subsampling or filtering. og.VideoInfo.alpha reports it. The flow guide §3.

og.Camera.backgroundTexture draws a texture behind the scene in the background's place, cropped to cover the view, as three.js Scene.background with a texture: a video plate (og.VideoPlayer.texture). It is drawn as given: exposure, the tone curve, bloom, depth of field, motion blur and fog leave it alone, auto exposure meters only the scene, and the frame's grading (LUT, grain, vignette) covers it as it covers the scene. It takes the drawn sky's place only: the scene's sky still lights the scene and is what reflections show. 0: none.

A timeline's own video track takes `layer under`: its footage plays behind the scene as og.Camera.backgroundTexture while the timeline plays (and is cleared after), so a live scene is drawn over it. The default, `layer over`, leaves the picture to the game's UI. og.flow.view's `texture` is 0 for a segment whose footage plays under. The flow guide §3.

Study arbitrary footage using source PTS: streamed timed PNGs and a contact sheet capped at 24 evenly spaced frames (indices in study.json), Oklab palettes per clip and cut segment, scene-change candidates, adjacent-sample FLIP and chronological window mean/median. No window ranking or quality verdict.

On the page, a TSX UI's controls (buttons, links, tabs, options, checkboxes, radios, switches, sliders, text fields) are elements at their boxes over the canvas, transparent, with their role, name and disabled state, so a page's own scan of its controls (an automated player's) finds and taps them. A pointer or wheel on one reaches the game through the canvas as before: hover, press, drag and wheel are unchanged, and a tap is one press.

A page fetches its split engine modules asynchronously (the referenced ones beside the primary, and a prefetch as content is prepared) with Subresource Integrity: each module's SHA-256 from the engine's `modules.json` (a CDN build) or of the copied file (`--modules local`), so the browser refuses other bytes. A module loaded synchronously by a call that arrived first, and a lanes pool Worker's own fetch, are not checked.

A built web page's probe answers `__runtime_probe__.perf("start" | "stop" | "report", budgets)`, the engine Worker's performance record (`og run --perf`'s lines; `report` answers `{ json, text }` with each line flagged against `budgets` in ms). Guide perf.

`bundles`, `bundles_recorded` and `bundles_direct` count the pass parts drawn from a render bundle, those whose bundle was recorded this frame, and those drawn call by call because their draws changed.

On the web, the performance record (`perf report`, the shell's `perf()`) names the WebGPU adapter its times were measured on: `json.adapter` and its text's first line, `vendor/architecture` with ` (software)` on a CPU rasterizer (the fallback adapter, SwiftShader, llvmpipe, lavapipe), so a time measured on CPU WebGPU is never read as a GPU's. The web trace's `otherData.adapter` names it too.
Its summary line, `--json` line, report.md and device.json name the adapter the frames were timed on (`chrome: webgpu on google/swiftshader (software), first frame …`).

A 2D game can hold the 3D world: terrain, scattered copies and grass, planar water, 3D fluids and volumetric fog draw in a 2D project's published build, loaded as the `world3d` module on first use. `og build --publish` and `og run --device` no longer refuse a 2D project whose scenes hold them, and og.terrain and heightfield colliders no longer answer a refusal there. RenderCapabilities.world3d is always true.

fixed.summary: A page served with a strict Content-Security-Policy (`style-src 'self'`, no `'unsafe-inline'`, as a platform's page is) no longer refuses the accessibility mirror's style: it added an inline `<style>` element, so the browser logged a `style-src-elem` violation and drew the mirrored sliders' native thumbs and tracks over the canvas. Its rules are now a constructed stylesheet the document adopts.

A strip that sizes to its content (in a centred row, such as a hotbar along the bottom) is as wide as its slots again, each --ability-bar-slot-size, instead of their minimum: its last slot no longer breaks onto a second line when the row has room.
Lists module `value`, `const`, and `column` members (e.g. `og api show systems`) and stops top-level module/guide overviews before section headings instead of dumping entire guide pages.
Indexes guide section heading titles in BM25F and omits type-only and non-component re-exports from `components.md` while resolving aliased components such as `DropdownMenu`.

Routes `dump` RPC calls through `dump_named` so all registered subsystem dumps (`physics`, `render`, `audio`, `ai`, `nav`, `flow`, `story`, `motion`, `stream`, `platform`, `pulse`, `lanes`, `room`, `memory`, `determinism`, `inspector`), `ui:layers`, and `ui:motion` work over protocol 5; adds `invariant` refusal in publish builds and aligns `probe.ogt` with wire fields (`SystemDump.totalMs`/`runs`, `EntityDump.render`, `UiDump.style`).

GTAO reads its far taps from a MIP chain of the view depth (XeGTAO's depth prefilter, a new `depth-mips` compute pass before `ao` where the device has compute) instead of the full-resolution depth: the same occlusion at less GPU time per frame, most at high resolutions and large aoRadius. og.render's gpuPasses and `og run --trace` list the new pass.

A section of the components guide no longer takes first place over the function that answers a query merely because its long description shares the query's words: `og api find "enemy blinks white when hit"` gives og.tween.flash first, not the Crosshair's section. An entry's aliases now count towards what it is asked for, a guide section is matched by its title and its prose rather than its number and its props table, and tables (props, parameters) no longer pull an entry towards every query. og.tween.flash's description now says what it is for (a hit's or damage's blink). A component that does what is asked is still found.

A long team name in the versus reveal breaks only between words and steps its type down until it fits three lines, instead of breaking mid-word (INVITATION / AL) and running to five lines in a wide face.
Assertions in start are recorded on the first engine boot, rather than only after an earlier engine has initialized the build type.

A large scene no longer loses its GPU device before its first frame on a desktop GPU with a cold shader cache: `auto` makes pipelines asynchronously on every GPU but Apple's, compute pipelines included, and every pipeline a frame makes is asked for asynchronously. Before the first frame a dispatch still compiling skips the rest of that frame, and grass, GPU-placed scatter, the environment and live sky bakes, the clouds' noise and shadow bakes, the cached shadow layers and the compute before the frame's passes (the wind field, the terrain's corner cache, GPU instance, meshlet and scatter culling) wait for their pipelines instead of drawing from unfilled buffers or compiling synchronously; meanwhile instances are culled on the CPU.

Recreating native renderers no longer retains their buffers, textures and devices until GPU memory is exhausted. Pending uploads now keep their resources only until the submission finishes, and abandoned uploads are released when their queue is dropped. This also fixes the atmosphere test sequence exhausting an L4 in one process.

Spatial audio now hears from the camera when a world sets no og.AudioListener entity (Godot's rule: the view is the ear), its pose og.Camera's, its movement the ear's Doppler velocity; the origin looking down -Z is left for worlds with no camera. A world that puts an og.AudioListener entity on its camera rig hears unchanged.

Draw rigid animated parts with their posed node frames instead of their rest placement, including between-tick interpolation. Preserve per-node mesh-instance offsets separately, without inverting rest frames.

Automatic quality no longer lowers the render scale and the graphics preset when doing so makes frames no faster. Each run of steps down is measured against the rung it began from; when it saves less than half of what its pixels (or the preset step) predict, the frame is not bound by them, so automatic quality returns to that rung and steps down no further until the settings or the frame cap change or the frame's cost there moves by half. Without GPU time (WebGPU without timestamp queries, every publish build) a run is judged once its predicted saving reaches the frame cap's interval. A game whose ~100 ms frames on Chrome were bound by something other than pixels went from render scale 1 to 0.5 and a preset step, ending slower than at 0.8; it now stays at 0.8. The budget and the step-down and step-up thresholds are unchanged, and the tick is untouched.

The bake reads the lights the renderer draws: a point or spot light's radius softens its baked falloff (color * intensity / (d^2 + radius^2)), a spot's cone is clamped as drawn (89 degrees at most), the defaults are the records', and movable lights are no longer baked. Under a running og.DayNight no directional light is baked (the cycle moves it): a day-night scene bakes the sky and its local lights, not its stored noon sun. Scenes bake differently; bake them again.

An enum field of an engine component (og.Collider.shape, og.PointLight.mobility) takes its variant by name in scene text (mobility static), and such components are packed with their record's layout instead of one inferred from the text.

A world.get or world.set refused because the system holds the column in a view now names the entity and the system, and outside a publish build ends with the game's line that made the call: world.get of 'Pos' on entity 'mover-0' is refused: system 'Move' took a column view of 'Pos' ... (at src/move.ts:42).

A development build (without --publish) measures its size table and downloads with brotli -q 5, codec "brotli-5" in og build --json, instead of brotli -q 11: -q 11 over the 61 MB development engine took over five minutes on the first build after the engine changed, so og build --json could outlast a caller's timeout; -q 5 takes about 3 s and reads about 30% larger for the engine module. A --publish build still measures brotli -q 11 (codec "brotli-11"), the numbers the size budget and the release report use; judge download size on a publish build.

A warm `og run`, `og test` or `og ui check` of an unchanged game reuses its native bundle again. Since development bundles carry the inspector's TSX panel, every bundle compiled an engine file the reuse plan did not list, so each run bundled the game again.

fixed: The physical projection guide recipe now checks lens shift from a system after the camera tick, so its assertion is recorded by og test.

fixed.summary: A cloud deck seen from above no longer shows its fine noise as a grid of equal bumps. The detail volume was read once, a tile every thirty-second of Clouds.scale along the world's axes, so every tile drew the same billows in rows out to the horizon; it is now read on two lattices of different tile size and turn that share no period short of the cloud field's own, so the billows are of two sizes and repeat only where the field does. Clouds.detail, scale and every other setting mean what they did; the cloud pass takes one more volume sample where it reads detail (about a tenth more GPU time for the pass on an NVIDIA L4).
The cloud march uses five fine samples per stride instead of six, reducing density and lighting evaluations without changing authored cloud settings, field shape or lighting.
Above a cumulus base, land fog no longer erases the cloud sea below the horizon; ground views retain their land fog.
Cloud bases can be below world y 0 and share PhysicalSky.altitude as the origin's sea-level height, so flying games need not move gameplay to high world coordinates.

A cloud layer whose base is below world y 0 without og.PhysicalSky's altitude to put the sea level under it (a cloud sea under og.Sky) is drawn from any height above it. The march from above the base stopped at the sea level's sphere, which lies over such a deck: an eye above y 0 looking down saw no clouds at all, only the sky's ground colour, and an eye at y 0 exactly saw the deck with rings of dark dots about the point straight below. The layer's own base ends that march now; a layer over the sea level draws as it did.

The clouds' billows no longer lean along the wind as they rise. The lean went by each cloud's own height, so low clouds were sheared three to ten times as steeply as tall ones: their billows were drawn out into brushed streaks, and the edge of a gap in a deck read as a row of teeth. The noise that shapes a cloud is now read the same at every height, and billows are round. The wind still moves the clouds and streaks the high layer. Every cloud's shape moves a little; nothing needs rewriting.

With antialiasing off the clouds no longer keep a fixed fine grain, and a cloud's shaded side no longer shows fine level lines: the march's dither turns every frame the cloud target has a history, whatever the antialiasing, and its starts are spread evenly over the marches a texel is blended from.
The clouds cost less to draw: on an NVIDIA L4 at 1080p their pass takes 0.6 to 1.6 ms where it took 1.0 to 1.8 ms.

Colour-vision filters explicitly decode stored sRGB bytes with the CPU filter's transfer curve instead of using approximate hardware texture decoding. On L4 Chrome, all correction and simulation modes now stay within 1/255 of the CPU result, including tritanopia correction near black. No author changes are required.

fixed.member: og run, og render, og replay record --commands-file
fixed.summary: Command files accept one step per line, blank lines and full-line # comments, as well as semicolon-separated steps. Hashes inside arguments and command escapes are preserved. Inline --commands keeps its existing grammar.

Compile-ahead now requests the full depth-prepass and order-independent transparency variants, including the weighted front and mark passes. A newly enabled lighting feature reuses the warmed full pipeline when no existing specialization covers it, rather than compiling another specialization during play; existing specialized pipelines remain in use.

Model UV conformance rejects atlas pages that cannot contain their chart footprints before running xatlas, and stops retrying once every chart is at its four-texel floor. Highly fragmented models under toy-3d no longer spend minutes repacking impossible pages; the existing source-atlas fallback preserves authored UVs and native texture resolution.

fixed.member: og cook: skinned and morphed models
fixed.summary: A model's #anim blob no longer cooks the model's primitives a second time (with their LOD bakes) for its skin and morph streams: it indexes them by the primitives the model cook made, and its intermediate passes for libraries and mirrors write no streams. The blobs are byte-identical; Night Shift's four #anim outputs take 0.04 s instead of 9.4 s.

fixed: A new engine build cooks again only the assets whose cooker changed: each part of the cook (textures, models, fonts, scenes and so on) has its own revision, and the engine's version is in no cook stamp or cache key. Before, any cooker change or a new release re-encoded every texture and model. Existing projects cook everything once more on this build.
og cook, og run, og build and og test report a long cook's progress on stderr: each stage and output that took 5 s or more, and every 10 s how many outputs are cooked and which one has run longest.

fixed.summary: The assets a game's code loads are read from the modules its bundle holds (the bundler's import graph), not from every TypeScript file under the project: a file the entry never imports (a scratch script, a playtest under tests/) no longer keeps an asset in the publish build, and its computed og.load no longer keeps a whole directory.

Recharting a model's LOD surface no longer takes minutes for a large level: xatlas's chart merge, quadratic in the chart count, now visits only each chart's neighbours and makes the same merges, so the charts and atlases are byte-identical. A 50,000-triangle level's charts take 4.7 s instead of 91 s; level errors and LOD choices are unchanged.

A texture whose border is fully transparent (a UI plate, a nine-slice frame, a sprite) keeps its clear texels clear in every mip level. The encoder's own mip filter spread alpha one or two texels past the art's edge, so a chamfered button drawn small showed a faint dark line beside its cut corner. Recook to take it.

A model's coarser levels of detail are stored once, in their meshlet draw order, instead of twice (simulation order and draw order): nothing simulates them. LOD 0, the mesh physics and og.render.raycast use, keeps its own order and its separate draw stream (og.ModelPrimitive 6). Drawn triangles, clusters and errors are unchanged.

A built-in component imported by its path (`@origingame/engine/ui/components/base/error-state.tsx`, `ui/controls/*`, `ui/screens/*`) bundles its string tables as the barrel import does: its text no longer shows raw keys such as `base.error.title`.

fixed.member: og cook: colour textures and LOD surfaces
fixed.summary: ETC1S encoding (colour textures, LOD surfaces) takes about a third less time on x86-64: the cook's basisu now has its SSE 4.1 kernels, which it picks at run time. The cooked bytes are identical to before and to other hosts'; Night Shift's ETC1S textures take 89 s of cook time instead of 138 s.

A look's `ui "<style>"` cooks again. Since the CSS style readers were removed, a look naming a built-in style (`ui "cartoon"`, as the toy-3d, neon-vector and pixel-3d-hybrid looks do) or a game's own `styles/<slug>` failed with "the look names asset(s) not under assets/: @styles/cartoon": the cook looked for the style's directory as an asset, and a style is now its directory's `pack.json`.

A normal-mapped model's MikkTSpace tangent is stored as its angle across the vertex normal (15 bits and the bitangent sign) in the position's spare fourth u16, instead of 8 more bytes a vertex: a third of a normal-mapped vertex stream, the tangent within 0.03 degrees of the one before (an 8-bit normal map resolves about 0.45) (og.ModelPrimitive 5). Blobs re-cook; shading is unchanged.

A cold cook no longer cooks its models one at a time: planning a model cooks it (its LOD surfaces are outputs of their own), and the plan now cooks every model at once before its ordered pass, which finds them done. The cooked files are byte-identical; Night Shift's cold cook takes 5m11s instead of 9m03s on 8 cores.

A font and a style pack are shared through the cook cache by their own input, as textures and sounds are, and so is the list of assets a pack's CSS names; no cached asset of its own input is keyed by the game's component schemas. Another project, or the same one after a code edit that changes a component, takes them from the cache instead of cooking them again. `og cook --watch --json` reports each cook's stages and its `watching` line the built-in styles' directory.

Planning a model no longer cooks it when the shared cook cache holds its blob: the plan reads the model's LOD surfaces from the cached blob, as it does from the last cook's. A warm cook of a fresh Night Shift checkout takes 3.8 s instead of 26 s; the cooked files are byte-identical to a cold cook's.

A plant's thinned leaf levels now draw the full mesh's own vertices, each kept leaf enlarged about its anchor by the level's leaf scale, instead of storing enlarged copies. The built-in pine, oak and willow kinds now cook within the default budgets.vertices of 65,536 (pine 95,697 to 63,297, oak 86,045 to 54,020, willow 76,343 to 50,828), and every leafy plant needs about a third less vertex memory. Triangles, levels, their errors and the drawn crowns are unchanged.

Outputs keyed by the project's inputs (model blobs, LOD surfaces, #anim, scenes, documents) now hit the shared cook cache (OG_COOK_CACHE) in a fresh checkout. Their key was never made: it named every input by its path in the project, and the engine's built-in UI manifest is outside it. The key now also covers the files outside the project a cook reads (style packs, built-in documents), so a change to one recooks.

A model blob carries its raycast BVH only when the project's sources, scenes or documents name `raycast` (og.render.raycast), or the model says `model { raycast true }`. Other games no longer download it, about a quarter of a model blob (Night Shift: 6.1 MB). A raycast at a model cooked without one builds it on first use, as `raycast false` already did; `raycast false` still leaves it out.

The cook reads what the game's code reaches from its bundle's import graph (the bundler's metafile), not from the project's source text: a game carries the string tables of exactly the engine components its bundle imports (no longer all of them, nor none for one imported by its path), the default face and the default pack's images when its bundle reaches the TSX UI, and a raycast BVH in its models only when a module the bundle holds reads `raycast` (a word in a comment, a document, a scene or a file the entry never imports no longer counts). og cook, og build and the other cooking commands bundle the code first (from the bundle cache when it is unchanged), so code that does not bundle stops the cook with the bundler's error; og run, og test and og dev type-check, bundle, then cook.

fixed.member: og cook: the shared cook cache
fixed.summary: A texture, sound or font cooked once on a machine is reused by every project there that cooks the same file the same way. Its entry in the shared cache (`~/.cache/origingame/cook-v1`) was keyed by all the cook's options, among them the paths of the game's own code, so no two projects with code ever shared one and each re-encoded every texture. The key is now the file's bytes, the output's type and its stamp. Entries written by older builds are not read.

A large normal, metallic-roughness or other UASTC texture encodes on the cores the rest of the cook leaves idle, with the same bytes as on one thread; before, each texture took one thread, so a cook ended waiting on its largest texture alone (a 2048x2048 normal map: 142 s on one thread of 16). Outputs with the least work cook first. The same cold cook of a model with 1024x1024 maps: 48.9 s to 19.5 s on 16 cores.

A model cooks beside the textures instead of before anything else: planning no longer cooks models to learn their LOD surfaces, which are cooked in a second round (the report's `derived` stage) once the model that charts them has. Models load on all cores, and a material's occlusion and metallic-roughness maps are packed into one texture when that texture cooks, not on every cook that loads the model.

fixed.member: og cook: the project's cook index
fixed.summary: The cook no longer copies every source file into the shared cache directory (a 932 MB project put 932 MB there); `.og/cook-index` keeps each file's hash by its stat. A new texture's or sound's fingerprint for the asset index is taken on all cores.

fixed.member: og cook: stale models and Rive images
fixed.summary: A model cooked while the game's code never raycast is cooked again, with its raycast structure, once the code begins to (`mesh.raycast` was in no cook stamp, so the model stayed as cooked). A Rive file's embedded images are cooked again when the texture settings change (`cook { color_textures }`), which their stamps did not hold.

fixed.member: og cook: colour textures and video posters
fixed.summary: ETC1S's SSE colour-distance kernels now agree with the scalar encoder for saturated colours instead of producing negative errors and aborting debug cooks. SSE acceleration stays enabled. Texture cache keys change so previously encoded results are rebuilt.

A game with a UI fails its cook, naming the image and the styles directory, when that directory lacks one of the default pack's shapes (an engine's styles/ older than og, or an OG_STYLES_DIR without shared/shapes/). Before, it cooked without them and every `nine-disc`, `nine-ring`, `nine-tile` and `nine-*-cut` drew nothing at run time, warning only there. Fix: point OG_STYLES_DIR at the engine's own styles, or reinstall the engine package.

A look's `ui "<name>"` finds a built-in style that has a pack.json and no CSS file. The built-in styles were listed by their `.css` files, so a pack written only as pack.json was reported as not a built-in style.

fixed.member: og cook: normal and linear textures
fixed.summary: UASTC textures (normal maps, metallic-roughness, occlusion, masks, and colour under `cook { color_textures uastc }`) encode at level 1 without rate-distortion optimisation instead of level 3 with RDO 1.0: about 14 times faster to cook (a 2048² normal map 8.9 s instead of 129 s on one thread) at equal or higher PSNR and about 10 % more bytes. Every UASTC texture cooks again once.

A style pack's art keeps its size under a pixel look again. Since the CSS style readers were removed, the images a `pack.json` names (its nine-slice panels, buttons, dividers, icons) were resampled to the look's sprite sizes like sprites: a 528x32 divider became 8x1 and lost every texel, and the cook failed with "<image>#palette: the palette holds no colours" (the `pixel` theme's divider and slot rim). They now take the look's palette and alpha only, as a layout the cook cannot move.

fixed: Title, pause, settings and save/load screens take their initial focus, so keyboard/gamepad confirm and back work immediately when they open. Main menu and save/load content respect device safe areas. The empty slider track uses the opaque track token rather than a low-contrast translucent fill.

fixed.summary: An interactive film (create block `form "film"`) has no genre: readAudioChoices reads its music and mood alone, and audioBrief without a genre briefs a film's scores (scene, tension, a choice stinger) and choice-window sounds, its `genre` reading `film`. `brief audio` in a film project no longer needs --genre.
Resolve the distribution's own CLI for scaffold string tables and pseudo-localization without requiring an og launcher on PATH.
Keep sunset terrain ambient and reflections current with the visible sky instead of retaining daylight across rapid dusk transitions.
Shows the view it names (physics, nav, bounds, …) again: it sent the name quoted as JSON, which matched no view, so every call showed none.
An edited component's styles (its <style>, :host rules) show at once in every mounted document that uses it, directly or through another component, instead of only after the page is opened again.

Dev builds are named dev.<YYYYMMDD>.<n> (the n-th of that UTC day), a number unrelated to the release numbers; their manifest.json and build record name the release they are based on (base) and their exact revision. The og launcher installs, lists and prunes them (a dev build orders after its base release and before the next), latest/ never names one, and og new without --engine takes the latest release. Dev builds of the old x.y.z-dev.n scheme (0.8.1-dev.100) stay installable.

og upgrade moves a release pin onto a dev build only when --to names it, then crosses the dev build's own unreleased changes, and never treats a dev build as newer than a release by its numbers. og doctor and the pin warning compare a dev pin as the release it is based on. og --version of a dev build names its base release.
Linux Chrome initializes its GPU before the device measurement opens the game, avoiding a null WebGPU adapter during startup.
When a tap on the play gate does not start play, the error carries the page's failure card or its first console error instead of only saying the tap did not start play.

A model fading in, an HLOD cross-fade, a model's level cross-fade and a scattered copy crossing to its impostor are cut by one dither (interleaved gradient noise turned with every drawn frame, the clock TAA's jitter turns by) instead of three: a scattered copy's crossfade used its own blue-noise tile and the reveal turned by the scene clock. A capture draws the same pattern whatever was drawn before it.

fixed.member: dump_ui and og ui check (TSX elements)
fixed.summary: An element under a transform, or under a moved ancestor (a scrolling strip such as the compass's tape), is now cut by its ancestors' scrollers and overflow where it is drawn: one moved entirely outside its clipping box is no longer listed, one moved partly outside is `clipped`, and its box is where it shows on screen instead of where it was laid out. Each element inside a clipping ancestor carries `clip`, the screen rectangle (x, y, width, height) it is drawn cut to, so a reader can skip the parts of its `textLines` that are not drawn.

fixed.member: probe dump_ui, og ui check frames (TSX UI elements)
fixed.summary: A shown node whose box is empty of itself, such as a text no face measures or a zero-size view, is listed again where it is laid out. The probe dropped every node with no visible area, meant for one a scroller or overflow clip cuts away entirely; it now drops only that.
Project and string-table readers use the same engine-local CLI as cooking, including install.sh archives and npm platform packages, rather than a different og from PATH.

The existing cloud march now composites over authored LDR, HDR and colour backgrounds as well as procedural skies, using the DirectionalLight and environment SH ambient. Decks below the camera show sunlit tops and distance fading without a horizon cut; authored LDR gaps retain their display colours.

Authored LDR backgrounds keep source detail in a separate cube: nearest power of two to source width / 4, capped at 2048, with box mips for minification and blur. Lighting size and GGX levels no longer reduce background resolution. Recook environments for blob schema 4. Upper-hemisphere sources report null lowerMirrorMean and lowerBlueFraction because they contain no lower hemisphere; wrap and clip still measure the source. The loading guide now shows the full DirectionalLight aim with lookAt.

Upper-only skies ease from each column's horizon colour to the ground colour over six degrees below the horizon, removing the hard step while preserving authored ground fill. Existing environment cooks are invalidated automatically.

`og explore` presses the game's own button actions again, not the UI's built-in `ui` map (confirm, back, tabNext, tabPrev, details, rotate) every game has had since that map arrived: those presses diluted the search, and a rare draw went unfound in its budget. Name any of them in `GameDesc.explore.actions` to have them pressed.

Auto exposure meters a frame the same on every GPU. On a GPU with subgroup operations (most desktop cards) the meter still dropped the darkest tenth and the brightest twentieth of the frame and counted black no lower than 2^-10, while the meter of every other host takes the mean log luminance of the whole frame down to 1e-5: the same view was exposed differently from one machine to the next, most where a frame holds large black or very bright areas. The subgroup meter now takes that same mean. A view with auto exposure may come out a little darker or brighter on such a GPU than it did; Camera.exposure compensates as before.

fixed: The film guide's §4 gives a complete recipe for showing a film's choices (it said to write film-choices' stores from the view, which og.ui.push could not take): mount FilmChoices with the view from a scope store read through useStore. `og new --form film` writes it, with assets/ui/film-view.tsx in place of film-view.svelte.

fixed.summary: The chinese-simplified font pack holds GB 2312 whole (6,763 hanzi, both levels) instead of level 1 alone (3,755), so a less common character such as 薇 in a name draws instead of a box. Its glyphs are still drawn from the outlines when first shown; run `og font add chinese-simplified` again to take the new face.

A restore called in a command (a script step, a probe command) now applies before the next tick moves anything, not when that tick ends, so the world no longer loses that tick: a save a command takes and restores at once leaves the world's tick and hash as they were (film guide §8). A restore in a system still applies as its tick ends.

A document's own strings (its `<meta name="strings">`, such as the built-in film-choices screen's English) are no longer checked as a locale's table: the cook stopped reporting the game's `en.ogt` as missing keys it has, and the screen's keys as not in the base table.

Text drawn at a weight or width of a variable face (the default UI face's bold, as the built-in film-choices and subtitles screens draw) now loads the installed font pack for characters the face lacks, as localization §3 says, before any strings table is loaded: Chinese in those screens no longer draws as boxes without a warning.

`og new --genre interactive-film` (or `--form film`, or the prompt's form `film`) makes an interactive film: the create block records `form "film"` and `genre "interactive-film"` instead of action-platformer, and the skeleton adds the picture's film-view screen and a src/main.ts that shows the film with the built-in subtitles and film-choices screens. The start guide points to the film guide.
§8 gives the snapshot round trip inside a choice window as one command whose restore keeps the run on the same ticks, so its hash compares with the uninterrupted run's.

Natively (a desktop window, `og run`), a game's first frame is drawn whole: it waits for the pipelines it draws with, as a capture does, instead of drawing without those still compiling. On a cold driver cache (an NVIDIA GPU's first run) the sky's light was left for a later frame, so the first frames showed a black ground behind the UI for seconds. On the web the engine Worker already draws its first frame again until it is whole.
Restarting a resident native renderer keeps its initialization future on the heap instead of overflowing an ordinary test or host thread's stack.

Scripted frames wait for newly enabled surface weather, including snow and its tracks, instead of drawing an older shader variant while the complete one compiles. Live display frames keep their non-blocking fallback.

A flex item with `aspect-*` and no cross size (an `items-center` row's card) now takes its cross size from its used main size through the ratio, as CSS does, with taller content still growing it; it was its content's size, so a 7:10 card in a row laid out as short as its text. A column sized to its items still takes its width from their widths, not from what their flexed heights give through their ratios (CSS's intrinsic cross size).

A live segment (a scene track and no footage of its own) played on a deck that had played footage before showed that footage's last frame over its scene for the whole segment: the view's picture was the deck's player texture, which a segment without a video track never touches. A segment without footage now has no picture (texture 0), so FlowScreen and FlowPicture show the live scene from its first frame.

A flow paused before it starts (og.flow.pause in GameDesc.start) shows its opening segment's first frame: its deck's timeline is evaluated at time 0, so the deck's og.VideoPlayer gets its video. Before, the deck was loaded but its video stayed 0 and nothing was drawn behind a title screen until the flow played.

Every flow cut calls og.render.snapCamera, so a segment's camera never blends from the last one's; and when one deck's timeline lets go of og.Camera as another takes it in the same tick, the new one takes the camera the old one handed back, whatever order the decks run in.

A spare deck warmed for a segment the flow can no longer cut to (the outcome or choice not taken, or any once the flow ends) is let go on the next tick, its player stopped and the scenes its segment placed no longer prepared, instead of holding them until a later warm needed the deck. The decks' records change, so a flow's world hash differs from 0.9.x before this; nothing else a flow shows or when it cuts does.

A node's `og-flow-title` is translated when a string table has it and otherwise shown as written, without the `og.i18n.t: no table has` warning, so a story written in its own language needs no table for its titles.

Volumetric fog over water now ends at the water's surface. The water, drawn blended, was not in the depth the fog was applied to, so each pixel of a sea, lake or river was fogged out to the sky or the bed behind it, through the water and under it, where height fog thickens without bound: any height fog flattened the sea to the fog's grey (a heightDensity of 0.0002 left a fifth of the waves' light and dark, 0.006 none). The waves now show through it as through the same fog drawn plain.

Fixed missing emitter velocity in `ParticleHistory`-backed ticks (restoring `inheritVelocity`), prevented `time_scale` changes from resurrecting stopped emitters past `stopTick`, added sub-tick emitter motion interpolation and gentle `collision die` parity on CPU, added `Capsule` collider support to `og.particles`, and rebased `particle_history` and `effect_meshes` on render-origin shifts.

fixed.member: og.Vfx determinism, streaming, leaks & bundle release
fixed.summary: Eliminated per-row JSON decoding from FX/collider extraction, made `before_tick` particle-only with live tick rate, separated uninterpolated simulation transforms from blended display transforms, added streamed `TextureArray` residency checks for VFX emitters, reclaimed finished child `AudioSource`/`Flipbook` entities on looping/persistent VFX, and guarded `og.load.release` against live `ParticleEmitter`/`EffectMaterial`/`VfxAsset` references.

Always emit `gravity 0 0 0` on zero-gravity Effekseer emitters, fix ring midpoint color sampling, 3-axis mesh spin, `SingleFCurve` parsing, open circle arc endpoints, line-to-spline emission, advanced material/force-field mappings, static parent folding, `emitter_references` for `shape mesh`, shader `param` bounds checking, `plan_effect`/`plan_vfx` dependency tracking, and `vfx2d` clamping.

Placed and mirrored merges retain authored tangent frames, transforming their direction and handedness with the geometry instead of discarding them. Model cook keeps explicit frames even when the initial material has no normal map, unless import settings explicitly disable tangents.
Evidence captures, motion sequences and effect timings now use each scene's render scale, matching the gfx harness instead of silently rendering half-resolution scenes at full resolution.

Every device with compute and indirect draws culls on the GPU, whatever the scene's size: small scenes no longer switch to the CPU path below 16,384 instances, so a scene that grows past that draws through the same path all along. Only a device without them (the GL tier) culls on the CPU.

fixed: GPU crowds cast shadows again into cached shadow layers that no other moving caster reaches.
WebGL2 and GLES devices (no compute) start again: the HDR mip chain's compute downsample and its storage textures are made only where the device has compute.
Cooked assets are cooked again (cooker r36): the overdraw-ordered LODs, single-channel textures and packed ORM maps reach existing projects.
Pre-skinned characters' tangents no longer go wrong on backends that flush subnormal or NaN floats; compact meshes drawn in the meshlet pool keep their shadows and occluder depth.
TAAU no longer leaves a checker in a moving object's wake under a still camera; FSR's shading-change mask is read at its own pixel, not half a pixel off.
Auto exposure meters the same mean on every host, with compute or without.

Grass shows in planar reflections again; GI probes update at their former rate; the underwater sun scatters as before (anisotropy 0.35); occlusion culling starts from 16,384 instances again; local shadow layers keep their full size on High.
Terrain roughness in the depth prepass matches the lit pass (height blending, wetness); scattered plants out of view keep casting long low-sun and shadow-box shadows.

Visibility-buffer surfaces keep puddles off curved crowns; the stylised (quantize, pixel) chain is undithered; depth of field's foreground blur reaches in-focus pixels without a hard edge; froxel fog keeps its history while the game is paused; screen-space reflections apply only where the surface was the one drawn.
Motion vectors and other half-float packs round to nearest instead of toward zero; the pipeline cache is written after the first frame and at exit, not mid-play.
2D lights' shadows draw on devices that cannot render to Rg32Float (the browser's Compat tier): their pipeline was invalid there and every frame with them failed.
Scenes with transmissive (glass) materials no longer stop on a capability assertion: the transmission copy's levels fill by render passes inside the main pass again, which needs no compute.

fixed.summary: Replaced the 148 B/px VisBuffer attribute buffer with a direct-pull 8 B/px tile-classified VisBuffer (eliminating high-resolution overflow) and wired analytic normal derivatives into specular AA and weathering normal bend.

Fixed FSR 3.1 exposure reset, motion jitter alignment, native sRGB dithering, contact shadow UV alignment, motion blur soft-Z and bent-normal blur, grass shadow depth clipping, and restored opaque Early-Z / Hi-Z by disabling alpha-to-coverage on non-discarding pipelines.

GPU particles keep a stable draw order when compacting live particles across workgroups, so repeated seeded runs and jumping to a tick render the same frame, including additive particles and paired trails.

A GPU pass's time is now its time alone on the GPU. Its beginning to its end included its waits: Metal samples a pass's beginning as its encoder starts, so on an M4 Pro a 90.7 ms frame's small post passes read about 20 ms each, 413 ms in all. gpuPasses and the gpu thread now give each pass's stretches with nothing else in flight; the gpu frame's args give each pass's alone (`passes`) and in-flight (`inFlight`) milliseconds and the frame's `overlapped` and `idle`, which with the alone time sum to its span. In-flight spans are named `<pass> (in flight)` on the `gpu in flight N` threads.

GPU pass times are each pass's own. A pass was timed from the end of the pass before it, so a pass the GPU ran beside a longer one read 0 ms and the longer one took its time (The Last Light's shadow cascades read 0 behind the scatter cull). Each pass now reports when it ran, from its beginning to its end: passes run at once may sum past the frame, whose span is the trace's `gpu frame` and its `args.passes` each pass's own milliseconds. In the trace a pass overlapping another is on a `gpu (overlapping) N` thread, and a pass the GPU could not time is an instant with `args.untimed` saying why (gpuPasses leaves it out) instead of 0 ms.
The grass's blue-noise tile ships baked instead of being made by the first frame that draws grass (116 ms of a web worker's first grass frame). Blades stand where they did.

On a Linux host without a GPU, the headless Chrome it starts keeps its WebGPU device. Chrome composited the canvas with ANGLE on GL while WebGPU ran on SwiftShader's Vulkan, could not share the canvas's swap-chain image between them at the first present, destroyed the device and then refused the page any adapter ("A valid external Instance reference no longer exists"), so every frame after the first drew nothing. It now starts Chrome with ANGLE on Vulkan over SwiftShader (`--use-angle=vulkan --use-vulkan=swiftshader --enable-features=WebGPU,Vulkan`); a host with a GPU keeps `--enable-features=WebGPU`.

On a Linux host with a GPU, the headless Chrome it starts draws its WebGPU canvas. With only `--enable-features=WebGPU`, Chrome on an NVIDIA host (an L4, Chrome 157) offered only SwiftShader adapters and lost the device at the first present, as on a host without a GPU; the switches that reach the NVIDIA adapter left the compositor in software, so the page showed its background while the game drew. Headless Chrome on Linux now always starts with ANGLE on Vulkan over SwiftShader (`--use-angle=vulkan --use-vulkan=swiftshader --enable-features=WebGPU,Vulkan`), so WebGPU and the compositor share one device; headed Chrome on a host with a GPU keeps `--enable-features=WebGPU`.

fixed.member: Desktop packages: frame cap, locale, fullscreen
fixed.summary: A desktop package now keeps og.render.setDisplay's frame cap and battery saver (it drew every vsync), takes the display's interval from its monitor's refresh for automatic quality (it assumed 60 Hz), asks og.i18n for the OS's locale (it passed none), and goes fullscreen or leaves it as the player's setting asks, reporting it back.
The compass, nameplates and other HUD text take a valid text shadow under the cartoon pack, and the compass caret draws as its triangle.

A game authored in another language than English (a Yarn file with `#og-locale:zh`, a base string table of zh) is played in it: the engine's own UI tables no longer make English the game's base or one of its locales, so with no locale requested, or one the game lacks, the game's base language is active; the built-in components (TitleScreen, MainMenu, FlowScreen) speak the active language's translation, and a Yarn line or choice of the base finds its text in every locale instead of warning `no table has` and showing the key.

An impostor card is drawn over the cook's outline of what its frames can show from any view, instead of its bounding sphere's whole square, so the lit, prepass and shadow passes no longer shade the transparent corners only to discard them. First Light's trees' cards cover 64 to 77% of the square they did. Models with `impostor true` are cooked again to carry the outline.

Over the prepass's own depth (single-sampled), the main camera's lit pass no longer searches an impostor card's frames for its surface again: it rebuilds the point the prepass found from its view depth and reads each frame there, and draws the card at its sphere's front without writing depth, so cards hidden behind nearer geometry are rejected before shading. First Light 2560x1440 (M4 Pro): main: scatter 23.0 -> 8.6 ms alone, GPU frame 81.2 -> 72.6 ms; the frame is the same to within 22/255 on the distant woods.

An impostor's card outline is cooked from the same ray-march rules the shader draws by (stated once in og-render-data and written into the shader), and those rules are part of the cooked model's stamp: a change to them cooks every impostor's outline again, so a card can no longer be trimmed by an older rule than the one it is drawn by. Impostors cooked before this version are cooked again once.

An impostor card in a shadow map that reads its atlases at a coarse level (a far cascade's card, a few texels across) samples its frames where its point projects, without their parallax steps, which move the sample by less than that level's texel. First Light 2560x1440 (M4 Pro): cascade.2 7.38 -> 6.86 ms alone; the frame is the same.
maxLength no longer splits a grapheme cluster (an accented letter or an emoji sequence): what does not fit whole is left out, and typing over a selection counts the room the selection frees.
Stream textures now park at 1x1 (4 bytes) when idle and close idle decoders, preventing VRAM/decoder OOM in long-form interactive films with hundreds of segments.

Web video stream/chunk files are evicted from WASM heap after read, backward seeks cancel stale rav1d worker outputs via a generation counter, failed chunk fetches cap retries, and WebCodecs decode failures propagate and fall back to rav1d-wasm.

Streamed video audio now streams directly from ffmpeg into chunked Opus with bounded memory (replacing gigabyte temp WAV + whole-file QOA) and supports two-pass linear EBU R128 loudness, posterSize scaling, and audioLocale dubbing tracks.

Fixed decks:1 self-loops, og-flow-dissolve audio/caption/picture conflicts, multi-option-group choice indexing, paused start events, Tick-1 texture assignment, footage-to-live 1-frame cut gap, and snapshot/restore determinism.

Fixed pointer-events blocking live 3D scenes, added aspect-accurate videoBox hotspot alignment for landscape and 9:16 portrait viewports, lifted subtitles above open choice bars, and added touch swipe/drag QTE input.

The key and button prompts in the built-in components (item card, loot, tooltip card, trade, crafting, backpack, action hints, arena lobby and draft, shooter loadout, racing garage and results, rhythm results and song select) draw only the binding's glyph art, one em square in their label's ink, without a white cap of their own around it, so a keyboard prompt is no longer a cap drawn inside a cap.

The drawn directional light is chosen once, by one key-light stage that the frame, the probe and `og bake lightmaps` all read. og.DayNight's sun and moon are its candidates in place of the og.DirectionalLight it drives, so the shadow settings are always that light's (they came from whichever light was brightest by its stored intensity), the sun and moon hand over by the same curve as two lights do (there were two curves), and another og.DirectionalLight brighter than the cycle at that hour (a lamp at night) is drawn instead of being lost. The probe's `get` answers the light it drives, not the first in entity order, and every og.DirectionalLight gains `keyShare`, its share of the light drawn. The lightmap bake bounces only the light drawn, not every directional light at its stored intensity. Dawn and dusk frames move.
`resolveCreationChoices` honours a custom `catalogue` path (its fourth argument).
Lists built-in theme slugs in invalid `ui "<name>"` look diagnostics instead of printing an empty list.
File-backed hosts without a browser location start their pool Workers from the helper URL instead of failing while reading the page origin.

An LDR sky whose sun is drawn below white (cream, pale yellow) no longer takes a star for its sun. A white region smaller than a disc 1° across is a star, never the sun, and a white region that a compact disc drawn below white outshines four times over is a star beside a sun drawn too dim. Both report the existing "none bright enough … draw the sun as a small white disc" note, naming the dim disc's colour. The cooker version moves to r34, so every sky re-cooks.

On a phone at large text the Global, Friends and League tabs step their type down to fit their thirds, and past the caption step end in an ellipsis inside their own segment, instead of running together as one word.

A baked static model draws again in a frame with one sample a pixel (TAA, FXAA or no antialiasing, the default): its lightmapped surfaces failed the depth test against the depth prepass and left the background showing where the model stands. 4x MSAA frames were unaffected.

fixed: Every release and dev build now draws its own look previews on the GPU host with its own og and addon, and publishes them beside the catalogue and the creation document at <version>/looks/catalogue.json, <version>/previews/ and <version>/creation.json, named in manifest.json's looks and creation sections and signed in SHA256SUMS, so a preview never shows an older engine's frame.

The 12 look previews (knowledge/previews/<slug>.webp) are drawn again by the current engine on the GPU host, so they show today's exposure, sky, fog, grass and lights: minimal-geometric's ground is one flat tone instead of a checkerboard, and inked-comic-3d hatches its shadows.

fixed.summary: A primary ActionButton's label and icon draw in `accent-fg` on its accent disc (17:1 in the default pack's dark scheme). They read `data-primary:` on themselves, but only the disc carries `data-primary`, so they kept `fg`, near-white on the light accent (1.4:1). The ink is now set on the disc and inherited, and the face's sheen follows the disc through `group-data-primary/disc:`, at 30% white so a dark accent (fantasy's red) keeps its white ink above 4.5:1.

A built-in pack's variants that paint their own ground (cartoon, fantasy and scifi's Button.plate, Button.plate.primary, Plate.frame and Chip.frame, and cartoon and scifi's Panel.frame) now set the ink for it, from the pack's new `art-fg` and `art-primary-fg` colours, so a label no longer takes the component's ink chosen for another ground: Loadout's Equipped, Results' Next, Daily quests' Claim and the hand's Play read in every pack. The default pack's Plate.frame is a nearly opaque `bg-glass` with `text-fg`, so a HUD plate's text reads over a bright scene (a notification's title over a light stage). `og check` reports a game pack's variant that paints a fill or untinted art without an ink (OG9107).

A frame with a prepass that draws one sample a pixel (taa, fxaa, smaa or off; not msaa4) now shades each pixel's nearest opaque surface only: the prepass draws into the main pass's depth, which the main pass loads instead of clearing, and opaque surfaces pass at their own depth. Before, surfaces hidden behind others were shaded too wherever a material cut pixels (alpha cut-off, dissolve, fade-in), which kept the GPU from culling them. Night Shift at 2560x1440 on an M4 Pro: the main pass from 184 to 99-110 ms, the GPU frame from 243 to 157-172 ms, with the same image. The prepass now cuts a retro look's affine-textured surfaces with the lit pass's uv, so their AO, SSR and outlines follow the pixels the lit pass keeps.
The round minimap stays a circle inside its bezel under a style pack that bevels its buttons (scifi), instead of being cut into a diamond.

A placed model no longer pops when its level of detail turns, to a coarser mesh or to and from its impostor: the two levels cross-fade over 0.4 s, dithered against each other as a streamed model fades in and an HLOD proxy cross-fades with its models. Every level's pipelines start when the model loads, so a turn waits for none. A posed model, a crowd member and a scattered copy's mesh levels still switch at once.
