A model program (`.shape.json`) that a `type model` variant names now cooks as a model of its own at its own values as well, as the model guide says. Before, the variant consumed it, so a game loading the program itself got "not in the cooked bundle".

Each on-demand engine module (physics, story, nav, motion, destruction, video) carries the read-only data only its functions read, including motion's shader text, instead of every game downloading it in the primary: a game's first download is about 24 KB (brotli) smaller, and a module is that much larger when the game loads it. modules.json lists each module's `data` bytes. Nothing a game calls changes.

A game that uses no optional module no longer downloads physics, story, nav, motion and destruction before its first frame: the split keeps in the primary wasm everything a frame, a canvas attach and a geometry call reach, and a generated geometry reaches physics only when a collider names it.

Clouds under og.PhysicalSky are now lit by the moon at night. They were lit by the sun alone, so once it had set even the undersides facing a bright moon stayed as dark as the sky's ambient left them. The clouds now take their key light the way og.DayNight takes the scene's: whichever of the sun and the moon is brighter at the cloud base, dimmed through the handover where the two are about equal, so the light passes from the setting sun to the moon without a jump. Moonlit cumulus stand pale against the night sky, and a rising moon lights the undersides on its side. Daytime and sunset clouds are unchanged, and the clouds still march one light column.

A stationary object beside a moving one no longer borrows the neighbor's velocity merely because it is nearby. Motion-blur dilation accepts a neighboring surface only when its centered, shutter-scaled sweep covers the pixel and the surface is not behind it. Object and camera motion still blur.

Check JSX classes with the runtime's resolver, including scheme and pack-image utilities, and gate built-in components on known classes. OG9110 warns when a data variant belongs on a known ancestor group; uncertain spreads and component forwarding are left unjudged. Correct Garage aspect ratio, Inspector data states and FlowPicture safe-area placement to supported class contracts.

A flex row sized to its content (a `justify-items-center` grid item, an absolutely placed box) now counts a `grow basis-0` item at its content width, as CSS does, instead of at its zero basis, capped by the room it has: a prompt between two rules is as wide as its text instead of squeezed to its widest word.

TSX text draws characters its font lacks from the fonts the UI falls back to: the style's Chinese companion, the locale's fonts (a Chinese, Japanese or Korean font pack), the game's `fallbackFonts` and the fallback face, as the documents' text did. A character none of them has loads the installed font pack that covers it, and text already on screen is measured and drawn again when `og.i18n.setLocale` or a pack brings new fonts. Before, the new core drew TSX text in the body face alone and left out every character it had no glyph for, so Chinese text showed blank.
A `Text` with `glyph` and no text of its own (`<Text glyph="details" />`) now lays out and draws its binding; before, its key cap drew empty.

`overflow-hidden` and `overflow-clip` now clip a TSX node's content; they styled nothing before. `overflow-x-hidden` and `overflow-y-hidden` set their own axis only, not both. A class that reads the window's exact size (`w-screen`, `h-dvh`, `h-[16vh]`) now resolves again whenever the window is resized; before, only at a breakpoint.

A drag follows the pointer: the node that heard `onPointerDown` hears `onPointerMove` and `onPointerUp` until the release, wherever the pointer or finger goes, as the DOM captures a touch. Before, moves went to whatever was under the pointer, so a drag that left its node lost its moves and its release.
A `glyph` prompt now shows the player's rebinding on the next frame: og.input.rebind, a reset, loaded bindings or an action defined again. Before, it changed only when the device did.

The TSX UI now lays out in og-ui units, as og-ui's documents do: `og.ui.configure({ unitScale })` and the surface's automatic unit (its height over 720 px, 1 to 2) enlarge it. Before, it laid out in the surface's px, so a sheet built for 1280×720 filled a quarter of a 2560×1440 surface. The probe's element boxes and the on-screen controls' zones stay in the surface's px.

Far cumulus under og.PhysicalSky no longer cuts a near-black, brown band out of a night or dusk sky down to the horizon. The air in front of a distant cloud, which replaces the air it hides, was lit by the sun alone, so with the sun set it was near black while the sky behind was lit by og.DayNight's moon and the night's floor. That air is now lit as the sky behind it is, by the sun, the moon and the floor: under a high moon the far clouds fade into the moonlit horizon's blue. Daytime clouds are unchanged. The clouds' own light at night is still the sky's ambient; direct moonlight on them is not drawn yet.

A look's `ui` switch shows in well under a second: the server warms the cook cache with the built-in packs the project does not use, in the background after each cold build, and the page fetches a change's cooked files in one request (`_dev/files`); each change's timings name the files and bytes fetched.

A game that imports the built-in TSX components (`@origingame/engine/ui/screens/*.tsx`, `ui/controls/*.tsx`, as every `og new` shell does) builds in the live dev server again; it failed with `Parse error` once per component while `og build` succeeded.
`--unlit` with named views draws each part its material's own colour with no edges, as og model compare draws it, so a preview shows the colours compare measures. It was ignored with --views.

The game process ends with `og run` however it ends (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGKILL, or its parent dying), so a killed `og run --port P` no longer leaves its probe answering on P: on Linux through the parent-death signal, on Windows through a kill-on-close Job object, and on macOS by the game process noticing it was re-parented.

fixed.member: og session (og run, og test, og ui check on a shared host)
fixed.summary: Commands run on the worktree's shared host again instead of each "running alone". A command's request now carries the environment its script runs with, og's plus what og sets for it (OG_COOK_FORMATS), which is the environment the host was started with.

A command run right after a session went away (its host crashed or retired, its supervisor still letting go of the worktree) waits for that session to release the worktree and starts a new one, instead of failing with "another session owns this worktree"; a batch of sequential runs no longer loses the run after a crash.

An FBX blend shape with in-between shapes now cooks each shape as a morph target of its own (the full shape keeps the channel's name, an in-between is named `<channel>@<percent>`), and the channel's weight and animated DeformPercent are spread over them as Maya does. Before, only the full shape was kept, and a face posed through an in-between was off by millimetres; Maya's in-between test file now lands within 0.05 mm.

og.Path2 and og.Shape arcs and ellipses flatten with the same f64 sine and cosine as the engine's mesh generators (og-core's), so a shape's points are the ones the cook and og model build from the same outline, bit for bit on both hosts. Points move by at most a few units in the last place.

A source clip whose skeleton faces another way than the target (a rig authored facing +X or -Z, say) is now turned by the quarter turn about +Y that best carries its rest joints onto the target's before it is retargeted, so the character no longer walks sideways or backwards. A `type animation` library's cook note says how far a clip was turned.
The walk no longer follows directory symlinks and skips `cooked/`.

A style with both theme.json and pack.json is checked as the cook lays them (the pack over the theme, both over the default pack); a default import of a string table (`import strings from "./x.en.ogt"`) counts as importing it; fixed side or corner radii and `nine-socket` count as visual literals.
Rewires a game's imports written with single quotes as well as double quotes.
A directory of `.css` files is no longer taken for a style pack.

`hello`'s `modules` names the engine's real modules: `destruction`, `motion`, `nav` (with og.ai), `physics`, `story` (with og.film) and `video`, the parts the web loads on a game's first call into one. It was a fixed list (`audio`, `cook`, `physics`, `render`, `ui`) whatever the build carried. Every engine carries every module: the builds that left one out, with calls answering a refusal naming the missing feature, are gone, and none ever shipped.
Synced `og <cmd> --help` with implemented flags across `run`, `test`, `replay`, `probe`, `mcp`, `dev`, `build`, `ui`, and `doctor`, and indexed all remaining guides in `start.md` §5.

Reconnected focused `<Input>` `text` (`TextTarget` in CSS px) and `copy` values in the frame response (`tick.rs`) so the web shell's hidden `<input>`/`<textarea>` activates for mobile keyboards, CJK IME composition, autofill, and clipboard copy/cut/paste.

fixed.member: probe view and turntable camera framing
fixed.summary: Fixed `view` and `turntable` bounds calculation to frame posed/deformed `skinned_instances` and rotated/anchored `sprites` alongside static meshes.

fixed.member: og style check-project skinned model texel density
fixed.summary: Fixed `measure_model` to place triangles through `CookedModel::node_draws` (bind-pose `skin_binds` for skinned meshes and GPU-instancing transforms) instead of raw node world matrices, eliminating the 100x texel-density over-reporting on rigged characters under scaled Armatures.

A pack.json face, image, icon or sound under `@styles/shared/` or `@styles/cjk/` joins the game's bundle. Before, only those a CSS `url()` also named did, so a pack naming any other built-in failed to cook with 'assets are missing'.

A scaled particle system is now the same effect larger: an effect spawned with `scale`, or an emitter under a scaled parent, has its particles' size (and so their trails' width and mesh particles) scaled with it, and in world space its gravity, noise strength and attractors' pull too, on the GPU and CPU paths alike. Before, only the birth shape and speed scaled, so a large explosion threw small sparks fast through unscaled gravity: long thin streaks instead of the same burst, and a small one crowded its sparks. Drag is a rate and is unchanged; noise frequency stays the world's.

The perf report counts the fades held while their pipelines compile (`fades held`, `frames compiling ahead`). A streamed model starts its pipelines when it is decoded, before a cell spawns it, so the frame that first draws it no longer waits for them.
The perf report names each pipeline it lists by its label as well as the engine line that made it (`shadow (renderer/pipelines.rs:625)`), so the late pipelines of one builder are told apart.

Switching og.Physics.profile at run time works in every build, a published one included: each web module carries both rapier3d and rapier2d, so a 3D game can play a 2D minigame (and a 2D game a 3D one) and switch back. Before, a publish build had only its project's profile and refused the other.
Rendered bones interpolate between tick snapshots using position lerp and short-arc quaternion slerp.
World-origin rebases shift root-space hang points and anchors along with physics and ragdoll targets.
Physics hierarchy lookup checks entity generations, ignores null parents, rejects invalid transforms and handles ancestor cycles safely.
Lazy collider geometry resolves on the engine thread before lane-pool synchronization; 2D outlines handle signed zero, duplicate triangles, pinch vertices and collinear chains consistently.
Asset-backed collider shapes are stripped in one serialization pass with checked hole offsets, retaining generated geometry and immediate restored query/hook state.

Bodies created for frame-zero scene queries retain their handles into the first simulation step, rather than leaving duplicate colliding bodies at their initial poses. Physics debug overlays no longer show a ghost chassis after a vehicle moves.

On the web a 3D physics world loads only the physics and physics3d modules: dimension-free code the 2D and 3D simulations share no longer sends a 3D world to fetch physics2d too. A world with no body or collider builds no rapier world (its snapshot carries no physics simulation), so a game without physics never runs rapier and its first download is about 270 KB smaller (brotli); its first body steps and restores as before.

fixed: Two-bone IK uses a relative safe reach interval and solves hinge constraints before root alignment; look-at rear-seam hysteresis is opt-in.
Ragdoll tunables update existing bodies without discarding velocity; rigs and targets are removed when their owner despawns.

fixed.summary: `pipelinesRequested` and `pipelinesReady` now count the same thing on every host: the pipelines the renderer's cache has asked for and how many of them are ready. Before, the web counted the browser's asynchronous requests and native counted compile-worker jobs.

fixed: A display frame now draws without a pipeline that is not ready on every host. Native display frames used to stop and wait for it, as the web's did not. The draw is skipped for that frame, and work that later frames keep (grass, GPU scatter placement, the bakes, the wind field, the terrain's corner cache, GPU culling) waits for a later frame. Scripted, recorded and capture frames wait for every pipeline they meet, on the web too.

fixed.summary: A water surface's planar reflection is drawn only while the surface is in view, as a second one's already was: with RenderOptions.planarReflections 1 (the default) nothing else reads the mirror, so a lake behind the camera no longer costs a second scene pass every frame, and it no longer takes the one mirror from another surface that is in view. In view is now the surface's own bounds against the frustum, not a sphere round them, which held a camera on the shore of a wide lake whichever way it looked. With planarReflections 2 the first surface still mirrors out of view, because material shaders read it (planar_reflection).

A plant's coarser level of detail is grown, not decimated: every leaf and petal drawn as its two-triangle kite through the full blade's corners, beside the whole wood. The simplifier shortened thin stems (a reed's level error was 0.55 m, so scattered grass never left its full mesh) and thinning moved leaf corners a third of a leaf; the kite level errs by millimetres to a few centimetres, adds no vertices, and draws blades in half the triangles. The plant's levels are one level fewer (the mesh and its kites). A glTF's MSFT_lod level meshes are cooked as levels only, no longer also as meshes of their own.

The first frame after the play gate no longer stalls for most of a second. Behind the gate, and once after og.render.compile, the engine builds, lays out and paints the game's UI documents on a copy of the UI, and physics builds its height fields' chunk shapes, without a tick, so that frame reuses their compiled code, shaped text and shapes. The UI's own pipelines (shapes, vectors, layer composites, mass elements) are now among those the gate and og.render.compile make ahead, so a HUD draws on the first played frame instead of seconds into play. The world, the UI, its stores and events are unchanged.
A browser with no usable WebGPU adapter reports the no-adapter reason to the Player and shows its corresponding advice instead of forwarding the renderer's missing-WebGPU text.

Web probe JSON-RPC requests and capture retries use the harness's scripted reference policy while the clock is stopped, so captures settle motion without retaining timing-dependent display history. Live-player captures keep the display's history.

A group's readiness and the hold gate now read one dependency closure per scene, recorded when it decodes: the models it places, the sub-scenes that spawn with it (not nested cells) and the prefabs its entities came from, each resolved from the bundle the spawn reads it from. A cell table named `StreamCell` counts as a cell for readiness as it already did for the gate, a model a parcel scene takes from another bundle is asked after where the spawn loaded it, and the gate no longer fetches the models of a prefab's own entities.
Also false while a tick is held for a cell's files (`dump_stream`'s `hold`).

fixed: `og render`'s frames and the probe's captures settle the same presentation work: textures being prepared, og.motion's results, every wanted terrain tile and every glyph asked for. A native capture now also waits for the textures being prepared, as a recorded frame did, and a recorded frame settles terrain tiles and glyphs, as a capture did.

fixed.summary: While the game plays on a page or a desktop window, `capture`, `capture_views` and `screenshot` show the frame the player sees next: drawn with the frame history (TAA, GI and reflection accumulation, exposure) at the display's render scale and graphics preset, so a TAA ghost or an automatic-quality blur shows in the capture. Where nothing is presented (`og run`, `og test`, `og render`) or a harness steps the frames (a web harness stepping `frame`, `og run --capture-only`) a capture is still a reference, a function of the scene alone at render scale 1, the same on every host. Every host now takes one capture path: the desktop window no longer captures at the automatic-quality scale in a script, and a capture also gets the frame's player graphics preset and loaded probe bakes.

A capture draws every texture in its frame, past the web's per-frame upload budget. A page whose GPU device was lost and made again captured its first frames' 1×1 stand-ins instead: a style pack's art (Button, Chip, Plate and Panel frames, a plain `<Image>`) was missing from the capture while the backdrop drew.

fixed.member: og run --json / og test: probe calls
fixed.summary: A probe call reads the last frame's GPU counts back only when it reports them (state().timings.triangles; dump_render and a timings.triangles check already read their own). Every call used to read them, and natively that read waits for the GPU, so `og run --json` draining assertion events each frame, and with it every playtest, put a GPU sync in every frame: a 1200-tick 1080p run took 18.7 s instead of 12.2 s, and playtest frameMs budgets measured that wait, not the game.

A `noise` layer's mask and jitter now span the whole 0..1. Fbm sat between 0.3 and 0.7 nine times in ten, so noise painted nearly one flat tone. Thresholds on noise layers now cut at the stretched value.

fixed.member: model program surface edges and cavities
fixed.summary: `edges` and `cavities` also find creases sharper than 40° within one surface, so a faceted part (a hex column, an eight-sided tower) wears on its corners. Before, only edges between two surfaces counted.

Rebuilt volumetric cloud 3D Worley/Perlin noise (full-range multi-octave fBM with vertical decorrelation), Nubis anvil/coverage/height-gradient shaping, dual-lobe Henyey-Greenstein + Beer-Powder + sunlit sunset/twilight/night scattering, jittered raymarcher with adaptive step refinement and full transmittance depth blending, and motion-reprojected variance-clamped temporal resolve.

Unified deterministic IEEE-safe Perlin/Simplex/Worley/curl/analytic-derivative noise and GPU noise.wgsl, fixed PCG32 bounded integer bias, fixed Poisson-disk spatial grid bounds, and upgraded WFC to AC-4 constraint propagation with Shannon entropy.

Fixed sky LUT/aurora/lightning determinism and coordinate consistency, ocean FFT Phillips/JONSWAP spectrum symmetry and buoyancy parity, 2D fluid/wind advection stability, terrain/grass/scatter placement parity, SFX PolyBLEP/SVF synthesis quality, and og-shape Voronoi/district/fracture edge cases.

A 2D game's look reads as 2D: `readLook` takes the profile from the create block's form, so `artBrief` asks for a sprite, not a model, for a prop or character of a `--form 2d` game (it passed 3D for every game without a `profile` line, overriding even a 2D-only style).

The art brief and engine host tools read the launcher's JSON Lines install events beside the single checked project object. Install errors retain their code and message; missing or duplicate project objects refuse the command. Native og's direct JSON output follows the same reader.

The 2D publish engine's on-demand modules are split using a 2D profile game, keeping the functions a module-free 2D game runs in its primary wasm. Preparing all publish variants no longer refuses the 2D engine for lacking physics3d.

Automatic quality prices each rung with the upscaler the frame draws there. Under the default `auto` upscaler, scale 1 resolves with TAAU and every lower scale with FSR 3.1, whose resolve costs several times more at the output's size. The ladder used to price a step by its pixels alone, so the first step below scale 1 saved less than predicted, was judged not to help, and the game went back to scale 1 and stayed there over its budget. Each rung's cost now adds its upscaler's fixed cost (measured from the GPU's timings where the device has them), and a rung that costs no less than the one above it is skipped both ways.
The quest name and steps are drawn in the theme's `fg` ink, not its `accent-hover`, so a pack with a coloured accent (fantasy's dark red) keeps them readable on the HUD plate.
A step row without a `tag` field draws no tag, as one with an empty tag; it used to draw an empty tag box after the step's text.

A desktop pad keeps its slot while connected: unplugging pad 0 no longer renumbers pad 1 as 0. Desktop and web pads are mapped once, by og-input, so a d-pad press on the web moves focus one step, not two.

A patch may now carry breaking changes, so a pin is compatible only when no version after it up to the installed engine has breaking entries in the engine's changelog.json (same minor, not older, as before). og doctor (its pin line and --json pin.compatible) and the pin warning of og run, test and build name the breaking versions crossed and point to og upgrade.

A scene with several directional lights draws the brightest (intensity times the colour's luminance), not the first found: a dawn sun rising while the moon, spawned first, fades to 0 now lights the scene instead of leaving it dark. Its cascades, the sky's sun, the clouds and the weather follow it; two within 1.5x of each other hand over, the drawn light turning from one to the other, so neither the light nor the shadows jump. A development build warns, naming them, when another shines with a quarter of the drawn one's light or more, as one directional light is drawn.

fixed: At the compatibility tier (`RenderTier.compat`), no vertex stage reads storage and no fragment stage reads more than four storage buffers or textures, so WebGPU's compatibility mode accepts every pipeline outside the meshlet path. The UI overlay and paint pass, the skinning palette, morph targets and baked clips, the terrain's corners, the grass, the 2D skin, the tile chunks and the strips read their data from textures. The GPU tilemap, strips and 2D skinning now run at that tier instead of falling back to the CPU. The UI paint pass draws its own layer there because views keep their texture's format. Frames look the same.

fixed.summary: Exports the declared pipeline preparation call on the TypeScript runtime for both hosts.

The engine splash shows the first frame's compile as "Preparing graphics 41/96" over the last 35 % of its bar, ready of requested, instead of a bar that sat in its last 8 % or went back while new pipelines were asked for. og:progress carries ready and requested with the present stage.

Retain every audio packet in capture mode, even across thousands of ticks between pumps. The live sink's bounded queue could discard the capture clock's first packet, shortening a headless run's WAV and causing ffmpeg to truncate a parallel render's video despite frames.json listing every frame. Realtime and null sinks remain bounded.

Each part of `og render --jobs N` runs the script from tick 0 without drawing up to its range instead of restoring a leader's world snapshot, so a terrain or other asset the script loaded on a later step is drawn in every part, not only the first (it warned `og.Terrain on entity ... names no loaded terrain`). The parts run at once; a leader process runs only with `--audio`.

fixed.member: og.render (Reverse-Z depth, PBR, GI, post-processing, stylisation and UI)
fixed.summary: Migrated camera depth passes to Reverse-Z (near 1, far 0) for far-field depth precision; preserved baked lightmaps, probe volumes and DDGI indirect bounce when Environment.intensity is 0; upgraded PBR/physical IBL to multi-scattering GGX with Lagarde specular occlusion and specular AA; fixed OIT saturation, FSR RCAS NaN and luma exposure, array-map shadows, TIR blackouts, Light2D compatibility, HDR AgX highlight headroom, silhouette-bleeding half-res particles, winter impostor shadows, skinned outlineGroup, PhysicalMaterial stylisation, form-shadow tinting, pixel/quantize post-AA suspension, 32^3 OKLab palette LUT, hardware-filtered UI effects and static UI mass-table caching.

Rendering continues through a game's snapshot restore instead of mistaking a rewound world tick for quit. Recording frames and local run limits count executed steps independently of snapshot time; scripted commands keep their remaining delays, including in native playtests.

fixed: The renderer's shaders keep WebGPU compatibility mode's rules on every tier, so a compatibility adapter no longer refuses them: flat inter-stage values take either vertex, compute workgroups (og.motion's included) have at most 128 invocations, depth is read as an unfilterable float texture, the screen-space reflections' depth pyramid and FSR's dilated motion are stored as rgba32float, and the sea's foam passes write textures of their own. Frames look the same.

fixed.summary: A published game's page loads only the engine modules it uses. Before, its first frames loaded `motion`, `nav`, `physics` and `world3d` whatever the game held: the probe stepped og.motion without an agent, the tick log asked the AI for warnings in the `nav` module, the play gate's warm-up built a physics view without a collider, and every frame looked for water. The probe GI, the vegetation's wind field and trample map and the crowds' impostor bake are now the on-demand module `render3d`, loaded the first frame that draws one, and the terrain's decoding joins `world3d`. Nothing a game calls changes.
Recreating a native renderer after device loss keeps its initialization future on the heap instead of overflowing an ordinary host thread's stack.

The restart check leaves out og.audio's own counters, which no game can turn back: og.AudioStream's hash, commands and nextVoice, og.AudioMix.rng, og.AudioPlayback.voice, og.AudioEvent's played and last, og.AudioEventVoice.play, and the voice id of og.SoundStarted and og.SoundEnded. Of each event queue it compares only the events the compared tick sent, not those carried from the tick before (a fresh start's music started in GameDesc.start). A game that plays music from start and restarts no longer needs these in `keep`.

A river's fall is drawn as the arc of water leaving its lip, a row every 0.25 m, glassy over the brink and taking air as it falls: streaked white water over the water's own colour, closing up near the foot. It was two flat quads from lip to foot, white from top to bottom under one hard line across the river, and the pool's churn ran up the sheet.
Foam on rivers, streams and contact bands is cut to the pixel's footprint: at a distance its edge is the pattern's average, not stair-stepped blocks of white and water.

Scattered copies cull far faster on the GPU. The cull ran one dispatch of one workgroup per chunk, which Metal runs one after another: The Last Light's 38k flowers and grasses took 8.3 ms a frame at 2560x1440. The chunks' copies now share a pool of pages, and a frame's chunks are culled in one dispatch per page, a workgroup per chunk. What is drawn is unchanged.

A large scatter no longer stops the frame on WebGPU. The GPU cull wrote every visible copy of every chunk into one list, bound whole; past about two million copies the list outgrew the 128 MiB a WebGPU storage binding may be, the device rejected the cull and no frame was drawn. The list now fills pages within the device's binding limit, each chunk wholly in one, so a scatter of any size culls and draws.

Cut-out and alpha-to-coverage copies (leaves, cards, flowers) also take the main camera's equal depth test over the prepass's depth, with a lit stage that discards nothing, so the GPU rejects their hidden fragments before shading them. Single-sampled the prepass already keeps exactly their covered pixels, so the frame is the same. First Light 2560x1440 (M4 Pro): the main pass's scatter 24.9 -> 23.0 ms alone.

The main camera's lit pass draws scattered copies over the prepass's depth with an equal depth test and no depth write (single-sampled, with the prepass), so the GPU rejects hidden fragments before shading them: the same frame at less GPU time where copies overlap densely. A material with alpha to coverage keeps the old test.

A scattered plant whose mesh has cooked foliage (a cooked plant, or a model with its foliage block) is now drawn as the same plant placed as a model is: its leaves grow, turn their autumn colours and drop through og.Season's year, flutter about their stems while their branches and trunk bend in the wind, and its crown darkens inside and passes the sun on through its leaves. Its levels and its impostor cards follow the year too, the cards leaf texel by leaf texel. Before, a scattered tree stayed green all year, swayed as one stiff piece and was lit without its crown.

A model's impostor card now follows the year as its meshes do: its leaves turn and drop in clumps about a leaf's size, so a seasonal tree no longer turns green again when it reaches its impostor level.

Scattered copies, their impostors, model impostors and crowd cards compile their lit and prepass pipelines with only the optional lit features the frame uses, as meshes and terrain do, instead of with every feature: on a cold web driver each took seconds before the first frame. The full pipeline draws once it is compiled; captures draw with it as before. Frames are the same.

A sea's caustics are as bright as a lake's for the same light: they were added at the sun's full light, pi times what a diffuse surface returns of it, so between their lines they took more light from the bed than the sun gave it and the shallows went dark.

A sea's waves are now evaluated once a frame at each point of its clipmap grid, in a compute pass. Before, every vertex of every pass that drew the sea evaluated them itself (the depth prepass, the frame and the reflection probes' faces), and each grid point was shared by up to six vertices. The surface drawn is the same. The Last Light at 2560x1440 on an M4 Pro, render scale 1, comparing the sea on and off: the sea's GPU cost falls from about 64 ms to about 27 ms in Chrome WebGPU (depth prepass +27 ms to +2.4 ms) and from about 28 ms to about 23 ms natively on Metal.

A shared session host no longer drops a command after the directory an earlier command ran in was deleted and recreated, such as a regenerated UI gallery project. The host used to fail with `session disconnected before its result`.

fixed.member: og run / og test: session inputs
fixed.summary: A session's frozen copy of the project leaves out `.amp/`, an agent's workspace (scratch, captures, portals), as it leaves out `.git` and `.og`. An agent's scratch counted as game input and pushed a project past the 512 MiB admission limit, so `og run` failed with "session inputs exceed 512 MiB".

A projectile whose shooter is despawned while it flies (an enemy killed with its bullets in the air) no longer fails the default live-entity invariant: og.Projectile.shooter is a weak reference, which the IDL now marks with `weak true` and the invariant skips.

The verdict's rule shows: the port drew its diamond alone, with no line and no width, under a head that had lost its row (the verdict's column shrank to the title). The head is a row again and the rule a 560 px line fading at both ends with the diamond at its middle. On a phone (compact) the panel hugs its page and buttons and sits centred, not a full-height panel with an empty block under the stats; it still scrolls from the verdict on a short phone.

og.destruction.damage, explode, fracture and info work when a game system calls them, as their docs say: they refused with "not available while a system runs" because they read the world outside the system's views. They now read it as world.has, world.alive and world.get do; naming a chunk needs read access to og.Chunk, and info needs og.Model.

A <For> without `key` keys an object item by its `id` (else the item itself, as before), so a keyed collection a view model makes afresh on every change keeps its rows, their entrances and their state. About seventy built-in lists over { id } items passed no key and made every row again on each update: StarRating's lit stars replayed their pop and never showed on a results screen, and Results' counted stats restarted.
The verdict's rule under the title is a bare line: its small diamond sat on the rule's middle under a left-aligned title, off the grade's stars, and read as a stray mark on a phone.

Every built-in full-screen screen (title, main menu, mode select, splash, loading, pause, settings, HUD editor, save and load, results, game over, leaderboard, calibration, credits, creator tools, the film's chapter, chart and gallery screens) fills the layer it is mounted in, also inside a game's own column, instead of shrinking to its content (a title drawn as a 133 px band, results cut to its buttons). Each takes a `class`, applied after its own, for the game's placement.

The ghost behind a boss's health (the health just lost, draining after the fill) is a light colour of its own: it was gold behind a legendary fill, the same yellow in the scifi pack, so a loss never showed; and it rests at the fill and lags it on a loss (it rested at width 0 and grew from nothing under the fill, after its delay). Without `ghost`, the bar shows each loss by itself.

The restart check no longer compares the queue of an event the input path delivered (og.input.intent, a replayed intent): og-input's sink marks each intent's event type as input, and its queue is left out as og.KeyDown's is. A game whose fresh start came from two intents (pick a stage, launch) and whose restart from one (Again) failed on `event queue <Type> holds 1, a fresh start's 2`; what the intents did to the world is still compared.

A text shadow draws every layer of its list, as CSS's text-shadow does: up to eight, painted last first under the fill, each with its own offset, blur and colour, each transitioning as a box shadow's layer does. Before, a TSX text kept only the widest layer. This changes what the theme classes with several layers mean: Tailwind's text-shadow-sm, -md and -lg now draw all their layers. A layer in currentColor (or with no colour) or contrast-color(currentColor) takes the ink of each text it reaches, as CSS inherits the keyword, so a halo written once on a HUD's root rings every text in its own contrast.

Their halo over the scene is text-shadow-tag (the style's --tag-halo) instead of text-shadow-2xs: the 81 texts that wrote text-shadow-2xs, which is Tailwind's 1 px drop at 15 % black and read about 1.1:1 over a white sky, now draw the eight-copy ring in contrast-color() of their ink, in TSX as the CSS path draws var(--tag-halo). OrbMeter's caption, which sits under the orb on the scene, takes the halo too instead of text-shadow-xs's soft drop. text-shadow-2xs itself is unchanged; a game that wrote it for a halo should write text-shadow-tag.

A look that draws its lines outside the silhouettes (`outlinePlace outside` or `both`) no longer runs all six full-resolution jump-flood passes every frame whatever its line's width: the flood starts from the widest line the frame can draw (the post outline's, the look's grown to its near cap, and each drawn material's), dropping its steps in pairs. anime-cel-3d's 2.5 px line runs four jumps instead of six, a 1 px line two, with the same image.
The roads between levels run from disc to disc again (they all stood at the lane's left edge), and a disc's Play, Open or Selected tag sits under it instead of over it.
The Next button draws its arrow, sized as Prev's (it was empty).
An offer's art has its height and a visible icon, and the Featured tag sits on the art at its top left in the accent instead of over the offer's name.

`og.render.compile(world)` now also makes the draw pipelines of every particle emitter and effect material the game has loaded, not only those of systems already alive, with the particle simulation and, for alpha billboards, their order-independent pass. A game that loads its effects at start no longer compiles particle pipelines on the frame its first effect appears (Star Focus: the first kill's 29.5 ms hitch is gone).

`og.render.compile(world)` now also makes the lit, prepass, shadow and order-independent pipelines of every material the game has loaded, on each kind of mesh it can draw, before any instance uses it, and also while nothing is drawn yet (a first model still loading). Previously only the plain opaque material was made ahead, so the first frame that spawned something blended or lean compiled its pipelines (Star Focus: 19.8 ms at its first landing and 17 ms at tick 197, both gone).

A terrain that moves now carries its scattered copies without placing them again: copies are placed about the terrain's position (with its turn and scale) and drawn moved to where it stands, so changing an `og.Terrain`'s position, or the scene's render origin, keeps every placed chunk. Before, any move re-placed every chunk in range each frame (85 chunks a step on the grass test scene). A copy's motion vectors follow the terrain's move. The hashes that pick which copies thin out with distance and each copy's wind phase now read its place about the terrain, so they stay put as it moves; for a terrain at the world's origin the frames are unchanged.

Whole-number fields of model program ops (`seed`, `levels`, `segments`, `octaves`) take parameter expressions: `"$seed + 1"` evaluates in f64, and a whole result is accepted instead of refused as "a whole number".

A model program file under assets/ (`rock.shape.json`) cooks as a model of its own, with levels of detail as a glTF's. It cooked to nothing, without an error: the program is the first file it reads, and the cook dropped every file a model read as part of that model, the program included. A `type model` text naming a program still takes the program in as its part.

The cook's "albedo baked into emission" warning no longer flags painted glow maps. With a base-colour map of the same size beside it, an emissive map is flagged only when it glows on at least half its texels and repeats the base colour there; glowing lines, seams and veins over a surface of another colour are not. Without one, the mean-luminance rule is unchanged.

A model program's painted surface counts the palette it was mixed from (each part's colour, each layer's colour and emission) against the look's `ArtPalette.maxColors`, not every shaded texel of its maps, so a textured prop no longer reports `overColours` by thousands.

The cook's locale check reads only the game's own string tables. Since the engine ships zh-CN tables for its built-in UI, a game whose code mounts a built-in got every one of its keys reported missing from its zh-CN table and every built-in key reported as not in its base table (over a thousand warnings for a complete table). The built-ins' tables are kept in step by the engine's own test.

fixed.member: Bloom over an authored LDR sky (RenderSettings.bloom, Environment.background)
fixed.summary: The glow round a bright shot now shows over an authored LDR sky and untonemapped sprites too. It used to be dropped there, so it showed only on the meshes near the shot and lit up their whole silhouettes.

On Metal (macOS, iOS) the GPU trails pipeline no longer fails validation and aborts the game the first time an effect with a trail or ribbon spawns: the trails shader bitcast a vec3 struct member whole, which Metal refuses for its packed vec3. It now writes the position per component.

A secondary camera is lit by the local lights its own view reaches. Before, it shaded only the lights the main camera kept, so a view looking where the main camera does not (a hangar turntable above the field, a portrait or minimap camera) drew its point, spot and rect lights as if absent. A light only the view sees is unshadowed; one the main camera also keeps keeps its shadow and cookie.

fixed.member: og session (og run, og test, og ui check on a shared host)
fixed.summary: A project past 512 MiB of files (its sources plus its cooked bundle) runs on the shared host again instead of failing with "session inputs exceed 512 MiB". The frozen inputs are clones, which cost no space; only files the filesystem cannot clone count against the 512 MiB copy budget.

fixed.member: og session (og run, og test, og ui check on a shared host)
fixed.summary: A project on another volume than the temp directory (an external or second APFS volume on macOS) is frozen into its own `.og/session-inputs`, where its files clone, instead of being copied across volumes and failing with "session inputs exceed 512 MiB of copies".

An LDR sky's sun is the white region holding the most light, not the last clipped pixel. Every clipped pixel ties at full luminance, so in a space or night sky the extraction took whichever star sat nearest the horizon: four of Star Focus's five AI skies got a deep-red sun under 6° up instead of their disc at 40–52°. Skies whose sun was found before measure the same disc.

The verdict line shows: it was transparent text over a gradient box (the port lost the clip to the glyphs), so Results drew a gold or red bar and no title, as did Game over and the puzzle summary. It is drawn in gold (danger red for a loss). Results' tab row is drawn only for a caller that switches tabs (onTab), as R3's rule for built-in rows, and its labels (Summary, Graphs, Scoreboard) come from the string table, with zh-CN.

A TSX component's strings and formatted numbers follow og.i18n.setLocale: they were read from the host with no dependency on the locale, so every string stayed in the language it was built in. They read the renderer's locale, set at each tick boundary, and redraw in the new language on the next frame.

An attribute written after a spread (`<View {...props} class={merged}>`) wins on every update, not only the first: when a reactive prop of the caller's changed (a `disabled` read from a signal), the spread set every prop again and the caller's bare `class` replaced the merged one, so a Button with a class of the caller's lost min-h-11 and its padding and stood 20 px tall instead of 44. Every built-in component built that way keeps its own class and attributes; an attribute written before a spread still gives way to it.
The load report counts snapshots that overtake an avatar's enter under loss as `early`, apart from decode errors; og.shared drops these early snapshots without a warning.

A game system that reads or writes an og.story record (og.StoryEvent, og.QuestUpdated, og.DialogueShown, og.DialogueEnded, og.DialogueCheck, og.BarkSaid, og.Story) no longer stops the engine at start with `no engine N`: og.story is granted what no story is loaded for yet without its engine.

Prepares missing or stale cooked content before unit suites as well as playtests; --no-check skips types, not incremental preparation. Dev, run and build retain their automatic cook. Asset queries and project diagnostics refresh their reports themselves.

Author help, runtime errors, blob errors and the API reference no longer ask agents to cook by hand. Missing declarations name content IDs and declaration sources; incompatible hosts name the matching-tools fix. Platform/CI/troubleshooting og cook and the post-new .og/cook/look.json contract remain available.

StreamStatus.ready no longer reads true for one tick when a cell loads with its group's pack and textures already in (read ahead of the anchor, or already resident): it stays false from the tick the cell loads until its models' fade-in is over, then true. og.loading.idle is busy through the same tick. The fade of a cell's models now starts in the tick that loads the cell instead of the frame or tick after it. Presentation only: ticks and hashes are the same.

StreamStatus.ready of a distance, volume or requested group also waits for its models' fade-in, as its description says: it read true as soon as the group's textures were prepared, while a model the world already placed was still fading in. Cell groups already waited. Presentation only: ticks and hashes are the same.

With object-space stylise, water surfaces and MSAA together, the water's front depth tests against the scene's real prepass depth. Before, the stylise pass discarded that depth, and the water was tested against zeros or undefined contents.
An SVG texture's `currentColor` now decodes white, as in a cooked vector, so a single-colour SVG is a mask its draw colour tints; before it decoded black. Cooked SVG textures re-cook.

TAA and TAAU reject an occluder's history on newly uncovered camera-reprojected background using the previous frame's depth, including its jitter. Colour clipping alone could retain that foreground colour when it fit the background's colour range. Depth is preserved with presentation checkpoints; history filters, blend weights and mode defaults are unchanged.

TAAU tests newly uncovered background against its own motion and depth before borrowing foreground motion from a neighbouring sample. Borrowed object motion could otherwise disable the background's visibility rejection and retain unrelated history at moving edges. Foreground-motion dilation, history filters, blend weights and mode defaults are unchanged.

TAAU excludes closer occluder taps as well as farther background when resampling camera-reprojected history. A mixed visibility footprint could previously retain the colour of an object that had moved away from thin foreground detail. Reconstruction filters, local depth-slope allowance, blend weights and defaults are unchanged.

TAAU below render scale 1 reprojects thin foreground detail with the closest surface's motion in its sampling neighbourhood, rather than borrowing background history when the nearest jittered scene sample misses that detail. Colour sampling, history filters, mode defaults and blend weights are unchanged.

TAAU excludes farther-surface history taps from camera-reprojected foreground and renormalizes the selected bilinear or Catmull-Rom filter. Previously, interpolation could put background colour back into newly uncovered fence detail after visibility rejection. The filter retains closer sub-pixel foreground coverage and accounts for local depth slope. Object-motion handling, blend weights and mode defaults are unchanged.

TAAU carries moving surfaces' previous depth into history resampling, applying the existing two-sided surface test instead of bypassing it for object motion. History filters, slope bounds, blend weights and defaults are unchanged.

TAAU reseeds newly uncovered surfaces with the current sample whose visibility was tested. Bilinear reconstruction could mix another surface into that seed and leave its colour in later history. First-frame reconstruction, history filters, blend weights and mode defaults are unchanged.
A terrain's heights are checked when its data is set or edited, no longer on every frame that draws it: terrain-grass spent 2.27 ms of each frame's CPU on the check (on the L4 host).

Loading a cooked terrain builds its whole height field and control map about 3× faster in the web build (First Light's 8 km valley, 2049² heights and a two-page 2048² control map: 1.09 s to 0.33 s in wasm), so a large terrain delays the first frame less. The field is byte-identical.

A terrain's holes are cooked once, as one byte per cell, which the renderer, scattering and physics all read; heights no longer carry a hole flag in their lowest bit, so a cell's height is exact. Cooked terrains are a new format (cooker r28): og cook cooks them again.

A terrain layer's normal map (a `kind normal` texture, or a layer of `layerNormals`) is lit correctly on adapters that hold normal maps as two channels (BC5 on desktop GPUs, EAC RG11 on mobile). The terrain shader read the missing z as stored instead of rebuilding it from x and y as materials do, so a layer's normal pointed into the ground and, with antiTiling, every hexagon's slope came out twenty times too steep: black and lit patches over the whole terrain, a honeycomb on snow, and the same patches on a lake's bed seen through shallow og.Water.

A layer normal map whose normals lean one way on average (a scanned map that kept its capture's tilt, such as Poly Haven's snow_02 at 13 degrees) no longer draws lighter and darker hexagons under antiTiling: the map's mean slope, read from its smallest mip, is taken out before each hexagon turns its copy. A map without that lean draws as before; antiTiling 0 keeps showing the texture's own repeat.

Its description no longer promises that a peak keeps its shape at any distance. The error is held only as far as clipmap levels of 128 quads reach (or lodRing's); past that a level's quads are about its distance / (0.37 × ring), so lodRing 256 is the way to draw distant terrain finer. World guide §2 gives the numbers.

A released pack's terrain now stays while a game's own record holds its handle in a TerrainData field, as the docs said; before, only the engine's records (og.Terrain, og.TerrainScatter, og.Grass) kept it, so a game's field could be left naming a freed terrain. A Geometry field holding the terrain's height field (TerrainInfo.geometry) keeps it too, a collider's or a game's: the loading guide now says so.

An input method's commit and the next word's preedit arriving in one frame no longer lose the preedit. A pasted line break becomes a space in a one-line Input (it was dropped, joining the words) and a newline in a multi-line one, Windows' CRLF included. On the web, the input method's candidate window opens at the caret instead of the field's left edge.

Manual soft hyphens and automatic language-dictionary breaks reserve and draw a shaped hyphen only when taken. hyphens-none suppresses discretionary breaks. Inheritance, reflow and probe word-break reporting follow the same layout.

fixed: A UI text whose content changes (a clock, a counter) is measured into a layout og-text keeps between measures, with each face's family and the features' settings made once, instead of a new layout, run list and style strings each time: a measure of a text in a face already seen allocates 3 times inside Parley instead of about 20.

fixed.summary: A TSX text's min-content width is its longest word (a `whitespace-nowrap` text's whole line), as in CSS, instead of its unbroken line. Grid `min-content` and `auto` tracks, `w-min`, `w-fit` and a flex item's automatic minimum width now let a text wrap down to its longest word.

Draw decoration styles and underline offsets, resolve em font sizes against the parent, and honor placeholder, caret and selection colors. Inputs support Shift-arrow/Home/End selections and Control/Command-A, replacing or deleting selections at grapheme boundaries.

World, screen, floating and debug text are laid out by the same Parley layout as the UI (shaping, kerning, bidi and fallback faces) and drawn from the run-time glyph atlas: a character the font lacks is drawn by the UI's fallback faces instead of nothing, a floating text mixing Latin and Chinese is one line, and measureText returns what drawing takes. An outline's width is a fraction of the run-time field's reach, the same for every font.

Paint and hit-test z-* in stacking-context order: z-auto descendants participate in the nearest explicit context, z-0 isolates its children, and negative and equal levels retain their background and document ordering. Layout, clips and transforms stay parent-first.

og.Time keeps the tick and the integer tick rate, and every time is counted from them: `dt` is exactly 1 / rate (0.016666666666666666 at 60 Hz, no longer the f32 0.016666668), `elapsed` is tick / rate, and `scaledDt` and `scaledElapsed` are f64 sums of exact steps. Effects, particles, physics water, AI, music beats, audio events, timelines, video, lightning and the probe now read the declared rate instead of rebuilding it from a rounded `dt` (which gave 59.999996 Hz in some and 60 in others). A save from an older engine restores at the rate it ran at, on its tick.

og.DayNight's `start` and `speed` and og.atmosphere.timeOfDay are f64, so an hour a game writes reads back as written and compares exactly with a JavaScript number: 6.9 no longer reads 6.9000001, which put a game's clock run to dawn a whole day ahead. Saves keep their values, widened.

Called in a system that does not declare og.DayNight among its reads, timeOfDay answered 9 h whatever the clock said, silently. The read is now refused like any undeclared access: it answers NaN and the engine logs once which system to declare og.DayNight in.

Called in a system that does not declare og.Season (or og.DayNight, for the hour's temperature) among its reads, season answered og.Season's defaults as if read, silently. The answer is the same, and the engine now logs once which system to declare it in.

og.video advances a playing player's `time` by `speed / rate` each tick, the one step the tick rate og.Time keeps gives, instead of multiplying a rounded tick length by `speed` (two roundings a tick): the playhead still moves with its sound's, and the step is exact to f64 from the integer rate. The frame a step lands on is unchanged (its 1e-6 slack); over an hour of playback `time` can read a hair earlier than the last engine summed it.

A deck that warms a segment holds it through og.Timeline.preroll instead of writing the deck's og.VideoPlayer itself, so the timeline is the one place a segment's start is prepared. A warming deck's player takes its first frame in og.timeline, one system later in the same tick than before; a save taken while a deck warms restores as before.

Preloading a scene now also loads what it spawns with, without placing it: its models and their textures into the renderer, their pipelines started, its sub-scenes and prefabs. That work moves from the tick of og.scene.change to the preload call. A timeline in pre-roll or playing prepares the scenes its scene tracks name the same way, and a display frame holds the clock while a scene a timeline cuts to is still being read or prepared (the page is told it is buffering, as for og.VideoPlayer.wait). A game that counted on og.scene.preload returning before a scene's models were decoded should call it earlier, such as when the previous level starts.
The d-pad's cross draws as one outline: its arms no longer overlap with seams across the middle.
The stick's ring darkens while a touch holds it; its pressed border had no width, so it showed nothing.

A stick's knob stays inside its ring when pushed to the edge (the ring's radius less the knob's), instead of hanging half over it; the stick's value still reads the finger to the ring's edge. Any node marked `knob` is held inside its touchStick the same way.

The stick's knob is filled with the theme's `knob` role instead of a thinned `fg` (`bg-fg/45`): it is opaque, so the ring's pressed tone no longer shows through it, and it follows a pack's `knob` colour.

The d-pad's dead middle is now the circle in its hub (0.4 of its radius), not the old document pad's 0.23, so a press on the hub reads no direction. A View's `deadZone` sets it on a `touchPad` as on a `touchStick`.
An on-screen control that is disabled or hidden while a finger holds it reads as let go: before, it kept `active:` and its knob's place until it was a control again.

The d-pad is one shape with one outline (`nine-cross` under `nine-cross-rim`) instead of two outlined bars under a cover, so no scale opens a seam in it: pressed (`active:scale-97`), the bars' inner outlines showed as faint lines across its middle. The arm of the way it reads now lights while it is held, two on a diagonal.
On a touch screen the device used last starts as touch, before any input: TitleScreen asks to tap, not to press any button, and glyphs show touch until a key, a pad or a mouse is used.

A traced run with --ticks and no --commands now takes its ticks one frame each, so its trace has the frames and their GPU passes; it advanced them at once and drew none, and `og cost` then reported no GPU timestamps. The gpu frame and pass spans no longer carry `args.submitted`, which was on the engine's clock, not the trace's: select a frame by its `ts`.

Derived f32 inputs now reject finite JSON numbers outside the Rust f32 range before serde can convert them to infinity. Source schemas intersect float bounds with existing domain ranges, including nested and context-expanded schemas; f64 values and schema default/example data remain unchanged.

Integer-key maps emit readonly string-indexed value types instead of failing on Schemars patternProperties. Pattern and additional value types are preserved; key patterns, ranges and overlaps remain runtime-validated. Typed maps can exclude reserved names with false properties, without relaxing the rejection of other named/indexed overlaps.

Content input schemas share an exact, ordered registry and a type-erased check that retains both schema validation and Rust decoding. Reflected schemas can bind an expanded document to the same decoder. Content references have one closed identity token instead of duplicating path and runtime-handle conventions. This is registration infrastructure, not a file-format switch or complete kind coverage.

Generator data is validated against the schema derived from its Rust input before decoding. Invalid values report their JSON Pointer within the result; cross-field height counts and finite-value checks remain terrain validation. This establishes the shared author-schema foundation, not a terrain file-format switch.

DamageNumbers imported the world components' string table from the hud directory, which failed every cook with "assets/@ui: @ui/components/hud/world.en.ogt: No such file or directory". The import is gone: the component reads no strings.
A pack may silence an event with `{ "volume": 0 }` and no `clips`; before, a sound without clips was refused even at volume 0.
A cooling slot's art is darkened once, by the sweep, instead of dimmed under it as well, so the art still reads; a quick item's count stands a step inside the art's well instead of on the slot's rim.

Shared [fontSize, lineHeight] values remain font-size pairs in both schemes. Adaptive values require an explicit object with light and dark fields; a two-number font-size pair is no longer mistaken for two scheme values, which made dark-mode UI text about one pixel tall.

A node anchored to a moving entity (a nameplate, a damage number) stays on it on frames drawn between ticks, where the entity is drawn at its blended place, instead of sitting where the last tick put it, up to a tick ahead.

Their icons draw again: a fighter without a portrait shows its icon, the roster shows each champion's, the lobby each slot's and its ready state. The TSX port passed them as glyph, which names an input binding, instead of name. ArenaVersus draws on a panel ground (the Panel.frame variant), so its team names and fighters read over any scene; a compact versus shrinks its portraits, and the local fighter's character and rank read in fg.

fixed: Fourteen main actions the action plate had missed wear it now: the item card's primary action, the hand's Play, crafting's Craft, trade's Buy and Sell, loot's Take all, the deck list's confirm, the puzzle summary's Next, the garage's Locked, and the retry and action of ErrorState, EmptyState and DataGrid. The pass track's Claim and its upgrade button are the plate in gold (data-tone=reward), the upgrade without the glow; --shop-premium-fill, -hover-fill and -text now alias the reward action's tokens. They were the plain primary button or a gold button of their own, a bright slab beside every other screen's action.

fixed.summary: One corner language in the default style: frames, plates, rows, cells, cards and wells, and the button, field, checkbox, radio card, panel, tooltip, HUD and slot controls are cut at 45° (corner-shape: bevel), the cut scaled to the part (frame 12 px, plate and card 8, cell, field and slot 6, button 6, row and well 4). Capsules, keys, avatars, dots and the round minimap stay round. The fantasy and cartoon packs keep their round corners by setting --<role>-corner-shape: round; a game's own pack that wants round corners does the same.

fixed: Built-in UI: a family's two-corner cut is a corner shape, not a hard-coded polygon. The 259 cut quest entries, HUD plates, party cards, tiles, sockets and tags are `border-radius: <cut> 0` with `corner-shape: var(--cut-shape)`, which follows `--plate-corner-shape`, so a style pack that rounds its plates rounds its cuts too, and one that sets `--cut-shape` parts them.
`clip-path: border-box` (and the other geometry boxes) now cuts along the box's own corners, each corner's radius and `corner-shape` included, where it was a round rectangle of one radius.

fixed.summary: The built-in components' families (front end, HUD, results, shop, selection, map, quests, cards, world) no longer draw with literal colours: their light derives from --seed-hud, their reward gold (--hud-gold) from --gold, and their grounds, rims and inks from the neutral seed, each held at the lightness it reads at on dark glass in either scheme. A style pack's or a game's seeds now recolour their contents, not only their frames and buttons. The default style looks as before. Rarity, status, tier and team hues stay their own, each written once (--hud-foe, --hud-boon, --hud-warn, --hud-ally, --chart-*), so a pack sets each in one place; the HUD's rare and epic items take --rare and --epic.
In the dark scheme it is the warmer reward gold the game components draw with (#ffcf5a, was #ffd60a).

fixed: Built-in UI: HUD text holds over any scene, in any style and scheme. A figure drawn over the scene now wears the style's halo (`--scene-halo`, which the HUD components set beside their `text-shadow`) where a style's `--figure-shadow` used to replace it, so the score no longer vanishes on a light scheme; a figure on a plate, row or cell keeps the style's shadow. The HUD's text outline (`--hud-stroke-color`) is drawn at 90 % rather than 62 %, so figures over bright bar fills (a party's health and mana) read, and the compass's distances take the halo.
Built-in UI: rhythm results keep room under the score for its comma's descender, which overlapped New best and the old best under it.

RpgParty, RpgEnemyInfo and RpgTurnOrder wear the HUD's grammar instead of the old soft card: the party's and the enemy's health and mana bars lean in the bar's well (their figures upright, in the HUD's ink with its stroke), the enemy's health is the bar's danger red, the turn order's portraits are the leader's lit octagons, and the round sits on a cut HUD tag instead of a capsule. Each follows the style's bar and HUD tokens.

The built-in components' main actions no longer come in eleven dresses (a rounded white pill, a gold pill, a green pill, a purple pill and others): results, game over, loading, mode select, settings, save and load, calibration, the store's purchase, chat, friends, inbox, daily quests, achievements, reveal, idle, arena, loadout, garage, racing and rhythm results, song select and quest detail all wear the action plate, a claim in gold and an accept beside a decline in green.

Built-in UI: every meter is one meter. A component's `.track` and `.fill` parts now draw as the HUD's bar (`--track-fill` is `--bar-well`, `--track-shadow` is `--bar-rim`, `--fill-gloss` is `--bar-gloss`), and the bar's light is a sheen that only adds light (`--bar-sheen`), so a fill keeps its colour in every style. A style pack's `--meter-track-fill` and `--meter-track-shadow` now dress the bar's groove as well as the core `<meter>`'s. A meter marked `data-meter=plain` (ProgressBar while indeterminate) is flat (`--bar-plain-gloss`).

The player's own row is no longer a lit white slab: on the leaderboard (in the list and pinned under it), the arena scoreboard and the versus card it takes the chosen wash, keeps its team's edge, and the leaderboard adds a YOU tag (string screen.leaderboard.you). The draft's active pick is a ringed tile, not a white slab.
Gold no longer means selected: a chosen friend, quest or conversation row, a chat tab and your own chat line take the chosen wash in the families' light; gold is left for what can be claimed.

Built-in UI: a row that stands alone in a list (an achievement, a daily quest, an inbox or news entry, a chat line, a deck list's card, a card) no longer draws as a grey slab. Its ground was a white wash over dark glass, which the engine's linear-light blending turns grey; it is now the frame's glass one step nearer (the new `--entry-fill`, from `--color-entry-hi` and `--color-entry-lo`, which follow the scheme). A locked, hidden or missed one, and an unowned card, wear faint stripes of that glass (`--entry-grain`, `--entry-dim-fill`) instead of a bright hatch. A style pack retunes all of them through these tokens.

Built-in UI: the game components follow the colour scheme. In a light scheme (a style pack's parchment or daylight, or `og.ui.configure({ scheme: "light" })`) their grounds, wells, rows, tiles, cards, plates and shades turn light, recessed still darker than raised, and their white inks (`--hud-ink`, `--hud-label-ink`, `--hud-ink-dim`, `--front-ink` and the rest) take the palette's inks; inks held light for dark glass (rarity, difficulty, card type, judgement) are deepened in their own hue. The dark scheme is unchanged. Inks on a coloured fill, the map and radar glass and keycaps keep one value.
Built-in UI: the garage holds a long car name to three lines and a smaller cap, so its ratings and Drive stay in view in wider fonts.

fixed.summary: An Avatar with a frame and no portrait shows its person glyph in a style pack that gives pictures a fill (fantasy, scifi, cartoon): the frame's ring no longer paints that fill over the glyph.

The cook holds a theme's inks on its art as drawn: each piece's stretched centre, its 10th and 90th percentile pixels (a gloss, a grain or a header band included), is a ground of its scheme, and every art slot's ink and every ink role moves in lightness until it holds 4.5:1 there (3:1 for the large-figure inks), not only on the colours the face was painted from. A fill the solve moves takes its own -fg ink along.
A theme's high-contrast layer (prefers-contrast: more) holds its body inks at 7:1 and its large-figure inks at 4.5:1 on the same grounds.
The selected song's row steps in from the left inside the list instead of running past its right edge, which cut its BPM off.

Backdrop captures now bind the filter shader's sampler, preventing native driver crashes when drawing glass panels such as MainMenuScreen news cards and timeline caption plates. No game changes are required.

A TSX element's `backdrop-blur-*` and its backdrop colour functions (`backdrop-brightness-*`, `backdrop-saturate-*`, `backdrop-grayscale` and the rest) are drawn: what lies under the element (the scene and the UI under it, or its filtered ancestor's layer) is blurred and colour-filtered and drawn under its box, rounded as the box is. Before, the backdrop blur was not drawn and the colour functions were ignored, so a glass panel showed only its own tint. Like CSS's backdrop-filter, the element is a stacking context: a `z-*` descendant orders inside it.

Check content overlaps inside a screen mounted as the base floating layer, instead of skipping the entire screen as an intentional overlay. Noninteractive background-only fills beneath content remain intentional underlays when covering the safe surface, or their parent's content box at negative z-index. Empty generated text boxes draw nothing; nonempty text, images and controls are still checked.

A box with cut corners (corner-shape: bevel, notch, squircle or a superellipse) no longer takes an extra painter level for its shadow: its shadow's bounds end where a round box's do, so text above a bevelled button or panel stays in the level below it. A style with bevelled controls drew the default sample in five levels instead of four.
A control state cleared with background: none draws no fill under any corner shape; under a bevelled corner it submitted a fully transparent shape.

A border side's own colour draws (`border-rim border-t-accent`): the sides that differ from the rest take their colour, split at the corners as CSS joins them. The whole border used to take the top side's colour, so a Spinner's arc did not show.

fixed.member: Button variant danger, ghost and quiet
fixed.summary: Each now draws on an opaque ground (danger on glass-lo, ghost and quiet on surface), so its label reads over any scene. Before, danger had a 10% tint and ghost and quiet no fill, and over a light scene their text read under 2:1.

A card face fills its box and wears its type's colour; rare, epic and legendary cards draw the gold card frame. The hand sizes each card at 192 x 274 px (120 x 171 compact) and reserves the lift and the Play plate's room, instead of collapsing below the frame; a reward offer is a whole card instead of a strip.

Celebration draws its particles again: `confetti` throws paper from the top edge in four roles, `burst` throws sparks with its ring, `levelUp` has embers rising under the level, and `fireworks` bursts five shells in turn, each in its own role. Since the TSX port, confetti drew nothing and the others only a ring or five dots. The level-up's rays are still not drawn; they wait for pack art.

A whitespace-only text beside an element on one line, such as `<View> <Text>x</Text></View>`, no longer aborts the TSX compile: outside a Text it makes no node, inside a Text it stays text, and any compiler panic now comes back as a compile error.

A game's `og check` reads the ui module from its declaration (types/ui.d.ts) instead of the engine's web sources, so a game without the DOM library no longer reports the engine's own DOM and TextEncoder errors.
A component's `import "./x.en.ogt"` type-checks: the engine's types declare `*.ogt` modules.

A store at its cap is a tile with a gold rim and the Full tag, as it was before the TSX port; the tile had taken the tag's gold fill and caps, which left its name, amount and rate unreadable on gold in every pack.
The Driving tag is the accent chip only where the pack draws no chip art; on a pack's chip art it takes the art's ink like the other tags, so it reads (it was dark text on dark art).
A worn-out tyre's figure is in the theme's danger ink, which reads on the packs' chip art; the foe ink it used fell under 4.5:1 there.
A resource's cap, its rate without a trend and the empty line are in the theme's muted ink instead of the body ink at 80% opacity, so they keep 4.5:1 in the light scheme.

fixed.member: brightness-*, contrast-*, grayscale, hue-rotate-*, invert, saturate-*, sepia, filter opacity
fixed.summary: TSX colour filter classes parsed but did nothing; they now filter everything an element and its subtree draw, as CSS's `filter` does on the encoded colour, composed in Tailwind's order, and a nested element's filters apply under its ancestors'. `blur-*` and `drop-shadow-*` in a filter still draw nothing.

The default look is consistent: radii come from the radius tokens (no `nine-socket` cuts or fixed corners left), display type no longer uses `tracking-tight`, keycaps use `text-key-fg` on the key gradient, accent text uses `text-accent-ink`, and rows that were missing `flex-row` lay out in a row again (Card, FlowChartScreen, ResultsScreen, LoadingScreen, RpgCrafting, PuzzleSummary, Reveal).

The `back` action reports onResume or onBack. Danger rows on the pause menu fill in the danger colour with its ink rather than red text on the accent. Save/Load's Delete is a danger button, and Delete and Load are disabled with no saved slot selected.

fixed.member: ResultsScreen, LeaderboardScreen, LoadingScreen, PauseScreen, HudEditorScreen, Subtitles
fixed.summary: Content stays inside the HUD safe area (`env(hud-inset-*)` plus the screen's own padding); HudEditorScreen's trailing `p-4` no longer overrode the insets. Subtitles take no presses.
Ranks are written `#1,284` in the player's locale instead of English ordinals, and second place is legible (it was gold ink on white).
The lit objective is the first one not done, even when an earlier one is still open; progress is clamped to 0..1.
The column count follows `columns` instead of a fixed three.
A leaf keeps its twisty's room with an inert spacer instead of an invisible button that still took focus.
Shows the slide `index` names; it always showed the first.

Cooldowns, timers and status durations show tenths under ten seconds; StatBar, BossBar and cooldown wipes guard a zero maximum; RadialMeter fills in order; QtePrompt and Combo no longer draw debug labels; Killfeed marks the player's own rows; DamageNumbers draws misses, heals and crits and takes no presses; HoldButton needs the full hold.
The dialog sits on its own ground, the pack's `Panel.frame` over `bg-plate-hi` with a rim, instead of drawing its question and buttons straight over whatever is behind it.

`uppercase`, `lowercase` and `capitalize` transform the drawn text; colours written as `currentColor` (fill, border, outline, shadow, stroke) follow the inherited text colour; the reduced-motion setting reaches class resolution.

Hit testing respects overlapping and clipped nodes, touch and gamepad focus move as on desktop, scroll and pointer capture release cleanly, and multiline Input edits (line moves, selection, paste) behave like a text area.

A whole-world restore brings back a text field's vertical scroll and starts clean: in-flight motion, rolling counts, text selection, undo history, held sticks and queued sounds and haptics are cleared.

Components that leaned on React Native's flex defaults lay out under CSS's: racing Results' standings column stretches to its grid row, so a long list scrolls above Retry and Continue instead of under them; Table's figure cells align right and every cell centres in its row; Daily quests' bar sits beside its count with no wrapper. Racing Results' player position reads 2nd, 3rd, 11th and so on, not 2th.

Large HUD panels and effect tiles expose their cut radius as role tokens, and song rows and world-map plates read their existing roles directly. Style packs can change these radii without local component aliases hiding the inputs; the default dimensions are unchanged.

A TSX element's `data-*` props drive its classes' `data-<name>:` variants, and `group-data-<name>/<group>:` reads the nearest ancestor `group/<group>`'s: `data-on={props.on}` with `data-on:bg-accent` now marks it. A prop is on unless its value is empty or `false`; changing it restyles the element and the group's descendants that read it.

A game with a TSX UI no longer cooks every image of the default pack, whatever it draws. Only the images a `nine-<name>` class names join its bundle, in the game's code, the built-in components it imports or a pack it holds, along with the ones its code or an emitter names by id (`@styles/shared/fx/coin.png`). A fresh project that imports one built-in component cooks about a third faster (6 s to 4 s), and a bundle carries none of the frame and effect art it never draws. A `nine-` class built in a template (`nine-${name}`) keeps every image its written part starts.

Seeds given at run time (a look's through og.render.applyLook, a faction's) recolour the TSX UI: they lie over the style pack as a pack's own seeds do, so every class colour and og.ui.theme's colors derive from them; null clears them. Before, only old og-ui read them.

The hover, press, open, close and error sounds reach the TSX UI, over the style pack's own sounds for those events. A press sounds when it completes (on release, as a click). success has no event in the TSX UI and plays nothing.

A transformed text's textTransform is now reported in a running game. It was always null there, because the host takes the tree's paint each frame and the dump read the transforms from it; the tree now keeps the transforms of its last paint. The accessibility tree's bounds of a transformed node read the same transforms.

The states that paint their own fill and ink (a claimed or owned tag, a podium place, a selected tool, the current page) set their own shape with it, so under a theme's art they show their fill instead of an ink on art it was not chosen for. Pagination's current page is a primary button; the reveal's rarity word reads in `fg-muted`.
toy-3d, cartoon-2d, neon-vector, painterly-3d and pixel-3d-hybrid now name ui "default", and the creation choices' ui enum is default alone, until the theme recipes land.
Its `success` sound plays (og.ui.feedback("success")): it was read but never reached the TSX UI's sounds.

A wide blur runs on a downsampled chain, as browsers do: the layer is halved until the remaining σ is at most 4 px (2 px for a shadow's alpha), blurred there and scaled back with the variance of each halving taken out, so it lands as the Gaussian asked for. A drop shadow is one fused pass, and a colour filter after a blur is applied in the blur's last pass. Adjacent siblings with the same filter whose boxes are apart (a blur's reach included) share one offscreen layer unless that would change the stacking order. A 1080p HUD with 14 filtered elements went from about 8 ms of GPU time to about 0.5 ms. Wide blurs look the same; edges of a very wide blur are a little softer than a full-resolution Gaussian, never banded or blocky.

A TSX element's `blur-*` and `drop-shadow-*` (CSS `filter: blur()` and `drop-shadow()`) are drawn: the element and its subtree draw through a layer of their own, blurred or shadowed in the order the classes list them, with its opacity and mask applied after the filter as CSS applies them. A transformed element's blur and shadow offset turn and scale with it. A frame draws at most 16 such layers covering at most 1.5 screens together; past that an element draws unfiltered and the log says so once, naming it. Like CSS's filter, the element is a stacking context: a `z-*` descendant orders inside it and stays filtered.

A filter's offscreen targets are kept from frame to frame and shared between its passes, so a steady frame makes no new GPU textures. Before, each pass took a target of its own and the pool was cut back to 32 every frame: a HUD with 14 filtered elements made some 50 textures a frame, and native GPU memory climbed until the device ran out. A target no frame uses for 8 frames is freed.
