An element mounted into a UI already on screen shows its classes at once, or enters from its `starting:` classes, instead of transitioning from no style over its `duration-*` (a screen mounted mid-game no longer fades its grounds in).

A wrapping row sized to its content (`w-fit`, or any automatic width) keeps its items on one line when they fit: it used to wrap its last item by a rounding error of the row's own width and keep a one-line height, so that item showed below the row (strategy/resources' "47 / 50 Near cap"). An item now wraps only past 0.01 px over the line, the slack a text keeps at its own width.

fixed.member: Theme art: panel and plate faces
fixed.summary: A material's gloss band (plastic, flat) is drawn on buttons and chips only. Panels and plates carry text from their top edge, and a light ink could not hold on a dark face under the band (candy's pause objective read at 3.3:1).
A project's drawn theme art (`.og/ui-art/`) is drawn again when the engine draws it differently, instead of keeping art an older engine drew until the recipe changed.

A theme holds each `<role>-fg` at 4.5:1 on its own fill in both schemes, moving its lightness away from the fill. Every engine theme's `accent-fg` sat on its accent at 1.0 to 1.8:1 in one scheme (cartoon's selected tab count read black on dark brown).

On a wide screen the pause column stands on the glass ground, fading into the scene to its right, so its title and rows read over a bright scene (the title read at 2:1 over a sky); a phone keeps its full-height ground.

A field with no placeholder colour of its own draws its placeholder in the theme's `fg-muted`, which the ink solver holds at 4.5:1 on every ground, instead of half its text's opacity, which read too faint on dark art (scifi, fantasy, pixel). `placeholder:text-*` still sets a field's own.

Their category rows are `Tabs` and `Tab` with `Tab.count` counts, the bumper glyphs outside the scrolling row, so labels and counts no longer crowd or overlap at 390 px and the counts read in every theme. The shop sits on `Panel.frame`, its offer cards on `Plate.frame` and their pictures on `Slot.frame`, so a theme's art dresses them; its offer grid scrolls inside the panel instead of running past the panel's bottom edge, which hid the last row's prices; and its kicker is `fg-muted`, not the disabled `fg-subtle`.

It resolves in the dark scheme in both schemes, as the title and main menu do: it always sits over footage, so its choices, hotspots and QTE prompts are dark components over the picture rather than light plates.

Answers the cursor-* class of the TSX element under the pointer, or of its nearest ancestor that names one (a cursor-pointer button shows the hand, over its label too), instead of always "default": it read og-ui's frame, which a TSX game never fills. The web shell's canvas cursor follows it.

A TSX UI follows the game while it plays: a display frame now sends the UI's changes at each tick boundary, as an advance does, so a store or signal a system writes reaches the screen instead of the screen keeping its first build.

og.ui.tick and og.ui.seconds count the world's ticks (the tick being built, from 1), so a restored snapshot's next frame answers that tick again instead of a count the UI kept on its own. og.ui.frameViewport, og.ui.framePointer and og.ui.frameDirection answer the same frame og.ui.begin recorded for the tick, in UI units.

Their shades over the key art are back (the TSX port left them as empty layers): the main menu darkens its left side and foot, the title its top and foot, and the loading screen's foot shade rises above the place name. Their text reads over any key art. The title's game name is set at display size again, the loading screen's place name at its heading size with its Now entering line in a row, and the legal, version and save lines use the fg-muted role, so a pack sets them.

Generated theme art shades a bevelled material's rounded corner along its arc instead of across a diagonal join, and a pixel shape's badge, rims and outlines are whole blocks with no doubled stepped edge. The art redraws on the next cook.
A compiled theme dresses a danger button (`Button.plate.danger`) in its generated danger art, with its own solved ink, instead of the plain button's.

A material's panel dressing (`panel.header`, a coloured header band) reaches the generated panel art; the `flat` material's panel draws a thin header band in the theme's accent, inside every panel's padding.
The generated `stitch` ornament stays dashed round every corner; at the top-left and bottom-right of a rounded piece it no longer turns into a solid stroke.

A generated piece with a `stitch` ornament tiles its edges (`repeat: "tile"`) with a dash period that fits the tile, so the stitch stays dashed along a stretched edge instead of becoming a solid line.

Generated gallery projects pin the running engine package's version, including dev releases, and are rebuilt from an empty project directory. Each run clears its previous diagnostics, index and selected captures before preparation, so an early failure cannot report old contrast findings.

A text's `textLines` are its line boxes before its transform, and a transformed text (a card fanned in a hand, a dialog scaling in) also carries `textTransform` `[a, b, c, d, tx, ty]`, so a line's quad on screen is exact instead of the upright box round it. The UI gallery's contrast pass reads the ground inside that quad, padded a fifth of the line's height, so a rotated card's label is read on its own band and short bold figures (a price) on the plate round them, not their own antialiased edges.

Song select's Preview button is `data-pressed` while previewing and carries its ink on the button, so the pressed plate's ink reaches Previewing in every pack (it read light on the accent fill) and its level bars draw in that ink. Loadout's price reads in the pack's `accent-ink`, which a pack sets for its own plates, beside the gold coin.

The gallery exits non-zero and writes defects.txt listing each fixture that threw at mount or drew a string table's key instead of its words. A fixture other than `default` is laid over `default`, as the component tests mount it, so a state fixture names only what it changes.

The default look is a clean frosted glass with fully rounded corners from the radius tokens; every control has complete hover, pressed, focus-visible, selected and disabled states (Button, Checkbox, Switch).
The shipped themes compile with the same radius roles and state set as the default pack.

A binding glyph drawn as the pack's key or button art takes its em square in the layout, whatever the font. Fonts without an em space (Fredoka, Lilita One and others) left it no width, so the key cap covered the next word ("X review" on song select's Preview).
The road runs on from every disc to the next behind its Play, Open or Selected word, instead of starting below the word as a detached piece.

ArenaScoreboard, ArenaLobby, ArenaDraft, ArenaReady, ArenaRoster, ArenaRoundHud, ArenaSpectator, ArenaVersus and ArenaVote draw their rows and plates on opaque theme grounds and pack slots in those grounds' inks, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack (the scoreboard's names, the lobby's Open slot and the draft's Lock in).
ErrorState fills its error mark in danger whole with the ground's ink, so its mark reads over a bright scene in every pack.
CardDeckList draws its rows on Row.frame with the selected row's variant, and CardReward rims its relic plate in gold whole, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack.
the primary button's gloss and pressed wash draw on the theme's sheen, lit and shade roles instead of literal white and black, so every pack and scheme dresses them.

The HUD's meters, bars, buttons, prompts and feed rows draw their grounds on pack slots and theme roles in those grounds' inks, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack (the action button's fill, the bar and orb-meter sheens, the killfeed and loot-entry rows and the QTE keycaps).

Compass, interaction prompt, minimap, minimap view and speech bubble draw their grounds on theme roles in those grounds' inks, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack (the compass and minimap ticks, the minimap view's heading cone and the speech bubble's progress line).

The inspector's tool buttons, tree rows, section headers and field editors use the surface-hover ground for hover and selection and the accent ground in its own ink for the on state, so their text reads in every pack.

IdleGenerators, IdleOffline, IdlePrestige, IdlePurchases and IdleResources draw their rows on pack slots in those rows' inks, their tags on the chip slot, and their panel hairline on the sheen role, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack (the generator list's selected row, the amount radio's checked chip and the upgrades' Not enough tag).

MetaAchievements, Chat, DailyQuests, DailyRewards, Friends, Inbox, News, PassTrack, Profile, Reveal, Shop and ShopConfirm draw their rows on Row.frame, their tags on Chip.frame, their wells and bubbles on opaque and glass grounds in those grounds' inks, their rims on rim roles and their state fills whole with their own inks, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack (the channel tabs, the reward calendar's today claim and the shop's Sold out, Owned and Not enough tags).

The Backpack's and Crafting's kickers are the muted ink (4.5:1).

The panels, shooter loadout and effects, and rpg character, menu-bar, prompt and stats components draw their rows, plates and chips on pack slots and opaque theme grounds in those grounds' inks, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack (rows take the pack's Row with its selected state, plates bg-glass, keycaps their own pair, and muted lines the muted ink).
PuzzleSummary, PuzzleLevelPath and PuzzleGoals draw their rims on rim roles instead of white washes, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack.

RacingBanner, RacingBoost, RacingGarage, RacingLapHud, RacingPedals, RacingResults, RacingStandings and RacingTrackMap draw on pack slots and opaque theme grounds (the lap times on a glass plate, lit and shade position cells, sheen highlights, key-hi keycaps) in those grounds' inks, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack; the lap hud's split tag keeps its ahead and behind fills with their own inks.

RhythmChain, RhythmGauge, RhythmLaneKeys, RhythmResults, RhythmSongPlate, RhythmSongProgress, RhythmSongSelect and RhythmTiming draw on pack slots and opaque theme grounds (rim roles on the jacket edges, key-hi keycaps, shade-deep dividers and veils, tile and surface rows) in those grounds' inks, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack.

The screens draw their rows, plates and washes on pack slots and opaque theme grounds in those grounds' inks, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack: the menu and pause rows, the settings and leaderboard rows, the save-load slots, the results and game-over titles, the mode-select and leaderboard backdrops and the subtitles band.

StrategyAlerts, StrategyCommands, StrategyGroups, StrategyMinimap, StrategyQueue and StrategyTower draw on pack slots and opaque theme grounds (bg-well rows, sheen tile bodies, shade-deep sweeps, key-hi keycaps) in those grounds' inks, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack.

43 data-X: classes that read an attribute only an ancestor carries now use group-data-X/<name>: against that ancestor, so they apply. Visible changes: compact rosters, versus and star bars, team-local fighter rows, combo, effect and status states, timer warn and critical, radial menu choice, rarity tiers in backpack, crafting and difficulty, racing leader and player rows, hit kinds, quest steps, ultimate abilities, confirm's danger button and table figures. fixed.member: Built-in components (Compass, Chart, Menu, TooltipCard, Stats, Character, Minimap, MinimapView, SplitView, Tree, Calibration, LevelPath, SpeechBubble, SplashScreen, RadialMeter, Garage)
