Garage's empty picture is a `tile`.

fixed.member: @origingame/engine/ui View, Text, Image, Icon, Scroll, Line, Particles, Input (called as functions)
fixed.summary: An element called as a function puts its children in once. It inserted them twice, so Text({ children: "Go" }) drew "GoGo". Compiled TSX was not affected.

Draws every part from the theme's Ability slots, as ShooterAbilities does: the theme's slot art, size, ring and sweep. An ultimate shows its charge in figures on its own chip and Ready when full. A disabled or locked slot greys only its art, so its seconds stay readable. Ranks are pips.
Draws the theme's Ability slots (its art, size and sweep) and nudges when it comes ready.
A round theme's ready ultimate glows round instead of in a square, the charge in figures sits on its own chip so it reads over a light scene, and a disabled slot's seconds keep their ink.
A nine-slice shape named only in a pack slot's dressing (nine-ring in Ring.fill) draws: the cook bundles the images the default pack's own slots name, not only those the code writes.
A defeated boss shows no lost-health ghost, and its phase marks are dark with a light rim, so they read on any fill.
The share still to fill is a ring of its own (Ring.rest), so it parts from the ring's middle.
The level-up title sits on a dark band and reads at AA over its burst.
Its plate, count and multiplier are the theme's Combo slots; the multiplier is in gold and the count rolls to a new value.
Its rows and names are the theme's Feed slots, as are PickupFeed's plate and DamageDirection's ring and arcs.

Small labels over the scene sit on a HUD plate (`Plate.frame` over `bg-glass`, the pack's plate art where a pack dresses it) instead of a 1.5 px text-stroke halo that read faint over a bright sky: AmmoCounter's reserve weapon, its weapon and fire-mode line, Reloading and Reload; Nameplate's name, title, cast and percent (one plate; compact, the bar alone, has none); Waypoint's label, now in `text-fg` with the kind's colour on the diamond; LapHud's places gained or lost. Large figures (the magazine count, the race position) keep the halo, and LapHud's total racers (/8) gains it. LapHud's lap label and lap total are `text-fg-muted` instead of a thinned ink, and Waypoint's far state no longer fades its distance tag. Fix: none; a game that wrapped these labels in its own plate can drop it.
A magazine tick lit for each round left is drawn in the ink (`bg-fg`) over an unlit `bg-track` tick, as is the continuous strip past 60 rounds; lit and unlit ticks were the same colour.
The health bar draws its fill, ghost and shield again: their clip box had no width, so the bar showed its track only.

fixed.member: HudHint, RacingBonus, RacingBoost, RacingCar, RacingPedals, RacingGarage, RhythmGauge, RhythmScoreHud, RpgVitals, ShooterDamage, ShooterObjectives, ShooterPrompt, ShooterSquad, ShooterVitals, ShooterRound, Minimap, RacingTelemetry
fixed.summary: Labels and figures under 24 px over the scene sit on a HUD plate (`Plate.frame` over `bg-glass`, the pack's plate art where a pack dresses it) instead of a 1.5 px text-stroke halo that read faint over a bright sky: each small label is a chip, and the round's score, the shooter vitals' health and the score HUD's accuracy and grade sit on one plate each. Minimap's area name is on a plate. Telemetry's dial has a glass face under its figures. Large figures (24 px and over) keep the halo. Objectives' other goals are `text-fg-muted` instead of a row at 66% opacity, and the round's and vitals' red figures use `text-foe-ink`. Fix: none.
Declares `ground = "panel"`: it is a piece of the strategy HUD's bottom panel and is drawn on that panel's ground, never straight over the scene; its name drops the text-stroke halo.
Its figure and name sit on their own ground, so they read on any liquid and over any scene (they fell to 2.3:1 on a health orb's fill).
Invulnerable and Defeated sit on their own ground and read at AA. Its health, stagger bar and notches draw the theme's Bar slots.
Stands 56 px by default (Ring.box), large enough to read its percent on a phone.
Its well, fill colours, ghost, notches and figure draw the Bar slots; StatBar and RadialMeter draw theirs too.

Unified the default UI pack and built-in components under a modern rounded clean glass language (Panel.frame, Plate.frame, Slot.frame, Chip.frame, Row.frame, overlays, buttons, and HUD bars), removing hardcoded cut-corner nine-slices, Tailwind fixed radii, asymmetric corners, double borders, and widthless border colour classes.

Fixed reactivity freezes, semantic ink ordering over Plate.frame, SVG/Line viewBox geometry, contrast, layout, focusGroup navigation, safe-area insets, and broken group-data-* selectors across built-in HUD, world, genre, and menu components.

UI presentation checkpoints now save and restore Tree interactive state (focus, keyboard modality, open modal stack, focusMemory, scroll offsets, Input text/caret, UI sound PRNG, and virtual cursor) alongside stores and feedback PRNG.

fixed: og check (OG9105) now loads the project look's UI theme/style and game theme.json when checking TSX class names; og style list/add discovers pack.json packs and templates/themes recipes; og ui eject copies and imports sibling locale .ogt tables and rewires all exported symbols and barrel aliases.

fixed.summary: A press, hover or drop on a transformed (moved, scaled, rotated or skewed) element lands where the element is drawn.

fixed: A removed UI element frees its slot and an inline style its cache entry, so a screen that mounts and unmounts many nodes no longer grows memory.
Colour emoji draw in their colours in UI text.
MTSDF text fills by the median of its channels and strokes and glows by its true distance, so outlined and glowing UI text no longer shows seams at its corners.
The default pack's Hit.arc, Hold.fill.danger and Bar.trail slots name classes that exist (stroke-arc, bg-danger-fg, duration-trail delay-trail-hold).

fixed.summary: The weapon keeps a gap from both names and gives way first on a narrow row, so names no longer run into it (`Feed.weapon`).
`tone` colours the full units as documented; they were always a life's red.
Type-checks under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, which the game template sets; importing the components index failed in a game's `og check`.
`text-shadow-none` on an element inside a parent with a text shadow now draws no shadow; it inherited the parent's before.

TSX `fill-*` classes parsed but did nothing; they now paint the icons in an element and its subtree, as CSS's `fill` inherits: `fill-red-500` colours them, `fill-current` gives them the text colour again and `fill-none` hides them. An icon with no fill takes the text colour as before.
`missions` drew as an empty square at small sizes; it is now a checklist that reads at 16 px.

An image whose texture is resized in place fits by its new size: a streamed video (FlowPicture, FlowScreen, a title screen's footage) starts as a 1x1 texture and takes its frame size when it plays, and `object-cover` kept fitting it as a square, so a 768x1344 clip after a flow jump was drawn 1.75 times too wide and cropped at the sides.

An inline style's border widths and radii take CSS lengths: `style={{ "border-top-width": "4px" }}`, `"border-radius": "0.5rem"` and the per-corner radii now apply instead of being dropped, so a box with only inline border widths draws its border.

fixed.member: TSX style lengths (left, top, right, bottom, width, height, min/max sizes, margin, padding, gap)
fixed.summary: An inline `calc()`, `min()`, `max()` or `clamp()` over lengths (px, pt, rem) and percentages, with `+ - * /` and parentheses, now resolves against the containing block at layout, as a browser resolves it (`left: calc(50% - 0.0715rem)`, `width: clamp(8px, 25%, 40px)`). It used to be dropped, so the element sat at 0: the crosshair collapsed into its corner, and the compass, star bar, boss bar, slider thumbs, minimap markers and tree indents were misplaced.

An inline style's length with a unit (`style={{ width: "28px" }}`, `1.5rem`) sizes the box. It was refused and left the box `auto`, so a Spinner stretched to the screen's width and its spin drew a long diagonal stroke.

Point-of-interest pips and icons, minimap markers and debuff edges take their kind's theme role (gold, hud-accent, foe-ink, ally-ink, epic; info, success, warn, foe; info, epic, success, warn, danger), paired per scheme by the pack, instead of a fixed colour. The compass's pips and the minimap's markers had been an inline `background` the UI never drew, so they did not show at all.
A radial meter's fill ring is inset to its arc again, and an overlay's colour ramp draws: both had been an inline shorthand (`inset`, `background`) the UI dropped.

TSX classes that parsed but did nothing. `invisible` keeps an element's place but draws neither it nor its subtree, and presses pass it (a `visible` inside does not show again). `pointer-events-none` lets presses, hover and the cursor through an element and the subtree under it to what lies beneath, as a HUD overlay needs; `pointer-events-auto` inside takes them back.

fixed: RpgItemCard: a sideways scrollbar no longer lies across the last line of the card's body. The figure table's header label (EQUIPPED, or a longer translation) was wider than its figure column and ran past the row, so the body scrolled sideways; the label now takes the empty change column's room beside it and ends over its own column.

fixed.summary: A TSX text with a joiner or a variation selector (a ZWJ emoji family, ❤️) no longer names them as missing glyphs, so they load no other script's font pack (an emoji line loaded the Arabic pack).

Both screens sit over a picture (the key art, the background or the scene) and carry `scheme-dark`, so in the light scheme their veils darken the art as in the dark scheme instead of washing it pale, and their text keeps the dark scheme's light ink.

fixed.member: animate-float, animate-pop and the other animate-* classes
fixed.summary: A keyframe animation on an element added to a UI that had not drawn for a while (a damage number over an idle HUD) started as if it had been playing since the UI last drew, so `animate-float` showed nothing at all. Animations now start at the frame that first shows them.

A key bound by a live action map ahead of the UI's is that map's alone: it no longer moves the UI's focus or presses the focused control (steering with the arrows focused the HUD's first button, and Space for an ability then pressed it). The UI's own actions were already muted that way; its raw key handling now is too. A focused Input taking text still gets every key.

A fill of a status or rarity colour carries its own ink (`bg-success text-success-fg`, and the same for danger, warn, info, epic, legendary and critical) in 27 components, where the ink was the page's ground or another colour's: Claimed, Missed, Cleared, Next and the player's row read in the light scheme.
The level-up's disc is the theme's glass, not the gold ink used as a fill (a solid black or white disc).

The milestone ribbon is `bg-epic text-epic-fg`; Round won is `text-gold`, which reads on the panel in light; a chosen tool is the `hud-accent` fill with its ink in every pack, where a pack's button art covered the fill.
Their words sit on a HUD plate (`Plate.frame`) instead of straight over the scene with a text shadow, so they read over any scene and a pack dresses them.
A disabled button has a ground: the `fill` wash over `surface`, where it was the wash alone and its label could not be read over a scene.
The fire mode (Auto, Burst, Single) and Reloading are `text-fg`, not `text-fg-muted`: with the UI blend as CSS's they read under 4.5:1 on their halo in the light scheme.

The top three ranks' medal chips are their gold, silver and bronze fill alone, where a pack's chip art covered the fill and left the dark medal ink on dark art; the player's footer row stands on the theme's glass in a `Plate.frame`, where it was text over the scene.

The confirm button takes the pack's primary ink on a danger confirm, where `text-danger` on the pack's red art read 3.4:1 (fantasy's "Delete everything"); the danger stays in the header's "Cannot be undone" mark.

fixed.member: og.ui (TSX components over the game's frame on a wide-gamut or HDR display, and on the web)
fixed.summary: On a wide-gamut or HDR display (the web's wide-gamut canvas, an HDR monitor), a translucent UI pixel directly over the game's frame now blends with it in sRGB-encoded values, as it does on an 8-bit sRGB output and in a browser. Before, it blended in linear light: 25, 50 and 75 % white over black read 137, 186 and 224 on the web against 64, 128 and 191 natively. A frame's wide colours and highlights under the UI keep their values. Only a caller's own render target that is not the renderer's still meets the UI in its own light.

TSX `line-clamp-<n>` classes parsed but did nothing; a text now shows its first n lines, its box n lines tall, and the last ends in an ellipsis when more follow (`line-clamp-none` shows them all). `truncate` and `text-ellipsis` now end a line wider than its box in an ellipsis instead of cutting it off.

GameDesc.ui may load an emitter: a UI built there that draws particles (Celebration, Flourish, and the Shop, Reveal and DailyRewards that use it) registered with the error `og_load_emitter is not allowed`. The load is render-side and kept by path, so a repeat returns the same handle.

fixed.member: ps-*, pe-*, ms-*, me-*, start-*, end-*, border-s-*, rounded-s-* and the other start and end classes
fixed.summary: TSX classes for an element's start and end sides parsed but drew nothing (`ps-4` gave no padding); they now set the left and right sides, the other way round on a right-to-left page.
Its entries are built-in `Button`s in the `menu` variant, and the credits and quit group is set apart by space instead of a hairline. Props are unchanged.
Its rows are built-in `Button`s in the `menu` and `menu-danger` variants, and the minor group (Quit to menu, Quit game) is set apart by space instead of a hairline. Props are unchanged.
The `menu` and `menu-danger` variants no longer fill themselves; the current entry takes the ink of the MenuList bar under it.
Their rows enter one after another (`List.cascade`), and the hairlines under the header and the tabs are gone.
The hairline under the controls header and the rules beside each credits section title are gone.

The north badge is the HUD's red fill with the ink that holds on it (`bg-foe text-foe-fg`), the same in every pack and scheme. It was the pale body ink on `danger`, which is itself a pale ink in the dark scheme, so the N read about 1.9:1.

Markers are filled again: an ally or point of interest in the ally ink, an enemy in the foe ink, an objective in gold and loot in epic, each paired per scheme by the pack, in a ring of the map's ground. Their fills had been a fixed colour the UI never drew, which left a dark outline that disappeared on a dark map.
A TSX UI no longer stops the engine on the page's first frame (an index out of bounds in the layout store): the accessibility tree waits for the layout to give its nodes their boxes.

Documents on og-ui's new core answer clicks and taps again: a press and a release over the same enabled button, or an element with onclick or ontap, reports `click` with its id and then `emit` with the handler its onclick or ontap names, with the key of the `{#each}` row it is in. A disabled one, or a release over another element, clicks nothing.

A TSX UI follows the page's `prefers-contrast: more` (and a game's high-contrast setting): its classes resolve against the pack's high-contrast theme. A node under a transform (a dialog scaling in) is reported to screen readers, the page's mirror and autoplay at the box it is drawn in, not its layout box.

The default pack's high-contrast edges and tiles (`border`, `tile`) now reach 3:1 against the surface and page in both schemes (they were 1.5–2.8:1), and its text reaches 7:1 on every ground. Text on a tile holds 4.5:1.

When og-ui's new core first paints a tree (a mount, a pack or scheme change), every run-time glyph its text needs renders on that frame, so text appears with its panels instead of filling in a few glyphs a frame on the web. That frame costs the glyphs' rendering at once.

A TSX UI's `env(hud-inset-*)` classes (`pt-[calc(env(hud-inset-top)+16px)]` and the other sides) read the HUD's safe area: the viewport's safe-area insets with the host's covered region (the web shell's Back, `cover` on the command channel) folded in, and the HUD band's cap on an ultrawide. Before, the new core laid them out as 0, so a HUD padded by them sat under a notch and under the shell's Back.

On og-ui's new core, an image element shows its texture: a .svelte `` and a TSX `` paint the Texture handle they name (`og.load.texture`, a video player's texture) as their box image, with its classes' slice, tint and wipe, and follow a texture that loads or is replaced. A new-core frame painted right after another is no longer dropped: every other repaint was, so a change could stay unseen until the next one.

On `uiCore next`, the cook compiles each document's styles against the project's style packs too, and the runtime maps the cooked look of the active pack, so a pack restyles the new core's documents without compiling a look at run time.
On `uiCore next`, the UI dump's elements list each element of the new core with a document id, with its box on screen and its text, so `touch_move_to` and `find_by_id` reach the HUD's elements.
On `uiCore next`, the new core keeps the stores itself: their values, reads and mount inputs, and a checkpoint or a save carries them, so loading a save brings the HUD's values back.
On-screen controls show what og-input reads from them: a stick, d-pad or button is active: while a touch holds it, for every finger and not only the first, and the stick's knob follows the thumb.

On og-ui's new core, a .svelte document mounted before play is built, laid out and painted behind the web page's play gate (with its glyphs), so the first played frame draws it whole instead of building it.

A `nine-<name>` frame on a box smaller than its insets draws them shrunk in proportion until they fit, as CSS border-image does, so its corners no longer cross: fantasy's filigree on a tooltip or a small tile.

A nine-slice image drawn much smaller than its art (a pack's chip or button in a small box) is no longer blurred at its edges and corners. Each slice now picks its texture detail from its own scale, not from the whole image's scale across the box, and a stretched middle filters by the scale across its stretch, so its thin edge line stays sharp.

A `nine-<name>` class under a variant holds only in that state or window, as any class does: `hover:nine-plate-lit` draws its art on hover alone, and the last one that holds wins, instead of the last one written applying always.

No built-in component or screen keeps a visual value of its own: every opacity, press or hover scale, duration, edge width and inline length now reads a theme token, so a theme restyles them all (`og check`'s literal list is empty). Values moved to the nearest step: dimmed and disabled parts take `dim` (0.45), secondary text `quiet` (0.78), pressed tiles `press` (0.94), quick transitions `fast` (180 ms) and 300 ms ones `control`.
The HUD inset and the screen's own spacing are separate pads, and FlowChoices keeps the device inset in its compact layout, where its choices sat under a phone's home bar.

fixed.member: object-contain, object-cover, object-none, object-scale-down, object-fill, object-<position>
fixed.summary: TSX `object-*` classes parsed but did nothing; an `<Image>`'s source now fits its box by its texture's size as CSS's `object-fit` and `object-position` place it: `object-contain` letterboxes it, `object-cover` fills the box and crops it about `object-<position>` (the centre by default), `object-none` shows it at its size. An image with no `object-*` still stretches to its box.

fixed: UI: an open select's list is opaque by default, so the labels under it no longer read through its rows. The default style's list gradient now lies on a ground of its own (`--dropdown-list-ground`); a style that wants a translucent list sets its own `--dropdown-list-fill` and a blur behind it with `--dropdown-list-glass`.

UI: an open select, colour picker or other control with a floating list keeps the box its document's CSS gives it. The open list used to take the control's CSS (its width, its margins) instead, so a `width: 160px` select fell back to filling its row beside its neighbours and its trigger spilled out past the panel's edge while the list was open.

fixed.summary: A built-in component's row that leaves out an optional text field (a tag, glyph, key, cost, player, rank, grade and the like) now reads it as none, as an empty string does, instead of drawing an empty box or caption for it: the fields were tested with != '', which a missing field passed (arena, idle, racing, rhythm, rpg, shooter, strategy, card, world, panels and the credits, settings, mode select and key-values screens).

The orb's depth, rim shade and gleam are drawn from the style's tokens (--color-shadow and --orb-meter-light) rather than fixed black and white, through three new roles a style pack can set (--orb-meter-lume-fill, --orb-meter-depth-fill and --orb-meter-shade-fill); its look is otherwise unchanged.

The notification's mark, a daily quest's well and a quest reward sit in an octagon socket whose rim takes the tone (gold when done or unique), and the versus badge glows from its top, instead of gradient squares.

In the light scheme the packs' dark art holds dark-scheme content: cartoon's and scifi's `Panel.frame` every pack's `Plate.frame`, `Chip.frame` and `Button.plate`, and fantasy's and scifi's `Button.plate.primary` carry `scheme-dark` (cartoon's gold primary carries `scheme-light`), so `text-fg`, `text-fg-muted` and the other roles inside them resolve in the dark scheme, where they were the page's dark inks on dark art (panel headings, tab labels, lap times, quest text, a button's price or count). Fantasy's panel is a frame over the theme's ground and follows the page's scheme as before.

A style pack's text draws again: its pack.json `fonts` register their faces, and its theme's `fontFamily` gives body, display, mono and rounded text the first of their families that has a face. A role whose families have no face draws in the default face instead of drawing nothing (the cartoon, fantasy and scifi packs drew no text).

fixed.member: fantasy, scifi and cartoon style packs: the HUD
fixed.summary: The three built-in packs dress the HUD over the scene, not only its typeface: fantasy in aged brass edges, parchment key caps and a crimson life bar; scifi in cyan glass edges, an inner-lit cyan ultimate ring and key caps and a violet mana bar; cartoon in ink-outlined key caps, tags and bars with a hard drop and candy colours. Each sets the shared --hud-* roles (edge, accent, gold, ally, foe, boon, harm, the life, mana, stamina and shield fills, key caps, tags, plate rim, the slot ring) in both schemes; the plates keep following each pack's neutral seed.
A game that names no scheme now takes its UI style pack's own scheme: light packs (minimal, ink, cartoon, storybook) no longer draw their light buttons and panels on the dark default page.

The fantasy, cartoon and scifi packs key their per-slot sounds by the slots the engine's TSX components declare (`Button.plate`, `Button.plate.primary`) instead of og-ui part names (`Button.base`), so a primary button plays its confirm sound and plate buttons their hover. Cartoon's sounds for `Button.base.danger`, `Radio.card` and `Tabs.tab`, slots no TSX component declares, are gone; those controls play the pack-wide sounds.

fixed.member: og.ui (TSX components: translucent colours, shadows, masks and edges)
fixed.summary: The TSX UI blends in sRGB-encoded values, as CSS and every browser do, instead of in linear light: `bg-black/50` over a white panel is the mid grey (128) a browser draws, not the lighter 188, a shadow is as dark as its colour says, and an antialiased edge is as heavy as a browser's. Every frame with translucent UI moves to where a browser puts it; a design made against a browser needs no change. The pass draws in the output's plain format (the output itself, or its plain view where it is sRGB); an sRGB output on a backend without view formats, and an HDR display, take the UI as one layer blended this way and drawn over the frame, so there only a translucent pixel directly over the game's frame meets it in linear light.

Documents on og-ui's new core paint through one uber-shader pass made at boot: panels, gradients, built-in icons and text draw in the same first frame instead of icons and panels appearing after text, and a one-value change reallocates no paint.
text-overflow: ellipsis on a widget part now cuts the part's label with an ellipsis inside the part instead of letting it run over its neighbours.

Each disc sits in the middle of its stop, with its stars across its foot and its Open or Selected word under it; the road runs on from every disc to the next; discs have their fills again (the current one on the accent), so the road no longer shows through a number.
Its panel draws on a phone: a compact-only shape class replaced the theme's panel art with an unfilled cut, so the dialog sat on the bare scene.
A jacket keeps its square beside a long title, and the pressed Preview button takes the primary button's plate, so Previewing reads on it in every theme.

A nine-sliced frame is its box's edge, as CSS border-image is: a box that draws a nine-* image with slices no longer also draws its border (the border keeps only its room in the layout), and its outline, the focus ring included, draws as the frame's own silhouette grown by the outline's width and positive offset, under the frame, instead of a rectangle round it. Before, a cut or rounded plate showed a second, rectangular edge.
71 framed elements in the built-in components drop the border classes the frame now replaces; the loot, crafting and idle purchase rows keep their leading rarity or accent edge.
Every framed surface in the built-in components now shows its frame: frames that had no fill get a layer, and a frame nested in another takes the next layer up instead of matching its parent.

Panel.frame fills with `layer-1`, Plate.frame with `layer-2` and Row.frame with `layer-3`, so a framed surface always shows its frame. The selected row (Row.frame.selected) marks itself with `layer-4` and an inset bar inside its frame instead of a leading border the frame hid.

Every status and rarity ink holds 4.5:1 on every surface layer: `xp` (and so `epic`) is lighter in dark (#de85ff), `gold` darker in light (#855500), each moved in OKLCH lightness only, and the light `accent-ink` any seed derives is a little darker.

The state variants NSH's Tailwind reads from a node's accessibility state now apply: `checked:` and `indeterminate:` (the `checked` prop, `"mixed"` for indeterminate), `aria-pressed:` (`pressed`), `selected:` and `aria-selected:` (`selected`), `aria-expanded:` (`expanded`) and `aria-busy:` (`busy`). A `group`'s states reach its descendants' `group-<state>:` classes (`group-hover:`, `group-checked:`, `group-aria-pressed:`), which until now never matched.

Settings draws its pages, toggles, ranges and choices with the built-in Tabs, Switch, Slider and Select (one Tab stop for the pages, the selected page's mark under it alone). The leaderboard's tabs are Tabs, and its list is as tall as its rows, so the pinned row stands under them instead of at the screen's foot, and on a phone each ranked row keeps its score at its end instead of dropping it under the rank. The song select's detail title wraps to two lines instead of cutting a long title short.

fixed.member: og probe dump_ui: TSX elements past the screen
fixed.summary: A TSX element that runs past the screen is listed at its whole box with clipped false again; only a Scroll or a box cutting its overflow cuts its bounds and sets clipped. Since the visible-part change the surface cut it too, so og ui check's safe-area rule, which skips clipped elements, missed a button off the screen.

fixed.member: og probe dump_ui: TSX elements under a scroller
fixed.summary: A TSX element is listed with the part of it that shows: a Scroll or a box cutting its overflow that hides part of it sets clipped and its bounds are that part, and one it hides entirely is not listed. Before, every TSX element was listed at its whole box with clipped false, so a row scrolled out of view read as on screen.

A node not laid out yet reads an empty box: a control classed while its screen is being built no longer read another node's box, or crashed the native host (rune-taffy store.rs) when it was the first.
A pointer not over the surface hovers nothing: before the mouse first moved, the control at the top-left corner showed hover:, as did the one under the mouse's last place.

A screen enters and leaves with its motion however it is shown: the elements built with a subtree that goes on screen (a <Show> branch's wrapper, a new mount) enter from their starting: records, not only its top, and an unmounted or removed subtree with no exit: of its own stays drawn while the elements under it play their exit: records. Before, a screen inside a new mount appeared and vanished in one frame.
Send presses: it calls onSend, as the row's submit action does; before, only Enter sent.
A finger hovers nothing: on a touch screen hover: no longer lights the control a finger last touched (sticky hover), and what the mouse lit goes out when the player switches to touch.

A plain, primary or danger Button takes the pack's Button.plate dressing (and Button.plate.primary or Button.plate.danger), so a pack's button art reaches every built-in Button; a ghost or quiet one keeps the plain surface. A caller's class still comes last and wins.

The default pack's motion is stronger: a control squashes to 0.94x under a press and springs back with a visible bounce (damping 0.42); a screen leaves in 120 ms and the next one enters in 180 ms from 1.04x; a dialog pops in from 0.9x on its own spring (damping 0.45, 340 ms response) with one overshoot. motion.css's pop row takes a damping and a duration like the press row.

A screen that replaces one leaving enters once the leaving one has gone, instead of fading over it: an absolutely placed element put on screen beside an absolutely placed sibling on its way out (a <Show> branch, another mount) holds its starting: pose until that sibling's exit ends. Rows that flow, such as a list's, still come and go together.

HudBar fills to value over max again: since the TSX port its fill was value x 100% wide, so any bar whose max is not 1 (2184 of 3420 health) drew full and a loss never showed. Its ghost now rests at the fill and lags it on a loss (Bar.trail), as BossBar's does, so a loss shows without a ghost prop; a game's ghost still holds it longer.

Celebration's levelUp sounds the pack's levelup event (it sounded reward), and RacingBanner sounds countdown on each step of its count. Other built-ins already sound hover, press, select, confirm and back through their input.
A caller's padding holds while a Button is pressed: it no longer restates `py-0 px-4` under `active:`, which won over the caller's class while pressed and shifted the label.

A spread sets only the props that changed (a ref is called once), and a changing child no longer makes its dynamic siblings again: a branch beside a changing figure keeps its node, its focus and its entrance, as NSH's native renderer does.

Opening a screen after closing a large one no longer aborts the game: a node taken out of the UI tree kept its layout slot after the store compacted, and reading its box (a scroller's, a hit test's) indexed past the end. A node out of the tree now reads an empty box.

A mounted component's grid cell no longer grows to its content: a screen with a long row (a confirm dialog's buttons, a card reward's row) stays on a 390 px phone instead of running off its right edge.

On a touch screen a finger that lands just off a small control (an icon button, a breadcrumb, a 32 px cancel) presses it: a press on no control goes to the nearest enabled one whose box, grown to 44 px square, holds it, and the press stays held while the finger stays in that grown box. A mouse still takes only the box.

It draws on a panel ground (the Panel.frame variant), so its title, column heads and position numeral read over any scene; the numeral no longer runs into the title; the player row's name, time and points take the row's ink; a retired or disqualified row mutes its text instead of fading the whole row; the Fastest lap chip sits on an opaque surface.

The radar's sweep is a conic fan masked to its inner range ring, as it was before the TSX port, instead of filling the whole well; its rim, range rings, blip rims, vignette and top sheen take the pack's theme roles, so a pack and the light scheme restyle them (the light radar no longer wears a black vignette). The map, the blips and the player's arrow are placed in percentages of the radar's own side: they had all stood at its top-left corner, and the compact radar now places them alike.

Radial and conic gradient backgrounds (`bg-radial`, `bg-radial-[…]`, `bg-conic-*`, `-bg-conic-*` and `bg-[radial-gradient(…)]` / `bg-[conic-gradient(…)]`) paint in the TSX UI, with their centre, ending shape and start angle; they painted nothing before. A gradient keeps up to 16 stops (8 before), so a two-colour gradient mixed in Oklab keeps every one of them.

rarity draws again: an item slot's rim and a pickup's edge and count take the rarity's colour. data-* attributes are on or off, so `data-rarity={"rare"}` never matched `data-rarity-rare:`; each rarity is now its own attribute.
A hot reload keeps the UI in memory instead of saving and restoring it through JSON: a code swap on a page of many components took seconds in the UI alone, now milliseconds.

One rem in a class string is the body type step, 14 px, as the UI documentation says; the default theme left it at 16. A bracketed rem length (`w-[17.143rem]`, `text-[0.857rem]`) now draws at the documented size, the same as the theme step for that length (`w-60`, `text-xs`), where it drew 14% larger. The engine's components written with bracketed rems draw at their designed sizes; a game's own `[…rem]` classes do too. A game's pack sets its own with the theme's `rem`.

Restoring a world rewinds the UI motion clock too, including snapshots taken before UI mounted. Repeated New game or load no longer leaves newly opened menus waiting for the abandoned future timestamp.
A card or relic offer is a 7:10 card again (aspect-[7/10] now gives a flex item its height) and its face fills it, instead of a card at its content's height.
A quest's count (20 / 20) sits beside its bar instead of running under the reward.

The screens write theme steps and roles only where they wrote brackets, literal colours and opacity modifiers: type sizes, tracking and leading, radii, rims and lit edges, glows in the state's role, halos on the background role, and the menu's and title's washes in the whole background role.

meta, idle, puzzle, base, card and controls components write theme steps and roles only: sizes, type, leading, borders, shadows and colours a pack can move, where they wrote brackets, literal colours and opacity modifiers.

The hud and world components and the inspector write theme steps and roles only, where they wrote brackets, literal colours and opacity modifiers: sizes and type steps (text-2xs to text-8xl, display-sm, reading, caption), leadings (tight, snug, normal, flat), radii (control, field, button, block, capsule), named shadows and rings (plate, float, key, raise, glow, inset-shadow-lit/sunk/lip, ring-rim/rim-strong/entry-hi/key-fg/shade-deep/well/gold/knob/warn/danger/critical/foe/mana/ally/xp/info/accent/late/sheen/knob) and grounds and inks by role (sheen, scrim, surface, raised-pressed, fg-muted, fg-subtle, rim, rim-strong, rim-soft, gold, gold-hi, gold-fg, success, danger, warn, foe, ally, mana, critical, late, xp, info, hud, hud-accent, tile, well, glass, lit, entry-hi, entry-grain). What a pack can restyle is a role, not a value. Data-driven inline widths are unchanged.

The panels, shooter and RPG components write theme steps and roles only: type sizes, tracking, leading and radii on the theme's scale, and their rims, underlines, keycaps, glows and scrims as the named shadows, rings and inks in the roles they play, where they wrote brackets, literal colours and opacity modifiers a pack could not move. Groundless text rows (the panels' breadcrumbs, the shooter's pickups rows and combat HUD plate) sit on the pack's plate; the lock-on reticle, minimap marks and score dash take the foreground ink; the commands' grounded shade wash is gone.
write theme steps and roles only: sizes, type, radii, shadows and colours a pack can move, where they wrote brackets, literal colours and opacity modifiers.

fixed.member: CreatorTools, ModeSelect, Settings, PassTrack, Commands, Tutorial, QuestDetail
fixed.summary: The last hand-written values outside shooter/radar are theme steps: `og check` reads no OG9109 or OG9108 in any other built-in component. Grid templates keep only `auto` and `fr` tracks, and the lengths they wrote are sizes on the items (CreatorTools' side panels `w-70` and `w-90` and its catalogue `h-50`, ModeSelect's tiles `min-h-80`, PassTrack's lane label `w-27.5`, Commands' cells `h-12.75`); Settings' rows are two equal columns. Tutorial's card and progress glow are the named shadows. QuestDetail's Track button writes the ink of its accent fill (`text-accent-fg`; it read 1.1:1 in `accent-ink`), and its Locate and Untrack buttons hover on `surface-hover`.

fixed.member: MainMenu, TitleScreen, FlowChoices, Compass, Telemetry, the inspector
fixed.summary: Washes that pass 2 had made whole roles fade again, in roles that name their strength. MainMenu's and TitleScreen's veils over the key art run from `bg` through the `material-*` roles to transparent, where they covered the art with a solid band. FlowChoices' hotspots are a gold ring over `material-thin` (`material-regular` on hover), where they were solid gold squares over the art. Telemetry's redline arc is dim (`opacity-35`) until the engine is in it. The inspector's content box is seen through (`opacity-45`). Compass's strip stands on `bg-glass`, one ground in both schemes, where it was a gradient between two equal stops.

A rounded `overflow-hidden` element now clips everything under it to its rounded padding box, antialiased: an image, a glyph, an icon, a line or a particle crossing a rounded corner (a minimap's grid and marks inside its round bezel) is cut round instead of square, as CSS clips.

A rounded element with `overflow-hidden` cut its children square: a child's background or gradient filling it (a slot's ground inside its round ring) showed square corners. A child's fill, gradient, border or inset shadow that reaches a corner now takes the clip's inner radius there, as CSS clips to the rounded padding box. An image or text crossing the corner is still cut square.

A skill slot placed on its own (outside RpgSkills, in a game's own layout) is as wide as its content: its art and its key cap stand in one column of the slot's width instead of the art centring in the whole place while the key cap stayed at its start.

fixed.member: rtl:, ltr:, ps-*, pe-* and the other start and end classes
fixed.summary: In a right-to-left locale (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, the ar-XB pseudo-locale) the TSX classes now read the locale's direction: start and end classes put the start on the right, and `rtl:` variants hold. Before, every locale was treated as left to right.
Their ground is translucent blurred glass rather than an opaque fill, so a pause-time settings or save screen shows the frozen game frame under it, as the screens' `under` (blur, dim) states.

A component's pack slot (Plate.frame, Chip.frame, Button.plate, Button.plate.primary) now carries its text colour on the slot element, and its children inherit it instead of setting their own, so a pack whose variant paints the ground sets the ink for every label on it (69 places across the arena, card, HUD, meta, panels, puzzle, racing, rhythm, RPG, shooter, strategy and world kits and the screens). Quieter labels on a slot use opacity instead of fg-muted. Loadout, rhythm Results and Song select sit on an opaque Panel.frame ground, the card face's ground is opaque, and the empty hand's line sits on a Plate.frame, so their text reads over a bright scene in every pack. Results' Failed tag reads in white, the Full combo and All perfect tags and Song select's New tag in black, and Song select's chosen row is a select-hi ground with an accent ring, not a translucent accent wash.

The slot draws its cell again: 51 px square (the design's HUD slot size), with its icon or glyph, cooldown sweep, time, stack count and unaffordable veil. Its size had been written into the class as a bare `3.657rem`, which is no class, so the cell had no size and only the charge pips and the key cap showed. The cell's face under the cooldown's text is an opaque ground (`bg-tile`, or the HUD accent's gradient when ready), where it was a translucent sheen.
A celebration's play and a banner sound the pack's `reward` again, and the game over title its `error`, as they did before the TSX port.

TSX `space-*` classes parsed but did nothing; they now give each child but the last its end margin (the start one with `-reverse`, the left side of `space-x` swapped in a right-to-left locale), as Tailwind 4 does. A child's own margin on that side wins.

A spotlight's hole takes the lit element's rounded shape (its border box and radii) instead of its square box: the shade no longer leaves square corners lit round a round button, and a press in a corner outside the arc goes to the shade.

A host element's spread (`<View {...props} />`) now puts the spread's `children` in the element when it has none of its own, as Solid does; before, they were dropped, so every built-in Button drew an empty plate with no label or icon.

The arena components (draft, lobby, roster, round HUD, scoreboard, versus, vote) write theme steps and roles only: type, tracking, leading, sizes and radii on the theme's scale, and their rims, lit edges and team glows as the named shadows and rings in the teams' roles, where they wrote brackets and literal colours a pack could not move. MinimapView's heading cone is a conic gradient in the HUD accent's role, where it wrote the role's variable into the class.

fixed.member: HUD and world components, the inspector
fixed.summary: The HUD and world components and the inspector write the theme's steps where they wrote the same value in brackets: type sizes, tracking, leading, lengths and sizes on the spacing scale, shares as fractions, and radii, so a pack's scale moves them. A type size that set no leading class now takes its step's line height. The values that match no step exactly are unchanged here.

fixed.member: Meta, idle, puzzle, base and card components, controls
fixed.summary: The meta, idle, puzzle, base and card components and the controls write the theme's steps where they wrote the same value in brackets: type sizes, tracking, leading, lengths and sizes on the spacing scale, shares as fractions, and radii, so a pack's scale moves them. A type size that set no leading class now takes its step's line height. The values that match no step exactly are unchanged here.

The panels, shooter and RPG components write the theme's steps where they wrote the same value in brackets: type sizes, tracking, leading, lengths and sizes on the spacing scale, shares as fractions, and radii, so a pack's scale moves them. A type size that set no leading class now takes its step's line height. The values that match no step exactly are unchanged here.

The strategy, rhythm and racing components write the theme's steps where they wrote the same value in brackets: type sizes, tracking, leading, lengths and sizes on the spacing scale, shares as fractions, and radii, so a pack's scale moves them. A type size that set no leading class now takes its step's line height. The values that match no step exactly are unchanged here.

The screens write the theme's steps where they wrote the same value in brackets: type sizes, tracking, leading, lengths and sizes on the spacing scale, shares as fractions, and radii, so a pack's scale moves them. A type size that set no leading class now takes its step's line height. The values that match no step exactly are unchanged here.

A touch stick's knob is drawn in the `stick` role. In the light scheme it was the white `knob` on the pale ring, about 1.25:1, and could hardly be seen; it is now about 7.5:1. The dark scheme draws as before.

A store a system sets is drawn in that tick's frame, not one tick later. The TSX renderer's ops waited for the next tick boundary, but og.ui.end lays the tree out inside the tick, after the game's systems, so a HUD's number (useStore) showed the previous tick's value in every frame and screenshot, natively and on the web. Each game call's ops now reach the tree when the call returns.

A game that uses UI stores but draws no UI (no TSX mount, no document) no longer warns at its first tick that the default pack's shapes (`@styles/shared/shapes/*.svg`) and glyph icons (`@styles/shared/glyphs/…`) are not in the cooked bundle: the UI loads its pack's images and icons once a TSX mount or a document mount draws, which is when the cook bundles them.

A built-in TSX component's text shows on og run, og test and every other native run that bundles with the bundle cache's plan: the plan's catch-all resolver left a component's `import "./x.en.ogt"` to the default resolution, which dropped it from the bundle as unused, and its table was never registered, so First Light's quest tracker drew the raw key rpg.quests.main and og.i18n.t warned that no table had the ability bar's and slot's keys. A string table now resolves ahead of it.
Answers the cursor in the surface's CSS px, as its doc says, at any og-ui unit: it answered the tree's units, off by the unit (unitScale 2 put the middle of a 1280×720 surface at 320, 180).

fixed: The inspector's panel takes the pointer over its whole box at any og-ui unit: its box was read in the tree's units and compared with the pointer in CSS px, so at a unit of 1.5 (a 1080p desktop) clicks on its lower right third reached the game.

fixed.summary: Consecutive dynamic children (a `Show` beside a `Switch`) follow their changes instead of showing their first value only.

text-stroke-* and text-shadow-* on a <Text> (or any element) reach the text inside it, as CSS inherits -webkit-text-stroke and text-shadow: HUD labels draw their outline and shadow again instead of bare glyphs. A child's own text-stroke or text-shadow still wins.

A character none of a text's families has is drawn from the game's `fallbackFonts`, the style pack's files, the locale's fonts and font packs, then the default face, so Chinese under a pack draws with no `fallbackFonts`; one no font has is named once in a warning and draws nothing, never a box.
An `Input`'s caret stands where the shaped text puts it (after kerning, ligatures and right-to-left runs), on the line that holds it.

A character a style pack's faces lack (→ in Fredoka, Newsreader and Barlow Semi Condensed) draws from the default face, Instrument Sans, before the locale's fonts, as a browser takes its default font.

A word wider than its text box now stays whole and overflows, as CSS's default `overflow-wrap: normal` does, instead of breaking between its letters ("P|r|e|s|s"). A text's smallest width is now its widest word, so a box sized to its content is no longer squeezed to a letter.

UI text takes the weight Chrome on Linux gives it: each glyph's coverage goes through Skia's text preblend (gamma 1.2, contrast 0.2, keyed on the ink's luminance) before it is blended, so light text on a dark panel reads as full as a browser draws it and dark text on a light one as crisp. Every frame with TSX text moves towards Chrome's; fills, blurred shadows and the blend itself are unchanged, and a design made against a browser needs no change.
`<Text>Gold: {n} coins</Text>` no longer lays its three runs out as boxes stacked one per line: they are one line of text.

A `<Text>` span with `onPress` inside a paragraph is now its own node for screen readers: a link named by its text, with the bounds of its glyphs on its first line. Before, the paragraph swallowed it, so a reader could not find or activate it.

Three inks hold 4.5:1 on their grounds where they did not: `foe-fg` on `foe` (it read 3.1:1), `gold-fg` on `gold` in the light scheme (2.9:1), and the `common` rarity colour as a name's ink on a panel (1.7:1; it was a border colour and is now the muted ink).

A transition's cover (fade, wipe, slide, iris, dissolve) is drawn by the TSX UI's paint, over everything, in CSS px: a dissolve's cells are 24 CSS px and an iris's bands 2 CSS px at every surface size. It draws in a game with no UI mounted, and reduced motion still makes it a fade.

Staged like a console attract screen instead of a still card: it fades up from black while the key art (or the background) pushes in slowly, the logo or wide-tracked wordmark rises into the middle over a soft shade, and Press any button arrives at the foot with the confirm binding's glyph and pulses. The legal line and the version sit in the lower corners (stacked on a compact screen). Props are unchanged.

Text with letter-spacing no longer breaks inside words ("Leaderb/oard"). Its box was measured with the spacing read as em instead of px, so it came out far too wide, and the glyphs were then broken onto lines by a different, unshaped measure. A text now draws on the lines its measure laid out, at the same widths.

A box that cuts its overflow (overflow-hidden, a Scroll) under a translate, scale or rotate now cuts where it is drawn, not where it was laid out. A lifted card in a hand lost its title, type, text and cost and showed its art offset; anything translated more than its own height lost its clipped content. Under a rotation the cut is the box that bounds the rotated one.

A fraction translate class (`-translate-x-1/2`, `translate-y-full`) moves the element by its own box's size at paint, as in Tailwind; it moved nothing, so an element centred with `left-1/2 top-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2` sat with its top left corner on the point. It animates with the rest of the transform.
Effects run in dependency order, `classList` merges with `class`, and a component's cleanups run when it unmounts.

fixed.member: Dialog, Sheet, Popover, ContextMenu, DropdownMenu, Select, Tooltip, ToastStack
fixed.summary: Modals draw their scrim and keep focus inside until closed; overlays play `close` as they leave; a context menu opens at the pointer; Select's left and right arrows step the value while it is closed.
Slider drags track the pointer across the whole track, number fields clamp and step correctly, and the settings and confirm screens report their actions and keep focus inside.

A game whose UI is TSX alone draws its text: the cook bundles the default face when the game's code imports `@origingame/engine/ui`, as it does for a `.svelte` document, and a cook after a code change that starts importing it bundles the face too.

A game that mounts the engine's TSX components (@origingame/engine/ui/components) runs on the native host: they are bundled and compiled with the game's TSX instead of loaded as external modules, which failed with "Export named 'Show' not found".
`mount` fills the UI's surface: a component's root lays out as in a full-screen column, so `absolute inset-0` covers the screen instead of collapsing to a zero-width box.

The ported components name their colours by what the role means, not by a default-pack colour that happened to share its value. White HUD and front ink (and its dim, label and faint alphas) is the theme's fg, white sheens, wells, ticks and edges are white, black veils and scrims are black, and the on-primary, focus, raised-panel and selected-row roles use accent-fg, focus, surface-raised and select-hi. Under cartoon, fantasy, scifi or a game's own pack, labels and highlights no longer take the accent colour (fantasy's dark red), and veils no longer turn light in a light scheme. The default look is unchanged but for ink at #edf6ff where it was pure white.

A TSX component's string table, imported beside it as `import "./x.en.ogt"`, is registered with the world before the component builds, so its t() shows the text instead of the raw key (First Light's quest tracker drew `rpg.quests.main`, and every built-in component with its own table warned `og.i18n.t: no table has …`). The cook bundles the built-in components' tables when a game imports @origingame/engine/ui/components. The rpg and strategy components now import their kit's shared table, which holds their strings.

A step with a `target` dims the screen around the element of that `name` (anywhere in the UI; name a View around an Icon), which stays lit and keeps its own presses while the shade takes every other, and its card stands under that element instead of at x and y, as the Svelte screen's spotlight did. `target` now names the element by its `name` prop; empty still dims nothing and stands the card at x and y.
The label and the score stand on the pack's plate (Plate.frame) instead of bare over the scene, where they fell under the contrast bar.
A resource's rate and note are never clipped to the width of its amount ("+0/s" drew as "+0/").

A step whose target is not on screen (no element of that name, or one hidden) no longer dims the whole screen and hides its card: nothing is dimmed and the card stands at x and y until the target shows, then the shade and the card under the target take over in the same frame.

The pad's virtual cursor works on TSX screens: it slows over and settles on a TSX control (the magnet found none before), its A presses the control under it through the pointer's path without confirming the focused one, and the style pack's focus, foreground and background colours draw it. og.ui.virtualCursor answers CSS px.
Play the tick haptic when pressed.

In the light scheme the tags, ledgers and headers on `well` read (daily rewards' days, the shop confirmation's ledger, the tower's stats, lap times, rhythm results and timing, the kill feed), and text in a HUD colour reads on a pale ground: 42 components take the `-ink` roles.
A box shadow that is neither moved, blurred nor spread (`ring-0`, `inset-ring-0`, a shadow transitioned to nothing) paints nothing, as in CSS; it used to leave a faint rim on rounded corners.
Lists fsr3 only where the device has compute: on the gl tier it listed fsr3 although the frame was resolved with TAAU.

fixed: The animation guide now points to an available joint-pose query and accounts for its one-tick latency in gameplay.

fixed.summary: Volumetric fog now honours start for global distance density, end's additional linear distance ramp, and maxOpacity for the global distance and height fog together, in both froxel and raymarch rendering and beyond volumetricDistance. start does not delay height fog, local FogVolumes or underwater media; the default start=0, end=0 and maxOpacity=1 retain the existing path. sunColor and sunPower remain plain-fog controls, now documented as such; anisotropy shapes volumetric scattering.

A failed `expect:frame` or `expect:region` now leaves the frame it compared, at the check's own tick, as its evidence: `.failure/<check>@<tick>.png` (`region`, or `frame-<the reference's file stem>`), with an `expect:frame`'s reference beside it as `<check>@<tick>.reference.png`, and its failure message names that file. Before, the only frame was the world's last tick's, `.failure/frame.png`, which a reader took for the compared one (a car's HUD read 40 km/h there where the checked frame read 39). That frame is now named for its tick, `.failure/last@<tick>.png`. Each `og test --json` failure capture adds `tick` (the world's last tick) and `files` (`{path, tick, what}`, `what` `compared`, `reference`, `last`, `world` or `snapshot`); `frame.path` names the renamed file.

The probe's `lanes:off` now keeps only that engine's ticks, frames and captures off the lanes pool, and its `dump_lanes` reports that engine's setting. Before, it switched lanes off for every engine in the process, so two engines in one host (a test beside a game) changed each other's threads. Results are the same either way; only where the work runs changes.

When `sun extract` finds no measurable sun in an LDR sky, the cook's message and the report's `environment.sun.missing` name the cause: none bright enough (with the brightest pixel's colour), a clipped area (white clouds joined to the disc) or a disc too large (its size and the limit).

A handle written to a `u32()` field or list (a clip from og.load.animation, an entity) is refused with what it is and the field type that holds it: "4294967298 is not a u32: it is a handle (generation 1, index 2) ... such as ClipAsset() for a clip", on both the JSON and the byte path.

An og and a native host library built from different engine sources (one rebuilt, the other not) are told apart before any asset loads: the host refuses to start, naming both cooked-format stamps and the command that rebuilds them together, instead of every cooked file failing with "holds type ..., re-run og cook", which no re-cook could fix.

A game made by `og new` outside the engine checkout whose `og` runs it type-checks clean: og now links that checkout's engine package into the game's node_modules (as it does for an installed engine), so the template's `types` entry `@origingame/engine/bun-test` resolves instead of failing with TS2688 and every run needing --no-check.

Corrects the claim that probe GI makes indoor fog as dark as its surroundings: local fog's hemisphere light and global fog's authored ambient have no geometric occlusion. Explains why scaling Fog.color does not change air contrast, distinguishes global and local fog's scattering gains, and states the content conditions for offscreen-sun shafts; no renderer or API behaviour changes.

A grass field's draw pipelines, a GPU-placed scatter's placement pipelines and the scatter cull's pipeline are made the first frame they are in the scene, as their other pipelines were, instead of in the frame the camera first reaches them. A camera jumping or walking into a wood no longer stalls that frame while a cold driver compiles them (NVIDIA L4, 1920x1080, a teleport into a 4-species wood with grass: the frame after the jump took 2.37 s with an empty driver cache; now the worst frame in the 2 s after it is 32.2 ms cold and 31.1 ms warm). Drawing is unchanged.

The 3D vehicle overlay shows the full suspension travel with cyan end stops beside the green current length, and arrowheads distinguish tyre-force and normal-load directions. Wheel outlines retain the simulated wheel poses, and force lengths retain their existing scale.

An effect with a `decal` is anchored on the `ground` whatever it draws below its origin (a glow about a circle on the floor), since the decal lands on the surface there. It was measured `centre` when a tenth of it lay below, and its shots raised it off the ground, so the decal showed nowhere.
A sheet (`<effect>.png`, `together.png`) is written at PNG's best compression: the same pixels in a fifth of the bytes or less (a 2880x1080 sheet of about 3 MB is 0.2 to 0.7 MB).
A fully transparent conformed texture no longer emits an empty adaptive palette that fails to cook when outline width is zero.

Generated recipe sheets again retain their authored resolution, ramps, dithering, alpha and outlines under a selected look. The texture conformance pass now honors their internal opt-out after the TypeScript import cutover; re-cook affected effects without adding author overrides.

Footage plays several times faster headless (og test, og run --headless) and costs less CPU in a native build: the native decoder's 4:2:0 to RGBA conversion, which a tick waits for and which took most of a frame's decode, now converts pairs of rows with vector instructions (AVX2 where the CPU has it) and splits a large picture across threads. 360 ticks of 1344x768 footage on an NVIDIA L4 host take 2.0 to 2.5 s instead of 12.1 s (1.7 s with the film paused). Its bytes are unchanged, so frames and world hashes are the same.
Write the actual final decoded frame, including a type video asset's maxSeconds cutoff, instead of the first frame in its final second.

A streamed video whose picture starts after its sound, or whose frames are not evenly spaced (a concatenation), cooks to its planned frame count on every ffmpeg: the count is `-frames:v` with the last frame held, and the picture starts at the file's start, its first frame held over a late start. Before, an output `-t` cut frames on ffmpeg 7.1.5 and the asset failed.
A streamed video cooks with libaom-av1 when ffmpeg has no libsvtav1: its key interval goes through `-keyint_min`, as libaom takes no `kf-min-dist` in `-aom-params`.

A spot light's beam in volumetric fog is sampled equi-angularly about the light (Kulla and Fajardo 2012): sixteen samples per pixel ray inside its cone, where the light is strong, instead of eight in every depth slice the cone crosses (up to about 240 shadowed samples a pixel). It is the same beam, cut by the same shadows, at a fraction of the cost: Night Shift's main pass at 2560x1440 on an M4 Pro no longer spends about 50 ms on its one shadowed spot.

og.render.compile and the web page's warm-up behind the play gate now make only the pipelines of the systems the world has (its meshes and terrain, water, scattered copies and grass, particles, ribbons and trails, lines, 2D lights, metaballs, fluids, sprites and text), plus the UI, the overlay and the post passes, instead of every pipeline the engine has. A UI-only scene makes 52 pipelines instead of 101, and nothing a frame draws changes. Spawn a system's content before calling og.render.compile: one added later compiles when it first draws, and the perf record names it under pipelines made after the first frames.

Where water meets the ground or a stone it fades into what lies behind over a pixel and a half, its tint and refraction growing from none at the contact: the line was a hard, stair-stepped cut, the thinnest film darkened to the full shallow colour and the stone's foot drawn shifted from the stone above it.

On flowing water the contact foam piles only where the current runs into a bank or stone (its upstream faces), and on any water it fades where the band is narrower than a few pixels: it drew a white rim round every stone and along each bank's whole length.

A fall's sheet thins at its sides into strands with what lies behind showing between them, more broken the further down: it was opaque to the ribbon's straight sides, a board with two vertical cuts hung in front of the rock.

Water mirrors the sky as bright as the sky is drawn. Its reflection of the environment was multiplied by a further 1.8, so at a grazing view, where the Fresnel nears 1, a river, lake or sea mirrored a sky nearly twice as bright as the one above it and read white; seen from below, Snell's window was as much too bright.

og.Weather.change is the one ramp a weather takes. The guide no longer leaves a game its own ramp with change 0 (the fix given when change was added): a game writes the weather it wants, sets change to its slowest switch over its heaviest intensity, and draws its own sky, fog, sea or wind from drawnKind, drawnIntensity, fadingKind and fadingIntensity.
2D web games no longer report WebGPU validation errors from the disabled 3D foliage and grass-trample features.

A screen reader's activation of a TSX control moves the UI's focus to it, as a press does, and the page's focus follows. A range's value reaches the reader rounded to twelve significant digits (0.95, not 0.9500000000000001), so it agrees with the native range's own value.

The engine Worker asks for its WebGPU adapter once, where boot first needs the device: after the wasm and the first world, as the renderer attaches to the canvas. Before, it also asked before fetching the wasm, which a cold Chrome could answer with null while its GPU process started. A browser with navigator.gpu but no adapter now downloads the wasm before the player shell says it is not supported; the page's own navigator.gpu check is unchanged.

A cold browser GPU process may initially return no adapter. Both the player's canvas renderer and offscreen renderers now retry adapter selection for up to 30 seconds, then report a timed-out adapter request with its reason instead of immediately rejecting a supported GPU. A request that never resolves is bounded too. Native adapter selection is unchanged.

The page no longer asks for a WebGPU adapter on its main thread. Chrome's first requestAdapter blocks the thread that calls it while WebGPU starts, which froze the boot splash for seconds on a busy GPU process and skipped its genesis. The engine Worker now asks before it fetches the wasm; a browser without an adapter gets the same card, unsupported sample and fail as before.

Splits `shape`, `tilemap`, `timeline`, `net`, `shared`, `smaa`, and per-module generated wire types out of the primary WASM, keeping in the primary what every page calls (the rooms' and og.shared's host side, flipbook loading), so a game that uses none of them loads none; precaches every split module the build carries for the page's variant, and a CDN build's referenced ones under their CDN URL (the rest cached on their first fetch); slims embedded `bindings.json` and drops `SourceMap` from publish JS bundles; removes leaked `.graph.json` files from `dist/`; resolves `destruction` to `destruction2d` or `destruction3d` by the og.destruction call a game makes (a `…2d` call is destruction2d's), else by the project's profile; and no longer reads a regular expression literal in game code as a string or comment when finding the modules it references.

Delayed browser readbacks no longer return another tick's frame. Captures validate the tick and view that started the readback, retain it until consumed, and report mapping failures, capacity exhaustion and deadlines instead of silently restarting or returning null. A playing Worker's pending captures also progress when presentation callbacks stop arriving. Screenshot commands preserve readback error causes.

On the web, a streaming cell whose sub-scene places several models from a runtime bundle (og.load.bundle, og.load.pack) loads, and its cell group becomes ready. The tick that would load it now waits once for every file of those models still being fetched (and for scenes nested in it and prefabs, then their models), as it already waits for the group's pack, instead of refusing the spawn at the first missing file and running out of retries. Natively nothing changes: those files read at once.

A web game whose GPU device is lost keeps asking for a new one, every 250 ms for up to 10 s, instead of stopping at the first attempt. Right after a loss a browser can answer no adapter for a moment (Chrome's SwiftShader WebGPU does, on its first device), and that one answer used to refuse every later frame with "the GPU device was lost and a new one could not be made". A capture (`probe("capture")`) also works after a loss: it makes the new device itself instead of waiting for a display frame, and a readback started on a device lost since is started again on the new one, where it used to answer null until the probe gave up.

Boot, cooked assets, fonts and lazy wasm/decoder loads share a body-limited fetch budget and retry HTTP 429, 503 and network failures with Retry-After and bounded backoff; exhausted errors name the URL and status.

A game whose start calls og.load.font on a face of its locale's font pack (Night Shift's HUD font, fonts/latin/NotoSans-Latin.ttf) starts on the web. The web fetches pack faces after the boot, so start threw that the font was still being fetched and the game never drew; start now waits at the tick boundary until the locale's faces have landed, as it waits for the boot scene.

No tick runs, and no game time accrues, before GameDesc.start has run: while start waits for the boot scene or the locale's font faces, a frame or a probe advance runs no systems. Before, ticks could run on the half-built world while the boot scene loaded, and a system reading what start makes threw. Tick 0 is still the first tick after start, so replays and the probe's ticks are unchanged.

A game whose UI uses a font pack (First Light's Instrument Sans and Noto Sans faces) draws its first frame on the web. The faces fetched after the first tick joined the font chain only on a later tick, and behind the play gate no tick runs, so the first frame waited for them, and the page stayed on its loading screen, for good.

Explicitly referenced font-pack faces are fetched before GameDesc.start on the web, including conservative candidates of computed paths and escaped loaders. Loading a declared font in start returns a ready, stable handle on both hosts, even outside the locale's font chain. Other pack faces remain on demand for og.i18n. Undeclared synchronous pack-face loads are refused on both hosts, independent of residency; declare hidden paths with project.ogt publish.keep and recook. The boot report lists each explicit face and its bytes, and the service worker precaches it; no simulation-timed completion or rendering behavior changes. Recook and rebuild existing games to update the bundle's optional preload entries.

A web harness's `frame` (the shell's `call("frame")`) answers once one frame is left on the GPU, as a native offscreen frame waits for frame N-2. No display paces those frames, and a software GPU fell a minute behind them: a probe `capture` asked next waited out its 20 s and answered null.

On the web a frame's lit, prepass, terrain and water pipelines are compiled with only the optional lit features the frame uses (weather, local and area lights, decals, GI, caustics, toon, dissolve and the rest), as natively, instead of with every feature: a cold driver compiles each full lit pipeline for seconds, and a large scene's first frame waited for dozens of them. The full pipeline is asked for when a feature turns on or behind the play gate, and draws once it is compiled; captures and diagnostic views draw with it as before. Frames are the same.

The player shell carries checked ProjectStartup objects from og-config through the Worker to createEngine, preserving project.ts clock, seed, scenes and save version in dev and web exports. Malformed startup data reaches the shared native/web decoder and fails visibly instead of silently using defaults. The removed project-text string form is not supported.

A still scene's opaque main pass, depth prepass and shadow layers play from render bundles, recorded once and re-recorded only when a part's draws change, on the web and natively. On WebGPU (Chrome, NVIDIA L4) crowd-lods' render call takes 2.27 ms instead of 2.78 ms and the browser's GPU process 1.92 ms instead of 3.25 ms a frame.

Scattered grass and models no longer lose visible copies in Chrome's WebGPU path: each scan step explicitly resets its addend, keeping compacted instance offsets correct without disabling GPU placement, culling or indirect drawing.

On the web every Basis texture is prepared the way it is natively: the engine asks the Worker's pool of transcoders for each texture when it needs it, whichever bundle, pack or runtime bundle it read it from, and keys the prepared copy by its bytes and encoding as the native cache does. Two open bundles' textures of one id no longer share a copy, a pack's textures no longer depend on the Worker finding its bundle's manifest, and a texture that fails to transcode stays failed instead of being transcoded again on every ask. The boot still prepares the game's bundle's textures before the first frame, by asking for them the same way.

On the web a clustered og.Model seen small (its clusters under about 24 pixels, as a distant building is, and more often below render scale 1, automatic quality's included) no longer loses whole patches of its surface. The visibility buffer's resolve asked the device about its pipelines again every frame, and the browser answers on a later frame, so the resolve was never drawn and the clusters handed to it were left out of the frame. Native hosts were not affected.

A page on Chrome on a Linux host with an NVIDIA GPU starts the engine instead of showing "No graphics adapter". The engine Worker's check asked for an adapter with no power preference, which that Chrome answers with none, while the renderer asks with one and gets the GPU. The check now asks for the renderer's adapter: `high-performance`, or `low-power` where the player chose it.
Published games can start their parallel simulation workers from Safari’s offline cache.
Development builds on WebKit no longer stall the game clock to read GPU pass timestamps. CPU pass timings remain available. Rendering and the device features used by games are unchanged.

fixed: The web renderer compiles its frame pipelines with wgpu's asynchronous pipeline calls (the fork's port of gfx-rs/wgpu#10438) instead of wrapping GPUDevice in the Worker; `publish { pipelines }` and the probe's boot pipeline counts work as before.

fixed.summary: A browser whose GPU runs only WebGPU's compatibility mode (an OpenGL ES or Direct3D 11 GPU) now runs the engine instead of reporting WebGPU unsupported: the engine asks for a compatibility adapter, the browser still gives a core adapter wherever it has one, and on a compatibility device the renderer runs its compat tier (no MSAA, no storage in the vertex stage outside the UI, the mode's limits and shader rules). The engine builds on origin-engine's wgpu fork (v30.0.2 with the upstream compatibility-mode patches) until wgpu releases them.

fixed: The web player's WebGPU check asks for an adapter once more when the browser's first answer is null, as Chrome's is while its GPU process starts on a Linux NVIDIA host.

fixed.summary: The wire's capture answers the frame at the size asked, or the full render target in device pixels when none is asked. It was fitted again to 1280 px on its long side, so a page at device pixel ratio 2 (a Retina Mac, a phone) answered half its frame.

The world server and `og world-server load` raise their soft open-file limit to the hard limit at startup (Linux and macOS), so a shell's default of 1024 no longer stops a server near 1000 players. When the hard limit is below what --max-players needs, the server says so in one line naming the number, serves the players it can hold and refuses the rest as full instead of failing their connections.

A 3D game's engine no longer downloads the 3D world at boot: terrain, scattered copies and grass, planar water, the 3D fluids and volumetric fog's shaders (with og.terrain) are the on-demand engine module `world3d`, loaded when a game first calls og.terrain or a frame first draws one of them, and prefetched with a scene that places an og.Terrain (cooked/.cook.ogt `modules world3d`). The 3D primary is about 155 KB (brotli) smaller; a game that uses the 3D world downloads the module, about 207 KB. Nothing a game calls changes.
