The white water below a river's fall now clears within a length set by the fall's drop (three drops, at least one width) instead of an exponential tail that left a 7 m river white some five widths downstream, and the churn is patches over the water's own colour rather than a grey veil under them: white at the fall's foot, thinning and fading into streaks drawn along the current, clear water within a few widths.

Scenes, cell scenes, prefabs and models resolve dependencies from their declaring bundle first and cache each bundle's loads separately. Missing ids fall back to the boot bundle and then ready bundles in open order, so simultaneously open versions can reuse asset paths without drawing each other's assets.

Unloading a streaming group frees its full meshes' cached raycast BVHs and keeps only one copy of each stand-in mesh. HLOD proxies keep their meshes and textures only while a scene or cell placement needs them; removing the last placement releases those resources, and placing it again reloads them.

Runtime-opened bundles register their own streaming groups: cell groups no longer freeze the world, and unloading releases full meshes, textures and budget usage through the declaring bundle. Conflicting group names fail the new bundle open, naming both bundles.

Native rendering drops recoverable decoded texture copies after their current revision uploads, reconstructing texels from the owning cooked bundle for device recovery or CPU reads, including the currently displayed mip tail or full chain. Deferred uploads, active CPU readers and pending mip swaps retain the data they need; mesh data used by simulation and compact-pipeline fallback stays available.

Each frame `og render` draws waits, natively, until the textures being prepared are, so a model loaded with og.load.gltf (or a scene) is drawn with its maps on the first frame instead of hidden for as long as the texture worker took, and two renders of one script draw the same frames. A display frame, and an `og run --commands` frame, still never waits; a stream group's model still waits for its group.

Resident sessions work with long HOME and temporary-directory paths on macOS and Linux. Sockets use a length-checked private per-user runtime directory, falling back to /tmp when necessary, and report a clear error if no safe location fits.

A joined session that hears nothing from its world server for 2 s (a snapshot comes every tick) counts as lost and reconnects at once, resuming its avatar: a WebTransport client whose NAT rebinds is back in about 2 s as the same og.RemoteAvatar on the others, instead of waiting for the transport's idle timeout and returning as a new visitor. The 2 s are real time measured by the connection, so a load hitch or a background tab is not taken for a loss. A reconnect keeps the og.RemoteAvatar entities it held: those the server enters again carry on with no og.PresenceLeft or og.PresenceEntered.

A normal-mapped decal no longer flattens the surface under its whole box. Its normal map now bends the surface's own shading normal instead of replacing it, so where the decal's map is flat (its margin) a normal-mapped plaster, stone or cobble surface keeps its relief, and a bullet hole shows as a hole instead of a smooth square.

Depth ink no longer draws a thick band where a ground plane recedes to the horizon. A silhouette is now a break in the inverse depth between opposite neighbours, which stays affine across any plane, as the hatching's contours already found it. Silhouettes and creases on objects keep their lines.

The first frame with clouds, a live sky or an aurora no longer compiles the clouds' noise, the live sky's capture, the cloud shadow's bake or the aurora's footprint on the renderer's thread before any of its other pipelines start: they compile beside them on the compile workers. The sky over the clouds and the clouds' resolve no longer compile a cloud march in their vertex stage that they never read. The picture is unchanged. The web is unchanged.

The sky, its sun, moon, stars and clouds stand where they are however far the camera is from the render origin. The view ray through a pixel was the difference of two points unprojected at the camera's place, rounded at its distance from the origin: 4 km out the sky was drawn up to 0.4° off (a degree at 14 km) and turned a little with every step. The ray is now built from the camera's rotation and projection alone.
Price grouped textures by the renderer's actual transcode format and exact mip block sizes before residency admission, including existing cooked packs, instead of charging every texture as RGBA8.

A stream group's prepared textures are handed to its models without being copied on the tick that loads a cell, and a group waiting for its last texture no longer copies the ready ones at every tick boundary: natively, a cell of 14 models with one 1024x1024 map each took 35 to 60 ms on its worst load frame in the engine's CPU timing fixture and takes 7 ms. A model whose textures are ready is shown while another of its group still waits. Presentation only: entities, StreamEvent, readiness rules and hashes are unchanged.

Natively the tick a streaming group becomes resident (and its StreamEvent) follows from ticks alone: at most one group is put in place per tick, and a frame that catches up runs a boundary per tick. It moved with the host's calls (one group per probe call, idle frame or catch-up frame), so og run and og run --json reached different hashes. Runs that called the probe between frames now see the plain run's ticks. On the web a pack's arrival stays host timing; the world guide §4 says how to wait deterministically.

Inside a system, world.despawn now takes the entity's descendants with it, as it does between ticks: every entity whose og.Parent chain reaches it when the despawn applies, including a child the same system spawned under it just before. Before, only the entity went, and its children stayed alive with og.Parent naming a dead entity.

A bright object that vanishes from one frame to the next (a lightning bolt, a light switched off) no longer leaves a ghost round thin bright detail. TAA clamped the history to the brightest sample beside each pixel, so a bolt over rain stayed at the streaks' brightness in a 3-pixel band round every streak it crossed, fading over several frames. A history over twice as bright as anything about it is now dropped rather than clamped. TAA and SMAA T2x frames are otherwise unchanged.

Adjacent terrains with the same declared `height` and equal 16-bit samples on their shared edge now load identical heights there. The cook keeps a 16-bit heightmap's samples as steps of `height` instead of re-quantising each terrain over its own lowest and highest height, which put up to a millimetre between neighbours. TerrainInfo's lowest and highest height are unchanged; terrains are re-cooked (og.Terrain v7).

A terrain with `holes` keeps every 16-bit step of its heightmap. The hole flags were stored in the heights' lowest bit, so since the cook kept a heightmap's samples as steps of `height`, every odd sample read one step low (1/65535 of the range) and a sector with a hole met a neighbour without one a step apart. The flags now travel beside the heights, one bit per sample; terrains are re-cooked (og.Terrain.tile v5).
Close one-pixel cracks between terrain clipmap levels by morphing fine vertices onto the coarser lattice in position as well as height.

A runtime bundle's terrains are freed with it: once the bundle is released and nothing names a terrain any more (no og.Terrain, og.TerrainScatter, og.Grass or other TerrainData field, no collider on its height field), the terrain goes whole at the next tick boundary: its cooked tiles, its field, its physics height field, its tiles on the GPU, and the bundle's layer textures and arrays no other terrain uses. A terrain still drawn outlives the release until its last og.Terrain despawns. Before, a loaded terrain was never freed, so a visitor walking through per-parcel packs grew without bound. A freed terrain's handle is refused (loading §10).

On a terrain's edge, og.terrain.sample interpolates only that edge's two samples, so a neighbouring terrain that shares the edge reads the same bits from its side; before, the two sides' triangle formulas could differ in the last bit.

Geometric transmission reuses the opaque main depth instead of redrawing its geometry in a prepass, skips exit capture for thin walls, and reuses Newton samples without reducing capture resolution or search quality.

Absolutely positioned auto-height labels resolve percentage block-size bounds against their containing block, not their own provisional height; final placement does not apply those bounds a second time.

fixed: Absolutely positioned UI descendants now draw outside intervening scrollers when their containing block is outside the scroller. Containing-block overflow and explicit clip paths still clip them.

fixed.summary: Badges with tone=accent now read the existing --badge-primary-fill and --badge-primary-ink hooks from the default stylesheet.
Blurred shadows on CSS bevel corners no longer show straight seams extending from the corner endpoints, including unequal horizontal and vertical corner radii.
Text inside content buttons inherits the button type role's label weight, just like a plain button label; explicit button and descendant font weights still override the default.
Buttons keep text beside conditional, repeated, keyed, rendered and await children inside the button content instead of dropping the surrounding label.

Warmed class changes that only retarget a built-in button's scale and opacity preserve the control instead of rebuilding it. Changes to real styles, shadow parts, inherited values or positioned content keep the full path. Inheritance bookkeeping revisits only changed values and declaration ownership. Both hosts share the mechanism.

An explicit line-height: normal applies normal leading to CJK text too, instead of retaining the default type ramp's extra CJK spacing. Inherited normal leading now places compact mixed-script labels consistently.
Clean UI roots reuse sizing in an unchanged available area while still updating placement, scrolling, clipping and container measurements.
Component props retain their declared names, including step and src, instead of being renamed as native HTML attributes. Native element attribute mappings are unchanged.

fixed: UI layout reuses CSS placement traversal and child-list buffers across roots and frames, reducing temporary allocations without changing placement.

fixed.summary: A category name under a bar stays on one line, on the same baseline as the others: with more than eight bars every other bar is named, and every third in a chart narrower than 520 px, instead of the names wrapping to two lines.

A figure is never cut with an ellipsis. In a narrow shell the value keeps its whole width and the name gives way. The tracks prop documents that a numeric column's track holds its widest figure in text-scaled units (calc(96 * var(--font-step-px))), so it grows with the player's text size.

Chart's category names were cut at 150 % text and its gridlines were reported as overlapping its bars; Carousel's next page overflowed its box; a long card title was cut and its body truncated. Each now fits or wraps whole.
Compose library or game components by their exact declared name with <ui:name>, including star-rating, key-values and banner; native tags and existing capitalised component tags are unchanged.
World anchor and mass-label placement reuse coordinate and collision working storage across queries and frames while preserving exact placement results.
Compare rewritten elements with their previous derived children so an unchanged screen does not rebuild tree and drawing orders every frame; real child and CSS order changes still invalidate them.

Reports painted descendants and unwrapped text overflowing across sibling flex or grid areas, including fractional intersections, without a result-count cap. Ancestor clips and invisible content remain excluded.

A delta that starts with + is drawn in the better green (class up) and one that starts with - in the worse red (new class down); an unsigned delta is plain. Every delta used to draw red, because the test for the leading sign never matched.
Document t() keeps ICU plural and select branches until its arguments are supplied, restoring plural labels, selected suffixes such as Results' Accuracy percent sign, and quoted literal braces.

fixed: Virtual list and grid rows with authored focusable controls now use structural wrappers without duplicate focus targets, option selection or built-in padding. Plain-content rows remain selectable options.

UI geometry reports now attribute text to its emitting element instead of guessing from overlapping boxes. Fully scrolled-out text no longer produces sheet-level clipping findings, and identical overlapping labels keep separate clips.

fixed.summary: Font-family lists synthesize missing bold and oblique per fallback face, so a real bold or italic Latin font no longer leaves regular CJK text underweight or upright. Synthetic bold uses FreeType/Skia's 1/24-em growth to preserve small counters without changing glyph advances or adding tracking. Mixed text preserves real styled faces and font-synthesis opt-outs.
Overflow clips an element's content before filtering, without cutting its own drop-shadow or blur output back to its box. Ancestor overflow, clip-path and masks still clip the resulting image.

Moves frames: the default style's --font-sans and --font-display name "Instrument Sans" first, so a default-style game with no font draws its body and display text in the engine's default face at real weights and widths.

line-height: normal uses the selected font's vertical metrics, with ascent, descent and line gap rounded separately as in the browser. The 1.2 fallback is retained only for faces without usable metrics; explicit numeric and length leading is unchanged.
The name set as a wordmark keeps whole words: it takes a share of the column's width, so a long name's longest word fits its line on a phone at a large text scale instead of breaking inside the word.
A mark without art (texture 0) is its name set as a wordmark, not an empty logo frame with the name under it.
HTML headings and small text keep the document's inherited font family and line height instead of resetting them through their default font shorthand; theme heading sizes and weights remain defaults.
The button's accessible name is its words alone (End turn): the key cap beside them is no longer read as part of the name (End turn E).
Hold progress paints over the button's base rather than behind its opaque plate, filling the actual control width while keeping its label visible.

Reduces tag and spawned-number placement work with exact-input anchor reuse, bounded occupancy sweeps and conservative free-space pruning, preserving placement preferences, clearance and screen containment.

The speed is held to half its dial face's width (the face is its size container, the share the figure has on a desktop), so on a phone at a large text scale the figure stays inside the face, clear of the arc's ticks and the shift lights. On a phone the gear's tag stands in the arc's opening under the face, and the face holds the lights, the speed and its units. The --hud-size-speed and --hud-size-speed-compact tokens carry the face's share.
On a phone a fallen companion's empty health bar sits directly under its name, level with the other plates' bars; its Fallen tag stands under the bar instead of moving it.

Raises only the static HUD budget from 1.0 ms to 1.1 ms with xiaomao's explicit approval on 2026-11-18: v5's complete placement (candidate search, containment, drawn bounds and mass avoidance) measures about 0.01 ms over 1.0 ms. Moving-camera and dense-menu budgets are unchanged.

The time on the order in production is held to its tile: a box narrowed by the figure's length (four characters take the tile) is its size container, so a long time (10:00:00) stays whole on the tile at any text scale instead of being cut.
The wave's title is never cut: it fits, or wraps onto a second line (WAVE 7 · SIEGE on a phone at 150 % text).
The selected units' cards lie on one row while they all fit, else in two even rows (twelve as six and six), never a full row and a short orphaned one.

Retained scalar transitions reuse unchanged native-part dependencies, avoid scanning shared inherited token maps, and skip unrelated computed-value motion phases and custom-effect cascades. Registered custom-property motion and before-change inheritance keep their existing behavior.

HTML links use their element's computed ink and text decoration, including inherited colors and text-decoration: none. Default links remain highlighted and underlined; components no longer need to work around link runs overriding CSS.
Positioning insets accept CSS length-percentage math such as max(0px, calc(50% - 130px)), min() and clamp(), resolving percentages against the containing block's corresponding axis.
A long title keeps two lines and ends in an ellipsis (its full text stays its name), so on a phone at large text sizes the grid always shows at least one whole row of items.

An item's name keeps two lines and ends in an ellipsis (its full text stays its name). In a narrow loot window, Take sits at the row's foot so the name has the row's width, and the description keeps two lines, so more than one item shows at large text sizes.
A tile's stack count is written short in the active locale (99,999 reads 100K), with the whole number as its name, so a large stack stays inside its tile on a phone at large text sizes.
On a phone at 150 % text a long tip was cut with an ellipsis after four lines; it now wraps whole.

LootLabel chips avoid danger without leaving their pile: placement-box selects chip collision bounds, max-shift caps travel independently of text scale, and clipped decoration no longer reserves invisible space. Local danger fallbacks report data-blocked instead of moving into the boss zone; ground glows remain at the items.

fixed: Cooking now refreshes built-in UI dependencies when only the component manifest changes, without requiring document edits or clearing the cooked cache.

fixed.summary: Mixed-unit min(), max() and clamp() margins now resolve at layout against the containing width, including logical margins and font-relative terms, rather than being rejected.
Keep active label widths in place instead of rebuilding their cache every frame, preserving placement and font/template invalidation.

A node's plate, icon and caption keep their text size only up to a share of the well's own width and height, so on a narrow well (a phone's, where the whole graph is scaled down to fit across it) a node's caption no longer lands on the node in the row below. Desktop graphs, and graphs with room to spare, are unchanged. The nodes and captions still grow with the text size where the well has room for them.

fixed.member: ArenaRoster, ArenaDraft, ArenaLobby, ArenaReady, ArenaVote, ArenaSpectator, ArenaVersus, ArenaRoundHud
fixed.summary: Redrawn to the approved character and party mockup in the default style's smoked glass and lit edges: the roster, draft, lobby, ready check and vote on cut cards, a character a tile with its portrait, the chosen one ringed in the accent, a locked or taken one grey with its reason on a tag; the draft's teams in their colours with bans as struck octagons and the slot being filled lit white; a lobby seat a cut row with an octagon portrait, Host on gold, You on the accent and Ready in green; the ready check's clock in gold and each answer on its row's edge; a vote's options as tiles with the tally at the end; the spectator's plate with the watched player washed in the accent; the versus bare over the scene, each side's name large in its colour, the second side mirrored, a gold hexagon seal between them; the round HUD's team plates with the team's colour along the foot and the round's verdict in the result's lit fill. Names and titles wrap on whole words and are no longer cut with an ellipsis; on a phone the round HUD puts the round and its clock on a line over the two teams. Parts and props are unchanged.

fixed.member: RpgCharacter, RpgStats, RpgMenuBar, Profile, Loadout, RacingGarage
fixed.summary: Redrawn in the same look: the character sheet and its stats on cut cards with ruled rows and condensed tabular figures, equipment slots cut and in their rarity, the chosen one ringed in the accent; the menu bar's tabs as tracked capitals with the chosen one underlined in the accent; the profile's rank on a gold tag and each figure on a cut plate; the loadout's items as cut plates with Equipped on a green tag and the price in gold, long names wrapping; the garage's shown car picture filling the page under a shade, its name in large slanted capitals, the ratings and the action on a cut card and the cars as cut tiles. Parts and props are unchanged.

A button with a key cap is named by its words alone: the lobby's Ready up and Cancel ready, the draft's Lock in, the loadout's Back and Equip and the garage's Back no longer read the key before the word.

At 150 % text on a desktop the verdict, the grade and the stat plates follow the text scale only up to a share of the screen's height, so the head no longer fills the top half and the stat figures show whole above the actions.

fixed: World-label placement encodes floating-point candidate order in place before sorting, preserving every coordinate bit without a second key buffer.

fixed.summary: Auto-height elements positioned by percentage, calculated or anchor insets measure their content at the resolved width, avoiding extra blank lines in wrapping columns and incorrect bottom placement.
Multiline target rows reserve vertical padding so the Watching caption stays clear of the button rim.
Level seals fit their label and level instead of scrolling two lines inside a fixed-height badge.

A chapter's header (its name, stars and star meter) holds to the top of the path while its levels scroll under it, so a path that opens scrolled to the level to play no longer shows the header half cut.
On a phone the road no longer runs under the Play plate: below a disc with words (Play, Open, Selected) it leaves only after a gap under them.

Size query containers exclude their descendants from intrinsic sizing on the queried axes, preventing container-unit text in content-sized flex items from feeding back into their own size and dropping the UI frame.

Transitions and keyframes now animate registered custom properties by their CSS types before resolving dependent variables, inherited values, layout and native-part paint. Interrupted and reversed transitions and saved motion resume from their current computed values; unregistered properties remain discrete.
UI registration can read the initialized locale, translations and localized formatters on both hosts; loading string tables and changing the locale remain prohibited during registration.

Redrawn to the approved results mockup in smoked glass and lit edges over the dimmed scene: the results verdict set large in a gold or red lit fill over a rule, the level in an octagon beside a leaning XP bar, the grade on a hexagon, Summary, Graphs and Scoreboard as fit tabs that show whole on a 390 px phone at 150 % text, stats on cut plates (a best in gold) and rewards as octagon art with the amount on a tag and the name under it; the leaderboard's segmented switch, the league's plate, the top three on gold, silver and bronze, the promotion zone edged green and the player's row pinned lit, with the score under the name on a narrow row; game over's red verdict, score against the best and the revive offer's gold ring and Revive button.

Redrawn bare over the stage in the results family's look: RhythmResults' slanted grade in the result's fill, its marks on cut tags and every figure on a cut plate under its name, its tally in each judgement's ink; RacingResults' player's place set large in the HUD's accent beside their time and points, over the classification as the racing HUD's tower; PuzzleSummary on a cut card with the earned stars drawn large in the star rating's glyph, popping in turn; ArenaScoreboard's teams side by side where the board is wide, each in its colour, the local row lit and a disconnected player's name kept, dimmed, beside its tag. Key caps hide under touch. Parts and props are unchanged.
A button with a key cap is named by its words alone: RacingResults' Retry reads Retry and RhythmResults' Next reads Next, not "X Retry" or "Esc Next".

Flat normal-blended shape paints retain geometry during supported transform and opacity animation, with generation-checked emitted shapes and changed-instance GPU uploads. Paint, clipping, topology and unsupported content changes keep the ordinary rendering path; both hosts use the same mechanism.

Warmed scalar class retargets keep their built-in button when CSS motion retains only idle before-change bookkeeping. The retained path commits the new recipe without rebuilding; computed-value transitions and animations still use the full path.
List and eject the six new rhythm HUD components through the built-in component catalogue.

fixed: Button content keeps its plate's text color when CJK spacing or other rich-text features are used, while explicitly colored inline runs retain their own ink.
CSS root tokens finish in shared storage, avoiding repeated token-overlay copies and comparisons when controls change state.

fixed.summary: Overlapping font strokes generate distance fields from their filled outline boundary, removing translucent seams and ghost strokes inside enlarged runtime glyphs while preserving counters and exterior edges.

fixed: New scroll containers in screen layers now honor scroll-initial-target on their first frame, after their viewport and content have been laid out.

fixed.summary: A level number of four or more figures (1,016) steps down to a share of its disc's width, so it stays inside the disc's ring at any text size.
The Preview button's accessible name is its words alone (Preview, or Previewing while it plays); its key cap no longer joins the name as "X Preview".
The time label rides under the played end of the line through a clamp() margin, held inside the line's ends at the start and the end of the song.
A title or byline too long for the plate scrolls instead of ending in an ellipsis.

Sharp CSS text-shadow halos draw without offscreen filter captures, leaving masks intact on dense HUDs instead of painting the compass strip as an opaque black band. Blurred and mixed shadow lists keep their whole-silhouette filters.
A level up's rays stop at the ring: an opaque shade fills the ring, so the word and the figure read on clear ground, and the word stands clear of the figure.

Stacked world labels mark each blocker's vertical collision interval once rather than rescanning the blockers for successive candidate positions. Placement choices, collision gaps and fallback behavior are unchanged.

Unchanged world wrappers reuse their kept paint instead of repainting their descendants every tick. Depth, occlusion and layer changes still invalidate the wrapped drawing, including when a wrapper appears or disappears.

fixed: Retained UI frames stream command splices into their final item list, avoiding large temporary command and item buffers without changing draw order or levels.

fixed.summary: SVGs with a viewBox and one definite CSS size derive their auto axis from the intrinsic aspect ratio, including percentage sizes; an explicit aspect-ratio still overrides it.
Synthetic bold text now refreshes its ink growth and one-device-pixel second copy when an inherited transform changes its device scale, matching fresh painting on both hosts.
Text-clipped backgrounds clear the whole box outside the glyph mask, so wide headings no longer leave solid gradient rectangles beyond their letters.
The generated component catalogue lists text-overflow's clip, ellipsis, string and -og-scroll travel/hold values instead of generic lengths.

CSS text shadows blur the complete glyph silhouette with a Gaussian and composite in sRGB space, preserving soft halos beyond tight line boxes without the atlas's rectangular cutoff. Authored overflow clips still apply.

The added or removed presence tag shows its translated label in the label's own case (Added, Removed), instead of forcing it to upper case, so the tag reads as the string a game or locale supplies and a reader of the card sees that string. A game that wants the tag in upper case sets text-transform on ::part(TooltipCard.change).
Store small world drawing markers directly in draw commands so rebuilding and copying moving-anchor lists does not allocate a box for each marker.

Waypoints avoid authored player reserves and retain only their own chevron; interaction prompts avoid telegraph danger bounds, including the rim. The world review sheet explicitly reserves its painted player's silhouette. Long nameplates fit the viewport at enlarged text scale, reserving the level badge before the name's edge-faded scrolling window. Anchor containment respects descendant transforms, preserving the inset for targeted nameplates near a screen edge.
Moving world wrappers preserve unchanged local paint while projection, occlusion and edge arrows are regenerated for the current frame.
World labels and damage numbers reuse unchanged measured widths across frames, invalidating them when fonts or their mass template change.

fixed: World UI reuses anchor wrapper and transformed-bounds traversal buffers across frames without changing placement or drawing.

fixed.summary: Nameplate, SpeechBubble and Waypoint previews frame the label's paint rather than extending to its ground marker. Other world crops and full-frame edge-clamped fixtures retain their framing.

World component reference previews now frame their subject instead of an empty stage, with level label cameras, 35° ground views, padded paint bounds and faint metre-grid/subject-post context. Deliberately edge-clamped fixtures retain their original camera and full frame.
World HUD frames reuse traversal indexes and avoid transient non-text glyph-scan and constant mass-timeline allocations without changing their draw order or number formatting.

The lit fog's shafts, what a 3D fluid and a transmissive material refract, and the water under a waterline no longer shift with the camera's distance from the render origin. Each rebuilt its view ray, and transmission its opaque depth, from points unprojected at the camera's place, rounded at its distance from the origin: 5 km out the shafts moved and glass drew rings in what it refracted. They read the view ray built from the camera's rotation and projection alone, as the sky does.

fixed: Volumetric spot beams integrate inside their finite cones instead of disappearing between depth samples. Froxel fog resolves spots on the pixel ray with the grid's extinction, so narrow beams retain their silhouette instead of breaking into lit and unlit blocks. Grid dimensions, depth strata and clustered-light limits are unchanged.

fixed.summary: A page whose Content-Security-Policy has no `'unsafe-eval'`, such as `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, now transcodes its Basis KTX2 textures. Before, every transcode under such a policy failed with "Evaluating a string as JavaScript violates the following Content Security Policy directive", and the page drew without its textures. The Basis transcoder (`basis/basis_transcoder.js`, Basis Universal v1.50 as before) is rebuilt so that its glue never calls `eval()` or `new Function()`. It is now an ES module, which the engine Worker and its transcoding pool import instead of evaluating its text.

On the web host an SDR display no longer gets an extended-range (HDR) canvas, which clipped everything above SDR white: og.Sky drew white by day where the native host draws it blue. The engine's Worker cannot ask `(dynamic-range: high)`, so the renderer took every display for HDR; the page now asks and tells it, and `best` stays at standard range (Display P3 where offered) on an SDR display. RenderCapabilities.hdr is false there.

On the web, a Basis-coded texture of a bundle opened at run time that no streaming group holds (an HLOD proxy's, or a model loaded outside any cell group) loads: the web host hands it to the Worker's transcoder when it is first used and answers pending until the Worker has transcoded it, so its model stays hidden for that time and then draws, as natively. Before, its load failed with "not transcoded": the Worker transcodes only the game's own bundle at boot and streaming groups' packs, and the web host has no Basis transcoder of its own.

On the web, every file of a bundle opened at run time is fetched against the Subresource Integrity its own manifest lists (`integrity "sha384-…"`), as a package from an asset base is: bytes that differ from what was cooked fail their load once, naming the integrity, instead of loading as if intact. As there, the browser does not tell a refused hash from a network failure, so such a fetch is not tried again.

On the web, a streaming group's pack from a bundle opened at run time has its Basis textures transcoded against that bundle's own manifest, as the game's packs are against the game's. Before, the Worker looked them up in the game's manifest, found none and handed the pack over untranscoded, and the web host, which has no Basis transcoder of its own, could not load those textures.

On the web, a streaming group's Basis textures are transcoded on other Workers, not on the engine's: a cell's load no longer stops the frames while its pack's textures transcode. Before, every texture of a pack was transcoded on the engine's Worker one after another without a frame between them, and the first pack of a session started the transcoder there too. Measured in desktop Chromium with 14 textures of 1024x1024 to BC7 per pack and the engine's side stood in: the longest stop went from about 280 ms (the first pack) and 120 to 160 ms (each later one) to 5 to 12 ms, where an idle loop already shows 4 to 6 ms, and a later pack is ready in about 70 ms where it took about 130. The Workers start with the first such texture (up to four, on machines with the cores for them) and stay. Where a Worker cannot start, the engine's Worker transcodes as before. The textures handed to the engine, world state and hashes are unchanged.

A built page runs whole under a strict Content-Security-Policy, `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, lanes included. index.html has no inline script or style: the shell's CSS is shell.css and a publish build's install hook is install.js, both content-hashed. Every Worker starts from a file on the page's origin, never a `blob:` URL. The lanes pool's helper starts its Workers from its own URL, and the audio decoder (audio-decoder.js) and the AV1 fallback (av1/av1-worker.js) are files of the build. Before, such a policy left the shell unstyled with its play gate off screen, and the engine single-threaded. SVG images in UI documents still need `img-src blob:` (docs/web-export.md §Hosting).

Inside a system or hook, world.has answers from the entity's archetype, as world.get does, whatever the caller's query declares. It read the caller's query views, so in a hook (which has none) it was always false.

An entity's name is free again once its despawn applies: inside a system when the system returns (a later system of the same tick, a later tick or a call between ticks may spawn the name again), between ticks at once. It stayed taken until a probe call brought the runtime's name table in line, so plain og run and published games refused the spawn while og test and og run --json did not.

Keep zoom-blur highlights continuous and sharp with three stratified eight-tap radial stages instead of repeated dotted copies or hundreds of full-resolution reads; centre-crossing strengths retain direct adaptive integration.

breaking.change: A walk gains speed at its new acceleration (0 uses 4 m/s²) instead of starting at full speed in its first tick, and the mover keeps its speed through a target when another walkTo or a jump is queued after it: it brakes only to the next walk's speed (less by the corner, none past a right angle) or to a jump's flight speed, and a jump's preparation keeps moving at the speed it arrives with, so a jump after a walk takes off running. Walks take longer from rest and chained walks arrive sooner, so a game's world steps differently and its world_hash moves. The og.motion state is saved as MOTION5 (each goal's acceleration and the mover's speed); a MOTION4 save restores with its walks at full speed from rest, as it ran.
breaking.fix: Nothing to edit for the new timing. A game whose logic needs the old instant start passes a large acceleration, such as `acceleration: 1000`; one that needs a stop at a target between two walks queues og.motion.pose or face between them. Re-record golden hashes of games that use walkTo.

breaking.change: Documents are version 2, the CSS dialect (docs/ui.md §10.4): an element's look and layout are CSS declarations (`width: stretch; max-width: 640px`, `padding: 8px 12px`, `background: var(--panel-raised)`, `font: var(--text-caption)`, `transition: -og-spring(300ms, 0.1)`), interaction states are pseudo-classes (`:hover`, `:active`, `:focus-visible`, `:disabled`), breakpoints `@media phone` and the game's extensions `-og-` properties. A version 1 document no longer loads; the subset is strict, so an unknown property or value is an error that names the form to write.
breaking.fix: Run `og ui migrate assets` (and on any other directory of .ogt documents): it rewrites each version 1 screen and component line for line with its comments, after checking the two read as the same document. Code that writes document text writes the version 2 form.

breaking.change: Styles are version 3, the CSS dialect (docs/ui.md §12.7): a dressing is a selector block (`Button::base.primary:hover { … }`, `Slot::frame[rarity=epic] { … }`), colour and length tokens are custom properties (`palette { --panel-raised: #211a15 }`, `space { --space-xs: 4px }`), and what a dressing sets is declarations (`-og-slice`, `-og-fill`, `-og-stroke`, `-og-effect`, `box-shadow`, `opacity`). og style new, upgrade, pack and art write version 3; versions 1 and 2 still load. The probe's UI pick (`pickUi`) names parts and matched rules in the selector form (`Button::base.primary`).
breaking.fix: Run `og ui migrate assets/styles` to rewrite a version 2 style as version 3, line for line with its comments, after checking the two parse to the same style. Code that appends dressings to a style's text writes the selector form.

breaking.member: og.ui layer stack order, pop and replace
breaking.change: The layer stack is ordered by layer kind (hud, menu, modal, popover, toast, tooltip, system), then by push order, as Unreal CommonUI's layer groups are: a modal pushed before a menu stays over it, and a toast pushed before a modal stays over it. og.ui.pop, og.ui.replace, a document's `pop` and Back act on the active layer (the top one whose input is menu or all; the topmost with none), not the topmost: a toast over a pause menu no longer swallows Back or a pop meant for the menu, and a document's pop pops its own layer.
breaking.fix: Nothing for most games. A game that pushed a toast or HUD screen and called og.ui.pop to remove it while a menu was open removes it by pushing it as a menu, or empties its viewmodel instead; a game that read the last of og.ui.layers as the focused layer reads the one whose active is true.

breaking.member: particle emitters: lit mesh blend default
breaking.change: An emitter drawn as lit meshes (render mesh with lit true) and no blend line now blends alpha, not additive: a solid chip, shard or splinter covers what is behind it instead of being added onto it, where a lit grey chip glowed white. Unlit meshes, billboards and sprites still blend additive by default, and a blend line always wins.
breaking.fix: Nothing for chips, shards and splinters: they now draw solid. An emitter that meant lit meshes to glow (lit embers, magic shards) adds a blend additive line.

breaking.change: The cards scroll between the header and the actions, so their elements moved from <id>/Options/<key> to <id>/Cards/Options/<key>.
breaking.fix: Update probe paths, playtests and og.ui.bounds or openSlot lookups that name <id>/Options/ to <id>/Cards/Options/.

breaking.change: The typography hierarchy now drives legacy ramp names, including weights, tracking and breakpoint sizes. Several legacy sizes alias one semantic role; hero adds the largest step. Version 1 styles derive that hierarchy from their ramp. UI frames and wrapping can change: xl3 and xl4 follow title (a ramp xl3 30 34 draws at the title size); displayXl2, displayXl, xl7 and xl8 follow hero, which without its own line is display x 1.5 (a 60 px line drew at 81); meta follows caption.
breaking.fix: og upgrade converts v1 styles to v2, archives a v2 style's superseded ramp as comments and writes a hero line keeping what displayXl2 drew (the ramp line, else 56 60). Edit typography, not ramp. xl3: set title to the old xl3 or accept the title size (one role cannot keep both). Review heading/title/display/hero and phone/150% sheets.

breaking.change: Text in the numeric font role (font: "mono": scores, timers, HUD numerals) sets tabular lining figures (tnum lnum), and a face without tnum sets its digits on the widest figure's advance, so a ticking number holds its width. Proportional digits widen: a lone "1" from 8 px to 14, a lap time by about 3 px.
breaking.fix: Leave room where a mono number sits in a fixed width; set digits that must stay proportional in another font role (body, display). Review HUD timers and score columns in the baseline sheets.

breaking.change: Terrain rendering, sampling, navigation baking and native height-field collision choose each cell's diagonal by the smaller corner height difference. Ties retain the (-x, -z) to (+x, +z) split. Terrain contacts can change simulation hashes.

breaking.change: Rest lengths and pinTop use the skeleton's skinned rest shape, including nonidentity bind transforms. Garment simulation hashes change. ActionState: pressed → justPressed, released → justReleased. og.Input: pressed() → justPressed(), released() → justReleased(), buttonPressed() → buttonJustPressed(), buttonReleased() → buttonJustReleased(), pressed0-3 → justPressed0-3, released0-3 → justReleased0-3, buttonsPressed → buttonsJustPressed, buttonsReleased → buttonsJustReleased. og.Pointers: pressed() → justPressed(), released() → justReleased(), pressedMask → justPressedMask, releasedMask → justReleasedMask. og.Gamepad: pressed() → justPressed(), released() → justReleased(), pressed0-7 → justPressed0-7, released0-7 → justReleased0-7. The old names are gone, so old code fails to compile instead of reading another state.
breaking.fix: Rename by the table. Where code meant the held state, use down (input.down, buttonDown, pointers.down, pads.down, ActionState.down), not justPressed.

breaking.change: World hashes name each record's fields, so the renamed component fields above move the hash of a world that holds one (og.Input, og.Pointers, og.Gamepad, og.Collider, og.Light2D, og.PlatformerController, og.AiAgent, og.Perception, og.Lockstep, og.VirtualCamera, og.CameraView, og.Mirror, og.Afterimage, og.ReflectionProbe). A trace recorded on an earlier version names the old fields, so og replay compare reports a difference at its first tick. No tick steps differently, and a save from an earlier version loads with its values under the new names.
breaking.fix: Re-record replay traces and pinned world hashes on this version.

breaking.change: Renamed selector to ReactiveFallback, matching its every-tick priority recheck and interruption semantics.
breaking.fix: Rename selector nodes to ReactiveFallback; no alias remains.

breaking.change: Renamed sequence to ReactiveSequence, matching its every-tick condition recheck.
breaking.fix: Rename sequence nodes to ReactiveSequence, not Sequence.

breaking.change: Renamed steps to Sequence: resumes running children and restarts after failure, success or interruption.
breaking.fix: Rename steps nodes to Sequence; this is not SequenceWithMemory.

breaking.change: Renamed invert to Inverter.
breaking.fix: Rename invert nodes to Inverter.

breaking.change: Renamed succeed to ForceSuccess; running remains running.
breaking.fix: Rename succeed nodes to ForceSuccess.

breaking.change: Renamed state enter actions to entry; exit and tick-machine timing are unchanged.
breaking.fix: Rename state enter blocks to entry; do not treat the machine as an XState actor.

breaking.change: Renamed rate-valued pitch to playbackRate in AudioSource, AudioEvent and reflected AudioPlayback, with no alias.
breaking.fix: Use playbackRate; 2 still doubles pitch and halves duration. pitchJitter remains semitones. ECS lifetime and startAt world seconds are unchanged.

breaking.change: Timeline and VFX sound keys use playbackRate instead of pitch.
breaking.fix: Rename sound key pitch to playbackRate. Do not rename procedural SFX pitch: it changes oscillator frequency independently of length.

breaking.change: UI SoundEvent, UiMotionEvent and styleTokens feedback JSON use playbackRate instead of pitch.
breaking.fix: Rename rate fields in UI sound descriptions and event consumers; camera tilt and sports-pitch fields are unchanged.

breaking.change: Action polling names say the state: actionDown→isActionDown, actionPressed→isActionJustPressed, actionReleased→isActionJustReleased, actionHeld→isActionHeld. No aliases remain.
breaking.fix: Use isActionDown for continuous down state and the Just variants for tick edges; isActionHeld still tests holdMs.

breaking.change: Renamed context to actionMap in ActionDesc, ActionInfo and BindingConflict; setContexts/contexts become setActionMaps/actionMaps.
breaking.fix: Rename map fields and calls. Action names remain world-global, map priority and W3C control names are unchanged.

breaking.change: Uses typed dynamic/fixed/kinematic strings instead of BODY_* numeric constants; fixed names Rapier's Fixed semantics.
breaking.fix: Use kind: 'fixed' instead of BODY_STATIC and the corresponding strings for other modes. Kinematic still integrates Velocity and treats Transform writes as teleports.

breaking.change: raycast, raycastAll and shapeCast are now castRay, castRayAll and castShape, without aliases.
breaking.fix: Rename the calls; castRayAll remains an engine-owned sorted, capped query. Box sizes remain full extents and applyForce still lasts one tick.

breaking.change: Collider.sensor and RigidBody.ccd are booleans instead of numeric flags.
breaking.fix: Use true/false. Contact.sensor remains the pair's sensor bitmask.

breaking.change: Uses GSAP names: linear→none, quad→power1, cubic→power2, quart→power3, and dotted in/out/inOut suffixes for every family. No old aliases remain. Expo and back.inOut now use GSAP 3.15.0 maths rather than the old Penner formulas.
breaking.fix: Use GSAP names in tween, camera and cutscene keys; expect changed intermediate samples for expo and back.inOut.

breaking.change: Renamed loops to repeat; still counts extra cycles, with -1 forever.
breaking.fix: Replace loops with repeat in tween descriptions.

breaking.change: Renamed loops to repeat for sequence and parallel groups.
breaking.fix: Replace loops with repeat in group descriptions.

breaking.change: UI tween transitions and eased keyframes use the shared GSAP Ease names; EaseName is removed without aliases.
breaking.fix: Use none for linear. Preserve the former out, exit and inOut curves with bezier arrays [0.23,1,0.32,1], [0.4,0,1,1] and [0.65,0,0.35,1], not approximate GSAP names.

breaking.change: world.get and world.set cross as the component's packed bytes in the shared buffer (og_host_shared), asked for by the component's number, not as JSON by name. The addon and the wasm module gain three lifecycle exports, and the binding ids after them move up. Game code is unchanged: world.get and world.set answer the same Results with the same values, key order and reasons, and worlds, snapshots and world hashes are the same bytes.
breaking.fix: Nothing in a game. A host's native addon or wasm module and the packages/engine runtime that loads it must be the same engine version, as a release always ships them.

breaking.change: A system's call no longer carries text. Its time scale and its query's archetypes are numbers in a shared buffer (og_host_shared); a column is asked for by the component's number (og_engine_component_id), not its name. og_query_archetypes, og_archetype_view_has and og_archetype_view_column are gone from the addon and the wasm module, and the binding ids after them move down. Game code is unchanged: Query.archetypes, ArchetypeView.has and ArchetypeView.column answer as before, and worlds, snapshots and world hashes are the same bytes.
breaking.fix: Nothing in a game. A host's native addon or wasm module and the packages/engine runtime that loads it must be the same engine version, as a release always ships them.

breaking.change: capture fits its PNG to a long side of 1280 (CAPTURE_FIT) by default, box-filtered, the size a model reads a whole frame at; a frame asked at a larger size, or a render target above 1280, now answers smaller. The answer also carries scale (PNG pixels per CSS pixel) and region.
breaking.fix: Pass fit 0 to keep the rendered size: `probe.capture(w, h, 0)`, or `{ "width": w, "height": h, "fit": 0 }` over the wire.

breaking.change: `cascade_map`, the sun's shadow cascades a lit shader has in scope, is now a `texture_storage_2d_array<r32float, read>` instead of a `texture_2d_array<f32>`, so it takes none of a lit pipeline's sixteen texture slots. Every engine read of it was already a `textureLoad`; the picture is unchanged.
breaking.fix: Drop the mip level from a `textureLoad(cascade_map, at, layer, 0)` in your material shader: `textureLoad(cascade_map, at, layer)`.

breaking.change: OG9101 (state outside the world) now also covers state a closure keeps and state on an imported object. A let, var, container const or parameter of a function, written by a closure handed to defineSystem or og.game (directly, by name, or from a callback inside it), is an error: it lives in that closure from tick to tick, outside the world snapshot. So is an object imported from another of the game's files (a relative import) written through a member in a function (`shared.count++`). A closure only called while its function runs (a forEach callback summing into a local) is not reported; a closure registered by its caller after being returned, a method called on an imported object and state on a class instance are still not seen.
breaking.fix: Keep the state in a component or a resource. --no-check runs anyway.

breaking.member: UI document scoped CSS (block-level text width)
breaking.change:
A

, a heading (

…

) or a text displayed block in a block's flow is now as wide as its containing block, as a CSS block box is, instead of only as wide as its text. Its background, border and hit area span the line, and column-span: all spans every column. A , , or a text displayed inline or inline-block still fits its text.
breaking.fix: Where a paragraph or heading should be only as wide as its text, give it `width: fit-content` (or `display: inline-block`).

breaking.member: UI: container queries and units through the container's writing mode
breaking.change: `@container (inline-size …)` and `(block-size …)` and the `cqi`, `cqb`, `cqmin` and `cqmax` units read a container's axes as its own writing mode names them: in a vertical container `inline-size` and `cqi` are its height. `cqw` and `cqh` read the nearest container that contains that physical axis, and a vertical `inline-size` container no longer answers `width` conditions. Horizontal documents are unchanged.
breaking.fix: A document that queries a vertical container's width writes `block-size` (and `cqb`), or gives the container `container-type: size`.

breaking.member: UI: `vi` and `vb` follow the root's writing mode; container variants read the inline size
breaking.change: `vi` and `vb` are the viewport's height and width when the document root's writing mode is vertical (CSS Values 4), not always its width and height. An immediate-mode `Props` variant with `Query::container` reads its element's inline size, a vertical element's height, and its patch keeps physical sides. Horizontal documents and elements are unchanged.
breaking.fix: A vertical document that meant the viewport's width writes `vw` (or `vh` for its height); a container variant on a vertical element states its range against the element's height.

breaking.member: UI: text on a path in a vertical element
breaking.change: Text on a path (`-og-text-path`) in a `vertical-*` or `sideways-*` writing mode is set as a vertical line along the path: upright clusters stand one vertical advance long with their tops back along the path, and sideways runs lie along it. It was set as horizontal text. Its box is unchanged (the path's extent).
breaking.fix: Text that should read as horizontal along a path sets `writing-mode: horizontal-tb` on the path text.

breaking.change: Layout change: a document's flex item that declares no flex, flex-grow, flex-shrink or flex-basis is CSS's initial `flex: 0 1 auto`, so an item with a definite width or height now shrinks with its siblings when its line overflows, as in a browser. It used to keep its size and overflow the line. An or with a px size shrinks no smaller than that size (its natural size). The built-in main menu and carousel keep their sizes.
breaking.fix: Give an item that must keep its size along an overflowing line `flex-shrink: 0` (or `flex: none`).

breaking.member: UI CSS position: absolute and fixed (top, right, bottom, left, inset)
breaking.change: Layout change: an absolute or fixed box's insets and percentage sizes are measured from its containing block's padding edge, inside the holder's border, as in CSS. They were measured from the holder's outer (border) edge, so a box at top: 0; left: 0 sat on the holder's border.
breaking.fix: Where an inset made up for the border (top: 2px under a 2px border), set it back to the intended distance from the padding edge (top: 0).

breaking.member: UI CSS white-space, white-space-collapse, tab-size and text-wrap
breaking.change:
Text change: a text's white space is processed from its computed white-space at build time, for bound text ({$value}, {expr}) and text with inline elements as for literal text. Before, the parser collapsed every text's spaces and line breaks HTML's way unless it was plain literal text, so pre, pre-line, pre-wrap, break-spaces and tab-size did nothing to a bound string, and a bound string under normal kept its runs of spaces and newlines as written. A
stays a line break under every value.
breaking.fix: A text that relied on a bound string's newlines or repeated spaces showing under the default white-space gives the element `white-space: pre-line` (newlines) or `white-space: pre-wrap` (spaces and newlines).

breaking.change: A block whose children lie in lines (it holds an inline-level box) beside a float is no longer narrowed whole as if it started its own formatting context: its lines are shortened one by one and those below the floats take the full width, and a float inside it now reaches the boxes after it.
breaking.fix: Give the block display: flow-root to keep it narrowed whole beside the floats and holding its own floats.

breaking.change: @font-face font-weight and font-stretch (font-width) default to auto, as CSS Fonts 4 says: a variable font's wght or wdth range, else 400 and 100 %. og_ui::css::FontFace's weight and stretch are Option (None: auto).
breaking.fix: Declare font-weight or font-stretch on an @font-face whose variable font should keep one weight or width; read FontFace.weight and .stretch as Option.

breaking.change: ui-monospace and ui-rounded no longer stand in for a style without a mono or rounded face of its own (ui-rounded used to take the display face), and ui-serif and math no longer take the body face ahead of later families: each matches nothing there and the next family in the list draws. FontFamily gains a Ui variant.
breaking.fix: End a family list with the generic that should stand in (monospace, sans-serif, fantasy), as in a browser.

breaking.change: In a grid, justify-content aligns the tracks (CSS Box Alignment) instead of each item in its cell, and justify-content: normal leaves auto tracks to stretch into the free room.
breaking.fix: To align items in their cells, write justify-items (or justify-self on the item).

breaking.member: UI document scoped CSS (the root element's auto width)
breaking.change: A document's root element with width: auto now fills the column or stack it is mounted in, as CSS's root block fills the initial containing block, instead of shrinking to fit its content. A wider child's min-content no longer widens the whole document past the viewport, so max-width: 100% and aspect-ratio below it hold to the viewport (a 640px card with max-width: 100% in a 16px-padded root at a 390 viewport is 358×201, not 640×360).
breaking.fix: Where a component should size to its content, give its root element `width: fit-content`.

breaking.change: CSS easing keywords in transition now use the CSS curves (ease-out is cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.58, 1)), not the style's own curves. animation no longer requires forwards, a missing 0% or 100% keyframe takes the element's value, and conditional animations are allowed.
breaking.fix: Recook documents. For the style's curves write the motion token, for example transition: opacity var(--motion-ui), or an explicit cubic-bezier(). Add forwards (or both) where an animation should hold its last keyframe.

breaking.change: Beam.tile (texture repeats per metre) is uvTile, metres per repeat, as og.Trail.uvTile and RibbonDesc.uvTile: one tiling for every strip. 0 now stretches the texture once from the entity to `end`; the default stays one repeat per metre. A saved og.Beam keeps its look (version 3 and a save step take the reciprocal).
breaking.fix: Rename tile to uvTile and give it 1 / the old value (tile 2 becomes uvTile 0.5).

breaking.change: SpriteBlend and StripBlend are one enum, Blend: alpha 0 and additive 1 everywhere (StripBlend had additive 0). og.Trail, og.Beam and RibbonDesc still default to additive, sprites to alpha; the variant strings are unchanged, so `blend: "alpha"` means what it did. A saved og.Trail or og.Beam keeps its blend (og.Trail and og.Beam take version 2 and a save step).
breaking.fix: Rename the type SpriteBlend or StripBlend to Blend where game code names it.

breaking.change: SpriteBlend is now Blend (see StripBlend).
breaking.fix: Rename SpriteBlend to Blend.

breaking.change: A composed effect's `flash` element is `glow` from `type vfx` version 2, so it no longer shares its name with og.tween.flash and PostEffects.flash; VfxInfo.elements reports it as `glow`. Version 1 files still load, their `flash` read as `glow`; a version 2 file that says `flash` is refused with the new name. og vfx import and the cook's Effekseer conversion write version 2.
breaking.fix: Write `glow { ... }` and `version 2` in a type vfx file (og upgrade rewrites a version 1 file's top-level flash elements).

breaking.change: og.Wind is the world's wind and `strength` is removed: `speed` is how fast the air moves (m/s, 0 by default: still), and vegetation leans 0.05 of its height for each m/s of it. `speed` used to be how fast the gusts travelled (3 by default) beside a separate lean.
breaking.fix: Set `speed` to the old `strength / 0.05` (a strength of 0.3 is 6 m/s) and drop `strength`. A save restores that way by itself.

breaking.change: Both are added to og.Wind (the clouds take it at twice its speed) and default to no drift of their own: clouds were carried at (12, 0.4, 4) and rain and snow at (1.5, 0, 0.5) whatever og.Wind said.
breaking.fix: Set og.Wind's direction and speed for a world whose clouds, weather and vegetation move together; for the old motion without it, set og.Clouds.wind to (12, 0.4, 4) and og.Weather.wind to (1.5, 0, 0.5).

breaking.change: og.Wind now pushes every rope, cloth and garment (its velocity in m/s as an acceleration), and each one's `wind` is added to it. They ignored og.Wind before, so a world with both moves differently.
breaking.fix: Nothing where the two should agree. For one that must hang still in a wind, set its `wind` to the opposite of og.Wind's velocity.

breaking.change: With followRotation the offset is x to the entity's right, y up and z behind it. It was turned by the entity's rotation as it stood, which put the default offset (0, 2, 6) six metres in front of an entity facing its +Z (a vehicle, a nav or motion agent), looking at its face.
breaking.fix: Where a game set followRotation and chose an offset by hand, negate the offset's x and z; a game that left the default now gets the camera behind the entity.

breaking.change: followRotation now turns followOffset with the followed entity (x to its right, y up, z behind it), and a shot with no lookAt keeps its own og.Transform rotation. Both read a rotation that was always the identity, so the offset stayed in world axes and such a shot looked down world -Z.
breaking.fix: Nothing where followRotation is off and the shot's entity is not rotated. A shot that set followRotation, or a rotated shot with no lookAt, now does what its fields say; re-record replays and pinned hashes of worlds with one.

breaking.change: SaveEdit.types answers a Result, as the host always did: { ok: true, value: SaveType[] }, refused once the save is closed. It used to be typed as the bare list, and the runtime answered [] for a closed save.
breaking.fix: Check `.ok` and read `.value`: `const t = edit.types(); if (t.ok) for (const type of t.value) ...`.

breaking.change: og.render.display is typed DisplayInfo | null: it answers null when the world has no engine or its renderer cannot be read at that moment, which it always did but the type did not say.
breaking.fix: Check for null before reading the answer: `const d = og.render.display(world); if (d) save(d.settings);`.

breaking.change: The inspector's panel is a built-in document now, styled only by tokens, so dump_inspector names its elements by the document's ids: a component's or resource's header is Inspector/Detail/Group#C:<Component>/Section (Group#R:<Resource>/Section), a field's row Inspector/Detail/Group#…/Field#<target>/Row and its text boxes …/Row/Part#<target>%23<n>, a hierarchy row Inspector/Tree/Row#<bits>/Entry#<bits>/Label. The toolbar keeps its paths (Inspector/Bar/Save, Inspector/Tools/Undo, Inspector/View/Strip/Track/Item#1).
breaking.fix: Find a field's text box by its set target: Inspector/Detail/F:Score.best/P0 is Inspector/Detail/Group#R:Score/Field#Score.best/Row/Part#Score.best%230, and Inspector/Detail/S:Score is Inspector/Detail/Group#R:Score/Section.

breaking.change: The style catalogue is twelve looks, every one offered to a new game: cinematic-realism, anime-cel-3d, inked-comic-3d, painterly-3d, faceted-low-poly, low-resolution-3d, pixel (was 16bit-pixel), minimal-geometric, neon-vector, toy-3d (new), cartoon-2d (new) and pixel-3d-hybrid. The look.frozen mark and the refusal of a frozen look are gone. Removed presets, previews and catalogue entries, with nothing resolving them: 16bit-pixel (now pixel); folded into a kept look's variant: muted-cinematic-3d (cinematic-realism muted), bold-comic-illustration and heavy-ink-shadows (inked-comic-3d bold-comic, heavy-ink), lush-painted-worlds, luminous-layered-painting and expressionist-painting (painterly-3d lush, luminous-layers, expressionist), monochrome-dither-3d (low-resolution-3d monochrome-dither), 8bit-pixel, monochrome-pixel, detailed-pixel, luminous-pixel, coarse-pixel and topdown-tile-pixel (pixel 8bit, monochrome, detailed, luminous, coarse, topdown), layered-silhouette (minimal-geometric layered-silhouette), voxel-worlds, sculpted-clay, miniature-diorama and paper-craft (toy-3d voxel, clay, diorama, paper), watercolor-wash, decorative-storybook and rubber-hose-animation (cartoon-2d watercolor, storybook, rubber-hose); deleted outright: illuminated-manuscript, black-figure-pottery, classical-painting-collage, gothic-contour, detailed-doodle and pencil-hatching. An old slug is an unknown look: extends, create and presetLook refuse it as any unknown name. painterly-3d and pixel-3d-hybrid now name ui "fantasy", neon-vector ui "scifi" and draws on a black sky, toy-3d and cartoon-2d ui "cartoon"; neon-vector's support is content (its line art is authored).
breaking.fix: Extend one of the twelve. For a removed style, extend its kept look and name the variant: `extends "pixel"` with `variant "8bit"`, `extends "toy-3d"` with `variant "voxel"`; for 16bit-pixel, `extends "pixel"`. For a deleted one, pick the nearest look (cartoon-2d for the manuscript, pottery, collage, gothic and doodle styles, inked-comic-3d for pencil-hatching).

breaking.change: A game file's module-scope let or var written from a function, or a module-scope container ([], {}, new Map, new Set, a typed array) mutated from one, is now an og check error (OG9101) instead of a warning in the first log: state in a JS module is outside the world snapshot and the presentation checkpoint, so a restore, a rollback or a fork does not bring it back. og run, og test and og build stop on it as on a type error. The check parses and resolves names (a local shadowing a module name is its own; a write as the module loads is not state); playtests and tests are not checked.
breaking.fix: Keep the state in a component or a resource, or derive it again where it is needed (og.load answers the same handles for a path loaded before). --no-check runs anyway.

breaking.change: A font's shaped forms (ligatures, joined letters, OpenType features' alternates) are keyed by glyph id past Unicode (0x110000 + id) instead of as the private-use characters U+F0000 + id, which collided with fonts that map characters there (icon fonts): such a character drew another glyph or failed to cook. The font blob is version 2; one cooked by an earlier engine is refused when it loads. A saved UI state of the previous version upgrades, its frozen texts' shaped forms read as glyph ids.
breaking.fix: Cook the project again (`og cook`). Every font recooks with the same charset, glyphs, pages and run-time mode; only the keys of its shaped forms move.

breaking.change: Each screen and component document is typed from its contract: `og ui types` writes `.og/types/ui/<name>.d.ts` (its props, the events it can send, its slots) and og check, run, build and dev write them before they check. These functions take the document's name as a type parameter, so for a declared name the viewmodel or props must match the contract (every prop given, of its type; a list's items as its fixtures show them) and og.ui.screenVm answers that type. A partial viewmodel or a prop of the wrong type no longer type-checks. A name no document declares stays untyped, as before. The wire is unchanged.
breaking.fix: Pass the whole viewmodel the document's `props` block declares (or declare the prop `any` there). A game made before this release adds ".og/types/**/*.d.ts" to its tsconfig's include to get the types.

breaking.change: og.Fluid2D steps with the solver og.Fluid3D uses: neighbours come from the spatial hash in its pair order, a particle pushed out of a solid loses its velocity into it and a little of its slide (as in 3D), and its spawn jitter differs. A 2D fluid settles to the same shape but not to the same particle positions, so the world hash of a world with one, and a snapshot or replay recorded on an earlier version, no longer match.
breaking.fix: Re-record replays and pinned hashes of worlds with an og.Fluid2D; restore no snapshot holding one across the version. No field changed.

breaking.change: An aligned follower now faces along the path as every object does: its +Z along the tangent. It used to be turned as a camera, -Z along the tangent, so a model travelled backwards. `offset` is unchanged (the path's right, up and backwards).
breaking.fix: Remove any half-turn a game added to its model or its children to face it along the path. For a camera riding a path, sample the path and set og.transform.lookAt(position, position + tangent).

breaking.change: A playtest file (`tests/*.og.ts`) is a bun:test file: describe, test and expect from "bun:test", each test awaiting `runPlaytest({ commands, ... })`, which plays the script in fresh processes of the game og test built and resolves to the PlaytestRun. `playtest()`, the default export, `PlaytestDesc.name` and `check(run, t)` with t.ok, t.equal, t.near and t.frame are removed. The script's expect: steps, invariants and require are one assertion: runPlaytest rejects with each failure. A test with no assertion fails. A frame read without a renderer outside `run.frame` now fails the test (FrameUnchecked) instead of ending the check.
breaking.fix: Write `test("what it proves", async () => { const run = await runPlaytest({ commands }); expect(run.quit).toBe(true); })`. t.ok(x) becomes expect(x).toBe(true) or a matcher on the value; t.equal compared JSON text, so use toBe for a primitive and toEqual or toStrictEqual for a structure; t.near(a, b, tol) is an absolute tolerance, `expect(Math.abs(a - b)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(tol)` (toBeCloseTo takes decimal places); t.frame(files, f) becomes run.frame(files, f). A game's tsconfig maps "bun:test" to `.og/engine/vendor/bun-types/test.d.ts`, as the template's does.

breaking.change: A publish build no longer writes the plain-name copies `origin-engine.js` and `origin-engine_bg.wasm`, nor the one-line `play.js` loader: `index.html` loads `./play.<hash>.js` directly, and every bundle, engine module and decoder exists only under its content-hashed name (docs/web-export.md §Content-hashed names; platform ask 18). A dev build keeps every plain name. A game's code is unaffected; a host, deploy script or check that reads a publish build's files by a plain name finds nothing.
breaking.fix: Read the served names from the build's og-build.json: `worker` (the engine Worker), `wasm`, `lanes.glue`/`lanes.wasm`, and `names` (each plain name to its served file, such as `names["play.js"]`).

breaking.change: Ease columns store a canonical 20-byte tag and parameter payload, not a named-only u32 enum index. Camera blendEase, soloEase and blendCurve accept the full shared timing vocabulary.
breaking.fix: Use Ease strings for every field; rebuild cooked scenes and start new recordings/snapshots containing Ease columns. Raw Uint32Array views have stride 5.

breaking.change: Removed: HDR is no longer opt-in. RenderOptions.output (left out `best`) presents extended range and Display P3 wherever the surface offers them, and the tone curve the game chose extends to the headroom instead of the LPM mapper replacing it. On an SDR display or surface nothing changes.
breaking.fix: Delete `hdr: true`. To keep a game at SDR on HDR displays, set `render: { output: "wide" }` (Display P3, standard range) or `output: "srgb"` in GameDesc.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `orthonormal_basis(n: vec3<f32>) -> mat3x3<f32>` (Duff et al.'s branch-free basis about a unit vector) in scope from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares its own `orthonormal_basis` no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's, or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader (material, post and UI shaders) now has `srgb_encode`, `srgb_decode`, `luma` and `const LUMA` (Rec.709 weights) in scope, from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares one of these names no longer compiles.
breaking.fix: Delete your own copy and call the library's (it is the standard sRGB curve and Rec.709 luminance), or rename yours.

breaking.change: Every game shader now has `is_sky_depth(d)` and `const SKY_VIEW_DEPTH` in scope, and lit material shaders `toward_eye(p)`, from the engine's one copy; a shader that declares one of these names no longer compiles.

breaking.change: The engine now reads the og.* components and resources it uses as their IDL types. breaking.change: A text's inline markup is elements: `<span>`, `<a href>`, `<b>`, `<i>`, `<ruby>`, `<rt>` and the other formatting tags inside a text are `inline` elements that class, id, attribute, structural, child and state selectors (`a:hover`) match, and every inherited text property, `vertical-align` and `display` styles their words. A document or pack rule such as `span { … }` or `.gold { … }` now reaches them, and HTML's formatting comes from the UA sheet, which rules override.
breaking.fix: Check rules whose selectors name span, a, b, i or a class that inline markup now carries; a box property (padding, background, width) on an inline element is ignored until its fragments are boxes.

breaking.change: `padding`, `border` and `margin` on a `<span>`, `<a>` or another inline element of a text were ignored; they now move the words after them and can change where its lines break.
breaking.fix: Drop inline padding or margin you did not mean to apply, or move it to a block around the text.

breaking.change: Forced Touch and Mouse density now override pointer/hover media features. Auto continues to report the device. Gamepad mode is exposed by the reflected (-og-input: pad) media feature.

breaking.change: A document's rule no longer reaches a component instance. A rule whose subject names one (#Mine, .loud, Badge, [data-tone] on <Badge id="Mine" class="loud"/>) is refused when the document is parsed; a rule that only sweeps over one (*, #Root > *) passes it by.

breaking.change: Genre kits are removed: extension.json's kind "kit" and its entry, types and components fields are refused, og ui add no longer installs a kit into assets/ui-kits/, nothing discovers assets/ui-kits/, og ui eject no longer takes <kit>/<document>, and documents under assets/ui-kits/ no longer land in a cascade layer of their own. The rpg and shooter documents are built-in components.
breaking.fix: Use a component by the name its document declares (<RpgBackpack/>, <Killfeed/>); the screen that uses it loads it. Delete assets/ui-kits/ and the og.load.document calls naming it, or keep a document you edited as the game's own (it then replaces the built-in one of its name); og ui eject <group>/<document> (rpg/backpack) copies one to edit.

breaking.change: Returns Result<number> and reports invalid timing text instead of silently substituting linear.

breaking.fix: Code that tested a screen value for null to learn the push left it out: give the prop a data-default the game never passes (such as -1 or "") and test for that, or pass the value explicitly. A prop every user must pass gets data-required, and a mount or push leaving it out is then refused with an error naming the instance and the prop.

breaking.change: A list a pushed screen iterates with {#each} has rows that each carry the key the each names ((row.id): a unique nonempty string id). breaking.fix: Give each row of an iterated list a unique string in the field the each keys it by.

breaking.change: A pushed screen whose component instance leaves out a prop the component declares data-required is refused with "<file>:<line>: <Component> leaves out its prop '<name>', which it requires (data-required); pass it", as a mounted document already is; the push used to build it with the prop unset. breaking.fix: Pass the props your own components mark data-required. The built-in components require none.

breaking.change: A document whose root is a block ({#if}, {#each}) is refused with "a document's root is one element; put the block inside it".
