fixed.member: shooter kit: CombatHud, Loadout; library StatBar
fixed.summary: Right to left, the combat HUD's corners mirror (the feed and ammunition on the left, the vitals on the right), and StatBar's damage ghost and segment blocks run from the right with its fill. The loadout's scrollbar room stays on the right beside the bar, and a slot's Equipped tag wraps under its figures when a translation leaves no room.

A required site counts as fired when any process of the playtest fired it: the script, a `then` relaunch or a room peer (an each's buckets are merged across them). It read only the first process before, so a site that fires after a relaunch could not be required.

A display frame between ticks (a 120 Hz screen on a 60 Hz tick, ProMotion) blends each og.motion agent's pose from the tick before's at the frame's alpha, as og-anim's poses are (translation and scale lerped, rotation slerped), instead of holding the tick's pose until the next. Captures, the probe and frames on a tick boundary draw the tick; the blend steps nothing and stays outside the presentation checkpoint and its hash.

A capture no longer depends on the frames drawn before it: drawing every frame from tick 0, drawing only the captured tick, and restoring a mid-run snapshot and going on give byte-identical PNGs. Particle systems step from each tick's emitter state, kept as the tick starts whether or not a frame is drawn. Every capture resets TAA, GI and SSR history and motion vectors, starts the jitter and shadow spiral at phase 0, meters exposure at once, draws streamed terrain tiles settled, and draws a fixed warm-up (a jitter cycle under TAA, 8 frames for GI or SSR without it), then leaves the display's history as it was. Reference frames taken under TAA move once: they are now the converged frame.

The drawn poses no longer depend on the wall clock or the machine's speed: the Presenter steps once a tick by the tick's dt (also when no frame is drawn), takes each model batch a fixed 0.5 s of ticks after it starts (waiting for it natively), decodes a batch whole, waits for the model's load once an agent needs it, and never skips frames to catch up. Two runs draw the same frames and feet, under load too. A probe snapshot's presentation checkpoint keeps every agent as drawn, the queued frames and the outstanding batch (run again on a restore), and they enter SnapshotInfo.presentation.

A presentation checkpoint now restores the display's whole frame history (TAA, SMAA, GI, SSR and FSR histories, the wind field, trample, the frame parity and phase, the previous camera, time, wind and sway), the interpolation pair, og.motion's previous palettes, the skinned palettes and the terrain streamer with its tiles, so display frames after a restore equal the uninterrupted run's byte for byte.

Tiles fade in by presentation ticks rather than frame seconds, and a requested tile is handed a fixed 4 ticks after its request, so what streams in and how far it has faded is a function of the tick on every host.
Restoring a probe snapshot undoes a `quit` that ran after it, so the restored world plays on instead of staying stopped.

A probe with mode realtime is captured again every interval ticks. Every probe drew as baked whatever its mode: a realtime one was captured once and never again, so what moved in its room never showed in it. A realtime probe costs six faces per update; raise interval before adding probes.

The markdown profile is rendered by og from bun's JSON profile, so every function and caller is named at its file and line in the game's source; bun's own markdown named the game bundle (`game.native.js`, no line) for a sample without a position, about one run in five. The tables are the same sections (hot functions by self time, the call tree, each function's callers, callees and hot lines, the time by file); the call tree is now indented by depth.

The size table's cache (each file's brotli size and the host's probe, by sha256) is no longer written into the engine's install as dist/.build-cache.json, where a read-only install silently recomputed brotli -q 11 of the engine modules on every build. Builds keep it in ~/.cache/origingame/build-v1/facts.json (OG_BUILD_CACHE names another directory; off keeps nothing), written atomically and merged with what a build running beside it wrote. A packed engine carries the facts of its own modules in dist/build-facts.json, so the first build of a new install does not compute them.

A cook after a change to code alone (src/ and the project's other TypeScript; nothing under assets/, nor project.ogt) no longer plans every asset again. It rewrites the asset index and the publish plan from the last cook and reports the stages index, code and save: 46-59 ms instead of 700-873 ms for a project of 1350 assets. A project whose code uses og.motion is still cooked whole.

A cook that plans again after an asset changed does its per-file work on the cook's threads: reading the sources, hashing them, parsing each scene for its streaming groups and the assets it names, and checking each cooked file against the manifest. On a project of 1350 assets (161 MB of sources) a cook after one scene changed takes 330-380 ms instead of 670-790 ms on 16 cores; the cooked files and the report are the same bytes.

The skeleton's tsconfig.json no longer includes `host.d.ts`, a file no project has; its `include` is `src/**/*.ts`, `tests/**/*.ts` and `.og/types/**/*.d.ts`. `og check` on a project without a tsconfig.json uses the same list. An existing project's own tsconfig.json is not rewritten and keeps working. The start guide names `tools/` as the place for scripts that generate sources: nothing there is cooked or bundled.
A no_fill error from the local fake (og run --platform-fake, PlaytestDesc.platform, a dev page) is retryable, as platform.ogt and the native runtime say; it read retryable false.

fixed.member: og check and og test of a game with playtests
fixed.summary: A game's type check failed with 8 errors in .og/engine/src/provider.ts and src/web/relay-rooms.ts (setTimeout, WebSocket, Event, MessageEvent and CloseEvent not found), so og test ran no playtest: the provider module, which @origingame/engine/playtest reaches, named DOM and timer globals a game's type check does not have. It now writes out the socket it needs and reaches the timer through globalThis; relayRooms and checkPlatformProvider behave as before.

og relay and og run --room carry an engine message up to its 16 MiB limit (a late joiner's world snapshot): its WebSocket frame, about 22.4 MiB as base64, was over the 16 MiB frame both ends read, so the sender lost its connection. A larger one is answered with the error too_large; a frame over 32 MiB is answered so too, and then its connection is closed.

A quick play room on og relay could be joined by anyone who knew its id (roomJoin of `quick-N`): it is joined by id only with the key its matched peers were given, which their clients use to come back after a lost connection.

In a lockstep room with two or more peers left running, a player that came back before its old seat's drop was agreed was admitted as a spectator (the seat was still held); the authority now admits a newcomer once the drops being agreed are done, so it finds its seat.

An aurora at the same tick renders identically regardless of GPU workgroup scheduling: equally near curtain segments use a stable tie-break, and crowded footprint tiles consider every segment rather than an arbitrary truncated subset.

FSR 3.1 costs less: its accumulation reads the history's colour from the engine's previous output instead of a copy of its own (the pass writes 12 bytes a pixel, not 20), reads that history in 8 fetches instead of 16, and the luma instability runs inside the reactivity pass (seven dispatches, not eight). The picture is the same within 0.05 dB against a 4-samples-a-pixel ground truth.

A large crowd costs the frame's render call less CPU: its members are read once a frame instead of twice, their tables reuse the last frame's memory, and their previous transforms upload straight from their table instead of being copied into the joint palette first (fifty thousand members: about 3 ms less a frame on a server CPU).

fixed.member: render CPU time of large still scenes
fixed.summary: A frame compares its instances with the frame before's once, in order, and every stage reads that answer: the sorted batches re-key only the instances that differ, the motion test reads whether one moved from the same pass, the sorted transforms are not uploaded or compared again when they are the ones the GPU culling's buffer holds, and each instance's sway is not copied again when none changed. Frames are unchanged. A still city of 94,865 instances under TAA went from 10.5 to 5.8 ms of `render` CPU a frame on a software Vulkan device; with one instance moving, unchanged.

fixed.member: render CPU time of large still scenes
fixed.summary: The static shadow cache no longer re-tracks every instance in a frame where nothing it reads changed: once every drawn instance has stood still long enough to be cached, a frame whose batches, instances, hashes and bounding spheres are the frame before's reuses its split. Frames are unchanged. A still city of 94,865 instances under TAA went from 12.5 to 10.0 ms of `render` CPU a frame on a software Vulkan device.

fixed.member: render CPU time of large still scenes
fixed.summary: The renderer's CPU work per frame no longer grows with the instances that hold still: the sorted batches compare the submission in its own order and recompute only the instances that changed, a frame under TAA or motion blur where no instance moved builds and uploads no previous-transform records (its motion vectors read the instances themselves, as they did), and a scene without foliage meshes no longer walks every instance for foliage bounds. Frames are unchanged. A still city of 94,865 instances under TAA went from 32 to 13 ms of `render` CPU a frame on a software Vulkan device; with one instance moving, from 30 to 22 ms.

A night under og.DayNight without og.PhysicalSky reads instead of drawing the land as black. The moon's light is 1 at full night, a third of the noon sun's (it was 0.45; get:og.DayNight's lightIntensity and the driven DirectionalLight's intensity answer the new value). The sky's light on surfaces out of the moon's light no longer falls below what it is at sunset: from sunset to sunrise the image-based light is raised as the eye adapts, in the night sky's blue, and a water surface's mirror of the sky stays as bright as the sky is drawn. The set sun's glow fades out with the twilight; it used to stay in the sky under the horizon and light the land from below in orange. Days are unchanged, dusk's shade is a little brighter, and nights under og.PhysicalSky are unchanged. A game that wants a darker night lowers DayNight.lightIntensity (the moon's light) or Camera.exposure by og.atmosphere.timeOfDay.

Reading sprites, models and the effect components for a frame is faster: their rows are read in place from the world's columns, where each row was first copied out through its entity, and a model's part list is no longer cloned every frame. What is drawn does not change. 20,000 models extract in 0.42 of the time and 20,000 sprites in 0.6 (a release build on a 2.6 GHz Xeon).

fixed.member: render CPU time of still scenes with many models
fixed.summary: A frame whose og.Model instances were all kept from the last frame tells the renderer so, and the renderer no longer compares those instances with the last frame's, nor tests them for motion when their previous transforms are known to be their own. Frames are unchanged. Sorting a still frame of 95,000 instances took 2.94 ms of CPU and now takes 0.015 ms (release, software Vulkan host).
Reports whether the renderer runs compute passes on this device, from the renderer's capability set, instead of always answering true.

A paced run (without --headless, such as one in a room) ends on tick N. A frame that caught up after a slow one could step past it, so the run and its summary ended on N+1 or later on a loaded machine.

fixed.member: CPU time of frames with many models
fixed.summary: Extraction keeps what each og.Model drew in the last frame and copies it when its inputs are unchanged (its model, look, lodBias, sway, variant and drawn place) under the same view (the camera, the view's height, RenderSettings.lodBias, the level view, baked lighting and the meshes and materials the cluster path can see) and its level of detail has settled, so a frame builds only the models that moved; a scene's HLOD proxies are copied when nothing changed. Frames are unchanged. 6,000 static houses (12,028 instances) took 33.6 ms of engine frame CPU against 38.0 a still frame, and 38.4 against 44.6 with one of them moving every frame (release build, a renderer that draws nothing).

fixed.member: og dev (a style that fails to apply on reload)
fixed.summary: The message "og dev: the style did not apply: …" now names the reason og.ui.configure refused the style; it printed null.

A scattered plant's leaves are lit as a placed model's: domed normals (the leaf material's domeNormals) and the sun through the leaf (translucency). Scattered copies drew their leaves with flat card normals and no light from behind, so a scattered wood looked harsher than the same plant placed as an og.Model.

A foliage impostor is as bright as its mesh. The cook bakes how much of the sun reaches each texel past the plant's own nearby leaves and branches into the card's material atlas, and the card is lit as the many small faces a texel stands for; cards were brighter and flatter than the trees in front of them, so the switch at impostorDistance showed as a band. Impostors bake again on the next cook. The models guide (§3) gives the distance at which a card is as sharp as its mesh.
The diffuse IBL, specular IBL and direct light debug views draw scattered copies and impostors; both showed the unsupported pattern.

Import settings named after a text asset with one more `.ogt` (`oak.ogt.ogt` beside the model text `oak.ogt`) reach it; they were read as settings for `oak`, so a `type model` could not be cooked with an impostor.

Called inside a system it names the scene in place (the one og.SceneChanged reported this tick), not always GameDesc.scene: a system that waits for its change to land can compare it with the scene it asked for.

Screen-space GI (method `screen` and `both`) gathers each ray's whole line of surfaces, each direction lit once by the nearest surface that fills it, instead of one hit a ray: in a closed room it now gathers about 0.78 of a path-traced bounce where it gathered 0.65, so shade under GI is brighter and takes more of its surroundings' colour, and a floor or wall leaving the frame goes on lighting what stands beside it. `rays` now defaults to 2 and `steps` to 16; a game that set them keeps its values, and more of either only smooths a frame without TAA.

The drawn sea is the sea bodies float on: the surface rises only with the waves og.physics.waterHeight and og.Buoyancy evaluate, which now reach down to a metre (48 waves, where 32 stopped at a 32nd of the peak's length: 2.6 m at 10 m/s, 10 m at 20 m/s). The shorter ripples the renderer adds shade the surface and no longer move it; they stood 2 cm RMS off the floated sea at 10 m/s and 14 cm in a gale. A body's motion on a sea differs from the version before.

The waves' crest lean is shared so the long waves lean whole and the sum still never folds: a sea of the same choppiness keeps sharp crests with more, shorter waves under them. Every reference frame of a sea moves.

The sea is one function of place and time: og.physics.waterHeight and og.Buoyancy evaluate all 32 waves of a wind's sea whole at any point (no grid, no surface size, no camera), and the renderer draws the same function at the same tick. The drawn surface differs from it only by the short waves the renderer adds (under 2% of the significant height in RMS: 2 cm at 10 m/s, 14 cm at 20 m/s) and the waves its vertices cannot hold far from the eye. The sea's waves now run from 1.6 times the peak's length down to 1/32 of it at the spectrum's own heights, so a body's motion on a sea differs from the version before.

A sea's look changes with its waves: the mid-length waves are no longer raised to carry the sea's slopes, which the short rendered waves carry instead. A gale reads as a long swell under small chop with fewer whitecaps; every reference frame of a sea moves.

A sea under a closed cloud deck no longer adds two scatter terms that were tuned for one storm view (a fixed teal on the upper half of every wave and on steep faces towards the eye, whatever the water's own colour). Its body is lit as every other surface under the deck is, by the dimmed sun and the sky's light, so an overcast sea reads grey-dark and takes its colour from Water.deep.

fixed.member: og.assert sites under og test's resident session
fixed.summary: A resident session (og test, og run in a project with a session) reported the og.assert sites of every game it had loaded: a project's report listed another project's sometimes and reachable sites as uncovered. Each bundle now hands its own sites to its og.game() token, and an engine reports its game's alone, as a run with OG_SESSION=0 does.

Automatic session startup reports an exited supervisor's error immediately instead of waiting for the readiness timeout. Missing build inputs name their path; concurrent starters still converge on the supervisor lock.
The anti-aliasing and the clouds' depth test call a pixel sky only where the prepass drew nothing; with a camera far plane past 100 km they took far surfaces for sky.

The stylised looks' palette match and ink wash took Oklab with negative light clamped to black, unlike the depth bands; both now keep its sign, so an out-of-gamut colour finds its palette colour by its own hue.

The probe GI's temporal estimator and the terrain's blend between layers weighed colour with Rec.601's luma weights (0.299, 0.587, 0.114) where every other pass uses Rec.709's for linear light; they now call the library's `luma`, so green counts for more and blue for less there.

The sun's cascades are nested round the camera's position and snapped to a grid, instead of fitted to the slice of the view each one shades. A camera that turns no longer redraws its shadows, and one that walks redraws a cascade once per grid cell it crosses, so still casters are drawn once however the camera moves. A point's cascade is picked by its distance from the camera, not its view depth: shadows end at shadowDistance in every direction (they reached farther towards the screen's corners), and a cascade's edge is a circle round the camera. A shadow layer under moving casters keeps its still ones only where drawing them again costs more than putting the kept layer back: a terrain or a crowd over a few props is one pass.

A shadowed 2D light's soft shadow is a smooth ramp at every sourceRadius. It used to be a staircase: nine point taps over a penumbra many shadow-map texels wide drew flat steps, 26 px wide at sourceRadius 1 six units behind a wall. Its lit end was also cut off in a jump by a blocker search narrower than the penumbra. The PCSS filter is now integrated exactly over the polar shadow map, and the blocker search covers everything the light's nearest occluder can shadow. The 10–90 % width now matches the geometry: 167 px where the geometry gives 166, and 273 px where it gives 274; before the fix it was 149 and 215 px.

Meshes take the light around them through the renderer's one shading entry. A physical material's reflection is now bent towards its normal by roughness squared before the environment is read, as a standard material's is: a rough physical surface reflects a little less of the horizon.

On a landscape phone the loadout shows several slot rows instead of one: the title is smaller and its heading margins go, the slots take one column, and Back and Equip stand beside the list at its foot. A slot's icon no longer shrinks and its Equipped tag ellipsizes when a long translation leaves no room.

The loadout's heading and category labels come from the kit's string table: an empty title takes shooter.loadout.title and an empty category label takes shooter.loadout.category.<id> (primary, secondary, melee, utility), so they translate with Back and Equip. A game's own non-empty title or label is shown as given.

fixed.member: og.Grass on a terrain with a height blend
fixed.summary: Moves frames: blades now grow by their layer's weight as the height blend draws it (at even heights a layer shows only within its window under the strongest), as og.TerrainScatter copies already do, not by the raw weight before the blend. Grass no longer thins out across rock whose control channel still holds a little grass; where the blend draws the layer whole every blade grows. A terrain without a height blend grows as before.

fixed.member: og.TerrainScatter on a terrain with a height blend
fixed.summary: Moves frames: a copy now grows by its layer's weight as the height blend draws it (at even heights, a layer shows only within its window under the strongest), not by the raw weight before the blend. Trees no longer stand on rock whose control channel still holds a little grass at a biome's edge; where the blend draws the layer whole every copy grows. A terrain without a height blend places as before.

fixed: Screen-space reflections no longer lose valid Hi-Z cells when neighbouring rays select different depth levels on software Vulkan. Mip bounds are derived per ray from the base extent instead of a divergent mip-size query; trace steps, thickness and quality settings are unchanged.

fixed.summary: A UI document that does not parse is an error of the check (OG9102, with its file, line and the cook's message) instead of a note beside "og check: ok"; og ui types exits non-zero on it. A document's @import sheets are read as the cook reads them, so such a document is typed.

A cooked colour texture given as normalMap or clearcoatNormalMap (a PNG without `texture { kind normal }` in its import settings) is a warning in the engine log, once a texture, naming the texture and the line to write. It was decoded as sRGB and lit the surface wrong with nothing to say why.

A new project holds only the skeleton's files, as the package manifest lists them. Files left in the template directory of a checkout (a run's output, stray assets) were copied into every new project.

world.instantiate works inside a system. The root is spawned as world.spawn spawns one there (og.Transform, and og.Parent for a parented root, among the system's writes; its id usable at once), and the scene's entities, or the glTF's og.Model and lights, are in the world when the system returns: the systems after it in the same tick, and a save they take, have them. A second instance of the same named scene in one system is refused at the call, as between ticks. It was refused with "world.instantiate inside a system needs og-ecs SystemContext packed-byte access".

The refusal of a scene whose entity name is taken no longer advises "instantiate the scene under a root", which does not help: names are unique in the world, under any root. It now names what works: despawn the entity that has the name, rename it in the scene, or make what is placed more than once a prefab (og.load.prefab spawns its entities unnamed). A name used twice inside one scene is reported as that.

og.timeline.play, pause, seek and stop work inside a system, as their doc says: the call is queued and applied at this tick's og.timeline. They were refused with "not available while a system runs". A system that does not read og.Timeline cannot check the entity has one; og.timeline then warns "entity N has no og.Timeline: nothing plays".

A document's <joystick action>, <dpad action> and <button data-og-touch> drive their actions on a mouse or pad surface above 720p (a desktop window, a scripted og run or playtest at 1920x1080) and under a pinned og-ui unit: their input zones are where the controls are drawn, not their layout before the surface's scale, so a press on the drawn control (touch_move_to:Stick, touch_start) reaches its action.
The type now has `dx12`, which the native host on Windows already reported.

A system's or hook's description is read through the IDL's SystemDesc and HookDesc like every other description: a field of the wrong type, or a `when` or `on` the IDL does not name, refuses the engine at creation with the field's path (`og.system 'late': desc.when: 'after' is not a StateWhen: during, enter, exit`), where it was read as left out and the system ran as `during` (the hook on `add`). A description TypeScript accepts reads as before.

A part's box-shadow colour written as a CSS colour function (rgb(from var(--x) r g b / 0.4), color-mix()…) is drawn; it was dropped because only #hex was read. A part named on a heading (<h2 part="…">) keeps the font size its rules give it; the host's font shorthand no longer undid it.

Lines treat foliage and ground as masses. A look's outline reached only meshes, while Stylise.ink and surface hatching drew every leaf and grass blade as an edge, so an inked or hatched look's forest and meadow were covered in ink blots. Scattered copies and model impostors now take the look's outline round each copy (never between its own leaves, thinning to nothing with distance), the terrain takes it on its silhouette, and on scattered copies, impostors, grass and terrain the ink keeps to silhouettes and the hatching is laid on the screen. Outline colours are stored with 5 bits a channel. Frames without an outline, ink or hatching are unchanged; a 3D look with MaterialStyle.outlineWidth now runs the depth prepass and the outline pass over scattered copies and terrain as well.

One shading rule for every lit surface. MaterialStyle.toon, shadowTint and shadowDarkness, and the toon ambient, reached only meshes (and toon and shadowTint the terrain and grass); scattered copies, model impostors and crowd cards were always lit as plain PBR, so a toon look's forest kept smooth shading beside cel-shaded characters. They now go through the same shading (the three built-in bands, matte), point and spot lights included, and the terrain and grass take shadowDarkness and the flat toon ambient as well. A material with styled false keeps its lit shading on scattered copies and impostors. Frames without a MaterialStyle are unchanged; a toon, shadowTint or shadowDarkness look's terrain, grass, scattered copies, impostors and crowds change.

The pack is a theme of CSS tokens: base.css (dark and light :root tokens), its art, its fonts, motion.css and sounds.css. Its controls and per-group files are gone, so it no longer restyles a component's internals part by part; every control and component wears the default style's rules in the pack's candy colours and one dark outline.

The pack is a theme of CSS tokens: base.css (dark and light :root tokens), its art, motion.css and sounds.css. Its controls and per-group files are gone, so it no longer restyles a component's internals part by part; every control and component wears the default style's rules in the pack's brass, crimson and walnut. Text over the scene takes a stronger --tag-halo, so a red name or damage number holds over a red ground.

fixed.member: fantasy, scifi and cartoon style packs
fixed.summary: The last pack pairs under 4.5:1 read: fantasy's light accent is a step deeper on parchment, its dark done ink (now inherited by objectives) and trend-down lighter; scifi's light uncommon, trend-up and heal green deeper; cartoon's light selected-row fill paler under its muted ink.

fixed.member: fantasy, scifi and cartoon style packs
fixed.summary: Text reads at 4.5:1 on what each pack draws under it, in both schemes. Fantasy's light scheme turns its walnut frames, plates, panels, cells, fields and slots to parchment and vellum with dark inks, draws its hex buttons as bevelled vellum plates with brass rims, and pales its crimson bands under the dark title. Scifi darkens its light hover and accent inks and its pressed tab, and lightens its dark danger. Cartoon darkens its red and violet plates under white text, its light accent, and its dark hover and pressed washes. Text over the scene takes the default's eight-copy outline in --ink-inverse under all three, and fantasy's focus ring follows its pointed plates.

fixed.member: fantasy, scifi and cartoon style packs
fixed.summary: Text holds 4.5:1 in more places under each pack. Scifi's dark frost is denser (about 96 %), so a panel's ink, the muted ink too, reads over a white sky while the blurred scene still glows through. Fantasy's light scheme gets parchment-deep trend, XP and legendary inks and a deeper brass button ink, and its dark selected row a deeper brass under its labels. Cartoon's light selection and legendary ink read under their inks. Under fantasy and cartoon, a name's dark drop shadow stays in the dark scheme.

The pack is a theme of CSS tokens: base.css (dark and light :root tokens), its art, motion.css and sounds.css. Its controls and per-group files are gone, so it no longer restyles a component's internals part by part; every control and component wears the default style's rules in the pack's glass, cyan rims and bevelled cuts. Frames, panels and dialogs are thinner frost that lets the blurred scene read through.

Text over scifi's glass holds 4.5:1 over the brightest and darkest scenes. The band, frame-top and inset cyan washes are thinner (a band peaks at 12 %), the light scheme's white frost is denser (about 90 %) and its selected-tab amber wash thinner, and the dark label, done, gold, XP, legendary and trend-down inks are lighter (the light ones deeper) so they read on glass with the scene behind it.

The engine package ships every built-in style pack that is a CSS directory, with the art its CSS names: a look's ui "fantasy" now resolves in an installed engine, not only in a checkout. Before, only packs with an extension.json were copied, and never their art/ directory.
A frame without valid TAA history compiles a current-frame-only resolve rather than the full history pipeline, retaining its sampling, upscaling and sharpening.

A layer without anti-tiling no longer tints itself by cellVariation when its normal map's alpha is opaque (no cells named): it read the opaque alpha as a cell of its own and moved the layer's tone very slightly. With anti-tiling it already left it alone.

Diagnostic views wait for complete lit pipelines instead of temporarily drawing an incomplete beauty variant while shaders compile. Switching from beauty to a terrain diagnostic now honours the requested view on its first frame. Beauty rendering remains non-blocking.

A terrain draws faster on native Apple GPUs: its shaders read each layer's settings in place, where every layer sampled copied the whole 192-byte layer record, some of them several times. At 1280x720 on an Apple M4 Pro the 2 km island takes 7.4 to 7.9 ms a frame (8.4 to 9.8 before) and a displaced terrain 7.7 ms (10.3 to 10.6); a few pixels move by one step in 255.
A terrain under a mirrored transform (a negative scale on one or three axes) draws its ground: its lit pass and depth prepass take clockwise as the front. It was culled to the background before.
A stamp mesh under a mirrored transform draws its outside, as a mirrored mesh does. It drew inside-out before.

Moves frames: a stamp's face turned past vertical (an overhang's or an arch's underside) takes the layers a vertical face takes. Its slope counted past 90°, which no layer's `slopeMax` can name, so no layer showed there and the first layer was drawn alone: grass under every overhang.

The terrain now takes the screen-space ambient occlusion (`post.ao`), as meshes, grass and scattered copies already did: whatever stands on the ground darkens it softly around its foot. Before, the terrain shader had no texture slot left for the occlusion and drew without it. The AO debug view now shows the terrain's occlusion instead of the unsupported checker. With AO off the frame is unchanged.

Moves frames: a stamp lays every layer on its mesh by the mesh's own normal, biplanar past 45° where the layer names no `projectSlope`. Within `blend` the layer was projected by the band's normal, the ground's: from above onto a steep side, where its texture stretched into vertical streaks. The band still takes the ground's layers and shading normal.

A cook trims ~/.cache/origingame/cook-v1 at most once an hour instead of after every cook. The trim reads every cached action, so each cook paid for the size of the whole store: about 5 s at 116k actions, even for a project of one scene. The store can now pass its cap (OG_COOK_CACHE_MAX_BYTES) by an hour's cooks; `og cache gc` still trims it on demand.

The size table compresses the build's files at once, one per core, where it compressed them one after another: a publish build's two engine modules no longer double the wait for a Brotli -q 11 the size cache does not hold.

A resident host is kept per worktree and environment. Commands in one worktree whose environments differ (OG_RENDERER, a terminal's variables) each start their own host, where before the second found the first's host, was refused and ran alone.

fixed: og test now defaults to hardware rendering and clearly reports software-only adapters as unavailable, leaving frame checks unchecked instead of silently rendering every tick on the CPU. OG_RENDERER=software explicitly opts into software rendering; OG_RENDERER=none still runs simulation only.

fixed.summary: Answers are written by types generated from the IDL, so they carry what the IDL declares: a binding in og.input.actions (bindings, defaults) and og.input.capture now has every declared field (control, negative, positive, up, down, left, right, scale, invertY, deadzone, zone, radius); a field at its default used to be left out.

Numbers the IDL declares f32 are written as f32, as the API types them: choices[].check.target and chance, lastCheck.target, displayHz, frameMs, parse's at and soundInfo's seconds can differ in the last digits (0.1 reads as 0.10000000149011612).

An active screen reader receives only the accessibility nodes that enter, leave, move or change. A row scrolling in or out no longer makes the native bridge read the whole tree; only the parents whose children changed are read again.

The hotkey cap under the slot is the scene's plate (--scene-plate) in the scene's ink (--scene-ink), the pair every pack sets for text over the scene, so it reads over a bright sky as over a dark floor; under the default style it was muted grey on a translucent cap and all but vanished over the sky.
Its hotkey caps take the scene's plate and ink, as AbilitySlot's do.
A locked slot hides its charges badge, as it hides its cost, so the badge no longer covers the lock.
An ultimate's charge percent sits on a small ground of its own (a pack sets it with --ability-slot-percent-ground; --scrim by default), so the ring's arc no longer runs through its digits.

The slot grows with the player's text scale (72 px square and 96 px ultimate at 150 %), so its icon, ring and the cost and charge badges, which already grew, keep their proportions; at 150 % a square slot's cost and charges no longer meet.
Its slots and the gaps between them grow with the player's text scale, as AbilitySlot's do.

An ultimate's cost sits centred at the top of its round slot instead of at the bottom corner, where its plate covered the charge percent (72 % read as 2 %); the two stay apart at every text scale. A square slot keeps the cost at its bottom leading corner.

A document element with an action trigger (`onconfirm={buy}`) is built only in a frame its action fires, not every frame, and its trigger now fires on a mounted screen whose ancestors are not rebuilt that frame: such elements are written in their own layer's context, so the layer's input and serial apply.

A `display: flex` box that sets no `align-items` now stretches its items across their line, as CSS's initial `normal` does (CSS Flexbox §8.3): in a column an item with an `auto` width fills the column, in a row an item with an `auto` height takes the line's height. It used to place them at the start at their content's size. A definite cross size, `align-self` or an authored `align-items` keeps its own; write `align-items: flex-start` where items should keep their content's size.

An anchored element is now placed against its anchor's box as drawn, with the anchor's (and its ancestors') transforms, `translate`, `scale` and `rotate` (CSS Anchor Positioning 1 §2.4.1); it used to read the untransformed layout box. Transforms are composed after layout, so when an anchor's transform changes the anchored element follows on the next frame.

A shorthand whose duration or delay is math over a token (animation: pulse calc(var(--motion-duration-slow) * 3) ease-out infinite) takes that time, and the parts after it keep their places. The calc() was read as a second name before.

The selected character's role wraps inside the footer instead of running past both edges of a narrow roster (it was one unbroken line that never shrank: 430 px across a 390 px phone at 150 % text in the scifi pack).

Document the landed named-store API, GameDesc.ui lifecycle, save v3 presentation boundary, recorded intents, Svelte syntax, structured dialogue spans, shared Ease and input vocabulary. Distinguish pending retained mounting, standard CSS completion and both-host spans verification from implemented support.
Its friends' and requests' avatars are round again; they had drawn as rounded squares since the shared roles.

The `background` shorthand resets the colour it leaves out to transparent, as CSS's does: a part dressed with `background: linear-gradient(…)` no longer keeps the widget's own ground under it. A core panel's or modal dialog's translucent pack fill now shows the scene (and its `backdrop-filter` blur) behind it.

Each base part wears one role, so a pack's role tokens reach it. Parts renamed for the role they wear: Avatar.name, ListItem.title, EmptyState.title, ErrorState.title and Steps.label are `headline`; ItemSlot.name, Currency.name and Pips.label are `caption`; Avatar's picture ground is Avatar.well; Steps.cell is Steps.row and Steps.title wears the title role; SkeletonGroup.art no longer lists `picture`. New parts: Currency.socket, Currency.full, Steps.track, Steps.fill, EmptyState.disc, ErrorState.disc, ItemSlot.plus. Ribbon's box draws nothing of its own, so the card under it shows.

Built-in components that centre or end-align their content lay it out as they did before the CSS layout landed. Hold button, HUD timer, star bar, orb meter, minimap, compass, kill feed, chart, celebration, overlay bar, placement ghost, telemetry and others had moved their content to the left edge. Their `<div>`s named `align-items`, `justify-content` or `flex-direction` without `display: flex`; on a CSS block those do nothing. They now say `display: flex`.

A `stretch` box clamped by its `max-width` or `max-height` across a flex line that is centred or end-aligned (`align-items: center`, `flex-end`) now sits where the line aligns it, as in CSS Box Alignment 3 §6.1. It used to sit at the line's start, which put the game-over, results, calibration and credits panels at the left of the screen.

Text inside a document ``) takes the button's ink as that ink changes, as slotted content inherits from its slot: after a style pack is set on a mounted document, after a scheme switch, and through the style's colour transition. Before, it kept the ink the button had on the frame it was built, often the old scheme's or the old pack's.

Moves frames: a button that is not disabled no longer fades its words with opacity. CreatorTools' unselected tools and Leaderboard's unselected tabs drop their rim and keep their ink (scifi light 3.39 and 3.72:1 before); Calendar's days of the next or last month take --ink-muted instead of fading to 45 % (1.26–1.84:1 before). A disabled button still fades.

A document button holding elements grows to fit content taller than its control height, as an HTML button does; the control height stays its least height and an authored height still holds. Before, a row of a name over its detail spilled below the button.

A `<button>`'s own box styles restyle its plate: `button.buy { background: #ff7a2e; border: 3px solid #102030; border-radius: 30px; padding: 12px; box-shadow: … }` now paints the button that way, replacing the style's fill and painted frame, as CSS on an HTML button does. The style's plate used to be drawn over the button's own box, inside its padding and at the style's own size, so the declared colour never showed and a round button got a square plate. The plate now covers the button's whole box with the declared padding inside it, and the button's `overflow` clip and outline keep its corners. A rule for the plate itself (`button.buy::part(base):hover { … }`) still wins and is where states go. A button that declared a background or border the plate used to hide now shows it, and one that declares `background: transparent` is unfilled until a state rule fills it; remove the declaration to keep the style's plate. A button with its own padding shows its plate under that padding, so it looks larger than before. The kits whose buttons declare their own box (`hero-button`, `action-button`, `hold-button`, `ability-slot`, `cooldown`, `radial-menu` and others) no longer carry the style's plate, with its hover and press tint, over it; `menu` and `action-hints` no longer declare a transparent background, so their entries keep the style's plate.

Moves frames: a document <button>'s own padding is above the style's ::part rules under a pack too, as docs/ui.md §3.2 says. A pack's button::part(base) padding replaced it, so a narrow button's face shrank to a few pixels and its text broke into many lines (StrategySelection's commands on a phone at 150 % text).

Moves frames: native button labels now honor overflow-wrap, text-wrap-style, text-align-last, text-justify and custom text-overflow markers through the same CSS text-content path as text elements. Long unbroken labels with overflow-wrap:anywhere wrap inside the button; white-space:nowrap still prevents wrapping.

A button whose label wraps (Confirm's actions, a Tree row's name) takes its padding above and below from --button-wrap-pad, --space-sm where a style sets none, so a pack whose plate has a thick frame keeps a wrapped label clear of it. The fantasy pack sets --space-md: a two-line action no longer sits against the plate's top bevel.

fixed.member: og.ui world state restore, UI patch batches
fixed.summary: Refused bytes now say what is wrong and at which byte, such as a truncated read, a count larger than the data, or trailing bytes. The world state used to report only "unreadable bytes". The bytes written are unchanged.

Base, RPG and puzzle components use shared role, layout and motion tokens instead of private look declarations; semantic parts, game-owned states and intents remain available. Ribbons and loading skeletons use the style's shared motion, and puzzle score breakdowns use the shared scroll fade.

Restyling a document's elements costs about a third less CPU: telling whether a CSS value holds a math function (calc(), min(), clamp() and the rest) no longer tries every function name at every character, so a menu whose cards change class on the same tick restyles in less time, with the same values.
The locale-fonts warning accepts an installed font pack and covers Devanagari, Thai, Cyrillic and Greek languages too.
A run-time font's glyphs render off the frame (natively on a thread, on the web a few a frame), so a new script's first frame no longer hitches (203 ms on Metal before); captures wait for them.

fixed.member: UI documents: popovers and dialogs in retained documents
fixed.summary: A retained layer rewritten in its own slot is no longer renamed `<id>~1` with a duplicate-layer warning; Back reaches the element owning the topmost scope or holding the focus; a press on a disabled option inside an open dropdown no longer closes it.

Once any document declares a property that carries computed values to its children (`list-style-type`, a wide keyword such as `inherit`, a bound declaration), a widget inside a document element (a `<kbd>` keycap in a primary `<button>`) no longer takes the colour the element only inherits (a frame's `--ink`) over its own ink. A widget's ink is over what its host inherits, as it is without carrying; what the host declares still reaches its parts.
Each element's motion channel keys are hashed once instead of every tick for every channel. A dense menu with 40 animating cards spends 0.48 ms a tick instead of 0.51 ms on Windows.

Text over a nine-slice, a border image, a pattern or a cover, contain, none or scale-down image is read on what that layer draws under it, placed as og-render places it (og-draw's UiImage::place and UiGradientImage::place, ui.wgsl's image_uv); such pairs were reported `unchecked`, their ratio leaving the layer out (fantasy's 152). The `unchecked` ground kind is gone.

A button that is a chosen radio (`role="radio" aria-checked="true"`, such as a quantity among ×1/×10/Max buttons or a segment) wears the default style's selection, as a button with `aria-pressed="true"` does: --button-selected-fill under --button-selected-ink, in every variant, at rest, hovered and held. It was drawn as a plain button, so the chosen one did not show.

`background-clip: text` cuts the background to the text of the element and of all its descendants (CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.1), drawn where the background is, under that text; it cut only to the element's own text, so a box whose text sat in child elements drew no background at all.

fixed.member: CSS relative colours in a stylesheet
fixed.summary: A relative colour whose channel uses math (`background: oklch(from var(--accent) l c calc(h + 180))`) no longer fails the declaration with "calc() does not take 'h'": the channel keywords are the colour's to resolve.
A colour whose alpha is `none` (`rgb(0 0 0 / none)`) draws transparent, as CSS Color 4 treats a missing component as zero; it drew opaque.
A space or punctuation after an emoji takes a text face's glyph instead of the emoji face's 1.25 em space.

`color` inherits between document elements, as in CSS: text under an element that declares it (`
…
`, a class, a role rule such as a frame's `--ink`) takes that colour, however deep, and follows it when it changes. Before, text that declared no colour drew the palette's ink. A `
A value written as #rgba now reads as that colour with its alpha dropped, as CSS reads it. It used to read as black.

The health bar has a length on desktop: the vitals plate is --measure-sm wide (within the safe area). It hugged its content, and a StatBar takes its container's width, so the bar drew 0 px wide and only the icon and the figure showed.

fixed.member: <dialog modal>, popover and -og-spotlight in a mounted document
fixed.summary: A container inside a modal dialog, a popover or a spotlight's callout now shows its content in a mounted (retained) document; before, its children were dropped from the first frame (a modal's footer of buttons showed empty), because they were named apart from the top-layer node they are built under.

An ancestor's ground counts under a text only where its box covers the text: a hotkey placed under its slot (RpgActionBar) is over the scene and takes the tag treatment, in every style (it read 1.0–1.36:1 under the packs).

ModeSelect's unselected and locked cards and SaveLoad's unselected slots dim their art, not their words, which keep their ink; StatusGrid's expiring buff blinks its icon, not its stack count; MinimapView's north mark wears --tag-halo instead of a soft offset shadow (3.73:1 on its bezel).
A locked cell ([data-locked=true]) keeps its words' ink, as it is still read (a locked card's rules); only a disabled one takes --ink-disabled. It keeps the empty cell's shadow.

Text over glass (a backdrop: -og-material glass, backdrop-filter) is read on what the glass makes of a black and a white scene, as og-render composes it; it was read as bare text on the scene (OverlayBar's names at 1.36–1.48:1).

fixed: Built-in UI name and dependency lookup now reads a generated package manifest instead of parsing every built-in document. UI type generation parses only the built-ins it needs.

fixed.summary: A component's prop may share a name with a property one tag owns (count, which is <og-counter>'s value) or with a renamed HTML attribute (hidden): on a component it is passed as the prop under its own name. On any other element it is still refused with the tag to write.

fixed.member: AbilityBar, AbilitySlot, ActionButton, Cooldown, HeroButton, HoldButton, RadialMenu, TouchControls, OverlayBar, StatBar
fixed.summary: HUD controls use HTML with CSS while retaining ids, parts and input contracts. Optional cooldowns, costs and hints occupy no blank space; labels stay visible when a hold has no alternate wording, and long confirmation labels wrap. Primary touch labels use their contrasting foreground and twin-stick actions wrap within phone width. Radial commands announce the current choice and show its label when no detail is supplied; the RadialMenu.well surface hook stops the scene halo at the centre. Overlay legends have explicit spacing and their choices scroll within the available width. Stat bars fill the slot supplied by their container.

HUD instruments use HTML with CSS and keep every existing id and part. StatBar's shield, healing and value layers are contained by their own tracks, orb values stay centered above contained liquid, and progress labels share the ring's center. Timers distinguish the caption from the numeric readout with consistent spacing and numeric typography. Optional labels and rings occupy no space when absent.

Compass edges fade as a sliding window, with the heading in a separately spaced readout below. A minimap without a texture shows a visible grid rather than an apparently blank surface. New Compass.readout and Minimap.grid parts let style packs restyle these pieces.

Navigation documents use HTML with CSS and retain their ids and parts. Map markers and rotating map content belong to their own positioned viewports. The compass centers its heading in the actual available width on a phone and separates objective icons and distances from the cardinal directions. Optional labels, textures and distances leave no blank space.

fixed.member: RacingTelemetry, RacingLapHud, RacingStandings, RacingBanner, RacingGarage, RacingResults
fixed.summary: Racing components use HTML with CSS and retain their parts, ids, intents and keyed replay. Telemetry has visible token-colored gauge tracks and centered speed and gear, optional readouts occupy no blank space, garage names wrap, and classification badges no longer squeeze the driver's name on a phone. Default review pages now load a readable font.

fixed.member: ShooterAmmoCounter, ShooterCombatHud, ShooterCrosshair, ShooterDamageDirection, ShooterKillfeed, ShooterLoadout
fixed.summary: Shooter components use HTML with CSS while retaining ids, parts and intents. Ammo and reload layers stay in their tracks, optional readouts leave no empty space, and a token-based reticle keyline keeps the aim visible against bright scenes. Loadout columns and the review sheet's non-shrinking footer remain usable at phone width.

fixed.member: DamageNumbers, OverheadBars, Nameplate, SelectionRing, Telegraph, PathLine, PlacementGhost, InteractionPrompt, LootLabel, SpeechBubble
fixed.summary: In-world documents retain their semantic anchors and ground projections while expressing their boxes in HTML with CSS. Nameplate health, shield and cast layers stay inside their tracks; placement grids and reach previews are contained by their footprint. Optional labels and shape branches occupy no blank space. Speech and interaction text use explicit spacing, loot counts have a distinct numeric readout, and overhead health bars follow the style's health token. All existing parts and ids remain available to style packs.

fixed.member: CardFace, CardCollection, CardDeckList, CardHand, CardPiles, CardReward, CardRunMap, NodeGraph
fixed.summary: Card components use HTML-with-CSS roots and conditional content. Card faces have two-line names, start-aligned rules and inset art wells; collection counts sit below cards instead of on their art, and phone collections use two readable columns. Deck size has a contained meter with a danger fill above the limit, pile counts have a solid ground, relics have an icon well, narrow rewards scroll as readable cards and map legends have a spaced surface. NodeGraph positions its graph inside its own well rather than the screen, keeping the run map visible. Existing ids, parts and intents are retained.

fixed.member: ActionHints, Celebration, Ribbon, SkeletonGroup, Spinner, SplitView, StarBar, StatusGrid
fixed.summary: Feedback components use HTML-with-CSS roots and conditionals while retaining their HUD halo hooks and style-pack parts. Loading skeleton shapes have explicit layouts; split panes fit phone widths and scroll their content; score stars sit above a separate inset track, with the final threshold inside the bar, and status countdown overlays measure against their own holders. Long action hints wrap inside the viewport and long ribbon labels ellipsize instead of spilling across the band. SplitView retains its game-owned ratio and raw resize intents.

fixed.member: Achievements, Chat, DailyQuests, DailyRewards, Friends, Shop, ShopConfirm
fixed.summary: General components use HTML-with-CSS roots, conditional optional content and bounded CSS scrollers. Names, descriptions and rewards have consistent spacing and readable hierarchy in the default style; reward calendars switch to four columns before narrow day states collide. Loading indicators remain visible, and existing ids, parts and keyed intents are preserved. The review sheet includes default-style desktop and phone pages.

fixed.member: Breadcrumbs, Carousel, Chart, DataGrid, Menu, TooltipCard
fixed.summary: Panel components use HTML-with-CSS roots and conditional optional content. Tooltip comparisons wrap inside phone viewports, chart layers are contained in their plot, grid text is start-aligned with numeric cells end-aligned, and carousel page dots stay in their own control row. Empty charts and carousels explain their state. Breadcrumbs expose the current page and reverse separators in RTL. Carousel navigation remains game-owned intents, disabled only with fewer than two pages. Existing ids, parts and virtualised list markup are preserved; isolated sheet fixtures expose individual panel states for review.
Keeps unavailable booster words and counts readable while dimming only their art, uses the shared opaque-surface halo reset, and labels the puzzle review sheet's empty board explicitly.
Keeps booster and summary panel text crisp without scene halos, and gives the scrolling score breakdown a fading edge above its actions.

Improves the default puzzle kit with stronger counter hierarchy, visible completion checks and earned stars, current-level and armed-booster emphasis, readable count badges, quieter disabled states and a separated score total. Uses HTML and token-based CSS, with conditional optional content and phone-sized booster cards. Review sheets now include the default style.

fixed.member: ui.RpgBackpack, ui.RpgQuestDetail, ui.RpgVitals, ui.RpgParty, ui.RpgEnemyInfo, ui.RpgWorldMap, ui.RpgItemCard, ui.RpgQuestTracker
fixed.summary: Wraps backpack categories, tightens quest spacing to expose rewards, grounds bar values on contrasting plates, distinguishes quest diamonds from waypoint dots, keeps item actions beside their content, and makes completed HUD objectives legible.

Improves the default RPG kit with visible health, mana and carry fills; grounded shortcut and quantity badges; clearer selected, acting and down states; quest progress marks; separated attributes and rewards; quieter supporting text; and readable phone tab spacing. Converts optional content and scrollers to HTML with token-based CSS. Default-style review sheets now keep desktop panels inside the viewport and give all phone equipment slots room above the stats.

Moves frames: arena documents use HTML with CSS and conditional content. The default look gives roster choices two readable phone columns, quieter role labels, distinct draft and lobby row surfaces, stronger versus names, and larger match scores. Ids, parts and gameplay intents are unchanged.

Moves frames: idle documents use HTML with CSS and conditional content. Default resource figures, generator names and prestige gains have clearer hierarchy; upgrade prices and states have their own column, earnings have quiet row surfaces, and the reset confirmation is more distinct. Review sheets load the default font. Ids, parts and gameplay intents are unchanged.

Moves frames: rhythm documents use HTML with CSS and conditional content. Default chart ratings, judgement calls, combo counts, grades and scores have clearer hierarchy; song details have a quiet surface, missing jackets have a music-icon fallback, and secondary metadata recedes. Review sheets load the default font. Ids, parts and gameplay intents are unchanged.

Moves frames: roster, generator and purchase scrollers show a stationary token-based bottom fade so partially visible phone rows read as scrollable, not broken. The idle review sheet adds an isolated bounded Welcome back page to show both claim actions entirely on phone; its combined reset page still scrolls between panels. The rhythm phone HUD gives song progress its own padded strip instead of straddling the playfield background.

Moves frames: strategy documents use HTML with CSS and conditional content. Selection health fills measure against their own positioned tracks; cooldown text no longer covers command icons. Production rows, tower stats and upgrade paths have clearer grouping, wave counts have clearer hierarchy, and phone actions wrap their text. Tower upgrade paths scroll within the height given, keeping long descriptions and disabled buy controls reachable above Sell. Review sheets load the default font. Ids, parts and gameplay intents are unchanged.

Repeating unchanged UI configuration retains mounted styles and text measurements. Loading or replacing a CSS texture or its shape-outside alpha updates only elements referencing that asset, rather than invalidating the whole UI; a late alpha now updates its float without another style change.

A call that keeps the style in effect (a scheme, a text scale, reduced motion) no longer installs it again, and one that returns to the default style takes the default stylesheet as already read. Before, every call without a style read the whole default stylesheet again.

Confirm stays whole on a phone at 150 % text: the question and the actions keep their place and what follows scrolls between them; the actions share a line and fill it, take a line each (the confirming one first) where both do not fit, and a long action wraps inside its button. The question is one type step smaller on a phone, and on a phone on its side the dialog widens with what it holds. The document declares an overflow fixture.

An element that reads its container's size (a container query or cq units) and has a child reading it too now takes its queried values on the first frame: settlement could resolve the child first and leave the element as the unmeasured build made it, so a card hand's slots drew 0×0 for a frame and the first focus landed on the one card that had a box.

A container variant that stops matching while its element is laid out (a box whose width follows its height by `aspect`, a block narrowed beside floats) no longer leaves its arrangement, grid columns, `hidden` and animatable values applied: they follow the inline size the element ends the layout with, as its box already did.

fixed.member: UI CSS position: absolute, position: fixed
fixed.summary: A document's absolutely positioned element is now placed against its nearest positioned ancestor (or a `<stack>`), else the document's outermost box, as CSS does (CSS Position 3 §2.1); it used to be placed in its parent's box whether or not the parent was positioned. A fixed element under a transformed ancestor, one whose `will-change` names a transform or filter, or one with `contain: layout` or `paint` is placed against that ancestor's box (CSS Transforms 1 §3, CSS Containment 2 §3.2), not the viewport. Give the intended parent `position: relative` where an absolute child relied on the old placement.

A control with an accent-color draws what sits on the accent in contrast-color() of it: a check mark on a navy accent in the dark scheme was the scheme's near-black on-primary ink (1.4:1) and now reads at least 4.58:1 on any accent. The fill of a checked box, a switch that is on, a chosen radio, a range's track and a progress bar take the accent as before.

A switch that is on keeps its knob readable on a light track: when the knob would vanish on the filled track (a light primary or accent-color), it takes whichever of the scheme's ink and inverse ink reads more on the track. In the light scheme a gold accent left a white knob, and the gold tick on it, at 1.35:1; it is now the dark ink.

A background layer's image or gradient tile is read where og-render draws it (its background-size, -position, -repeat and -origin): fantasy's 58 px filigree corners were read stretched over each frame, under every text in it. A pair over an image the check does not sample (nine-slice, border image, pattern, cover, contain) is reported over "unchecked" instead of a ratio that leaves its look out.

The default ink on a warn fill (Nameplate's cast name on its bar) is contrast-color(var(--warn)), so it reads 4.5:1 or more on any warn a style gives without its own --ink-on-warn (it was --ink-inverse).

An element's style attribute (and style: directive) takes the inherited text properties a <style> rule takes, such as accent-color, caret-color, color-scheme, text-wrap-style and -webkit-text-fill-color; they were refused as unsupported.

The default style's tag halo (--tag-halo, on a nameplate's name, a waypoint's label and a status grid's time left) is an outline: eight unblurred copies of the glyphs 1–1.5 px round them in the ink's inverse, with no drop. The blurred halo with a 1 px drop covered at most half at the glyphs' edge, read 1.09:1 over a white sky and drew an embossed second copy under each label; the outline reads 12.3:1 there (16.7:1 for the light scheme's dark ink over a black scene). Packs that set --tag-halo keep theirs.
The +n tile's count reads over the scene: it takes the figure ink and the tag halo, like an effect's time left. In muted ink, bare on the cell's translucent fill, it read 1.5:1 over a bright sky.

A slider or a <details> resized by a container query draws its new size in that frame: the slider's knob is placed by layout at its value instead of from last frame's track, and the disclosure's root takes the queried width as its summary row does.

revert-layer in a rule that reaches an element from another document (a ::part() rule on a control document's part) rolls back that document's layers only and then falls to the element's own document, instead of also discarding the element's own rules.

A separator is drawn by the default style's hr rule (a --stroke-hairline line in currentColor, --line by default; vertical stands it up) instead of by og-ui, so hr { color; block-size } and any other rule for hr restyle it as CSS does.
A slot now draws the `--slot-shadow` a pack sets; a later rule had cleared it. It is none by default, and a component cell keeps the well shadow it drew, so the default style is unchanged.

A `var()` whose value is `revert` or `revert-layer` rolls the cascade back as the keyword written would (CSS Variables 2 §3): `background: var(--fill, revert-layer)` keeps the layers below until `--fill` is set, instead of being refused as an invalid colour and leaving the property unset.

A control a component names for a role (`<button part="Bag.cell">`, any part ending in `.frame`, `.cell`, `.row`, `.badge` and the other roles) wears its role and the role's tokens alone, as `appearance: none` gives a browser's button its page's look: `button::part(base)` and the control's other own-part rules no longer paint their plate, padding or border image over it. A part named for no role (`Shop.buy`) keeps its control's dress. A control's focus ring is its `focus` part alone and never draws the base's fill, border or border image again over the focused control.

A control a document builds styles its parts as itself from the tick it is built: a rebuilt <button> no longer matched its parts against the enclosing element (a <column part=…>) for that tick, so a focused primary button in a screen no longer switched between two looks on alternate ticks and rebuilt itself while nothing changed.

A font whose face has tabular figures (`tnum`) now cooks them into its atlas without a `features tnum` line, since the default style turns tabular numerals on for its figures and badges. A struck price or a value with inline markup in such a face draws tabular digits that hold their width, and the cook no longer warns about its proportional figures. Fonts re-cook once with this version.

A retained document no longer stops building when a store hides a list row in the same refresh as a change among that row's children; a <select> without <option>s keeps its bound items; screens that declare props may read the engine's $ui store.
A counter styled with a CSS text property (font, letter-spacing and the like, its own or inherited) or named as a part shows its number; it showed nothing.
A counter lands on its value exactly; a value past 16,777,216 was rounded to a float and shown a few units off.

A transition or keyframe animation between `anchor()` insets, or between `anchor-size()` sizes, moves through the lengths they resolve to (CSS Anchor Positioning 1), following an anchor that moves meanwhile, instead of jumping from one anchor to the other. An inset and an anchor size also take `calc()` of weighted terms added, `calc(0.5 * anchor(--a right) + 0.5 * anchor(--b right))`.

fixed.member: CSS vertical-align on an inline block
fixed.summary: An inline block aligns by its last baseline (baseline-source: auto, CSS 2.1 §10.8.1): a two-line inline block beside text sits with its second line on the text's baseline, not its first. baseline-source: first keeps the first. A table cell's vertical-align: text-top and text-bottom place its content at the start and end.
They now blend sRGB-encoded values, as CSS Compositing does, instead of linear light; mid-tones under them are lighter than before.

Bound false HTML boolean attributes are absent from attribute selectors in both document builders; true values are present with an empty string. Data and ARIA false values remain selector-visible. Retained :default follows the checked attribute's presence.
Linear and radial gradient colour stops accept reduced calc() sums of percentages and pixels, including mask-image fades with a fixed pixel tail.
A display: block box with an auto width fills its block parent's content width, as in CSS block flow, instead of shrinking to its content.

fixed.member: UI: CSS clip-path cuts the element's own shadows and borders
fixed.summary: As CSS has it, clip-path now cuts the element's box shadows, borders and outline with its background and children; before, only the background and children were cut. A `#` inside parentheses in a declaration (`url(#id)`) is no longer read as a comment.

Document landed lexical CSS variables, cascade and selector semantics, native layout settlement, and bounded missing-art placeholders. Keep CSS queries, motion completion, sibling and structural selectors, and retained mounting explicitly pending.

counter-reset: reversed(name) with no value starts where CSS Lists 3 says, from the increments and the first counter-set in its scope, so items that count down by one end at 1; it started at 0 and counted below it. Its readers take the start from the tick after the scope is counted.

Resolve cursors over noninteractive boxes in paint order, including inherited values, URL images, transforms, overflow clipping and pointer-events. Passive boxes no longer expose an unrelated underlying control's cursor. Held controls retain their cursor and passive boxes gain no input handlers.

An element's clip-path now bounds where its cursor and its descendants' apply: outside any basic shape, path() or shape() by its fill rule, or a url(#id) <clipPath>, the cursor is that of what lies beneath.

fixed.member: UI: dashed borders on round corners
fixed.summary: A uniform dashed border or outline is dashed side by side with a dash on every corner; the pattern no longer laps the outline and leaves its remainder as a thick arc on the top-left corner.

Load and register document CSS texture assets, including imported stylesheets and inline styles, on initial load and document reload. Inline URLs resolve beside the document. Cooked SVG files supply mask images and cursor pixels without manual texture loading.

A text's pseudo-element styles draw: ::first-letter, ::first-line, ::before and ::after colours, fonts and decorations were replaced by the element's plain style once its CSS fields applied. ::first-letter takes the first letter, number or symbol with the Unicode punctuation around it (“¿Q, (1)) and a base with its combining marks, as CSS Pseudo-Elements 4 §2.2 says; it took only ASCII punctuation before a single character.

Blends that read the destination inside a UI layer (a filtered, masked or material ancestor) draw instead of being dropped; a layer's composite honours its blend instead of drawing normal; multiply over a layer's transparent pixels no longer darkens them, and screen and plus-lighter keep the layer's alpha.

::selection and ::target-text follow highlight inheritance (CSS Pseudo-Elements 4 §3.5), as ::highlight() does. Each property the text's own element leaves unset comes from the nearest ancestor's rule that sets it, background-color included, so `div::selection { color: red }` now styles the selection in the paragraphs inside that div.
Accept valid MIME parameters in type() descriptors and discard malformed descriptors before resolution deduplication. Asset discovery and rendering use the same selection rules.
Preserve quoted strings during math-function discovery and scan Unicode at character boundaries, avoiding a panic on non-ASCII MIME parameters and accidental evaluation of literal calc() text.
Preserve percentage slice and automatic-width metadata through the renderer instead of clamping it away; automatic widths account for image-set density.

Inline !important declarations, including Svelte style:prop|important, outrank stylesheet !important declarations across cascade layers. Removing a bound inline value restores the underlying declaration.

Moves frames: a justified line ends at its box's edge. Each glyph after a widened space was moved by the extra room twice (by the pen and again by its offset), so a justified line ran past its box by its free room.

fixed.member: UI: a background gradient on an element with a border
fixed.summary: It is placed in the padding box and repeats under the border, as CSS's background-origin default does, instead of stretching over the border box.
Repeating radial and conic gradients repeat the interval between their first and last stops, including negative positions; coincident stops render their CSS average colour.
counter(list-item) in a <ul>'s ::marker or ::before reads the item's number; it read 0 unless the list was numbered.

fixed: Review missing-art fallback slots at natural wide, tall, full-bleed and icon sizes rather than square cells.

fixed.summary: A document whose CSS rule body holds a character of more than one byte (`--icon: é`) no longer crashes its parse.

New parts measure before entering the layout cache. Retained content preserves logical IDs while attaching under its physical part box. Settled animations reuse paint, and removing and reinserting a host retires its parts.
An empty field's placeholder keeps its `::placeholder` colour (else the style's placeholder ink) when the field sets its own `color`; the field's colour inked the placeholder before.

A popover opens and closes as HTML's top layer does. Closed, it keeps no style, so it opens from its `@starting-style` and shows from the frame `:popover-open` matches, one tick after the press, instead of transitioning from its closed style. Its own `opacity`, `transform`, transitions and animations now move its shown layer, not an empty placeholder. Closing with an `allow-discrete` transition of `overlay` or `display` keeps it shown, inert, until that transition ends while its closed style transitions in, where it vanished at once. An open popover keeps its anchor across `restoreState`.

data-og-instant settles the first @starting-style entrance for channel and computed values. Whitespace no longer makes a discrete display exit disappear halfway through; retained display exits retire their render subtree on completion.

fixed.member: Widget part placement in right-to-left frames
fixed.summary: A widget part's own placement is no longer mirrored a second time in a right-to-left frame: a switch's knob stays on its track. Part boxes keep their widget's enter and exit presence.
Evaluate resolution descriptors through the shared CSS math engine: calc(), min(), max() and clamp() accept mixed x, dppx, dpi and dpcm units for document and widget-part images.

Non-repeating CSS gradients preserve stops outside 0..100%; translate:none clears percentage and length offsets; hidden masked boxes preserve subtree layer pairing without painting; column flex items derive auto cross sizes from their final flexed height and aspect ratio.
Built-in CSS packs may reference SVG images inside art/ subdirectories, just like other relative asset directories.
Select popup parts retain their markup host's selector attributes and document stylesheet without changing independent popovers. Part inspection includes persistent part boxes.

Button text uses the host's installed font-family, with part-local font overrides taking precedence. Divider color reaches the drawn rule. Tab indicators retain their layout motion. Persistent content boxes retain host interaction states and focus radii, and select borders preserve default text positions.

A text length in em or a percentage (line-height: 200%, letter-spacing: 0.5em, text-indent, tab-size) resolves against the element's own font-size even when its rule declares that size after it, as CSS computes it; it took the parent's size before.

Moves frames: a CSS text stroke is centred on the glyphs' edge over the fill at its width, as browsers draw it (it ran wholly outside the edge), takes color rather than -webkit-text-fill-color when it names no colour, and paint-order: stroke paints it under the fill so only its outer half shows.

CSS `touch-action` is read from the element a touch lands on (intersected with its ancestors), as Pointer Events 3 says, not from the scroll container the drag moves: `touch-action: pan-y` on a card inside a two-axis scroller now keeps its drag vertical. UI state is version 24 (version 23 upgrades with no touch in progress).

text-underline-position: under puts the underline at the font's descent, clear of every descender, with text-underline-offset measured from there; text-underline-offset: from-font and text-decoration-thickness: from-font take the font's own post underline position and thickness.

Boolean media features follow Media Queries 4 §2.4.4: a feature matches unless its value is 0, `none` or a value it names false. `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` now matches in both schemes, where it used to match in neither. `@media (hover)` and `(any-hover)` no longer match on a coarse pointer, whose `hover` is `none`.

`initial` on `direction`, `unicode-bidi`, `writing-mode`, `text-orientation` and `text-combine-upright` now gives the property's initial value (`ltr`, `normal`, `horizontal-tb`, `mixed`, `none`). It used to keep the parent's value, as `inherit` does: `direction: initial` under an rtl parent stayed rtl.

A document's `ex`, `cap`, `rex` and `rcap` now read the body face's own x-height and cap height (OS/2) instead of 0.5em and the ascent. `ch` and `ic` use the advance of the face's `0` and 水, and fall back to CSS Values 4's 0.5em and 1em when the face lacks the glyph. They used to take the .notdef advance.

A `box-sizing: content-box` size written as `round()`, `mod()`, `rem()`, `abs()` or `hypot()` adds its padding once to the result; it used to add it to each argument, so `round(down, 60%, 50px)` also moved its step.

A custom property registered with `@property` and a `<length>` syntax now computes to px where it is set, so `--gap: 2em` is the setting element's em and its children inherit those pixels. Children used to re-read `2em` at their own font size.

Transition and animation longhands and the `transition` and `animation` shorthands take math their element resolves (viewport and font units, `env()`, `random()`, the tree-counting functions): the value is checked when the element resolves, as a `var()` is, instead of being refused when the document is defined.

white-space: pre, pre-wrap, pre-line and break-spaces (and white-space-collapse) keep the spaces, tabs and line breaks a document's literal text was written with: the text was HTML-collapsed when the document was read, so they had nothing left to keep. pre-wrap may break after a run of spaces, break-spaces after each one, and a tab advances to the next tab-size column.
The capacity readout uses its strings table, so locales can translate the separator and built-in component documents cook without an untranslated-text warning.

Moves frames: adds pinned Lucide fallback vectors for apple, bomb, crown, drop, fire, gear, gem, heart, home, key, leaf, pause, potion, shield and sword, so built-in documents and their sample data draw these icons without a game atlas. Game-supplied icons still win.

Built-in UI icon names now have on-demand vector fallbacks when neither the game's atlas nor fallbackIcons supplies them, including check, lock, close and all three chevrons. Game-supplied icons retain precedence.

Moves frames: default-style games with no font use the licensed Instrument Sans variable outlines in every UI role, ahead of locale fallback faces. The cook ships no atlas and loads the separate face only when needed; games without UI documents carry no default face. A game's own font and other fonts' cook settings remain unchanged.

font-weight and font-stretch now select a role font's wght and wdth axes, including fonts supplied through UiDesc.font. Real supported bold is not synthesised; explicit @font-face descriptor ranges still constrain selection.

fixed: og dev regenerates UI types and restarts source checks when a .svelte document changes, instead of watching the obsolete .ogt document extension.

fixed.summary: A disabled control's input-action handler (`ondetails`, `onconfirm`, …) no longer fires: pressing X over a disabled Track button sent `track` although a tap sent nothing. A `<fieldset disabled>`'s controls are silent too.
